# Capability Catalog

The full Open Capability Framework catalog — 455 capabilities across 36 domains, grouped Segment → Domain → Focus Area. Each capability carries a six-point behavioral profile on the capability-side [P1–P6 proficiency scale](proficiency_scale.md). Note the two-axis split: proficiency (P1–P6) is intrinsic to the capability and measures *how well*; scope ([S1–S6](scope_levels.md)) is a property of the **role** and measures *how broad*. Role records under `roles/` combine the two.

Each capability has a stable anchor equal to its lowercased id (e.g. `#em-03`) so role ladders can deep-link here.

## Engineering & Technology

### Software Engineering (SWE)

#### Code & Quality

<a id="swe-01"></a>
##### SWE-01 — Writing Code

*Type:* Technical — Produces correct, readable, idiomatic code.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes working, readable code in the team's language; debugs own changes.
  — *Why this level:* Writing working code in the team's language while debugging only their own changes under review is Dreyfus's novice band -- explicit rules, no situational judgment; McConnell's construction fundamentals (naming, control structures, defensive basics) are exactly the checklist-level practice novices are taught. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); McConnell, Code Complete: A Practical Handbook of Software Construction, 2nd Edition (Microsoft Press, 2004).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Proficient in the primary language/ecosystem; handles errors, async and concurrency basics correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Handling errors, async, and concurrency basics unsupervised across the primary ecosystem is McConnell's construction-as-discipline bar for a working professional -- routine variation handled without escalation, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* McConnell, Code Complete: A Practical Handbook of Software Construction, 2nd Edition (Microsoft Press, 2004).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Code is a reference others learn from; debugs the hard problems (races, memory, nondeterminism).
  — *Why this level:* Code other engineers learn from, plus independently debugging races, memory issues, and nondeterminism, is autonomous handling of ambiguous, hard cases -- SFIA's 'apply' responsibility level (works with minimal supervision, exercises judgment) and the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Mastery across multiple stacks/paradigms; solves problems others can't; sets implementation patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Mastery across stacks and setting implementation patterns others adopt is Software Engineering at Google's distinction between programming and software engineering: code that outlives its author and shapes how a team builds, the Dreyfus proficient/teaching band. *Sources:* Winters, Manshreck & Wright, Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time (O'Reilly, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets implementation standards adopted across the org; anticipates where code breaks at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide implementation standards and anticipating scale failures moves beyond one team's patterns to organizational policy -- SFIA's set-strategy/influence responsibility band, applied to how the whole engineering org writes code. *Sources:* Winters, Manshreck & Wright, Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time (O'Reilly, 2020); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Industry-level depth; authors foundational primitives and idioms others build on.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring foundational primitives and idioms other engineers build on is IEEE SWEBOK's boundary between practicing the discipline and shaping its body of knowledge -- the Dreyfus master band, externally credible beyond one employer. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-02"></a>
##### SWE-02 — Code Quality & Maintainability

*Type:* Technical — Keeps code healthy, modular and maintainable.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes functional, readable code; uses version control correctly; responds well to review.
  — *Why this level:* Functional, readable code with correct version-control use and responsiveness to review is McConnell's baseline construction hygiene, applied under supervision -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); McConnell, Code Complete: A Practical Handbook of Software Construction, 2nd Edition (Microsoft Press, 2004).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Writes clean, documented, modular code; gives useful review feedback.
  — *Why this level:* Clean, documented, modular code and useful review feedback is Clean Code's core thesis -- code as communication -- practiced independently on routine work, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Martin, Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship (Prentice Hall, 2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs for maintainability; leads refactors of problem areas; review feedback teaches.
  — *Why this level:* Designing for maintainability and leading refactors of problem areas is Fowler's refactoring discipline applied with judgment to ambiguous, already-messy systems -- the Dreyfus competent band, setting the local standard. *Sources:* Fowler, Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code, 2nd Edition (Addison-Wesley, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in code health at scale (shared libraries, deprecations, large migrations).
  — *Why this level:* Expert code health at scale -- shared libraries, deprecations, large migrations -- is Refactoring's discipline applied at Software Engineering at Google's organizational scale, where changes affect a system's whole trajectory, not just one component. *Sources:* Fowler, Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code, 2nd Edition (Addison-Wesley, 2018); Winters, Manshreck & Wright, Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time (O'Reilly, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Shapes org-wide engineering standards for long-lived codebases.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping org-wide engineering standards for long-lived codebases is Software Engineering at Google's central concern (managing the effect of time and scale) elevated to setting policy for the whole engineering org. *Sources:* Winters, Manshreck & Wright, Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time (O'Reilly, 2020).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good engineering looks like company-wide; externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good engineering looks like company-wide and holding external recognition is IEEE SWEBOK's practitioner-to-discipline-shaper transition -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-03"></a>
##### SWE-03 — Testing & Verification

*Type:* Technical — Designs tests that give real confidence to ship.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes unit tests with guidance; tests own changes before merging.
  — *Why this level:* Writing unit tests with guidance and testing only one's own changes before merging is explicit, rule-following practice under review -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies the testing pyramid; everything shipped arrives tested; mocks dependencies sensibly.
  — *Why this level:* Applying the testing pyramid and shipping nothing untested is Cohn's testing-pyramid framework from Succeeding with Agile, executed independently on routine work -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Cohn, Succeeding with Agile: Software Development Using Scrum (Addison-Wesley, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs testable systems (contract, property-based, replay from prod); owns a test strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Designing testable systems (contract, property-based, replay-from-prod) and owning a test strategy is Beck's test-driven-development discipline extended from unit-level practice to system design judgment -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Beck, Test-Driven Development: By Example (Addison-Wesley, 2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in test strategy at scale (test data, environments, deployment safety).
  — *Why this level:* Expert test strategy at scale (test data, environments, deployment safety) is the practice DORA's empirical research ties to elite delivery performance -- beyond one system's tests to the pipeline that ships all of them. *Sources:* DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets testing/verification discipline across the org.
  — *Why this level:* Setting testing/verification discipline across the org is DORA's organizational capabilities (test automation, deployment safety) turned into enforced policy -- SFIA's strategy-setting responsibility band. *Sources:* DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes the company-wide quality culture; advances verification practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping company-wide quality culture and advancing verification practice beyond one employer is IEEE SWEBOK's software-quality knowledge area elevated to discipline-defining contribution -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-04"></a>
##### SWE-04 — Code Comprehension & Review

*Type:* Technical — Reads, reasons about and reviews others' code.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Navigates the codebase and understands code shown; reviews small changes.
  — *Why this level:* Navigating a codebase and reviewing only small changes under guidance is explicit, bounded practice -- the Dreyfus novice band; Google's review guidelines describe exactly this scope for new reviewers finding their feet. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Engineering Practices Documentation: How to Do a Code Review (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently understands unfamiliar code; gives timely, specific review feedback.
  — *Why this level:* Independently understanding unfamiliar code and giving timely, specific feedback is Google's Standard of Code Review bar for a qualified reviewer working without oversight -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band applied to review. *Sources:* Google, Engineering Practices Documentation: How to Do a Code Review (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Quickly grasps complex/legacy systems; reviews raise the bar across a domain.
  — *Why this level:* Quickly grasping complex/legacy systems so reviews raise the bar across a domain matches Cohen's Cisco study finding that experienced reviewers catch defects and elevate team code quality, not just individual changes -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Cohen, Best Kept Secrets of Peer Code Review (SmartBear, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert at reviewing high-risk changes; review standards spread across teams.
  — *Why this level:* Reviewing high-risk changes as an expert and spreading standards across teams is Feathers's legacy-code expertise (understanding code no one else fully grasps) turned into a transferable review standard beyond one team. *Sources:* Feathers, Working Effectively with Legacy Code (Prentice Hall, 2004).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Authority on review practice org-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Being the org-wide authority on review practice is Google's published review standard elevated from team convention to organizational policy -- SFIA's advise/ensure responsibility band. *Sources:* Google, Engineering Practices Documentation: How to Do a Code Review (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good review looks like; shapes industry-facing practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good review looks like and shaping industry-facing practice is IEEE SWEBOK's software-quality/maintenance knowledge area advanced beyond one company -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

#### Design & Architecture

<a id="swe-05"></a>
##### SWE-05 — Software Design & Architecture

*Type:* Technical — Structures software — modules, boundaries, interfaces.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements designs specified by others; asks why, not just how.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing designs specified by others while asking why, not just how, is explicit rule-following with emerging context-awareness -- the Dreyfus novice-to-advanced-beginner transition. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs sound components; understands coupling, cohesion, interface design.
  — *Why this level:* Designing sound components and understanding coupling, cohesion, and interface design independently is applying the Gang of Four's pattern vocabulary to real, if bounded, design problems -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Gamma, Helm, Johnson & Vlissides, Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software (Addison-Wesley, 1994).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs systems for evolution: clean seams, versioned interfaces, replaceable parts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing for evolution -- clean seams, versioned interfaces, replaceable parts -- is Software Architecture in Practice's quality-attribute-driven design applied with judgment to ambiguous tradeoffs -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Bass, Clements & Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice, 4th Edition (Addison-Wesley, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Mastery of architecture for complex systems; sets patterns and prevents drift.
  — *Why this level:* Architecture mastery for complex systems, setting patterns and preventing drift, is Bass, Clements & Kazman's architecture-evaluation discipline exercised at a scope other engineers adopt patterns from. *Sources:* Bass, Clements & Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice, 4th Edition (Addison-Wesley, 2021); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets multi-year architecture direction across the org.
  — *Why this level:* Setting multi-year architecture direction across the org is Software Architecture in Practice's strategic architecture-governance role, sustained beyond a single system's lifecycle. *Sources:* Bass, Clements & Kazman, Software Architecture in Practice, 4th Edition (Addison-Wesley, 2021).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Authoritative and externally credible; defines architectural approach others follow.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible and defining the architectural approach others follow is IEEE SWEBOK's software-design knowledge area advanced to discipline-shaping contribution -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-06"></a>
##### SWE-06 — Debugging & Systems Diagnosis

*Type:* Technical — Diagnoses defects and anomalies methodically.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Debugs issues in own code with support; uses basic tooling.
  — *Why this level:* Debugging own-code issues with support and basic tooling is Zeller's description of ad hoc, unsystematic debugging before the discipline is internalized -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zeller, Why Programs Fail: A Guide to Systematic Debugging, 2nd Edition (Morgan Kaufmann, 2009).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently diagnoses defects in own area systematically.
  — *Why this level:* Independently and systematically diagnosing defects in one's own area is Why Programs Fail's core thesis -- debugging as a repeatable, scientific process rather than guesswork -- applied unsupervised, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Zeller, Why Programs Fail: A Guide to Systematic Debugging, 2nd Edition (Morgan Kaufmann, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Leads diagnosis of hard, cross-cutting failures; root cause not symptoms.
  — *Why this level:* Leading diagnosis of hard, cross-cutting failures by root cause is the Google SRE book's postmortem culture (blameless root-cause analysis over symptom patching) exercised with judgment -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert at the rare/systemic failures; builds tooling that makes them visible.
  — *Why this level:* Being expert at rare/systemic failures and building tooling that makes them visible is SRE's observability and toil-elimination practice elevated to building the diagnostic infrastructure others depend on. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** The person called for the worst failures; sets diagnostic practice org-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Being the person called for the worst failures and setting diagnostic practice org-wide is the SRE book's incident-command and postmortem-review practice turned into enforced organizational policy. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Authority on diagnosis; advances the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Being an authority on diagnosis who advances the discipline is IEEE SWEBOK's software-maintenance knowledge area extended into original, externally recognized contribution -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-07"></a>
##### SWE-07 — API & Service Design

*Type:* Technical — Designs clean, durable interfaces between systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands HTTP/REST and the deploy pipeline; makes guided changes.
  — *Why this level:* Understanding HTTP/REST and the deploy pipeline while making only guided changes is applying Fielding's REST constraints as given rules rather than judged tradeoffs -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs clean APIs; understands rate limits, retries, timeouts, idempotency.
  — *Why this level:* Designing clean APIs with correct rate limits, retries, timeouts, and idempotency is applying REST's architectural constraints (statelessness, uniform interface) independently to routine service design -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs services for scale and cost; understands distributed failure modes.
  — *Why this level:* Designing services for scale and cost while understanding distributed failure modes is Newman's Building Microservices core content (partial failure, service boundaries) applied with judgment to ambiguous tradeoffs -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in platform/service design (multi-tenancy, capacity, shared services).
  — *Why this level:* Platform/service-design expertise -- multi-tenancy, capacity, shared services -- is Building Microservices's scaling concerns, both organizational and technical, mastered at a level that sets patterns other services follow. *Sources:* Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets interface standards used across the org.
  — *Why this level:* Setting interface standards used across the org is service-design practice elevated to enforced platform policy -- SFIA's strategy-setting responsibility band applied to API governance. *Sources:* Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines company-wide API approach; trusted with irreversible interface bets.
  — *Why this level:* Defining company-wide API approach and being trusted with irreversible interface bets echoes Fielding's own role: an architectural style whose constraints outlived one project and shaped an industry -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-08"></a>
##### SWE-08 — Type-System Domain Modeling

*Type:* Technical — Uses a static type system as a design medium — encoding domain rules and invariants in types so invalid states are unrepresentable and whole defect classes are eliminated at compile time.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes correctly typed code without escape hatches (`any`-equivalents), uses the codebase's existing types and generics correctly, and reads compiler errors to the actual cause with guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Writing correctly typed code without escape hatches and reading compiler errors to their real cause, with guidance, is explicit rule-following on a well-defined task -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Models feature domains so invalid states fail to compile — sum types / discriminated unions over boolean flags, narrowing over assertions — preferring type-level constraints where the compiler can carry the load.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling domains so invalid states fail to compile -- sum types over boolean flags, narrowing over assertions -- is Wlaschin's 'making illegal states unrepresentable' thesis applied independently to routine feature work, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Wlaschin, Domain Modeling Made Functional: Tackle Software Complexity with Domain-Driven Design and F# (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs the shared domain types a capability is built on, keeping inference ergonomic for consumers; judges when type-level sophistication pays and when it obscures, and unwinds accumulated type erosion in others' code.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the shared domain types a capability is built on, and judging when type sophistication pays versus obscures, is Domain Modeling Made Functional's design judgment plus King's parse-don't-validate discipline exercised on ambiguous, real tradeoffs -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Wlaschin, Domain Modeling Made Functional: Tackle Software Complexity with Domain-Driven Design and F# (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018); King, Parse, Don't Validate (lexi-lambda.github.io, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Sets type-design conventions multiple teams adopt — strictness policy, shared type libraries, branded identifiers, result types — and leads migrations that raise strictness without halting delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Setting type-design conventions multiple teams adopt (strictness policy, branded identifiers, result types) and leading strictness migrations is parse-don't-validate elevated from one codebase's discipline to a transferable, org-adopted convention. *Sources:* King, Parse, Don't Validate (lexi-lambda.github.io, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns an organization's type-system posture — compiler baselines, monorepo type architecture, upgrade cadence — measured by defect and velocity outcomes.
  — *Why this level:* Owning an organization's type-system posture -- compiler baselines, monorepo architecture, upgrade cadence -- measured by outcomes is strategy-level ownership, SFIA's set-strategy/ensure responsibility band applied to a technical platform. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Makes company-level language and type-platform bets and represents the practice externally (talks, upstream contributions, published patterns).
  — *Why this level:* Making company-level type-platform bets and representing the practice externally (talks, upstream contributions) is IEEE SWEBOK's software-construction knowledge area advanced into original, publicly credited contribution -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="swe-09"></a>
##### SWE-09 — Boundary Validation & End-to-End Type Integrity

*Type:* Technical — Validates untrusted data into precise types once at every system boundary (network, storage, configuration, third parties) and propagates a single source of type truth across client, server, and wire so contracts cannot silently drift.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses the codebase's shared contract types and schema validators at boundaries rather than hand-casting external data, and can point to where a type is checked at runtime.
  — *Why this level:* Using the codebase's existing contract types and validators at boundaries rather than hand-casting, and being able to point to where a type is runtime-checked, is following King's parse-don't-validate pattern as given convention rather than judged design -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); King, Parse, Don't Validate (lexi-lambda.github.io, 2019).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Puts runtime validation at every I/O boundary they touch — requests, messages, configuration — deriving static types from the runtime schemas so compile-time and runtime cannot drift.
  — *Why this level:* Putting runtime validation at every I/O boundary touched and deriving static types from runtime schemas is parse-don't-validate's core prescription -- parse at the boundary -- applied independently across routine boundaries, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* King, Parse, Don't Validate (lexi-lambda.github.io, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs end-to-end type integrity for a capability — schema-first contracts, generated clients, contract drift caught in continuous integration — and blocks unsound casts and unvalidated edges in review.
  — *Why this level:* Designing end-to-end type integrity -- schema-first contracts, generated clients, drift caught in continuous integration -- and blocking unsound casts in review is NIST SSDF's produce-well-secured-software practice (validate all externally sourced input) exercised with design judgment across a whole capability -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* NIST, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1, SP 800-218 (2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds the code-generation and contract-typing infrastructure multiple teams inherit, making boundary safety the default rather than a discipline, and resolves cross-team type drift at its source.
  — *Why this level:* Building the code-generation and contract-typing infrastructure multiple teams inherit is NIST SSDF's boundary-validation practice turned into default platform tooling rather than a discipline individuals must remember to apply. *Sources:* NIST, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1, SP 800-218 (2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's boundary-safety standard and the platform tooling that enforces it, with incident evidence showing the failure classes it removed.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's boundary-safety standard and platform tooling, evidenced by incidents it removed, is SSDF's organizational secure-development practice elevated to enforced policy with measured outcomes -- SFIA's strategy-setting band. *Sources:* NIST, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1, SP 800-218 (2022); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Owns contract-integrity strategy across products and external interfaces where a broken contract is a business event, and advances the state of practice publicly.
  — *Why this level:* Owning contract-integrity strategy across products and external interfaces, where a broken contract is a business event, and advancing the state of practice publicly, is IEEE SWEBOK's software-requirements and software-design knowledge areas extended into externally credible, discipline-shaping contribution. *Sources:* IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

#### Code & Quality

<a id="swe-10"></a>
##### SWE-10 — AI-augmented development

*Type:* Behavioral — Works effectively with AI coding tools and agents while remaining accountable for the output - calibrating what to delegate and what to hand-write, verifying generated changes with the same rigor as hand-written ones, and setting the review and provenance practices that keep quality intact.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses AI coding tools with the output treated as a draft - reads every generated line, tests it, and can explain any part of the diff when asked.
  — *Why this level:* Treating AI output as a draft -- reading every generated line, testing it, explaining any part of the diff -- is the verification discipline Peng et al.'s controlled Copilot study assumes as the baseline condition for safe use; without it the study's measured speedups don't hold, the Dreyfus novice band of explicit checking without calibration. *Sources:* Peng, Kalliamvakou, Cihon & Demirer, The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot (arXiv, 2023).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Calibrates when generation helps and when it misleads for the work at hand; catches plausible-but-wrong generated code before review, and their AI-assisted changes pass review at the same rate as hand-written ones.
  — *Why this level:* Calibrating when generation helps versus misleads, and catching plausible-but-wrong code before review, is exactly the skill METR's 2025 randomized trial found experienced developers lacked -- the study measured a 19% slowdown from miscalibrated trust, making demonstrated calibration the Dreyfus advanced-beginner-to-competent differentiator this capability is built around. *Sources:* Becker, Rush, Barnes & Rein (METR), Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity (2025).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Sets the norms for AI-assisted work in a domain - what may be delegated to agents, what verification it requires, how provenance is noted in review - and coaches others out of over-trust and under-use.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the norms for AI-assisted work in a domain and coaching others out of over- or under-trust is DORA 2024's organizational-capability layer (AI adoption paired with quality practices) applied by an individual with authority over local practice -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines AI-assisted engineering practice across teams - where agents run in the delivery lifecycle, what gates their output - justified by throughput and defect data rather than vendor claims.
  — *Why this level:* Defining AI-assisted engineering practice across teams, justified by throughput and defect data rather than vendor claims, mirrors DORA's own empirical method -- measuring delivery outcomes rather than trusting adoption claims -- applied at cross-team scope. *Sources:* DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Drives an organization's AI-augmented engineering strategy - tooling selection, workflow redesign, skill expectations - and adjusts policy from measured delivery outcomes.
  — *Why this level:* Driving an org's AI-augmented engineering strategy and adjusting policy from measured delivery outcomes is DORA's research method turned into enforced organizational policy -- SFIA's set-strategy responsibility band. *Sources:* DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how software engineering itself changes with AI at company and industry level; a credible public voice on what changes and what doesn't.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how software engineering changes with AI at company and industry level, as a credible public voice, is the discipline-level contribution IEEE SWEBOK's knowledge areas are periodically revised to absorb -- the kind of empirical, industry-shaping public research METR itself represents. *Sources:* Becker, Rush, Barnes & Rein (METR), Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity (2025); IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

### Frontend & Client Engineering (FE)

#### UI Construction & Rendering

<a id="fe-01"></a>
##### FE-01 — Component-based UI architecture

*Type:* Technical — Composing user interfaces from reusable, encapsulated UI components with clear boundaries and contracts.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds simple components from existing patterns; relies on review to validate boundaries and props.
  — *Why this level:* Composing a page from existing components by following someone else's decomposition, with props/state wiring checked in review, is applying React's 'Thinking in React' steps without yet owning them — Dreyfus novice: works from the recipe, doesn't set it. *Sources:* Meta, Thinking in React (React documentation, accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Composes reusable components independently, handling standard prop, state, and event wiring with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently wiring standard props, state, and events across components is Thinking in React's single-responsibility decomposition applied routinely to familiar UI shapes — advanced-beginner: correct on the standard case, not yet designing the hierarchy. *Sources:* Meta, Thinking in React (React documentation, accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs component hierarchies and clear interfaces autonomously; resolves tricky composition and reuse trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a component hierarchy and resolving reuse/composition trade-offs autonomously is doing Atomic Design's atoms-to-organisms decomposition work itself, not just following someone else's — the Dreyfus competent band, where the practitioner sets the local structure. *Sources:* Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the component architecture and conventions teams adopt; untangles deeply coupled or overgrown trees.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the component conventions a whole codebase or multiple teams adopt, and untangling overgrown trees, is publishing the atomic-design taxonomy other teams inherit — SFIA's ensure/advise reach beyond one's own work. *Sources:* Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide component design strategy; anticipates how composition models should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide component design strategy and anticipating how composition models should evolve is SFIA's initiate/influence level — authority spanning multiple teams' architecture, not just one team's. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good component architecture means industrywide; shapes practice through widely adopted patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good component architecture means industrywide, in the way Atomic Design itself became a widely cited vocabulary beyond its author's own projects, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band extended past one organization's boundary. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016).

<a id="fe-02"></a>
##### FE-02 — Declarative UI rendering & reactivity

*Type:* Technical — Expressing UI as a function of state and managing efficient re-rendering when data changes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Binds data to views and updates state for simple cases under review.
  — *Why this level:* Binding data to a view and updating state for simple cases under review is applying a Presentation Model's separation of view-state from view without yet owning where that state lives — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Fowler, Presentation Model (martinfowler.com, 2004); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds reactive views independently, managing derived state and updates with routine review.
  — *Why this level:* Building reactive views and derived state independently for standard flows is routine application of the presentation-model pattern to familiar shapes — advanced beginner, correct without needing to design the data flow. *Sources:* Fowler, Presentation Model (martinfowler.com, 2004); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reactive data flows autonomously; debugs subtle re-render and dependency issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing reactive data flows and debugging subtle re-render/dependency issues autonomously is doing Flux's job of enforcing a single, predictable direction for state changes — the practitioner is now designing the flow, not just consuming one, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Facebook, Flux Application Architecture (2014); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines reactivity patterns others follow; resolves the hardest update and consistency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the reactivity patterns other engineers follow and resolving the hardest update-consistency problems is publishing the unidirectional-flow discipline Flux itself popularized beyond one app — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Facebook, Flux Application Architecture (2014); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for declarative rendering models; anticipates where reactivity paradigms head.
  — *Why this level:* Setting strategy for declarative rendering models across systems and anticipating where reactivity paradigms head is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority over direction, not just a single app's data flow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry understanding of reactive UI; pioneers widely emulated rendering approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry understanding of reactive UI, the way the presentation-model/MVVM lineage itself reshaped a generation of UI frameworks, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level stretched to industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fowler, Presentation Model (martinfowler.com, 2004).

<a id="fe-03"></a>
##### FE-03 — Document structure & semantic markup

*Type:* Technical — Structuring content with meaningful, well-formed markup that conveys semantics and hierarchy.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes valid markup using common semantic elements for simple pages under review.
  — *Why this level:* Writing valid markup with common semantic elements (header, nav, main) for simple pages under review is applying the HTML Living Standard's vocabulary without judgment calls on structure — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Structures documents independently with correct semantics for standard content layouts.
  — *Why this level:* Structuring standard content layouts independently with correct semantics is routine, correct application of the HTML Living Standard's sectioning-content model — advanced beginner: right on the common case. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs robust semantic structures autonomously; handles complex, dynamic, or nested content.
  — *Why this level:* Designing robust semantic structures for complex, dynamic, or nested content autonomously means resolving cases the spec leaves as author judgment (implicit ARIA roles, sectioning ambiguity) — the Dreyfus competent band, setting the local standard. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines markup conventions teams adopt; resolves ambiguous structural and semantic edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining markup conventions a team adopts and resolving ambiguous structural edge cases is producing the interpretive guidance the living standard itself defers to authors — SFIA's ensure/advise reach across a team's codebase. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organizational standards for semantic document structure; anticipates evolving markup capabilities.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organizational standards for semantic structure and anticipating evolving markup capabilities (new HTML elements, evolving sectioning model) is SFIA's initiate/influence band, authority beyond a single team's conventions. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry norms for semantic markup; influences standards and widely referenced practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry norms for semantic markup — the kind of practice that feeds back into WHATWG standards discussions — is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level extended to shaping the standard itself, not just applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="fe-04"></a>
##### FE-04 — Client-side rendering strategies

*Type:* Technical — Choosing among client, server, static, and hybrid rendering approaches to balance speed and interactivity.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements basic client rendering for simple views under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing basic client rendering for simple views under guidance is executing one branch of Osmani's rendering-on-the-web taxonomy without yet choosing between branches — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Osmani, Rendering on the Web (web.dev / Google, 2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard rendering approaches independently, handling routine hydration and load cases.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard rendering approaches independently, handling routine hydration and load cases, is correctly operating within a chosen point of that taxonomy for familiar app shapes — advanced beginner. *Sources:* Osmani, Rendering on the Web (web.dev / Google, 2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Chooses and tunes rendering strategies autonomously across varied app and performance needs.
  — *Why this level:* Choosing and tuning rendering strategies autonomously across varied app and performance needs is doing the CSR/SSR/SSG/hybrid trade-off analysis Osmani's taxonomy and Grigorik's network-performance model exist to inform — the Dreyfus competent band, owning the decision. *Sources:* Osmani, Rendering on the Web (web.dev / Google, 2019); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines rendering-strategy approaches teams adopt; solves hard hydration and timing problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining rendering-strategy approaches a team adopts and solving hard hydration/timing problems is producing the kind of reusable guidance Osmani's own taxonomy distilled from practice — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Osmani, Rendering on the Web (web.dev / Google, 2019); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets rendering strategy across systems; anticipates shifts in client rendering models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting rendering strategy across systems and anticipating shifts in client rendering models is applying network-performance-model thinking at a portfolio level — SFIA's initiate/influence authority. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for rendering strategies industrywide; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for rendering strategies industrywide, the way Osmani's rendering taxonomy itself became a reference point beyond one team, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Osmani, Rendering on the Web (web.dev / Google, 2019).

#### State & Data on the Client

<a id="fe-05"></a>
##### FE-05 — Client-side state management

*Type:* Technical — Modeling, storing, and synchronizing application and UI state across the client at appropriate scope.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Reads and updates simple shared state following established patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Reading and updating simple shared state following an established pattern under review is following someone else's presentation-model design without owning it — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Fowler, Presentation Model (martinfowler.com, 2004); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages component and shared state independently for standard flows with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing component and shared state independently for standard flows with normal review is routine, correct use of an existing state pattern — advanced beginner. *Sources:* Fowler, Presentation Model (martinfowler.com, 2004); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs state architecture autonomously; resolves complex synchronization and ownership issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing state architecture autonomously and resolving complex synchronization/ownership issues is doing the architectural work Flux's unidirectional-store pattern exists to solve — the Dreyfus competent band, owning the design. *Sources:* Facebook, Flux Application Architecture (2014); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines state-management patterns others adopt; untangles tangled global and derived state.
  — *Why this level:* Defining state-management patterns others adopt and untangling tangled global/derived state is publishing the kind of disciplined store architecture Flux itself popularized beyond one codebase — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Facebook, Flux Application Architecture (2014); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets state-management strategy across the organization; anticipates evolving paradigms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting state-management strategy across the organization and anticipating evolving paradigms is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority over direction across many codebases. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good client state management means; shapes industry patterns and practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good client state management means, in the way Flux's unidirectional-flow idea itself reshaped an industry's default state patterns, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Facebook, Flux Application Architecture (2014).

<a id="fe-06"></a>
##### FE-06 — Client-side data fetching & caching

*Type:* Technical — Retrieving, caching, revalidating, and synchronizing remote data within the client lifecycle.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Fetches and displays data for simple endpoints under review.
  — *Why this level:* Fetching and displaying data for simple endpoints under review is calling an API without yet applying HTTP caching semantics — Dreyfus novice, correctness only. *Sources:* Fielding, Nottingham & Reschke, HTTP Caching, RFC 9111 (IETF, 2022); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements fetching with loading and error states independently for standard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing fetching with loading and error states independently for standard cases is routine, correct client behavior but not yet reasoning about cache freshness — advanced beginner. *Sources:* Fielding, Nottingham & Reschke, HTTP Caching, RFC 9111 (IETF, 2022); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs fetching and caching strategies autonomously; handles invalidation and race conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Designing fetching/caching strategies autonomously and handling invalidation and race conditions is applying RFC 9111's freshness/validation model and RFC 5861's stale-while-revalidate semantics as design tools, not just following defaults — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Fielding, Nottingham & Reschke, HTTP Caching, RFC 9111 (IETF, 2022); Fielding & Nottingham, HTTP Cache-Control Extensions for Stale Content, RFC 5861 (IETF, 2010); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines fetching and caching patterns teams adopt; solves hard staleness and consistency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining fetching and caching patterns a team adopts and solving hard staleness/consistency problems is producing the kind of reusable revalidation policy RFC 5861 formalizes for reuse beyond one request — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Fielding & Nottingham, HTTP Cache-Control Extensions for Stale Content, RFC 5861 (IETF, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for client data access and caching; anticipates evolving data-sync models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting strategy for client data access and caching across the org and anticipating evolving data-sync models is SFIA's initiate/influence authority, beyond a single app's cache policy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for client data fetching and caching; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for client data fetching and caching, the way the HTTP caching standard itself is refined through such practice, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Nottingham & Reschke, HTTP Caching, RFC 9111 (IETF, 2022).

<a id="fe-07"></a>
##### FE-07 — Client-side routing & navigation

*Type:* Technical — Managing in-application navigation, route state, and history without full reloads.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds routes and links for simple navigation under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Adding routes and links for simple navigation under guidance is using the History API's basic push/pop mechanics without owning the routing design — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements nested and parameterized routing independently for standard flows.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing nested and parameterized routing independently for standard flows is correct, routine application of session-history mechanics to familiar app shapes — advanced beginner. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs routing architecture autonomously; handles guards, lazy loading, and deep linking.
  — *Why this level:* Designing routing architecture autonomously — guards, lazy loading, deep linking — is doing the design work the History API only provides primitives for; the practitioner is now architecting navigation state, not just calling pushState — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines routing patterns others adopt; resolves complex navigation and state-preservation cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining routing patterns others adopt and resolving complex navigation/state-preservation cases is publishing reusable navigation architecture built on session-history primitives — SFIA's ensure/advise reach across a team. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets navigation architecture strategy across applications; anticipates evolving routing models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting navigation architecture strategy across applications and anticipating evolving routing models is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority spanning multiple applications' navigation design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for client routing industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for client routing industrywide is shaping how the wider ecosystem uses session-history primitives beyond any one framework — SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07).

#### Layout & Visual Styling

<a id="fe-08"></a>
##### FE-08 — Responsive & adaptive layout

*Type:* Technical — Designing layouts that fluidly adapt across viewport sizes, orientations, and device capabilities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided responsive rules to simple layouts under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying provided responsive rules to simple layouts under review is using Flexbox properties someone else chose, without design authority — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds responsive layouts independently across common breakpoints and devices.
  — *Why this level:* Building responsive layouts independently across common breakpoints and devices is correct, routine application of the CSS Flexible Box and Grid Layout standards to familiar page shapes — advanced beginner. *Sources:* W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1; W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Flexible Box Layout Module Level 1; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs adaptive layout systems autonomously; handles complex fluid and content-driven cases.
  — *Why this level:* Designing adaptive layout systems autonomously for complex fluid and content-driven cases is doing the two-dimensional layout design CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1 exists to enable, not just following a template — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines responsive layout approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest cross-device challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Defining responsive layout approaches a team adopts and solving the hardest cross-device challenges is publishing reusable layout architecture built on the Grid/Flexbox standards — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1; SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organizational strategy for responsive and adaptive layout; anticipates new device classes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organizational strategy for responsive and adaptive layout, anticipating new device classes, is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority beyond one team's layout system. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for responsive design; pioneers widely referenced layout techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for responsive design, feeding back into how layout standards like CSS Grid get used at scale, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1.

<a id="fe-09"></a>
##### FE-09 — Visual styling & presentation systems

*Type:* Technical — Applying scalable styling approaches for visual presentation, theming, and consistent appearance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies existing styles and tokens to components under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying existing styles and tokens to components under review is consuming someone else's design-token system without owning its structure — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Design Tokens Format Module (draft); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements styling independently following design systems for standard components.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing styling independently following a design system for standard components is correct, routine use of an existing token/style system — advanced beginner. *Sources:* W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Design Tokens Format Module (draft); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs scalable styling systems autonomously; resolves specificity, theming, and reuse issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing scalable styling systems autonomously and resolving specificity, theming, and reuse issues is working the CSS cascade/specificity algorithm directly to solve real conflicts, not avoiding them by convention — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* W3C CSS Working Group, CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines styling architecture and conventions others adopt; untangles fragile, sprawling styles.
  — *Why this level:* Defining styling architecture and conventions others adopt, untangling fragile sprawling styles, is publishing the kind of token taxonomy the Design Tokens Format standard exists to make portable across a team — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Design Tokens Format Module (draft); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets styling-system strategy across the organization; anticipates evolving presentation approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Setting styling-system strategy across the organization and anticipating evolving presentation approaches is SFIA's initiate/influence band, authority beyond one team's design system. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good styling architecture means industrywide; shapes widely adopted systems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good styling architecture means industrywide, the way Atomic Design's vocabulary itself became a shared reference beyond its origin, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016).

<a id="fe-10"></a>
##### FE-10 — Cross-browser & cross-device compatibility

*Type:* Technical — Ensuring consistent behavior and appearance across differing rendering engines and environments.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Fixes obvious compatibility issues on common browsers under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Fixing obvious compatibility issues on common browsers under guidance is patching symptoms the Interop project's own focus-area scores would already flag, without diagnosing root cause — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tests and resolves standard cross-browser problems independently.
  — *Why this level:* Testing and resolving standard cross-browser problems independently is routinely handling the kind of divergence the Interop project tracks as common, already-triaged gaps — advanced beginner. *Sources:* WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs compatibility strategies autonomously; diagnoses obscure rendering and behavior differences.
  — *Why this level:* Designing compatibility strategies autonomously and diagnosing obscure rendering/behavior differences is doing root-cause interoperability analysis of the kind the Interop project's focus areas are built from — the Dreyfus competent band, ahead of documented gaps. *Sources:* WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines compatibility approaches teams adopt; solves the most elusive cross-environment bugs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining compatibility approaches a team adopts and solving the most elusive cross-environment bugs is producing reusable diagnostic practice beyond any single bug — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets cross-browser and device strategy; anticipates platform fragmentation and capability shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting cross-browser and device strategy, anticipating platform fragmentation and capability shifts, is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority over direction, not just resolving individual gaps. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for compatibility; pioneers influential approaches to fragmentation.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for compatibility, in the way engineers who file and drive Interop focus areas influence what browser vendors prioritize, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026).

<a id="fe-11"></a>
##### FE-11 — Animation & motion implementation

*Type:* Technical — Implementing performant, purposeful transitions and motion that enhance usability without distraction.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements simple transitions from provided specs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing simple transitions from provided specs under review is executing someone else's timing/easing choices without applying animation-principle judgment — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Thomas & Johnston, Disney Animation: The Illusion of Life (Abbeville Press, 1981); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard animations independently with attention to timing and smoothness.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard animations independently with attention to timing and smoothness is routine, correct application of a published motion system's duration/easing tokens — advanced beginner. *Sources:* Google, Material Design 3 Motion guidelines; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs performant motion systems autonomously; handles complex sequencing and interruption.
  — *Why this level:* Designing performant motion systems autonomously, handling complex sequencing and interruption, is applying animation principles like anticipation, follow-through, and easing (Thomas & Johnston) as engineering judgment on interruptible, performant UI — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Thomas & Johnston, Disney Animation: The Illusion of Life (Abbeville Press, 1981); Google, Material Design 3 Motion guidelines; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines animation patterns others adopt; solves hard performance and choreography problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining animation patterns others adopt and solving hard performance/choreography problems is publishing the kind of systemized motion language Material Motion itself formalizes for reuse beyond one screen — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Google, Material Design 3 Motion guidelines; SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets motion-design implementation strategy; anticipates evolving animation capabilities.
  — *Why this level:* Setting motion-design implementation strategy and anticipating evolving animation capabilities is SFIA's initiate/influence band, authority spanning a product's motion language. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for motion implementation industrywide; shapes widely adopted techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for motion implementation industrywide, the way animation principles first codified for film shaped a generation of UI motion design, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Thomas & Johnston, Disney Animation: The Illusion of Life (Abbeville Press, 1981).

#### User Experience Quality

<a id="fe-12"></a>
##### FE-12 — Accessibility engineering

*Type:* Technical — Building interfaces usable by people with diverse abilities and assistive technologies per inclusive standards.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies basic accessibility fixes following checklists under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying basic accessibility fixes following checklists under review is executing WCAG success criteria someone else selected, without judgment on which apply — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements accessible components independently meeting standard requirements.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing accessible components independently to meet standard requirements is correctly satisfying WCAG 2.2 Level AA criteria for familiar component shapes — advanced beginner. *Sources:* W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs accessible experiences autonomously; resolves complex assistive-technology and interaction cases.
  — *Why this level:* Designing accessible experiences autonomously and resolving complex assistive-technology and interaction cases is applying WAI-ARIA 1.2's roles/states/properties model to cases the spec leaves to author judgment (custom widgets, dynamic content) — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* W3C, Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines accessibility approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest inclusive-design problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining accessibility approaches a team adopts and solving the hardest inclusive-design problems is producing reusable ARIA/WCAG interpretation guidance beyond a single component — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023); W3C, Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 (2023); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets accessibility strategy across the organization; anticipates evolving standards and needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting accessibility strategy across the organization and anticipating evolving standards and needs is SFIA's initiate/influence band, tracking WCAG's own version evolution at an organizational level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry accessibility practice; influences standards and widely referenced guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry accessibility practice and influencing standards is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level extended to contributing back to bodies like the W3C's WAI-ARIA working group, not just applying their output. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); W3C, Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 (2023).

<a id="fe-13"></a>
##### FE-13 — Frontend performance optimization

*Type:* Technical — Optimizing load, render, and runtime responsiveness through asset, network, and rendering improvements.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies known performance fixes to simple cases under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Applying known performance fixes to simple cases under guidance is executing one of Souders' 14 rules without diagnosing which applies — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Souders, High Performance Web Sites: Essential Knowledge for Front-End Engineers (O'Reilly, 2007); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Profiles and improves standard performance issues independently.
  — *Why this level:* Profiling and improving standard performance issues independently is routinely moving Core Web Vitals metrics (LCP, INP, CLS) toward field-data thresholds for familiar cases — advanced beginner. *Sources:* Google, Core Web Vitals, built on the Chrome User Experience Report (2020-); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and optimizes performance autonomously across rendering, loading, and runtime.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and optimizing performance autonomously across rendering, loading, and runtime is doing the network- and rendering-level root-cause analysis Grigorik's performance model and Core Web Vitals field data are built to inform — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Google, Core Web Vitals, built on the Chrome User Experience Report (2020-); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines performance approaches teams adopt; solves the most stubborn bottlenecks.
  — *Why this level:* Defining performance approaches a team adopts and solving the most stubborn bottlenecks is producing the kind of transferable rule set Souders distilled from Yahoo-scale practice, reusable beyond one page — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Souders, High Performance Web Sites: Essential Knowledge for Front-End Engineers (O'Reilly, 2007); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets frontend performance strategy and budgets; anticipates emerging performance concerns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting frontend performance strategy and budgets across products, anticipating emerging performance concerns, is SFIA's initiate/influence band, operating at the portfolio level Core Web Vitals is meant to be tracked at. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Core Web Vitals, built on the Chrome User Experience Report (2020-).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good frontend performance means industrywide; pioneers influential techniques.
