  — *Why this level:* Defining what good frontend performance means industrywide, the way Grigorik's network-performance model itself became a widely taught reference, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).

<a id="fe-14"></a>
##### FE-14 — Internationalization & localization

*Type:* Technical — Adapting interfaces for multiple languages, locales, formats, and writing directions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Externalizes strings and applies locale formatting for simple cases under review.
  — *Why this level:* Externalizing strings and applying locale formatting for simple cases under review is calling ECMA-402 Intl APIs someone else selected, without owning locale-data decisions — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Ecma International, ECMA-402: ECMAScript Internationalization API Specification (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements internationalization independently for standard content and locales.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing internationalization independently for standard content and locales is correct, routine use of the Intl formatting APIs for common locale shapes — advanced beginner. *Sources:* Ecma International, ECMA-402: ECMAScript Internationalization API Specification (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs i18n architecture autonomously; handles pluralization, bidirectionality, and complex formatting.
  — *Why this level:* Designing i18n architecture autonomously and handling pluralization, bidirectionality, and complex formatting is applying CLDR's plural-rule and bidi data directly to cases ECMA-402's APIs only expose as primitives — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Unicode Consortium, Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR); Ecma International, ECMA-402: ECMAScript Internationalization API Specification (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines internationalization approaches teams adopt; solves hard multilingual and cultural cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining internationalization approaches a team adopts and solving hard multilingual/cultural cases is producing reusable locale architecture on top of CLDR data, beyond one feature — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Unicode Consortium, Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets i18n and localization strategy across products; anticipates expanding locale and market needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting i18n and localization strategy across products and anticipating expanding locale/market needs is SFIA's initiate/influence band, authority across a portfolio of products. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for internationalization; pioneers widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for internationalization, the way contributors to CLDR itself influence the locale data the whole industry consumes, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Unicode Consortium, Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR).

<a id="fe-15"></a>
##### FE-15 — Progressive enhancement & offline capability

*Type:* Technical — Delivering resilient experiences that degrade gracefully and function under intermittent connectivity.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds basic fallbacks and simple offline behavior under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Adding basic fallbacks and simple offline behavior under guidance is applying Champeon & Finck's progressive-enhancement principle to a case someone else scoped, without designing the enhancement layers — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Champeon & Finck, Inclusive Web Design For the Future (SXSW Interactive, 2003); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements progressive enhancement and standard offline support independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing progressive enhancement and standard offline support independently is correct, routine use of the Service Workers specification's caching/fetch-interception model for familiar cases — advanced beginner. *Sources:* W3C, Service Workers specification (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs resilient offline-capable experiences autonomously; handles sync and conflict cases.
  — *Why this level:* Designing resilient offline-capable experiences autonomously, handling sync and conflict cases, is doing the offline-first architectural work Russell's Progressive Web Apps doctrine calls for beyond the basic service-worker cache — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Russell, Progressive Web Apps: Escaping Tabs Without Losing Our Soul (Infrequently Noted, 2015); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines progressive-enhancement patterns teams adopt; solves hard offline and degradation problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining progressive-enhancement patterns a team adopts and solving hard offline/degradation problems is producing reusable resilience architecture beyond one feature — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Russell, Progressive Web Apps: Escaping Tabs Without Losing Our Soul (Infrequently Noted, 2015); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for resilience and offline capability; anticipates evolving connectivity scenarios.
  — *Why this level:* Setting strategy for resilience and offline capability, anticipating evolving connectivity scenarios, is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority across a product portfolio's resilience posture. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for progressive enhancement industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for progressive enhancement industrywide, the way Champeon & Finck's coined term itself reshaped a generation of web-design doctrine, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Champeon & Finck, Inclusive Web Design For the Future (SXSW Interactive, 2003).

#### Client Platform & Tooling

<a id="fe-16"></a>
##### FE-16 — Client build tooling & module bundling

*Type:* Technical — Configuring build pipelines, bundling, and transpilation to package and optimize client artifacts.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs and tweaks existing build configurations under review.
  — *Why this level:* Running and tweaking existing build configurations under review is operating someone else's module-resolution setup without owning it — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* TC39 / Ecma International, ECMAScript Modules, ECMA-262 section 16.2 (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Configures standard build and bundling setups independently.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring standard build and bundling setups independently is correct, routine application of ECMAScript module-resolution semantics to familiar project shapes — advanced beginner. *Sources:* TC39 / Ecma International, ECMAScript Modules, ECMA-262 section 16.2 (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs build pipelines autonomously; optimizes bundling, splitting, and asset handling.
  — *Why this level:* Designing build pipelines autonomously, optimizing bundling, splitting, and asset handling, is applying network-performance-model trade-offs (request count vs. payload size, critical-path loading) as design judgment, not defaults — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines build-tooling approaches teams adopt; solves hard performance and configuration problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining build-tooling approaches a team adopts and solving hard performance/configuration problems is producing reusable pipeline architecture on top of ECMAScript module semantics — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* TC39 / Ecma International, ECMAScript Modules, ECMA-262 section 16.2 (2024); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets build and bundling strategy across projects; anticipates evolving tooling models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting build and bundling strategy across projects, anticipating evolving tooling models, is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority spanning multiple projects' build systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for client build tooling; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for client build tooling, the way network-performance thinking itself reshaped a generation of bundler defaults, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level at industry scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).

<a id="fe-17"></a>
##### FE-17 — Browser platform & runtime fundamentals

*Type:* Technical — Leveraging core client runtime capabilities, event models, storage, and rendering pipeline behavior.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses common platform APIs for simple tasks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Using common platform APIs for simple tasks under guidance is calling primitives the HTML Living Standard defines without understanding their runtime model — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies browser runtime and lifecycle knowledge independently for standard work.
  — *Why this level:* Applying browser runtime and lifecycle knowledge independently for standard work is correct, routine use of platform APIs for familiar cases — advanced beginner. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Leverages platform internals autonomously; debugs subtle runtime and event-loop behavior.
  — *Why this level:* Leveraging platform internals autonomously and debugging subtle runtime/event-loop behavior is reasoning directly from the HTML Living Standard's formal event-loop and task-queue model, not from folk heuristics — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines platform-usage approaches teams adopt; solves deep runtime and capability problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining platform-usage approaches a team adopts and solving deep runtime/capability problems is producing reusable, spec-grounded guidance beyond one bug — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for platform adoption; anticipates evolving browser capabilities and standards.
  — *Why this level:* Setting strategy for platform adoption and anticipating evolving browser capabilities and standards is SFIA's initiate/influence band, authority over direction across projects. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative understanding of the browser platform; shapes industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative understanding of the browser platform, the kind of expertise that feeds back into WHATWG standards discussions, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level extended to shaping the living standard itself. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); WHATWG, HTML Living Standard (accessed 2026-07).

### Backend & Distributed Services (BE)

#### Data Persistence & Modeling

<a id="be-01"></a>
##### BE-01 — Relational data modeling & querying

*Type:* Technical — Designs normalized relational schemas, relationships, and set-based queries for transactional data.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes simple queries and follows existing schemas under review.
  — *Why this level:* Writing simple queries and following existing schemas under review is the Dreyfus novice band: the learner applies Codd's relational rules (keys, joins, normal forms) as given, with correctness checked externally rather than reasoned about. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Models standard entities and writes correct queries independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling standard entities and writing correct queries independently with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying Codd's normalization and set-based query rules to familiar, well-bounded schemas without case-by-case coaching. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs normalized schemas autonomously; writes complex queries and resolves modeling trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing normalized schemas autonomously and resolving modeling trade-offs is the Dreyfus competent band: choosing normalization depth and join strategy per Kleppmann's data-modeling trade-off framework for ambiguous cases is the ownership judgment this level requires. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines data-modeling approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest schema and query problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining modeling approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest schema/query problems matches Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's application of Codd's normalization rules and Kleppmann's schema-evolution guidance becomes the reference pattern others are advised to adopt. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets relational modeling strategy across systems; anticipates evolving data and access needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting relational-modeling strategy across systems and anticipating evolving access needs is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide data-modeling direction built on Codd's relational model and Kleppmann's evolution patterns, not one schema. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for relational modeling industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Codd's 1970 paper did not describe an existing practice — it originated the relational model the industry's query languages and schema conventions still rest on, the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

<a id="be-02"></a>
##### BE-02 — Non-relational data modeling

*Type:* Technical — Models document, key-value, columnar, and graph data shaped around access patterns rather than normalization.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Stores and retrieves simple documents or records following patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Storing and retrieving simple documents or records following patterns under review is the Dreyfus novice band: Sadalage & Fowler's aggregate-oriented model is applied as a fixed template, not reasoned about. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sadalage & Fowler, NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence (Addison-Wesley, 2012); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Models standard non-relational structures independently for known access patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling standard non-relational structures independently for known access patterns is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying Sadalage & Fowler's aggregate/denormalization guidance to familiar workloads without new judgment calls. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sadalage & Fowler, NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence (Addison-Wesley, 2012); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs non-relational schemas autonomously; optimizes for access patterns and denormalization.
  — *Why this level:* Designing non-relational schemas autonomously and optimizing for access patterns is the Dreyfus competent band: Kleppmann's access-pattern-first modeling framework is exactly the denormalize-vs-reference trade-off reasoning this level owns without oversight. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sadalage & Fowler, NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence (Addison-Wesley, 2012); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines non-relational modeling approaches teams adopt; solves hard data-shape and scale problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining non-relational modeling approaches teams adopt and solving hard data-shape/scale problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's aggregate design, grounded in Sadalage & Fowler's model, becomes the reference pattern for others' access-pattern decisions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sadalage & Fowler, NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence (Addison-Wesley, 2012); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for non-relational data modeling; anticipates evolving workload and access needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting strategy for non-relational modeling across evolving workloads is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide data-shape direction spanning Kleppmann's access-pattern trade-offs across many collections, not a single one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sadalage & Fowler, NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence (Addison-Wesley, 2012); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for non-relational modeling; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Sadalage & Fowler's polyglot-persistence framework did not invent NoSQL stores but became the field's reference vocabulary for choosing among them — codifying that vocabulary at industry scale is the SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sadalage & Fowler, NoSQL Distilled: A Brief Guide to the Emerging World of Polyglot Persistence (Addison-Wesley, 2012); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

<a id="be-03"></a>
##### BE-03 — Consistency & transaction design

*Type:* Technical — Applies transactions, isolation levels, and consistency models to keep data correct under concurrent access.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses provided transaction patterns for simple operations under review.
  — *Why this level:* Using provided transaction patterns for simple operations under review is the Dreyfus novice band: applying Gray & Reuter's ACID transaction template without reasoning about isolation-level trade-offs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gray & Reuter, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques (Morgan Kaufmann, 1993); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard transactions and isolation independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard transactions and isolation independently with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: routine application of Gray & Reuter's transaction model to familiar, low-contention cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gray & Reuter, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques (Morgan Kaufmann, 1993); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs consistency and transaction boundaries autonomously; resolves concurrency and isolation issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing consistency and transaction boundaries autonomously and resolving concurrency/isolation issues is the Dreyfus competent band: choosing an isolation level per Kleppmann's consistency-model trade-offs for ambiguous, contended cases is the ownership judgment this level requires. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gray & Reuter, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques (Morgan Kaufmann, 1993); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines consistency approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest correctness and contention problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining consistency approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest correctness/contention problems matches Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's transaction-boundary conventions, grounded in Gray & Reuter's ACID model, become what other engineers are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gray & Reuter, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques (Morgan Kaufmann, 1993); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets consistency and transaction strategy across systems; anticipates distributed-correctness challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Setting consistency and transaction strategy across systems and anticipating distributed-correctness challenges is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide consistency-model direction across many transactional boundaries per Kleppmann's distributed-correctness framework, not one system's isolation level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gray & Reuter, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques (Morgan Kaufmann, 1993); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for consistency design; shapes industry understanding of correctness.
  — *Why this level:* Gray & Reuter's Transaction Processing formalized ACID and the transaction concept the industry still designs against — authoring the field's foundational correctness model is the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gray & Reuter, Transaction Processing: Concepts and Techniques (Morgan Kaufmann, 1993); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

<a id="be-04"></a>
##### BE-04 — Indexing & query optimization

*Type:* Technical — Designs indexes and query plans to meet latency and throughput targets at scale.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds suggested indexes and reads query plans under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Adding suggested indexes and reading query plans under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: following Selinger et al.'s access-path output without independently interpreting cost trade-offs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Selinger, Astrahan, Chamberlin, Lorie & Price, Access Path Selection in a Relational Database Management System (ACM SIGMOD, 1979); Comer, The Ubiquitous B-Tree, ACM Computing Surveys 11(2), 121-137 (1979).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Identifies and resolves standard slow queries independently.
  — *Why this level:* Identifying and resolving standard slow queries independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying Comer's B-tree indexing conventions to familiar, well-understood slow-query patterns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Selinger, Astrahan, Chamberlin, Lorie & Price, Access Path Selection in a Relational Database Management System (ACM SIGMOD, 1979); Comer, The Ubiquitous B-Tree, ACM Computing Surveys 11(2), 121-137 (1979).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs indexing strategies autonomously; tunes complex queries and execution plans.
  — *Why this level:* Designing indexing strategies autonomously and tuning complex queries/execution plans is the Dreyfus competent band: reasoning through Selinger et al.'s cost-based access-path trade-offs for ambiguous, non-obvious cases is exactly this level's judgment call. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Selinger, Astrahan, Chamberlin, Lorie & Price, Access Path Selection in a Relational Database Management System (ACM SIGMOD, 1979); Comer, The Ubiquitous B-Tree, ACM Computing Surveys 11(2), 121-137 (1979).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines query-optimization approaches teams adopt; solves the most stubborn performance problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining query-optimization approaches teams adopt and solving the most stubborn performance problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's indexing conventions, combining Comer's B-tree structures with Selinger et al.'s cost model, become what others are advised to apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Selinger, Astrahan, Chamberlin, Lorie & Price, Access Path Selection in a Relational Database Management System (ACM SIGMOD, 1979); Comer, The Ubiquitous B-Tree, ACM Computing Surveys 11(2), 121-137 (1979).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets indexing and optimization strategy across systems; anticipates evolving workload patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting indexing and optimization strategy across systems and anticipating evolving workload patterns is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide performance direction spanning Selinger et al.'s cost-based approach across many query plans, not one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Selinger, Astrahan, Chamberlin, Lorie & Price, Access Path Selection in a Relational Database Management System (ACM SIGMOD, 1979); Comer, The Ubiquitous B-Tree, ACM Computing Surveys 11(2), 121-137 (1979).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for query optimization; pioneers widely referenced techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Selinger et al.'s 1979 paper originated cost-based query optimization and Comer's paper canonicalized the B-tree as the field's default index structure — both are the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band query optimization still rests on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Selinger, Astrahan, Chamberlin, Lorie & Price, Access Path Selection in a Relational Database Management System (ACM SIGMOD, 1979); Comer, The Ubiquitous B-Tree, ACM Computing Surveys 11(2), 121-137 (1979).

<a id="be-05"></a>
##### BE-05 — Search & indexing

*Type:* Technical — Builds full-text and faceted search using inverted indexes, ranking, and relevance tuning.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements basic search queries against existing indexes under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing basic search queries against existing indexes under review is the Dreyfus novice band: using Manning et al.'s inverted-index query mechanics as given, without independent relevance-tuning judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval (Cambridge University Press, 2008).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard search and indexing pipelines independently.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard search and indexing pipelines independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying Manning et al.'s indexing pipeline (tokenize, invert, rank) to familiar corpora without new design calls. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval (Cambridge University Press, 2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs search and relevance strategies autonomously; tunes ranking and indexing trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing search and relevance strategies autonomously and tuning ranking/indexing trade-offs is the Dreyfus competent band: Manning et al.'s ranking-function trade-offs (precision vs. recall, term weighting) are exactly the ambiguous judgment this level requires. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval (Cambridge University Press, 2008).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines search architecture teams adopt; solves hard relevance, scale, and freshness problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining search architecture teams adopt and solving hard relevance/scale/freshness problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's ranking and indexing approach, grounded in Manning et al.'s IR model, becomes the pattern others are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval (Cambridge University Press, 2008).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets search strategy across products; anticipates evolving retrieval and ranking needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting search strategy across products and anticipating evolving retrieval/ranking needs is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide retrieval direction spanning Manning et al.'s relevance framework across many indexes, not one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval (Cambridge University Press, 2008).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for search and indexing industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Manning, Raghavan & Schütze's text did not invent information retrieval but became the field's reference model for ranking and indexing — that discipline-codifying authorship is the SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Introduction to Information Retrieval (Cambridge University Press, 2008).

#### Data Access & Caching

<a id="be-06"></a>
##### BE-06 — Caching strategy & invalidation

*Type:* Technical — Selects cache placement, eviction, and invalidation strategies to balance freshness against performance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds simple caching following established patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Adding simple caching following established patterns under review is the Dreyfus novice band: applying a given cache-aside pattern without reasoning about invalidation correctness. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook (USENIX NSDI, 2013); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard caching with basic invalidation independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard caching with basic invalidation independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: routine application of familiar TTL/cache-aside patterns per Nishtala et al.'s baseline Memcache usage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook (USENIX NSDI, 2013); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs caching strategies autonomously; resolves invalidation, staleness, and coherence issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing caching strategies autonomously and resolving invalidation/staleness/coherence issues is the Dreyfus competent band: Nishtala et al.'s lease-based invalidation and thundering-herd mitigation are exactly the ambiguous coherence trade-offs this level owns without oversight. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook (USENIX NSDI, 2013); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines caching approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest invalidation and consistency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining caching approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest invalidation/consistency problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's invalidation strategy, drawn from Nishtala et al.'s Memcache techniques and Kleppmann's staleness trade-offs, becomes what other teams are advised to reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook (USENIX NSDI, 2013); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets caching strategy across systems; anticipates evolving consistency and scale demands.
  — *Why this level:* Setting caching strategy across systems and anticipating evolving consistency/scale demands is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide cache-coherence direction spanning Nishtala et al.'s invalidation techniques across many services, not a single cache. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook (USENIX NSDI, 2013); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for caching and invalidation; shapes industry understanding.
  — *Why this level:* Nishtala et al.'s Facebook Memcache paper documented invalidation and coherence techniques (leases, thundering-herd protection) that became the industry's reference caching architecture — the discipline-shaping SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nishtala et al., Scaling Memcache at Facebook (USENIX NSDI, 2013); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

<a id="be-07"></a>
##### BE-07 — Data partitioning & sharding

*Type:* Technical — Splits and distributes data across nodes to scale storage and access while managing rebalancing.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Operates within existing partitioning schemes for simple tasks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Operating within existing partitioning schemes for simple tasks under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: using a given shard key or key range from an established scheme without independently reasoning about skew. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Chang et al., Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (USENIX OSDI, 2006).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard partitioning following defined strategies independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard partitioning following defined strategies independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying a familiar range- or hash-partitioning scheme without new rebalancing judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Chang et al., Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (USENIX OSDI, 2006).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs partitioning and sharding schemes autonomously; handles rebalancing and hotspot issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing partitioning and sharding schemes autonomously and handling rebalancing/hotspot issues is the Dreyfus competent band: resolving skew and rebalancing per Chang et al.'s tablet-splitting approach is exactly this level's ambiguous, no-textbook-answer judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Chang et al., Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (USENIX OSDI, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines partitioning approaches teams adopt; solves hard distribution and skew problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining partitioning approaches teams adopt and solving hard distribution/skew problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's sharding scheme, combining DeCandia et al.'s consistent hashing with Chang et al.'s tablet model, becomes the pattern others are advised to reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Chang et al., Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (USENIX OSDI, 2006).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets partitioning strategy across systems; anticipates evolving scale and topology needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting partitioning strategy across systems and anticipating evolving scale/topology needs is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide distribution direction spanning DeCandia et al.'s partitioning model across many datasets, not one shard key. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Chang et al., Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (USENIX OSDI, 2006).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for partitioning and sharding; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* DeCandia et al.'s Dynamo paper and Chang et al.'s Bigtable paper each originated a partitioning model (consistent hashing; range-partitioned tablets) that seeded an entire generation of distributed stores — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Chang et al., Bigtable: A Distributed Storage System for Structured Data (USENIX OSDI, 2006).

<a id="be-08"></a>
##### BE-08 — Replication & data distribution

*Type:* Technical — Replicates data across nodes and regions, reasoning about lag, failover, and read/write trade-offs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Operates replicated setups for simple tasks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Operating replicated setups for simple tasks under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: following a given leader-follower replication configuration without reasoning about lag or failover trade-offs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Configures standard replication independently following defined patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring standard replication independently following defined patterns is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: routine setup of familiar synchronous/asynchronous replication without new failover judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs replication topologies autonomously; resolves lag, conflict, and failover issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing replication topologies autonomously and resolving lag/conflict/failover issues is the Dreyfus competent band: DeCandia et al.'s vector-clock conflict resolution and quorum trade-offs are exactly the ambiguous distributed-correctness judgment this level owns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines replication approaches teams adopt; solves hard distribution and consistency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining replication approaches teams adopt and solving hard distribution/consistency problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's replication topology, grounded in DeCandia et al.'s quorum model and Kleppmann's lag/conflict trade-offs, becomes what others are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets replication and distribution strategy across systems; anticipates evolving topology needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting replication and distribution strategy across systems and anticipating evolving topology needs is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide replication direction spanning Kleppmann's replication trade-off framework across many clusters, not one failover config. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for replication and data distribution; shapes industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* DeCandia et al.'s Dynamo paper originated the eventually-consistent, quorum-based replication model later adopted industry-wide (Cassandra, Riak, DynamoDB) — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DeCandia et al., Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store (ACM SOSP, 2007); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

#### Messaging & Eventing

<a id="be-09"></a>
##### BE-09 — Message & event-driven architecture

*Type:* Technical — Designs asynchronous, decoupled systems using queues, streams, and publish-subscribe flows.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Produces and consumes messages for simple flows under review.
  — *Why this level:* Producing and consuming messages for simple flows under review is the Dreyfus novice band: wiring a given queue or topic per Hohpe & Woolf's basic messaging pattern without reasoning about coupling. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Kreps, Narkhede & Rao, Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB Workshop, 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard event-driven flows independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard event-driven flows independently with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar publish-subscribe patterns to known integration cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Kreps, Narkhede & Rao, Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB Workshop, 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs event-driven architectures autonomously; resolves ordering, delivery, and coupling concerns.
  — *Why this level:* Designing event-driven architectures autonomously and resolving ordering/delivery/coupling concerns is the Dreyfus competent band: choosing among Hohpe & Woolf's messaging patterns (competing consumers, dead-letter, correlation) for ambiguous coupling cases is this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Kreps, Narkhede & Rao, Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB Workshop, 2011).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines event-driven approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest decoupling and flow problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining event-driven approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest decoupling/flow problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's event-flow conventions, combining Hohpe & Woolf's pattern catalog with Kreps et al.'s log-based design, become the pattern others are advised to reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Kreps, Narkhede & Rao, Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB Workshop, 2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets event-driven architecture strategy across systems; anticipates evolving messaging models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting event-driven architecture strategy across systems and anticipating evolving messaging models is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide messaging direction spanning Kreps et al.'s log-centric architecture across many services, not one topic's flow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Kreps, Narkhede & Rao, Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB Workshop, 2011).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for event-driven architecture; shapes industry understanding.
  — *Why this level:* Kreps, Narkhede & Rao's paper originated the log-based messaging model (Kafka) that redefined event-driven architecture industry-wide, and Hohpe & Woolf canonicalized the pattern vocabulary the field still uses — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Kreps, Narkhede & Rao, Kafka: a Distributed Messaging System for Log Processing (NetDB Workshop, 2011).

<a id="be-10"></a>
##### BE-10 — Event modeling & stream processing

*Type:* Technical — Models domain events and processes continuous streams for real-time and derived state.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements simple stream consumers and event handlers under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing simple stream consumers and event handlers under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: wiring a given consumer per an established windowing model without reasoning about out-of-order handling. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing (VLDB, 2015); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard stream-processing flows independently.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard stream-processing flows independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar windowing/aggregation patterns to well-bounded streams. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing (VLDB, 2015); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs event models and stream pipelines autonomously; handles windowing and state.
  — *Why this level:* Designing event models and stream pipelines autonomously and handling windowing/state is the Dreyfus competent band: Akidau et al.'s trade-offs between event-time windowing, watermarks, and triggers for out-of-order data are exactly this level's ambiguous, no-single-answer judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing (VLDB, 2015); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines stream-processing approaches teams adopt; solves hard ordering and throughput problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining stream-processing approaches teams adopt and solving hard ordering/throughput problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's event model, grounded in Akidau et al.'s Dataflow windowing model and Kleppmann's stream-processing trade-offs, becomes what other pipelines are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing (VLDB, 2015); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets event-modeling and streaming strategy across systems; anticipates evolving processing needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting event-modeling and streaming strategy across systems and anticipating evolving processing needs is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide streaming direction spanning Akidau et al.'s unified batch/stream model across many pipelines, not one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing (VLDB, 2015); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for event modeling and stream processing; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Akidau et al.'s Dataflow Model paper originated the unified batch/streaming, event-time windowing model that became Apache Beam's industry standard — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Akidau et al., The Dataflow Model: A Practical Approach to Balancing Correctness, Latency, and Cost in Massive-Scale, Unbounded, Out-of-Order Data Processing (VLDB, 2015); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

<a id="be-11"></a>
##### BE-11 — Idempotency & reliability patterns

*Type:* Technical — Applies idempotency, retries, deduplication, and delivery guarantees to make operations safely repeatable.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided idempotency and retry patterns for simple cases under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying provided idempotency and retry patterns for simple cases under review is the Dreyfus novice band: using a given idempotency-key pattern per Helland's framing without independently reasoning about duplicate delivery. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Helland, Idempotence Is Not a Medical Condition, ACM Queue 10(4) (2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard reliability and retry handling independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard reliability and retry handling independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: routine application of familiar retry/dedup patterns to known failure cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Helland, Idempotence Is Not a Medical Condition, ACM Queue 10(4) (2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs idempotent, reliable flows autonomously; resolves duplicate and partial-failure cases.
  — *Why this level:* Designing idempotent, reliable flows autonomously and resolving duplicate/partial-failure cases is the Dreyfus competent band: Helland's framing of idempotence as a first-class property — making at-least-once delivery safe through commutative, retriable operations — is exactly the judgment this level owns for ambiguous partial-failure cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Helland, Idempotence Is Not a Medical Condition, ACM Queue 10(4) (2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines reliability patterns teams adopt; solves the hardest exactly-once and recovery problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reliability patterns teams adopt and solving the hardest exactly-once/recovery problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise), matching the Google SRE book's treatment of reliability as an engineering discipline others are advised to practice, not just an individual habit. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Helland, Idempotence Is Not a Medical Condition, ACM Queue 10(4) (2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets reliability and idempotency strategy across systems; anticipates evolving failure modes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting reliability and idempotency strategy across systems and anticipating evolving failure modes is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide reliability direction, per the SRE book's error-budget and postmortem-driven strategy setting, not one endpoint's retry logic. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Helland, Idempotence Is Not a Medical Condition, ACM Queue 10(4) (2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for reliability patterns industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Helland's essay reframed idempotency as a first-class reliability property that shaped how the industry designs retriable APIs, and the Google SRE book effectively named and defined the site-reliability-engineering discipline itself — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Helland, Idempotence Is Not a Medical Condition, ACM Queue 10(4) (2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

<a id="be-12"></a>
##### BE-12 — Background processing & scheduling

*Type:* Technical — Designs deferred, batched, and scheduled work to offload and coordinate long-running tasks.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements simple background jobs following patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing simple background jobs following patterns under review is the Dreyfus novice band: scheduling a given job per an established pattern without reasoning about contention or timing. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Verma et al., Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg (ACM EuroSys, 2015); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard scheduled and queued jobs independently.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard scheduled and queued jobs independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: routine application of familiar scheduling/queueing patterns to known workloads. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Verma et al., Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg (ACM EuroSys, 2015); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs background-processing systems autonomously; handles retries, concurrency, and timing.
  — *Why this level:* Designing background-processing systems autonomously and handling retries/concurrency/timing is the Dreyfus competent band: Verma et al.'s Borg scheduling trade-offs (priority, preemption, resource bin-packing) are exactly the ambiguous judgment this level owns for non-trivial job-scheduling cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Verma et al., Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg (ACM EuroSys, 2015); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines background-processing approaches teams adopt; solves hard scheduling and throughput problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining background-processing approaches teams adopt and solving hard scheduling/throughput problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's scheduling conventions, grounded in Verma et al.'s Borg model, become what other systems are advised to reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Verma et al., Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg (ACM EuroSys, 2015); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets background-processing strategy across systems; anticipates evolving workload demands.
  — *Why this level:* Setting background-processing strategy across systems and anticipating evolving workload demands is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide scheduling direction, per the SRE book's capacity-driven planning and Verma et al.'s cluster-wide bin-packing, not one job's cron schedule. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Verma et al., Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg (ACM EuroSys, 2015); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for background processing and scheduling; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Verma et al.'s Borg paper documented the cluster-scheduling model that directly seeded Kubernetes and reshaped how the industry schedules background work — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Verma et al., Large-scale Cluster Management at Google with Borg (ACM EuroSys, 2015); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

#### Service Interfaces & Protocols

<a id="be-13"></a>
##### BE-13 — API contract & versioning design

*Type:* Technical — Defines stable interface contracts, schemas, and versioning strategies for evolving consumers.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements endpoints against existing contracts under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing endpoints against existing contracts under review is the Dreyfus novice band: filling in a given REST resource per Fielding's constraints without reasoning about compatibility. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs standard API contracts independently with consistent conventions.
  — *Why this level:* Designing standard API contracts independently with consistent conventions is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying Fielding's resource/representation conventions to familiar, well-bounded endpoints. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs API contracts and versioning autonomously; manages compatibility and evolution.
  — *Why this level:* Designing API contracts and versioning autonomously and managing compatibility/evolution is the Dreyfus competent band: choosing a versioning and backward-compatibility strategy consistent with Fielding's uniform-interface constraint, for ambiguous evolution cases, is this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines API-design approaches teams adopt; solves hard versioning and compatibility problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining API-design approaches teams adopt and solving hard versioning/compatibility problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's contract conventions, grounded in Fielding's REST constraints, become what other services are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets API contract and versioning strategy across the organization; anticipates evolving needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting API contract and versioning strategy across the organization and anticipating evolving needs is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide interface direction applying Fielding's uniform-interface constraint across many services, not one contract. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for API design; shapes industry standards and conventions.
  — *Why this level:* Fielding's dissertation originated REST, the constraint set most of the industry's HTTP API contracts and versioning conventions still derive from — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000).

<a id="be-14"></a>
##### BE-14 — Synchronous & asynchronous protocol design

*Type:* Technical — Chooses and designs request-response, streaming, and real-time communication protocols for service interaction.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements communication over established protocols for simple cases under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing communication over established protocols for simple cases under review is the Dreyfus novice band: using a given request-response or streaming call per an existing protocol without independently choosing sync vs. async. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); Belshe, Peon & Thomson (eds.), Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2), RFC 7540 (IETF, 2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard synchronous and async interactions independently.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard synchronous and async interactions independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar protocol choices (REST call, message queue) to known interaction cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); Belshe, Peon & Thomson (eds.), Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2), RFC 7540 (IETF, 2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs protocol interactions autonomously; chooses sync/async trade-offs and handles failures.
  — *Why this level:* Designing protocol interactions autonomously and choosing sync/async trade-offs is the Dreyfus competent band: weighing Fielding's stateless request-response model against RFC 7540's multiplexed-streaming model for ambiguous latency/coupling cases is this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); Belshe, Peon & Thomson (eds.), Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2), RFC 7540 (IETF, 2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines protocol-design approaches teams adopt; solves hard latency and coupling problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining protocol-design approaches teams adopt and solving hard latency/coupling problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's protocol choices, combining Fielding's REST constraints with RFC 7540's stream multiplexing, become what other services are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); Belshe, Peon & Thomson (eds.), Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2), RFC 7540 (IETF, 2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets protocol-design strategy across systems; anticipates evolving communication models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting protocol-design strategy across systems and anticipating evolving communication models is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide protocol direction spanning Fielding's and RFC 7540's models across many integrations, not one transport choice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); Belshe, Peon & Thomson (eds.), Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2), RFC 7540 (IETF, 2015).
