- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for protocol design industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Fielding's REST dissertation and RFC 7540 (the IETF HTTP/2 standard enabling multiplexed streaming) each defined a protocol model the industry converged on — reaching RFC/standard-track status is itself the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fielding, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures (PhD dissertation, University of California Irvine, 2000); Belshe, Peon & Thomson (eds.), Hypertext Transfer Protocol Version 2 (HTTP/2), RFC 7540 (IETF, 2015).

<a id="be-15"></a>
##### BE-15 — Authentication & authorization

*Type:* Technical — Designs identity, credential, token, and access-control mechanisms to protect services and data.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies existing auth mechanisms to simple endpoints under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying existing auth mechanisms to simple endpoints under review is the Dreyfus novice band: wiring a given OAuth 2.0 (RFC 6749) flow without reasoning about token or trust design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, Special Publication 800-63-3 (2017); Hardt (ed.), The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, RFC 6749 (IETF, 2012).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard authentication and authorization flows independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard authentication and authorization flows independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar RFC 6749 grant types to known client cases without new trust-boundary judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, Special Publication 800-63-3 (2017); Hardt (ed.), The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, RFC 6749 (IETF, 2012).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs auth models autonomously; resolves complex identity, token, and permission cases.
  — *Why this level:* Designing auth models autonomously and resolving complex identity/token/permission cases is the Dreyfus competent band: choosing assurance levels per NIST SP 800-63-3 and token scoping per RFC 6749 for ambiguous, high-risk cases is this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, Special Publication 800-63-3 (2017); Hardt (ed.), The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, RFC 6749 (IETF, 2012).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines auth approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest access-control and trust problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining auth approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest access-control/trust problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's identity/token architecture, grounded in NIST 800-63-3's assurance levels and RFC 6749's grant model, becomes what other services are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, Special Publication 800-63-3 (2017); Hardt (ed.), The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, RFC 6749 (IETF, 2012).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets authentication and authorization strategy across systems; anticipates evolving threats.
  — *Why this level:* Setting authentication and authorization strategy across systems and anticipating evolving threats is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide identity direction, per NIST 800-63-3's assurance-level framework, not one endpoint's auth check. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, Special Publication 800-63-3 (2017); Hardt (ed.), The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, RFC 6749 (IETF, 2012).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for auth; shapes industry standards and security understanding.
  — *Why this level:* NIST SP 800-63-3 and RFC 6749 are themselves the authoritative standards the industry's auth practice is built on; setting or shaping standards at that level is the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, Special Publication 800-63-3 (2017); Hardt (ed.), The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework, RFC 6749 (IETF, 2012).

<a id="be-16"></a>
##### BE-16 — Rate limiting & traffic shaping

*Type:* Technical — Protects services with throttling, quotas, backpressure, and graceful degradation under load.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided rate-limit rules to simple endpoints under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Applying provided rate-limit rules to simple endpoints under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: enforcing a given quota per the SRE book's baseline overload-protection pattern without independently reasoning about fairness. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard rate limiting and throttling independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard rate limiting and throttling independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar token-bucket/fixed-window limits to known traffic cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs traffic-shaping strategies autonomously; handles bursts, fairness, and backpressure.
  — *Why this level:* Designing traffic-shaping strategies autonomously and handling bursts/fairness/backpressure is the Dreyfus competent band: the SRE book's treatment of graceful degradation and backpressure under overload is exactly the ambiguous trade-off judgment this level owns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines rate-limiting approaches teams adopt; solves hard fairness and abuse problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining rate-limiting approaches teams adopt and solving hard fairness/abuse problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's throttling conventions, grounded in the SRE book's overload-handling chapter, become what other services are advised to reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets traffic-management strategy across systems; anticipates evolving load and abuse patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting traffic-management strategy across systems and anticipating evolving load/abuse patterns is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide overload-protection direction, per the SRE book's cascading-failure-prevention strategy, not one endpoint's limiter. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for rate limiting and traffic shaping; pioneers influential approaches.
  — *Why this level:* The Google SRE book's chapter on handling overload effectively defined the industry's reference approach to graceful degradation and backpressure at scale — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

#### Scalability & Resilience

<a id="be-17"></a>
##### BE-17 — Scalability & load management

*Type:* Technical — Scales systems horizontally and vertically and distributes load to meet demand elastically.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies known scaling adjustments to simple services under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Applying known scaling adjustments to simple services under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: adding a given replica or resizing per instruction without reasoning about scaling limits. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gunther, Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services (Springer, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard scaling and load-handling measures independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard scaling and load-handling measures independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar horizontal/vertical scaling patterns to known load cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gunther, Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services (Springer, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs scalable systems autonomously; resolves bottlenecks and load-distribution challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Designing scalable systems autonomously and resolving bottleneck/load-distribution challenges is the Dreyfus competent band: applying Gunther's Universal Scalability Law to diagnose contention- and coherence-driven scaling limits for ambiguous cases is this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gunther, Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services (Springer, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines scalability approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest scaling and contention problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining scalability approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest scaling/contention problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's scaling architecture, grounded in Gunther's Universal Scalability Law and the SRE book's capacity practice, becomes what other systems are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gunther, Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services (Springer, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets scalability strategy across systems; anticipates growth and evolving load profiles.
  — *Why this level:* Setting scalability strategy across systems and anticipating growth/evolving load profiles is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide scaling direction, per the SRE book's capacity-planning strategy, not one service's autoscaler. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gunther, Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services (Springer, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for scalability; shapes industry understanding of scaling.
  — *Why this level:* Gunther's Universal Scalability Law gave the industry a quantitative model for predicting scaling limits before they're hit — originating a widely referenced technique is the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gunther, Guerrilla Capacity Planning: A Tactical Approach to Planning for Highly Scalable Applications and Services (Springer, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

<a id="be-18"></a>
##### BE-18 — Fault tolerance & failure isolation

*Type:* Technical — Designs timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, and bulkheads to contain and survive partial failures.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided resilience patterns to simple services under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying provided resilience patterns to simple services under review is the Dreyfus novice band: wiring a given timeout or retry per Nygard's stability-pattern catalog without independently reasoning about cascading failure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard fault-tolerance and isolation measures independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard fault-tolerance and isolation measures independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar circuit-breaker/bulkhead patterns from Nygard's catalog to known failure cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs resilient systems autonomously; resolves cascading-failure and degradation concerns.
  — *Why this level:* Designing resilient systems autonomously and resolving cascading-failure/degradation concerns is the Dreyfus competent band: choosing among Nygard's stability patterns (circuit breaker, bulkhead, fail fast) for ambiguous, non-obvious failure modes is this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines fault-tolerance approaches teams adopt; solves the hardest isolation and recovery problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining fault-tolerance approaches teams adopt and solving the hardest isolation/recovery problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's resilience architecture, grounded in Nygard's stability patterns, becomes what other services are advised to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets resilience strategy across systems; anticipates emerging failure modes and risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting resilience strategy across systems and anticipating emerging failure modes is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide fault-isolation direction, per the SRE book's cascading-failure-prevention practice, not one service's circuit breaker. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for fault tolerance industrywide; shapes widely adopted approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Nygard's Release It! coined and popularized the circuit-breaker and bulkhead patterns that are now the industry's default vocabulary for fault isolation — the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

<a id="be-19"></a>
##### BE-19 — Capacity planning & resource budgeting

*Type:* Behavioral — Forecasts demand and provisions compute, storage, and connection resources against budgets.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers usage metrics and applies simple capacity estimates under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering usage metrics and applying simple capacity estimates under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: following a given headroom rule of thumb per the SRE book's baseline capacity-planning process without independent forecasting judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces standard capacity forecasts and resource budgets independently.
  — *Why this level:* Producing standard capacity forecasts and resource budgets independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: applying familiar demand-forecasting methods from the SRE book's capacity-planning chapter to known workloads. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Plans capacity autonomously; models demand, headroom, and resource trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Planning capacity autonomously and modeling demand/headroom/resource trade-offs is the Dreyfus competent band: the SRE book's organic-plus-inorganic-growth forecasting model, applied to ambiguous demand-shift cases, is exactly this level's ownership judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines capacity-planning approaches teams adopt; solves hard forecasting and efficiency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining capacity-planning approaches teams adopt and solving hard forecasting/efficiency problems is Dreyfus's proficient stage and SFIA level 5 (Ensure, advise): the practitioner's forecasting method, grounded in the SRE book's capacity-planning chapter, becomes what other teams are advised to reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets capacity and resource-budgeting strategy across systems; anticipates long-term demand shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting capacity and resource-budgeting strategy across systems and anticipating long-term demand shifts is SFIA level 6 (Initiate, influence): org-wide budgeting direction across many systems' headroom, per the SRE book's capacity-strategy practice, not one service's forecast. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for capacity planning; pioneers influential approaches to resource budgeting.
  — *Why this level:* The Google SRE book's capacity-planning chapter defined the reference forecasting and budgeting practice the industry now builds on, matching the discipline-defining SFIA level 7 (Set strategy, inspire, mobilise) / Dreyfus mastery band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

### Architecture & System Design (ARC)

#### Architectural Styles & Decomposition

<a id="arc-01"></a>
##### ARC-01 — Architectural styles & patterns

*Type:* Technical — Selects and applies layered, modular, service-oriented, and event-driven structural patterns to fit context.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies a chosen architectural style to a component under guidance, following existing patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Applying a chosen style to a component under guidance, with the choice reviewed, is Dreyfus' novice band: following a supplied rule without judging fit. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard styles independently for routine systems, selecting from familiar patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting from familiar patterns for routine systems independently is the advanced-beginner band: recognized situations matched to known styles without weighing novel context. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Selects and combines styles for ambiguous systems, justifying fit against constraints autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously combining and justifying styles against constraints for ambiguous systems is the Dreyfus competent band, and is the deliberate trade-off practice Fowler's pattern catalog and Richards & Ford's architectural-characteristics method assume a practitioner applies unaided. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fowler et al., Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (Addison-Wesley, 2002); Richards & Ford, Fundamentals of Software Architecture: An Engineering Approach (O'Reilly, 2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines reference architectures and pattern catalogs others adopt across multiple systems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reference architectures and pattern catalogs others adopt across systems is authoring the kind of artifact Fowler's own catalog is; SFIA9's higher responsibility bands describe this as setting technical direction others follow, not merely applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fowler et al., Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (Addison-Wesley, 2002).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's architectural style strategy and anticipates emerging structural shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's architectural style strategy and anticipating structural shifts matches SFIA9's strategic-influence band: judgment that shapes direction across the organization, not a single system. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Originates architectural styles and patterns the wider industry recognizes and adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Originating styles the wider industry recognizes and adopts is the discipline-shaping band SFIA9 reserves for its highest responsibility level; Fowler's and Richards & Ford's own catalogs are examples of individuals operating at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Richards & Ford, Fundamentals of Software Architecture: An Engineering Approach (O'Reilly, 2020).

<a id="arc-02"></a>
##### ARC-02 — Service decomposition & boundary design

*Type:* Technical — Partitions systems into services and modules with clear ownership and coupling boundaries.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Splits a service along boundaries already defined, with decomposition reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Splitting a service along boundaries already defined, with the decomposition reviewed, is the novice band: executing someone else's decomposition decision. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Decomposes routine systems into services using established boundary heuristics independently.
  — *Why this level:* Decomposing routine systems using established boundary heuristics independently is the advanced-beginner band applying Newman's recognized decomposition-by-capability recipes without novel judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd ed. (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs boundaries for complex domains, resolving overlap and ownership ambiguity autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing boundaries for complex domains and resolving overlap and ownership ambiguity autonomously is the competent band; it is the hard case Newman's decomposition chapters address, where heuristics alone don't resolve the boundary. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd ed. (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines decomposition methods and boundary heuristics teams reuse across products.
  — *Why this level:* Defining decomposition methods and boundary heuristics teams reuse across products is authoring guidance at Newman's own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting method, not just applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd ed. (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise-wide boundary and ownership strategy, anticipating decomposition pressures.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise-wide boundary and ownership strategy, anticipating decomposition pressures, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band extending beyond any one product. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the industry reasons about service boundaries and decomposition.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the industry reasons about service boundaries and decomposition is the pioneer band; it is what made Newman's own writing a reference for the field. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Newman, Building Microservices: Designing Fine-Grained Systems, 2nd ed. (O'Reilly, 2021).

<a id="arc-03"></a>
##### ARC-03 — Domain modeling

*Type:* Technical — Models business concepts, language, and boundaries to align software structure with the domain.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Translates given domain rules into a model under review.
  — *Why this level:* Translating given domain rules into a model under review is the novice band: rules handed down, not derived. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds models for familiar domains independently, capturing standard entities and relationships.
  — *Why this level:* Building models for familiar domains independently, capturing standard entities and relationships, is the advanced-beginner band applying Evans' entity/value-object vocabulary without yet needing to negotiate it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Evans, Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software (Addison-Wesley, 2003).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models ambiguous domains, surfacing hidden invariants and resolving conflicting expert input.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling ambiguous domains, surfacing hidden invariants and resolving conflicting expert input, is Evans' core practice of knowledge-crunching toward a ubiquitous language: the Dreyfus competent band, where standard vocabulary no longer suffices. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Evans, Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software (Addison-Wesley, 2003).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines modeling approaches and shared language others apply across domains.
  — *Why this level:* Defining modeling approaches and shared language others apply across domains is authoring strategic-design guidance (bounded contexts, context maps) at Evans' own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting a method others adopt. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Evans, Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software (Addison-Wesley, 2003).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets domain-modeling strategy and standards organization-wide, anticipating evolution.
  — *Why this level:* Setting domain-modeling strategy and standards organization-wide, anticipating evolution, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band applied across many domains, not one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances domain-modeling practice recognized and taught across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing domain-modeling practice recognized and taught across the industry is the pioneer band; DDD's own adoption as an industry vocabulary is the exemplar of work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Evans, Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software (Addison-Wesley, 2003).

<a id="arc-04"></a>
##### ARC-04 — Coupling, cohesion & dependency management

*Type:* Technical — Manages dependencies and direction of coupling to keep components changeable and independently deployable.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Removes obvious dependencies and follows cohesion guidance under review.
  — *Why this level:* Removing obvious dependencies and following cohesion guidance under review is the novice band: applying a checklist, not diagnosing structure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages coupling in routine modules independently, applying standard dependency rules.
  — *Why this level:* Managing coupling in routine modules independently, applying standard dependency rules, is the advanced-beginner band's situational recognition of Parnas' information-hiding heuristic without yet needing to invent decomposition criteria. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Parnas, On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 15(12), 1053-1058 (1972).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and restructures tangled dependencies in complex systems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and restructuring tangled dependencies in complex systems autonomously is the competent band; it is exactly the decomposition-criteria judgment Parnas argues cannot be reduced to a checklist and must be reasoned from what is likely to change. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Parnas, On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 15(12), 1053-1058 (1972).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines dependency governance and cohesion principles teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining dependency governance and cohesion principles teams adopt is authoring decomposition criteria at Parnas' own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting the principle, not applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Parnas, On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 15(12), 1053-1058 (1972).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide coupling strategy and anticipates structural debt accumulation.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide coupling strategy and anticipating structural debt accumulation is SFIA9's strategic-influence band, spanning systems rather than one codebase. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what healthy coupling means for the discipline, influencing wider practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what healthy coupling means for the discipline, influencing wider practice, is the pioneer band; Parnas' 1972 paper is the founding example of a single paper reshaping how the field defines a module boundary. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Parnas, On the Criteria to Be Used in Decomposing Systems into Modules, Communications of the ACM 15(12), 1053-1058 (1972).

#### Distributed Coordination

<a id="arc-05"></a>
##### ARC-05 — Consistency models

*Type:* Technical — Reasons about strong, eventual, and causal consistency to choose correct guarantees per use case.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies a specified consistency model under guidance, with choices reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Applying a specified consistency model under guidance, with choices reviewed, is the novice band: following an assigned choice, not evaluating it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects standard consistency models for routine cases independently.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting standard consistency models for routine cases independently is the advanced-beginner band: recognized situations mapped to known guarantees. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Chooses and reasons about consistency trade-offs in ambiguous distributed scenarios autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Choosing and reasoning about consistency trade-offs in ambiguous distributed scenarios autonomously is the competent band applying the CAP trade-off (Brewer's conjecture, proved by Gilbert & Lynch) to a specific system's constraints rather than citing it abstractly. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brewer, Towards Robust Distributed Systems (PODC keynote, 2000); Gilbert & Lynch, Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services, ACM SIGACT News 33(2), 51-59 (2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines consistency-model guidance others rely on for hard correctness problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining consistency-model guidance others rely on for hard correctness problems is authoring the kind of cross-system reference Kleppmann's replication and consistency chapters provide; SFIA9 marks this as setting guidance others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets consistency strategy across systems and anticipates new model needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting consistency strategy across systems and anticipating new model needs is SFIA9's strategic-influence band spanning the organization's systems portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances how the industry understands and applies consistency models.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing how the industry understands and applies consistency models is the pioneer band; Gilbert & Lynch's formal proof of Brewer's conjecture is the exemplar of a single result changing industry-wide reasoning. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gilbert & Lynch, Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services, ACM SIGACT News 33(2), 51-59 (2002).

<a id="arc-06"></a>
##### ARC-06 — Consensus & coordination

*Type:* Technical — Applies leader election, distributed locks, and consensus to coordinate state across nodes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures coordination using established primitives under review.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring coordination using established primitives under review is the novice band: operating a given tool, not designing the protocol. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard consensus and coordination mechanisms to routine problems independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard consensus and coordination mechanisms to routine problems independently is the advanced-beginner band: recognized patterns (leader election, distributed locks) applied without re-deriving correctness. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs coordination for complex failure scenarios, resolving liveness and safety trade-offs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing coordination for complex failure scenarios, resolving liveness and safety trade-offs autonomously, is the competent band doing the reasoning Raft's own design process made explicit and teachable: trading pure optimality for provable, defensible correctness under a specific failure model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ongaro & Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft), USENIX ATC 2014.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines coordination approaches others adopt and solves intractable agreement problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining coordination approaches others adopt and solving intractable agreement problems is contributing at Paxos' own level: a named protocol other engineers adopt rather than re-derive; SFIA9 marks this as setting approach others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Lamport, The Part-Time Parliament, ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 16(2), 133-169 (1998).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets coordination strategy organization-wide, anticipating distributed-coordination challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Setting coordination strategy organization-wide, anticipating distributed-coordination challenges, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry understanding of consensus and coordination.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry understanding of consensus and coordination is the pioneer band; Paxos and Raft are the field's own examples of individuals originating a consensus model the wider industry now builds on. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Lamport, The Part-Time Parliament, ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 16(2), 133-169 (1998); Ongaro & Ousterhout, In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm (Raft), USENIX ATC 2014.

<a id="arc-07"></a>
##### ARC-07 — Distributed transactions & saga design

*Type:* Technical — Coordinates multi-service state changes using sagas, compensations, and eventual consistency.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements a defined saga or transaction flow under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing a defined saga or transaction flow under review is the novice band: executing a specified flow, not designing it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard distributed transactions and compensations independently for routine flows.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard distributed transactions and compensations independently for routine flows is the advanced-beginner band applying Richardson's cataloged saga and outbox patterns as recognized recipes. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Richardson, Microservices Patterns: With Examples in Java (Manning, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs saga and consistency-recovery patterns for complex multi-step flows autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing saga and consistency-recovery patterns for complex multi-step flows autonomously is the competent band; it is the original saga problem Garcia-Molina & Salem posed: decomposing a long-lived transaction into compensable steps for a specific, non-routine flow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Garcia-Molina & Salem, Sagas, Proc. 1987 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data, 249-259.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines distributed-transaction patterns and failure-handling approaches teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining distributed-transaction patterns and failure-handling approaches teams adopt is authoring pattern guidance at Richardson's own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting approach others reuse across a codebase or org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Richardson, Microservices Patterns: With Examples in Java (Manning, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for cross-system transactional integrity, anticipating coordination needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting strategy for cross-system transactional integrity, anticipating coordination needs, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band spanning systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for distributed transactions across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for distributed transactions across the industry is the pioneer band; Garcia-Molina & Salem's 1987 paper originating the saga concept is the exemplar of a single contribution reshaping how the field designs long-running transactions. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Garcia-Molina & Salem, Sagas, Proc. 1987 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data, 249-259.

#### System Quality & Trade-offs

<a id="arc-08"></a>
##### ARC-08 — Capacity estimation & back-of-envelope modeling

*Type:* Technical — Estimates load, storage, and bandwidth to size systems and validate feasibility early.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs simple capacity calculations from given assumptions under review.
  — *Why this level:* Performing simple capacity calculations from given assumptions under review is the novice band: plugging numbers into a supplied formula. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Estimates capacity for routine systems independently using standard models.
  — *Why this level:* Estimating capacity for routine systems independently using standard models is the advanced-beginner band: recognized load and storage models applied without deep uncertainty handling. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Builds defensible capacity models for ambiguous, large-scale systems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Building defensible capacity models for ambiguous, large-scale systems autonomously is the competent band; it is the demand-forecasting and capacity-planning discipline the Google SRE book documents as requiring judgment about growth, headroom and failure-domain sizing, not a lookup table. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines estimation methods and reference figures others reuse.
  — *Why this level:* Defining estimation methods and reference figures others reuse is authoring the kind of capacity-planning guidance the SRE book itself codifies for an organization; SFIA9 marks this as setting method others adopt. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets capacity-planning strategy and anticipates scaling inflection points organization-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Setting capacity-planning strategy and anticipating scaling inflection points organization-wide is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across the portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances how the discipline approaches capacity modeling.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing how the discipline approaches capacity modeling is the pioneer band; the SRE book's own codification of Google's capacity-planning practice into an industry reference is the exemplar of work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

<a id="arc-09"></a>
##### ARC-09 — Non-functional requirement design

*Type:* Technical — Designs for latency, availability, durability, and consistency targets as first-class constraints.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Documents non-functional requirements from given targets under review.
  — *Why this level:* Documenting non-functional requirements from given targets under review is the novice band: transcribing supplied targets. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Defines standard non-functional requirements independently for routine systems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining standard non-functional requirements independently for routine systems is the advanced-beginner band applying ISO/IEC 25010's quality characteristics (performance efficiency, reliability, etc.) as a recognized checklist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC 25010:2011, Systems and Software Engineering — Systems and Software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — System and Software Quality Models.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Elicits and reconciles conflicting quality requirements in ambiguous contexts autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Eliciting and reconciling conflicting quality requirements in ambiguous contexts autonomously is the competent band: trading off ISO 25010's characteristics against each other for a specific system rather than applying the taxonomy mechanically. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC 25010:2011, Systems and Software Engineering — Systems and Software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — System and Software Quality Models.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines NFR frameworks and quality taxonomies others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining NFR frameworks and quality taxonomies others adopt is authoring guidance at the standard's own level, extending or specializing ISO 25010's model for an organization's context; SFIA9 marks this as setting a framework others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO/IEC 25010:2011, Systems and Software Engineering — Systems and Software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — System and Software Quality Models.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide quality-attribute strategy, anticipating emerging non-functional concerns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide quality-attribute strategy, anticipating emerging non-functional concerns, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for defining and reasoning about system qualities.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for defining and reasoning about system qualities is the pioneer band; ISO/IEC 25010 itself, as a standard adopted industry-wide, is the exemplar of discipline-shaping work at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO/IEC 25010:2011, Systems and Software Engineering — Systems and Software Quality Requirements and Evaluation (SQuaRE) — System and Software Quality Models.

<a id="arc-10"></a>
##### ARC-10 — Architectural trade-off analysis

*Type:* Behavioral — Evaluates and justifies design options against competing quality attributes and constraints.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compares options against given criteria under review.
  — *Why this level:* Comparing options against given criteria under review is the novice band: scoring against someone else's rubric. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Evaluates standard trade-offs independently for routine architectural choices.
  — *Why this level:* Evaluating standard trade-offs independently for routine architectural choices is the advanced-beginner band applying Richards & Ford's trade-off analysis process to recognized, low-stakes decisions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Richards & Ford, Fundamentals of Software Architecture: An Engineering Approach (O'Reilly, 2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Structures and defends trade-off decisions for ambiguous, high-stakes designs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Structuring and defending trade-off decisions for ambiguous, high-stakes designs autonomously is the competent band; it is the scenario-based reasoning ATAM formalizes: eliciting quality-attribute scenarios and reasoning about sensitivity points for a specific architecture, not a generic checklist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kazman, Klein, Barbacci, Longstaff, Lipson & Carriere, The Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method, SEI Technical Report CMU/SEI-98-TR-008 (1998).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines trade-off analysis methods and decision frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining trade-off analysis methods and decision frameworks others adopt is contributing a method at ATAM's own level; SFIA9 marks this as setting a framework others reuse rather than a single evaluation. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kazman, Klein, Barbacci, Longstaff, Lipson & Carriere, The Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method, SEI Technical Report CMU/SEI-98-TR-008 (1998).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets how the organization makes architectural trade-offs, anticipating future tensions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting how the organization makes architectural trade-offs, anticipating future tensions, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across the organization's decision process itself. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances trade-off-analysis practice recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing trade-off-analysis practice recognized across the industry is the pioneer band; ATAM's own adoption as a widely taught, SEI-originated method is the exemplar of work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kazman, Klein, Barbacci, Longstaff, Lipson & Carriere, The Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method, SEI Technical Report CMU/SEI-98-TR-008 (1998).

### Computer Science Foundations (CS)

#### Data Structures & Algorithms

<a id="cs-01"></a>
##### CS-01 — Algorithmic problem solving

*Type:* Technical — Selects data structures and algorithmic strategies to solve problems correctly and efficiently.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Solves well-defined problems using known algorithms under review.
  — *Why this level:* Solving well-defined problems using known algorithms under review is the novice band: applying a named algorithm to a recognized problem shape. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects and applies appropriate algorithms to routine problems independently.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting and applying appropriate algorithms to routine problems independently is the advanced-beginner band: matching a problem to one of CLRS's cataloged techniques without needing to invent one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Devises efficient solutions for novel, ambiguous problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Devising efficient solutions for novel, ambiguous problems autonomously is the competent band: composing or adapting CLRS's design paradigms (divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, greedy) for a problem that doesn't map cleanly to a textbook case. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines solution approaches and decomposition techniques others learn from.
  — *Why this level:* Defining solution approaches and decomposition techniques others learn from is authoring pedagogy and technique at CLRS's own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting an approach others adopt. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for algorithmic problem solving and anticipates new problem classes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for algorithmic problem solving and anticipating new problem classes is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across the organization's engineering practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Originates algorithmic techniques the wider field adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Originating algorithmic techniques the wider field adopts is the pioneer band; CLRS itself, compiling techniques from originators like Cook, Karp and Tarjan into the field's standard reference, exemplifies work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).

<a id="cs-02"></a>
##### CS-02 — Computational complexity analysis

*Type:* Technical — Analyzes time and space complexity to compare approaches and predict scaling behavior.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Determines complexity of simple algorithms under review.
  — *Why this level:* Determining complexity of simple algorithms under review is the novice band: applying a known Big-O rule to a straightforward loop or recursion shape. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Analyzes time and space complexity of routine algorithms independently.
  — *Why this level:* Analyzing time and space complexity of routine algorithms independently is the advanced-beginner band applying Sipser's complexity-class definitions to recognized algorithm structures. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed. (Cengage, 2012).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Analyzes and optimizes complexity for intricate algorithms autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Analyzing and optimizing complexity for intricate algorithms autonomously is the competent band; it is the NP-hardness and reduction reasoning Garey & Johnson's guide formalizes: recognizing when a problem resists polynomial solution rather than looking up a known bound. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability: A Guide to the Theory of NP-Completeness (W.H. Freeman, 1979).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines complexity-analysis methods and teaches rigorous reasoning to others.
  — *Why this level:* Defining complexity-analysis methods and teaching rigorous reasoning to others is authoring guidance at Garey & Johnson's own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting a method others learn from. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability: A Guide to the Theory of NP-Completeness (W.H. Freeman, 1979).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for complexity reasoning, anticipating where bottlenecks emerge.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for complexity reasoning, anticipating where bottlenecks emerge, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances how the field reasons about computational complexity.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing how the field reasons about computational complexity is the pioneer band; the complexity-theory results Sipser's text compiles (Cook-Levin, hierarchy theorems) exemplify individuals originating the field's own reasoning tools. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation, 3rd ed. (Cengage, 2012).

<a id="cs-03"></a>
##### CS-03 — Core data structure design

*Type:* Technical — Applies and adapts foundational structures like trees, graphs, hashes, and heaps to model problems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses appropriate standard data structures under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Using appropriate standard data structures under guidance is the novice band: picking from a supplied list. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects and adapts standard structures for routine needs independently.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting and adapting standard structures for routine needs independently is the advanced-beginner band applying CLRS's catalog (trees, hashes, heaps) to recognized access-pattern needs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs custom structures balancing competing constraints for hard cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing custom structures balancing competing constraints for hard cases autonomously is the competent band: composing or augmenting CLRS's structures (e.g., augmented trees) when no cataloged structure fits the constraint mix. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines structure-selection principles and novel structures others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining structure-selection principles and novel structures others adopt is authoring at the level of the field's structure originators whose work CLRS compiles; SFIA9 marks this as setting a principle or structure others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets data-structure strategy and anticipates evolving access patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting data-structure strategy and anticipating evolving access patterns is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Originates data structures recognized and used across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Originating data structures recognized and used across the industry is the pioneer band; the named structures (red-black trees, Fibonacci heaps) CLRS documents are themselves exemplars of individual contributions reaching this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest & Stein, Introduction to Algorithms, 3rd ed. (MIT Press, 2009).

#### Concurrency & Computation

<a id="cs-04"></a>
##### CS-04 — Concurrency & parallelism

*Type:* Technical — Designs concurrent and parallel execution using synchronization, isolation, and shared-state discipline.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes concurrent code using given primitives under review.
  — *Why this level:* Writing concurrent code using given primitives under review is the novice band: using a supplied lock or queue as instructed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard concurrent patterns independently for routine workloads.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard concurrent patterns independently for routine workloads is the advanced-beginner band: recognized patterns (producer-consumer, thread pools) applied without deriving new correctness arguments. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs correct, efficient concurrency for complex shared-state problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing correct, efficient concurrency for complex shared-state problems autonomously is the competent band; it is exactly the correctness-condition reasoning (linearizability, lock-freedom) Herlihy & Shavit formalize for problems where standard patterns don't already prove correctness. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Herlihy & Shavit, The Art of Multiprocessor Programming (Morgan Kaufmann, 2008).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines concurrency patterns and reasoning others adopt to avoid subtle defects.
  — *Why this level:* Defining concurrency patterns and reasoning others adopt to avoid subtle defects is authoring a reasoning model at CSP's own level of contribution; SFIA9 marks this as setting reasoning and patterns others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hoare, Communicating Sequential Processes, Communications of the ACM 21(8), 666-677 (1978).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets concurrency strategy organization-wide, anticipating parallelism challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Setting concurrency strategy organization-wide, anticipating parallelism challenges, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry understanding of concurrency and parallelism.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry understanding of concurrency and parallelism is the pioneer band; Hoare's CSP is the field's own example of a single formal model reshaping how the industry reasons about concurrent composition for decades. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hoare, Communicating Sequential Processes, Communications of the ACM 21(8), 666-677 (1978).

<a id="cs-05"></a>
##### CS-05 — Memory & resource management

*Type:* Technical — Reasons about allocation, references, and lifetimes to use memory and resources safely and efficiently.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Manages memory and resources following established patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing memory and resources following established patterns under review is the novice band: applying a supplied allocation or cleanup pattern. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Handles standard allocation and cleanup independently for routine code.
  — *Why this level:* Handling standard allocation and cleanup independently for routine code is the advanced-beginner band: recognized ownership and lifetime patterns applied without diagnosing novel failure modes. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and resolves complex leaks, contention, and lifetime issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and resolving complex leaks, contention, and lifetime issues autonomously is the competent band; it is the allocator and fragmentation trade-off reasoning Wilson et al.'s survey formalizes for cases where standard allocation patterns already fail. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wilson, Johnstone, Neely & Boles, Dynamic Storage Allocation: A Survey and Critical Review, Proc. IWMM 1995, LNCS 986.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines resource-management approaches others adopt for hard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining resource-management approaches others adopt for hard cases is authoring guidance at the survey's own synthesizing level; SFIA9 marks this as setting an approach others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wilson, Johnstone, Neely & Boles, Dynamic Storage Allocation: A Survey and Critical Review, Proc. IWMM 1995, LNCS 986.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets resource-management strategy, anticipating efficiency and lifetime concerns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting resource-management strategy, anticipating efficiency and lifetime concerns, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances how the discipline reasons about memory and resource management.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing how the discipline reasons about memory and resource management is the pioneer band; the allocator designs (best-fit, segregated free lists) the survey traces to individual originators exemplify work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wilson, Johnstone, Neely & Boles, Dynamic Storage Allocation: A Survey and Critical Review, Proc. IWMM 1995, LNCS 986.

<a id="cs-06"></a>
##### CS-06 — Computation & execution models

*Type:* Technical — Understands how programs map to processes, threads, scheduling, and the underlying machine.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Reasons about basic execution behavior under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Reasoning about basic execution behavior under guidance is the novice band: following a supplied explanation of what a process or thread does. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard execution-model knowledge to routine work independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard execution-model knowledge to routine work independently is the advanced-beginner band applying Silberschatz et al.'s process and scheduling model to recognized situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Leverages deep execution-model understanding to solve subtle behavioral problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Leveraging deep execution-model understanding to solve subtle behavioral problems autonomously is the competent band: reasoning through scheduler and memory-model interactions the textbook documents in principle but does not resolve for a specific, ambiguous failure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines execution-model guidance others rely on for performance and correctness.
  — *Why this level:* Defining execution-model guidance others rely on for performance and correctness is authoring reference-level guidance at the textbook's own level of synthesis; SFIA9 marks this as setting guidance others reuse. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for execution-model reasoning, anticipating model shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for execution-model reasoning, anticipating model shifts, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across systems and platforms. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances the field's understanding of computation and execution models.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing the field's understanding of computation and execution models is the pioneer band; the scheduling and virtualization models the textbook compiles from their individual originators exemplify contributions recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).

#### Systems & Networking Fundamentals

<a id="cs-07"></a>
##### CS-07 — Networking & protocol fundamentals

*Type:* Technical — Applies layered networking, addressing, and transport concepts that underpin distributed communication.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Diagnoses basic connectivity using given tools under review.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing basic connectivity using given tools under review is the novice band: running a supplied diagnostic command. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard protocol knowledge to routine networking tasks independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard protocol knowledge to routine networking tasks independently is the advanced-beginner band applying Kurose & Ross's layered model to recognized connectivity and configuration situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kurose & Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8th ed. (Pearson, 2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and designs around complex protocol and network behavior autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and designing around complex protocol and network behavior autonomously is the competent band: reasoning from the TCP standard's own state-machine and congestion-control behavior to explain a non-obvious failure, not just citing the layer model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IETF, RFC 9293: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) (2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines protocol-usage guidance and solves obscure networking problems for others.
  — *Why this level:* Defining protocol-usage guidance and solving obscure networking problems for others is authoring reference guidance at the textbook's own synthesizing level; SFIA9 marks this as setting guidance others rely on. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kurose & Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8th ed. (Pearson, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets networking strategy and anticipates protocol-level shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting networking strategy and anticipating protocol-level shifts is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across the organization's systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry understanding of networking and protocols.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry understanding of networking and protocols is the pioneer band; an IETF standard like RFC 9293 for TCP is the exemplar of individuals and working groups originating the protocols the industry builds on. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); IETF, RFC 9293: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) (2022).

<a id="cs-08"></a>
##### CS-08 — Operating system & runtime fundamentals
