*Type:* Technical — Leverages OS-level concepts of processes, I/O, and resource isolation to reason about runtime behavior.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses OS and runtime features following guidance under review.
  — *Why this level:* Using OS and runtime features following guidance under review is the novice band: calling a supplied API as instructed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard OS and runtime knowledge to routine tasks independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard OS and runtime knowledge to routine tasks independently is the advanced-beginner band applying Silberschatz et al.'s process, I/O and isolation model to recognized situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses subtle OS and runtime interactions for hard problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing subtle OS and runtime interactions for hard problems autonomously is the competent band: reasoning through scheduler, page-cache, or isolation interactions the textbook documents in principle but that manifest ambiguously in a specific system. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines runtime-behavior guidance others rely on.
  — *Why this level:* Defining runtime-behavior guidance others rely on is authoring reference-level guidance at the textbook's own level of synthesis; SFIA9 marks this as setting guidance others reuse across teams. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for OS and runtime reasoning, anticipating platform shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for OS and runtime reasoning, anticipating platform shifts, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across the organization's platforms. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances the field's understanding of operating-system and runtime behavior.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing the field's understanding of operating-system and runtime behavior is the pioneer band; the process and scheduling models the textbook compiles from their individual originators exemplify work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Silberschatz, Galvin & Gagne, Operating System Concepts, 10th ed. (Wiley, 2018).

<a id="cs-09"></a>
##### CS-09 — Data encoding & serialization

*Type:* Technical — Chooses encoding, serialization, and schema-evolution formats for storage and cross-service exchange.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies given encoding and serialization formats under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying given encoding and serialization formats under review is the novice band: using a format someone else chose. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects and uses standard serialization formats independently for routine data.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting and using standard serialization formats independently for routine data is the advanced-beginner band applying Kleppmann's format comparison (JSON, Avro, Protocol Buffers) to recognized, low-stakes use cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs encoding schemes balancing compatibility and efficiency for hard cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing encoding schemes balancing compatibility and efficiency for hard cases autonomously is the competent band; it is Kleppmann's schema-evolution reasoning (forward and backward compatibility across service boundaries) applied to a specific, non-routine system rather than cited abstractly. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines serialization and schema-evolution approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining serialization and schema-evolution approaches others adopt is authoring guidance at the book's own synthesizing level; SFIA9 marks this as setting an approach others reuse organization-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets encoding strategy organization-wide, anticipating interchange needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting encoding strategy organization-wide, anticipating interchange needs, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band across the organization's service boundaries. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for data encoding and serialization.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for data encoding and serialization is the pioneer band; Kleppmann's own synthesis, now a widely taught industry reference, exemplifies work recognized at this level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

### Mobile Engineering (MOB)

#### Mobile UI & Interaction

<a id="mob-01"></a>
##### MOB-01 — Native mobile UI construction

*Type:* Technical — Building screens and views with platform UI paradigms, navigation patterns, and lifecycle awareness.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds UI screens from given designs using standard components under review.
  — *Why this level:* Assembling screens from given designs with standard components under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: context-free rules (Apple HIG's documented components) are followed exactly, with judgment supplied by the reviewer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Constructs standard native interfaces independently for routine screens.
  — *Why this level:* Constructing standard native interfaces unsupervised for routine screens is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply) and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: recurring screen patterns from the Material Design 3 component catalog are applied without guidance, but not yet generalized beyond documented cases. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Material Design 3 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Builds complex, polished native UI resolving tricky layout and rendering cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving tricky layout and rendering edge cases autonomously, where the component specs run out and judgment calls begin, is the Dreyfus competent band and SFIA9 level 4 (Enable): the engineer is the local go-to for UI problems with no documented recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines UI-construction patterns and component libraries others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining UI-construction patterns and component libraries other engineers adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise) authoritative-guidance behavior: the engineer produces the internal equivalent of the HIG component catalog other teams draw from, not just consumes it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets native-UI standards and anticipates platform UI evolution.
  — *Why this level:* Setting native-UI standards and anticipating platform UI evolution matches SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): the engineer shapes org practice ahead of the platform changes the way Apple's own HIG revisions anticipate new device form factors. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for native mobile UI construction.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for native mobile UI construction is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7 (Set Strategy/Inspire/Mobilize): externally recognized influence comparable to the authors of the platform-level guidelines the whole industry converges on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="mob-02"></a>
##### MOB-02 — Touch & gesture interaction design

*Type:* Technical — Implementing touch, gesture, and input handling aligned with mobile interaction conventions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Wires up standard touch handlers following guidance under review.
  — *Why this level:* Wiring up standard touch handlers from given guidance under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: the documented gesture vocabulary (HIG's tap/swipe/pinch set) is followed by rule, with target-sizing judgment supplied by review. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines: Gestures (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements common gestures and touch interactions independently for routine flows.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing common gestures independently for routine flows is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): the engineer applies the HIG's standard gesture set and NN/g's minimum touch-target thresholds without guidance for well-understood flows. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Harley, Touch Targets on Touchscreens, Nielsen Norman Group (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs complex, conflict-free gesture systems with natural feel autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing complex, conflict-free gesture systems with natural feel autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: resolving gesture-conflict and target-size tradeoffs that NN/g's research shows break novice designs is judgment work with no documented recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Harley, Touch Targets on Touchscreens, Nielsen Norman Group (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines gesture-interaction patterns others adopt across apps.
  — *Why this level:* Defining gesture-interaction patterns other apps adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's internal gesture-conflict and sizing rules become the org's reusable reference, the way HIG's own gesture chapter is reused industry-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines: Gestures (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets interaction standards and anticipates new input paradigms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting interaction standards and anticipating new input paradigms beyond touch (spatial, haptic) is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence) org-wide standard-setting ahead of platform input shifts. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for touch and gesture interaction.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for touch and gesture interaction is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution comparable to the usability research and platform guidance the whole industry currently draws on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="mob-03"></a>
##### MOB-03 — Adaptive layout for device fragmentation

*Type:* Technical — Adapting layouts across varied screen sizes, densities, form factors, and orientations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adjusts layouts for given screen sizes following guidance under review.
  — *Why this level:* Adjusting layouts for given screen sizes under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: the engineer applies Android's documented window-size-class buckets (compact/medium/expanded) by rule, not judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Android Developers: Window Size Classes (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds responsive layouts independently for common device classes.
  — *Why this level:* Building responsive layouts independently for common device classes is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): using the documented window-size-class breakpoints unsupervised for the well-populated device classes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: Window Size Classes (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs layouts robust across the full fragmentation spectrum autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing layouts robust across the full fragmentation spectrum autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: Han et al.'s empirical finding that vendor/device fragmentation drives a long tail of edge-case bugs is exactly the ambiguity this level must resolve without a documented recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Han, Zhang, Fan, Hindle, Wong & Stroulia, Understanding Android Fragmentation with Topic Analysis of Vendor-Specific Bugs, WCRE (2012).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines adaptive-layout strategies and breakpoint systems others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining adaptive-layout strategies and breakpoint systems others adopt is SFIA9 level 5: the engineer authors the internal equivalent of the HIG layout/adaptivity guidance for the org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines: Layout (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets fragmentation-handling standards, anticipating new form factors.
  — *Why this level:* Setting fragmentation-handling standards and anticipating new form factors is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide policy that gets ahead of the device-landscape churn Han et al. show fragmentation constantly produces. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Han, Zhang, Fan, Hindle, Wong & Stroulia, Understanding Android Fragmentation with Topic Analysis of Vendor-Specific Bugs, WCRE (2012).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for adaptive layout across devices.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for adaptive layout is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: the externally recognized authority that produces guidance like the HIG layout chapter or the window-size-class standard itself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Device Platform Integration

<a id="mob-04"></a>
##### MOB-04 — Device sensor & hardware integration

*Type:* Technical — Accessing cameras, sensors, location, and other on-device hardware through platform interfaces.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Reads sensors using given APIs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Reading sensors using given APIs under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: the engineer calls the documented Sensor Manager API by rule with no fusion judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Android Developers: Sensors Overview (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Integrates standard sensors and hardware independently for routine features.
  — *Why this level:* Integrating standard sensors independently for routine features is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): standard accelerometer/GPS integrations per the documented Core Motion API contract, unsupervised. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., Core Motion documentation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs robust sensor fusion and hardware handling for complex cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing robust sensor fusion for complex cases autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: combining multiple sensor streams via Core Motion's device-motion fusion to handle noise and edge cases the platform API alone does not resolve. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., Core Motion documentation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines sensor-integration patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining sensor-integration patterns others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's fusion and calibration approach becomes the org's reusable reference beyond the base sensor API. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: Sensors Overview (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets hardware-integration strategy, anticipating new sensor capabilities.
  — *Why this level:* Setting hardware-integration strategy and anticipating new sensor capabilities is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): tracking and shaping org-wide response to platform sensor-roadmap changes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for device sensor and hardware integration.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for device sensor and hardware integration is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution at the level that shapes platform sensor-API design itself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="mob-05"></a>
##### MOB-05 — Platform permissions & privacy controls

*Type:* Technical — Requesting, managing, and respecting runtime permissions and platform privacy requirements.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Requests permissions following platform guidance under review.
  — *Why this level:* Requesting permissions per platform guidance under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: the runtime-permission call is made by documented rule (Apple's App Privacy disclosure requirements), with data-minimization judgment left to the reviewer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., App Privacy Details (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard permission and privacy flows independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard permission and privacy flows independently is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): meeting OWASP MASVS's baseline (L1) storage/permission requirements without further guidance. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OWASP Foundation, Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (MASVS) (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs privacy-respecting permission strategies for complex data needs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing privacy-respecting permission strategies for complex data needs autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: meeting MASVS's stricter L2 requirements for sensitive-data apps and NIST SP 800-124's mobile-app risk guidance calls for judgment neither standard spells out as a recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (MASVS) (accessed 2026-07); NIST, SP 800-124 Rev. 2: Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines permission and privacy patterns others adopt across apps.
  — *Why this level:* Defining permission and privacy patterns other apps adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's privacy playbook becomes the org's reference implementation of NIST 800-124 controls. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, SP 800-124 Rev. 2: Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets privacy-control strategy, anticipating regulatory and platform shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting privacy-control strategy while anticipating regulatory and platform shifts is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): tracking evolving NIST guidance and platform privacy-label requirements ahead of enforcement. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, SP 800-124 Rev. 2: Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for mobile permissions and privacy.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for mobile permissions and privacy is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: the standard-setting work that produces frameworks like OWASP MASVS itself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, Mobile Application Security Verification Standard (MASVS) (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="mob-06"></a>
##### MOB-06 — Push notifications & background processing

*Type:* Technical — Implementing remote messaging and background tasks within platform execution constraints.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements basic notifications and background tasks following guidance under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing basic notifications and background tasks per given guidance under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: following the documented Firebase Cloud Messaging setup steps without independent judgment on constraint tradeoffs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Firebase Cloud Messaging documentation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard push and background workflows independently for routine needs.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard push and background workflows independently for routine needs is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): wiring BackgroundTasks-scheduled work per the documented API contract, unsupervised. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., BackgroundTasks framework documentation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reliable notification and background systems under platform constraints autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing reliable notification and background systems under platform constraints autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: working within Android's Doze/App Standby background-execution limits without a documented recipe for every failure mode is the judgment call this level owns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Android Developers: Background Work Overview (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines push and background-processing patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining push and background-processing patterns others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's retry/backoff and scheduling approach becomes the org's reference around the platform's background constraints. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: Background Work Overview (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets notification and background strategy, anticipating platform restrictions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting notification and background strategy while anticipating platform restrictions is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): tracking how background-execution limits tighten release over release and adjusting org strategy ahead of them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: Background Work Overview (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for push and background processing.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for push and background processing is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally recognized contribution at the level that shapes how platform messaging and scheduling APIs themselves evolve. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Mobile Runtime Quality

<a id="mob-07"></a>
##### MOB-07 — Mobile app lifecycle & state restoration

*Type:* Technical — Managing app and process lifecycle, suspension, and seamless state restoration across interruptions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Handles lifecycle callbacks following given patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Handling lifecycle callbacks from given patterns under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: following the documented Activity lifecycle callback sequence by rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Android Developers: The Activity Lifecycle (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard state save and restore independently for routine flows.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard state save/restore independently for routine flows is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): using the documented onSaveInstanceState/state-restoration contract unsupervised for well-understood screens. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: The Activity Lifecycle (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs robust lifecycle and restoration handling for complex state autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing robust lifecycle and restoration handling for complex state autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: reconciling multi-screen or async state across the process-death/restoration boundary that Apple's lifecycle documentation frames only as a contract, not a recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., Managing Your App's Life Cycle (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines lifecycle and restoration patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining lifecycle and restoration patterns others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's state-restoration architecture becomes the org's reusable reference against the platform's lifecycle contract. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., Managing Your App's Life Cycle (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets state-management standards across apps, anticipating lifecycle changes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting state-management standards across apps while anticipating lifecycle changes is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide policy tracking how platform lifecycle contracts shift across releases. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: The Activity Lifecycle (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for app lifecycle and state restoration.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for app lifecycle and state restoration is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: the standard-setting work behind the lifecycle contracts platforms themselves publish. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="mob-08"></a>
##### MOB-08 — Mobile performance, memory & battery optimization

*Type:* Technical — Optimizing responsiveness, memory footprint, and energy use under constrained device resources.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies given optimizations and measures with provided tools under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying given optimizations with provided tools under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: running the documented Xcode/Android profiler workflows against known Android Vitals thresholds without independent diagnosis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., Improving Your App's Performance (accessed 2026-07); Google, Android Vitals (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Profiles and fixes common performance and memory issues independently.
  — *Why this level:* Profiling and fixing common performance/memory issues independently is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): resolving the well-known culprits Li et al. show dominate Android energy use (API misuse, unnecessary network calls) unsupervised. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Li, Hao, Gui & Halfond, An Empirical Study of the Energy Consumption of Android Applications, ICSME (2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and resolves complex performance, memory, and battery problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and resolving complex performance, memory, and battery problems autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: going beyond Li et al.'s documented top energy culprits to novel, app-specific bottlenecks with no existing playbook. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Li, Hao, Gui & Halfond, An Empirical Study of the Energy Consumption of Android Applications, ICSME (2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines optimization methods and budgets others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining optimization methods and budgets others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's performance budget becomes the org's reference against Android Vitals' own bad-behavior thresholds. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Vitals (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets mobile-performance strategy, anticipating efficiency challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Setting mobile-performance strategy and anticipating efficiency challenges is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide policy tracking how vitals thresholds and platform performance expectations tighten over time. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Vitals (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for mobile performance and efficiency.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for mobile performance and efficiency is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution at the level that produces research like Li et al.'s energy-consumption study. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Li, Hao, Gui & Halfond, An Empirical Study of the Energy Consumption of Android Applications, ICSME (2014).

<a id="mob-09"></a>
##### MOB-09 — Offline-first data & local persistence

*Type:* Technical — Persisting data locally and synchronizing reliably across unreliable mobile connectivity.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements local storage following given patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing local storage from given patterns under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: following Android's documented offline-first reference architecture by rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Android Developers: Build an Offline-First App (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard offline storage and caching independently for routine cases.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard offline storage and caching independently for routine cases is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): applying the documented cache-then-network pattern unsupervised where conflicts are rare. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Android Developers: Build an Offline-First App (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs robust offline-first sync and conflict resolution for complex data autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing robust offline-first sync and conflict resolution for complex data autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: Shapiro et al.'s conflict-free merge theory is precisely the tool this level must apply without a documented recipe when concurrent offline edits collide. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Shapiro, Preguica, Baquero & Zawirski, Conflict-free Replicated Data Types, Rapport de recherche RR-7687, INRIA (2011).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines offline-first patterns and sync strategies others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining offline-first patterns and sync strategies others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's conflict-resolution approach, CRDT-based or otherwise, becomes the org's reusable reference. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Shapiro, Preguica, Baquero & Zawirski, Conflict-free Replicated Data Types, Rapport de recherche RR-7687, INRIA (2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets local-persistence strategy, anticipating connectivity and sync needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting local-persistence strategy while anticipating connectivity and sync needs is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide policy on sync architecture ahead of new connectivity patterns. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for offline-first data.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for offline-first data is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution at the level of Shapiro et al.'s foundational CRDT research that the industry's offline-sync tooling now builds on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Shapiro, Preguica, Baquero & Zawirski, Conflict-free Replicated Data Types, Rapport de recherche RR-7687, INRIA (2011).

<a id="mob-10"></a>
##### MOB-10 — Cross-platform mobile development

*Type:* Technical — Sharing logic and UI across platforms while honoring each platform's conventions and capabilities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds shared features following established cross-platform patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Building shared features from established cross-platform patterns under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: following the documented React Native bridge/component model by rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Meta, React Native Documentation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard cross-platform components independently for routine needs.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard cross-platform components independently for routine needs is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): using the documented Flutter widget/rendering architecture unsupervised for well-understood screens. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Flutter Architectural Overview (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs cross-platform architecture balancing sharing and platform fidelity autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing cross-platform architecture balancing sharing and platform fidelity autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: Suri et al.'s empirical finding that frameworks trade CPU/rendering performance against platform fidelity differently is exactly the judgment this level must resolve without a documented recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Suri, Taneja, Bhanot, Sharma & Raj, Cross-Platform Empirical Analysis of Mobile Application Development Frameworks: Kotlin, React Native and Flutter, ACM ICIMMI (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines cross-platform approaches and abstractions others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining cross-platform approaches and abstractions others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's shared-vs-native boundary decisions become the org's reusable reference, informed by empirical tradeoffs like Suri et al.'s. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Suri, Taneja, Bhanot, Sharma & Raj, Cross-Platform Empirical Analysis of Mobile Application Development Frameworks: Kotlin, React Native and Flutter, ACM ICIMMI (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets cross-platform strategy, anticipating platform divergence.
  — *Why this level:* Setting cross-platform strategy while anticipating platform divergence is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide framework and architecture policy tracking how native platforms and cross-platform frameworks diverge release over release. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for cross-platform mobile development.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for cross-platform mobile development is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution at the level that shapes frameworks like Flutter's or React Native's own architecture. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Flutter Architectural Overview (accessed 2026-07); Meta, React Native Documentation (accessed 2026-07).

#### Release & Distribution

<a id="mob-11"></a>
##### MOB-11 — Mobile release & store delivery

*Type:* Technical — Packaging, signing, submitting, and managing app distribution through store review and rollout processes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares release builds and submissions following given steps under review.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing release builds and submissions from given steps under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: following the documented App Store Review Guidelines submission checklist by rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Apple Inc., App Store Review Guidelines (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard store submission and release processes independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard store submission and release processes independently is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): navigating Google Play's documented policy gates unsupervised for routine releases. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Google Play Policies (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs release pipelines handling complex store and rollout requirements autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing release pipelines handling complex store and rollout requirements autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: Forsgren et al.'s finding that release-engineering maturity (frequent, low-risk deploys) predicts org performance is the judgment this level must operationalize against store-review constraints without a documented recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines release and store-delivery practices others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining release and store-delivery practices others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's pipeline becomes the org's reference implementation of Accelerate's deployment-frequency practices within store-review constraints. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets release strategy, anticipating store-policy and distribution shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting release strategy while anticipating store-policy and distribution shifts is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide policy tracking how Apple's review guidelines evolve ahead of enforcement. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Apple Inc., App Store Review Guidelines (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for mobile release and store delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for mobile release and store delivery is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution that influences store-review and release-engineering discourse itself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="mob-12"></a>
##### MOB-12 — Over-the-air updates & version adoption

*Type:* Technical — Delivering updates and managing fragmented version adoption across an installed user base.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Ships OTA updates following given configuration under review.
  — *Why this level:* Shipping OTA updates from given configuration under review is Dreyfus's novice stage: a documented rollout-percentage config is applied by rule, with judgment about pacing left to the reviewer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard OTA delivery and version targeting independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard OTA delivery and version targeting independently is SFIA9 level 3 (Apply): staged rollouts and version-targeting rules applied unsupervised for routine releases. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs safe OTA rollout and adoption strategies for complex fleets autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing safe OTA rollout and adoption strategies for complex fleets autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band: StatCounter's live data showing the installed base spans many concurrent OS/app versions is the fragmented-fleet problem this level must manage without a documented recipe, while respecting Apple's App Store Review Guidelines restriction on downloading executable code outside the store gate. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); StatCounter, Android Version Market Share Worldwide (accessed 2026-07); Apple Inc., App Store Review Guidelines (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines OTA-update and adoption-management patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining OTA-update and adoption-management patterns others adopt is SFIA9 level 5 (Ensure/Advise): the engineer's staged-rollout and version-targeting approach becomes the org's reusable reference. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets update-delivery strategy, anticipating version-fragmentation challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Setting update-delivery strategy while anticipating version-fragmentation challenges is SFIA9 level 6 (Initiate/Influence): org-wide policy tracking how the installed base's version spread shifts adoption risk over time. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); StatCounter, Android Version Market Share Worldwide (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances industry practice for over-the-air updates and version adoption.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing industry practice for over-the-air updates and version adoption is Dreyfus's master stage and SFIA9 level 7: externally credible contribution shaping how the industry measures and manages fragmentation itself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

### Data Engineering & Analytics (DATA)

#### Data Pipelines & Integration

<a id="data-01"></a>
##### DATA-01 — Batch & streaming pipeline design

*Type:* Technical — Designs batch and real-time data flows that move and transform data reliably at scale.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds simple batch jobs from clear specs, with output and logic reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Building simple batch jobs from clear specs under review sits at Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA's Level 2 Assist -- supervised execution of predefined data-movement logic, not yet designing pipeline structure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs routine batch or streaming pipelines independently, handling common volume and ordering cases.
  — *Why this level:* Designing routine batch or streaming pipelines independently for common volume/ordering cases applies Reis & Housley's standard ingestion-to-transform pipeline pattern without deviation; Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band matches SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs robust pipelines for ambiguous workloads, balancing latency, throughput, and cost autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing latency, throughput, and cost autonomously for ambiguous workloads is Dreyfus's competent band -- full ownership of a bounded but non-routine design space, matching Kleppmann's framing of pipeline design as continuous engineering trade-offs rather than a fixed recipe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines reusable pipeline patterns others adopt and resolves intractable backpressure or exactly-once problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reusable pipeline patterns and resolving exactly-once/backpressure problems others cannot is Dreyfus's proficient band, where practice is codified for reuse; Kleppmann names exactly-once delivery and backpressure as the genuinely hard, still-debated problems, so solving them for others is P4-grade. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's batch-versus-streaming strategy and anticipates emerging processing paradigms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's batch-versus-streaming strategy and anticipating processing-paradigm shifts is org-wide standard-setting beyond any one pipeline's design -- Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good pipeline architecture means industry-wide and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good pipeline architecture means industry-wide and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Reis & Housley's own lifecycle framework occupies as a public reference model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).

<a id="data-02"></a>
##### DATA-02 — Data ingestion & integration

*Type:* Technical — Acquires and consolidates data from heterogeneous internal and external sources into usable form.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Connects to documented sources and loads data under guidance, with mappings reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Connecting to documented sources and loading data under guidance is supervised execution of a known interface -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently integrates standard sources, handling routine schema and format variation.
  — *Why this level:* Independently integrating standard sources while handling routine schema/format variation applies Reis & Housley's cataloged ingestion patterns (batch, CDC, API) to a new source without inventing a new pattern -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Reliably integrates messy, undocumented, or high-volume sources and resolves hard reconciliation cases.
  — *Why this level:* Reliably integrating messy, undocumented, or high-volume sources and resolving hard reconciliation cases autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner owns judgment calls the pattern catalog doesn't answer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines ingestion frameworks and connector patterns others reuse across diverse source types.
  — *Why this level:* Defining ingestion frameworks and connector patterns others reuse across source types is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying the ingestion stage of Reis & Housley's data engineering lifecycle into reusable infrastructure rather than solving one integration at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets integration strategy and standards, anticipating new source modalities and protocols.
  — *Why this level:* Setting integration strategy and anticipating new source modalities/protocols is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for source integration and is externally credible on the topic.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for source integration and being externally credible on it is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- practice recognized beyond one organization. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-03"></a>
##### DATA-03 — Workflow orchestration & scheduling

*Type:* Technical — Coordinates dependent data tasks into reliable, repeatable, scheduled pipelines.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures predefined workflow steps and dependencies under review.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring predefined workflow steps and dependencies under review is supervised use of an existing orchestration definition -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and schedules routine multi-step workflows independently with normal retry handling.
  — *Why this level:* Building and scheduling routine multi-step workflows independently with normal retry handling applies the standard DAG/dependency/retry model Reis & Housley describe as the orchestration stage of the data engineering lifecycle, without redesigning it -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Orchestrates complex interdependent workflows autonomously, resolving tricky timing and failure cases.
  — *Why this level:* Orchestrating complex interdependent workflows autonomously and resolving tricky timing/failure cases is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner is the go-to for cases the standard scheduler patterns don't cleanly cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines orchestration patterns and guardrails others adopt for reliability at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Defining orchestration patterns and reliability guardrails others adopt at scale is Dreyfus's proficient band -- the shift from running workflows to authoring the guardrails others' workflows must follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets orchestration strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in scheduling and dependency management.
  — *Why this level:* Setting orchestration strategy and anticipating shifts in scheduling/dependency management is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for workflow orchestration across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for workflow orchestration across the discipline and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-04"></a>
##### DATA-04 — Change data capture & incremental processing

*Type:* Technical — Captures and propagates source data changes efficiently without full reprocessing.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs configured incremental loads and verifies row counts under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Running configured incremental loads and verifying row counts under guidance is supervised execution against a defined check -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard change-capture and incremental jobs independently for common scenarios.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard change-capture and incremental jobs independently for common scenarios applies an established CDC pattern to a routine source without redesign -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reliable incremental processing for late-arriving, out-of-order, or deleted-record cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing reliable incremental processing for late-arriving, out-of-order, or deleted-record cases autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band; Kleppmann treats exactly these cases as the genuinely hard part of change propagation separating a working CDC job from a correct one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines incremental and capture patterns others adopt to guarantee correctness and replayability.
  — *Why this level:* Defining incremental and capture patterns others adopt to guarantee correctness and replayability is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying Kleppmann's correctness guarantees (ordering, idempotency, replay) into reusable patterns rather than re-deriving them per pipeline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the strategy for change propagation and anticipates evolving capture techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting change-propagation strategy and anticipating evolving capture techniques is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry standards for change data capture and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry standards for change data capture and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Data Modeling & Storage

<a id="data-05"></a>
##### DATA-05 — Data modeling & warehousing

*Type:* Technical — Structures data into warehouses and lakes optimized for storage, access, and analytics.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements predefined tables and relationships under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing predefined tables and relationships under review is supervised execution of someone else's model -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs standard warehouse models independently for routine subject areas.
  — *Why this level:* Designing standard warehouse models independently for routine subject areas applies Kimball & Ross's established dimensional-modeling technique to a new subject area without inventing new structure -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models ambiguous domains autonomously, resolving hard normalization and historization trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling ambiguous domains autonomously and resolving hard normalization/historization trade-offs is Dreyfus's competent band; Kimball & Ross treat historization (slowly changing dimension) design as the recurring hard judgment call separating a working schema from a correct one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines modeling conventions and warehouse architecture others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining modeling conventions and warehouse architecture others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- moving from modeling one domain to authoring the conventions Kimball's own methodology calls the enterprise bus that other teams' models must conform to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise data-modeling strategy and anticipates shifts in storage paradigms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise data-modeling strategy and anticipating storage-paradigm shifts is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good warehouse modeling means industry-wide and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good warehouse modeling means industry-wide and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register Kimball & Ross's own toolkit occupies as an industry reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).

<a id="data-06"></a>
##### DATA-06 — Dimensional & analytics modeling

*Type:* Technical — Designs facts, dimensions, and analytical schemas that make data intuitive to query.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds facts and dimensions from supplied designs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Building facts and dimensions from supplied designs under review is supervised execution of someone else's dimensional design -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs standard star schemas independently for routine analytics needs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing standard star schemas independently for routine analytics needs applies Kimball & Ross's star-schema technique to a new mart without deviation -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models complex grains, slowly-changing dimensions, and conformance issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling complex grains, slowly-changing dimensions, and conformance issues autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band; grain and SCD-type selection are exactly the judgment calls Kimball & Ross document as separating textbook star schemas from production ones. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines dimensional modeling patterns and conformed-dimension standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining dimensional modeling patterns and conformed-dimension standards others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the conformed-dimension bus Kimball & Ross describe as the enterprise-wide integration layer, not just building one mart. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets dimensional strategy across analytics domains and anticipates modeling evolution.
  — *Why this level:* Setting dimensional strategy across analytics domains and anticipating modeling evolution is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for dimensional modeling and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for dimensional modeling and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-07"></a>
##### DATA-07 — Relational analytics & query design

*Type:* Technical — Composes set-based queries and joins to answer analytical questions over relational data.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes simple queries from clear requirements, with logic reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Writing simple queries from clear requirements with logic reviewed is supervised execution of a specified query -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Writes correct multi-join analytical queries independently for routine questions.
  — *Why this level:* Writing correct multi-join analytical queries independently for routine questions applies Codd's relational join/projection operations correctly and unsupervised for standard cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6), 377-387 (1970).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs complex queries handling tricky aggregations, window logic, and edge semantics autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing complex queries handling tricky aggregations, window logic, and edge-case semantics autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- full ownership of ambiguous set-based logic beyond the textbook relational operators. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines query patterns and reusable analytical building blocks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining query patterns and reusable analytical building blocks others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying query technique into shared building blocks rather than answering one question at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for analytical query design and anticipates shifts in query paradigms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for analytical query design and anticipating shifts in query paradigms is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for analytical querying across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for analytical querying across the discipline and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-08"></a>
##### DATA-08 — Query & storage optimization

*Type:* Technical — Tunes data layout, indexing, and query plans to balance speed, scale, and resource use.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies suggested indexes or partitions under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying suggested indexes or partitions under review is supervised execution of someone else's tuning decision -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tunes routine slow queries and storage layouts independently.
  — *Why this level:* Tuning routine slow queries and storage layouts independently applies documented indexing/partitioning technique -- the storage-engine trade-offs Kleppmann catalogs -- to a familiar bottleneck -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and resolves hard performance and storage-cost problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and resolving hard performance and storage-cost problems autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- reasoning through the storage-engine internals Kleppmann describes (B-trees, LSM-trees, query planning) rather than applying a known fix. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines optimization playbooks others adopt and solves pathological bottlenecks.
  — *Why this level:* Defining optimization playbooks others adopt and solving pathological bottlenecks is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying tuning judgment into a playbook rather than fixing one query at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets optimization strategy and anticipates emerging storage and execution techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting optimization strategy and anticipating emerging storage/execution techniques is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry standards for query and storage optimization and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry standards for query and storage optimization and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Data Quality & Governance

<a id="data-09"></a>
##### DATA-09 — Data quality & validation

*Type:* Technical — Defines and enforces checks for accuracy, completeness, and consistency across datasets.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs predefined quality checks and flags failures under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Running predefined quality checks and flagging failures under guidance is supervised execution of someone else's rule set -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard validation rules independently and triages common quality issues.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard validation rules independently and triaging common quality issues applies DAMA-DMBOK2's data-quality dimensions (completeness, accuracy, consistency) to routine checks without designing a new framework -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs comprehensive quality frameworks and resolves ambiguous root-cause cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing comprehensive quality frameworks and resolving ambiguous root-cause cases autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- full ownership of quality-framework design per DAMA-DMBOK2's quality-management function, not just rule execution. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines quality-checking patterns and severity frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining quality-checking patterns and severity frameworks others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying DAMA-DMBOK2's quality dimensions into a severity framework other teams reuse. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets data-quality strategy and anticipates evolving validation approaches.
