  — *Why this level:* Setting data-quality strategy and anticipating evolving validation approaches is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good data quality means industry-wide and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good data quality means industry-wide and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-10"></a>
##### DATA-10 — Data governance & lineage

*Type:* Technical — Tracks data origins, ownership, and movement to ensure trust, compliance, and traceability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records lineage and metadata into provided systems under review.
  — *Why this level:* Recording lineage and metadata into provided systems under review is supervised data entry against someone else's governance model -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Maintains governance documentation and lineage for routine assets independently.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining governance documentation and lineage for routine assets independently applies DAMA-DMBOK2's data-governance function to standard assets without designing the governance model -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Establishes governance and lineage for complex, cross-team data flows autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing governance and lineage for complex, cross-team data flows autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- owning governance design across boundaries the documented model doesn't already cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines governance frameworks and lineage standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining governance frameworks and lineage standards others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the DAMA-DMBOK2-aligned framework other teams' governance work must conform to, not applying one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise governance strategy and anticipates regulatory and stewardship shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise governance strategy and anticipating regulatory/stewardship shifts is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for data governance and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for data governance and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-11"></a>
##### DATA-11 — Master & reference data management

*Type:* Technical — Maintains consistent, authoritative definitions of core business entities across systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains reference lists and match rules under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining reference lists and match rules under guidance is supervised upkeep of someone else's mastering rules -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard master and reference data independently with routine deduplication.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard master and reference data independently with routine deduplication applies DAMA-DMBOK2's master-data-management practices to routine matching -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves hard entity-matching, survivorship, and hierarchy conflicts autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving hard entity-matching, survivorship, and hierarchy conflicts autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- survivorship and hierarchy conflict resolution are exactly the judgment calls DAMA-DMBOK2's MDM function reserves for experienced stewardship, not rule automation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines mastering and stewardship patterns others adopt across domains.
  — *Why this level:* Defining mastering and stewardship patterns others adopt across domains is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying matching/survivorship logic into reusable patterns rather than resolving one entity conflict at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets master-data strategy and anticipates evolving entity-resolution approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Setting master-data strategy and anticipating evolving entity-resolution approaches is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for master data management and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for master data management and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-12"></a>
##### DATA-12 — Data privacy & access stewardship

*Type:* Behavioral — Safeguards sensitive data through appropriate classification, access, and retention practices.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies predefined access and masking rules under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying predefined access and masking rules under review is supervised execution of someone else's control set -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard privacy controls and access grants independently.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing standard privacy controls and access grants independently applies documented GDPR-aligned access/masking controls (Article 25's data protection by design) to routine grants -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) (2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs access and privacy schemes for ambiguous, sensitive cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing access and privacy schemes for ambiguous, sensitive cases autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- GDPR's risk-based, case-specific proportionality requirement (Article 32) is exactly what turns a checklist into a scheme requiring independent judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) (2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines privacy and access-control patterns others adopt across the data estate.
  — *Why this level:* Defining privacy and access-control patterns others adopt across the data estate is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying GDPR-compliant control patterns into estate-wide standards rather than designing one scheme at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) (2016); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets privacy and stewardship strategy and anticipates regulatory and risk shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting privacy and stewardship strategy and anticipating regulatory/risk shifts is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6, tracking how regulation itself is shifting. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) (2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry standards for data privacy stewardship and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry standards for data privacy stewardship and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Analytics & Insight

<a id="data-13"></a>
##### DATA-13 — Exploratory data analysis

*Type:* Technical — Profiles and explores data to surface patterns, anomalies, and analytical opportunities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Profiles datasets and produces basic summaries under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Profiling datasets and producing basic summaries under guidance is supervised execution of a defined summary task -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Explores routine datasets independently, surfacing distributions and obvious anomalies.
  — *Why this level:* Exploring routine datasets independently, surfacing distributions and obvious anomalies, applies Tukey's standard exploratory techniques (stem-and-leaf, box plots, summary statistics) to a new dataset without inventing new technique -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Tukey, Exploratory Data Analysis (Addison-Wesley, 1977).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Uncovers non-obvious patterns and data issues in ambiguous datasets autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Uncovering non-obvious patterns and data issues in ambiguous datasets autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band; Tukey framed exploratory analysis as detective work with no fixed procedure -- the unscripted, self-directed inquiry that separates competent from advanced-beginner use of his own techniques. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Tukey, Exploratory Data Analysis (Addison-Wesley, 1977).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines exploration approaches others adopt and frames what questions data can answer.
  — *Why this level:* Defining exploration approaches others adopt and framing what questions data can answer is Dreyfus's proficient band -- moving from applying Tukey's toolkit to authoring the exploration approach a team standardizes on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Tukey, Exploratory Data Analysis (Addison-Wesley, 1977).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for rigorous exploration and anticipates new analytical techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for rigorous exploration and anticipating new analytical techniques is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for exploratory analysis across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for exploratory analysis across the discipline and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register Tukey's own founding text occupies. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Tukey, Exploratory Data Analysis (Addison-Wesley, 1977).

<a id="data-14"></a>
##### DATA-14 — Statistical inference & hypothesis testing

*Type:* Technical — Draws defensible conclusions from data using probability and significance testing.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs prescribed tests and reports outputs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Running prescribed tests and reporting outputs under review is supervised execution of a specified test -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects and applies standard tests independently for routine questions.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting and applying standard tests independently for routine questions applies Casella & Berger's standard inferential procedures (t-tests, confidence intervals) to textbook-assumption cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Casella & Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd Edition (Duxbury Press, 2002).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs sound inference for tricky, assumption-violating cases autonomously and interprets correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Designing sound inference for tricky, assumption-violating cases autonomously and interpreting correctly is Dreyfus's competent band; Casella & Berger devote their advanced chapters precisely to what happens when standard-test assumptions fail, which is the judgment this level requires. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Casella & Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd Edition (Duxbury Press, 2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines inferential methods others adopt and corrects subtle statistical misuse.
  — *Why this level:* Defining inferential methods others adopt and correcting subtle statistical misuse is Dreyfus's proficient band -- teaching and correcting others' application of inference, not just performing it correctly oneself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Casella & Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd Edition (Duxbury Press, 2002).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for statistical rigor and anticipates methodological advances.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for statistical rigor and anticipating methodological advances is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for applied inference and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for applied inference and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-15"></a>
##### DATA-15 — Metric definition & semantic layers

*Type:* Technical — Defines consistent, reusable business metrics and the shared semantics behind them.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements metric definitions as specified under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing metric definitions as specified under review is supervised execution of someone else's metric spec -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Defines and documents standard metrics independently with consistent logic.
  — *Why this level:* Defining and documenting standard metrics independently with consistent logic applies Reis & Housley's serving-layer/semantic-layer pattern to a new metric without redesigning the model -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous or conflicting metric definitions and edge semantics autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous or conflicting metric definitions and edge semantics autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- owning the judgment calls Reis & Housley flag as the recurring failure mode of ungoverned metrics: multiple teams computing the same number differently. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines semantic-layer patterns and metric governance others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining semantic-layer patterns and metric governance others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the semantic-layer governance Reis & Housley describe as a lifecycle-wide serving concern, not defining one metric. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reis & Housley, Fundamentals of Data Engineering: Plan and Build Robust Data Systems (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets metric and semantic strategy and anticipates shifts in measurement practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting metric and semantic strategy and anticipating shifts in measurement practice is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for metric and semantic design and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for metric and semantic design and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-16"></a>
##### DATA-16 — Data wrangling & transformation

*Type:* Technical — Cleans, reshapes, and enriches raw data into analysis-ready datasets.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies prescribed cleaning and reshaping steps under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying prescribed cleaning and reshaping steps under review is supervised execution of a specified transform -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Transforms and cleans routine messy data independently.
  — *Why this level:* Transforming and cleaning routine messy data independently applies Wickham's tidy-data structure (each variable a column, each observation a row) to a standard dataset without inventing new reshaping logic -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wickham, Tidy Data, Journal of Statistical Software 59(10), 1-23 (2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Wrangles severely malformed or complex data into reliable shape autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Wrangling severely malformed or complex data into reliable shape autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- the cases Wickham's tidy-data framework doesn't resolve out of the box (irregular nesting, inconsistent encodings) that the practitioner must independently reshape. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wickham, Tidy Data, Journal of Statistical Software 59(10), 1-23 (2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines transformation patterns and reusable cleaning logic others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining transformation patterns and reusable cleaning logic others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying wrangling technique into shared logic rather than cleaning one dataset at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for transformation rigor and anticipates evolving wrangling techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for transformation rigor and anticipating evolving wrangling techniques is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry best practice for data transformation and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry best practice for data transformation and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register Wickham's own tidy-data paper occupies as a widely adopted standard. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wickham, Tidy Data, Journal of Statistical Software 59(10), 1-23 (2014).

#### Decision Support & Reporting

<a id="data-17"></a>
##### DATA-17 — Data visualization & storytelling

*Type:* Behavioral — Turns analysis into clear visuals and narratives that drive understanding and action.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Produces standard charts from given data and specs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Producing standard charts from given data and specs under review is supervised execution of a specified chart -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Creates clear, correct visuals independently for routine reporting needs.
  — *Why this level:* Creating clear, correct visuals independently for routine reporting needs applies Tufte's basic graphical-integrity principles (accurate axes, appropriate chart-to-data-type mapping) to a standard report -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (Graphics Press, 1983).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs compelling narratives that drive decisions for ambiguous audiences autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing compelling narratives that drive decisions for ambiguous audiences autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band; Knaflic's audience-and-context-first method for building a narrative around a specific decision is exactly the judgment layer above Tufte's graphical-integrity baseline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nussbaumer Knaflic, Storytelling with Data: A Data Visualization Guide for Business Professionals (Wiley, 2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines visualization patterns and storytelling standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining visualization patterns and storytelling standards others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the storytelling standard other analysts follow, not just telling one story well. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nussbaumer Knaflic, Storytelling with Data: A Data Visualization Guide for Business Professionals (Wiley, 2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's data-storytelling approach and anticipates shifts in communication norms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's data-storytelling approach and anticipating shifts in communication norms is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good data storytelling means industry-wide and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good data storytelling means industry-wide and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register Tufte's own founding text occupies. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Tufte, The Visual Display of Quantitative Information (Graphics Press, 1983).

<a id="data-18"></a>
##### DATA-18 — Dashboard & self-service reporting design

*Type:* Technical — Builds reusable dashboards and reports that let stakeholders explore data independently.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds dashboard components from provided requirements under review.
  — *Why this level:* Building dashboard components from provided requirements under review is supervised execution of a specified component -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs functional dashboards and self-service views independently for routine needs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing functional dashboards and self-service views independently for routine needs applies Few's dashboard-design principles (single-screen, at-a-glance layout) to a standard use case -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Few, Information Dashboard Design: The Effective Visual Communication of Data (O'Reilly, 2006).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs intuitive, performant self-service experiences for ambiguous user needs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing intuitive, performant self-service experiences for ambiguous user needs autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band -- resolving the layout/performance/usability trade-offs Few treats as dashboard-specific design judgment, for users whose needs aren't already documented. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Few, Information Dashboard Design: The Effective Visual Communication of Data (O'Reilly, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines dashboard and self-service design patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining dashboard and self-service design patterns others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying Few's design principles into a reusable pattern library rather than designing one dashboard. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Few, Information Dashboard Design: The Effective Visual Communication of Data (O'Reilly, 2006).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets self-service reporting strategy and anticipates shifts in analytics consumption.
  — *Why this level:* Setting self-service reporting strategy and anticipating shifts in analytics consumption is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for self-service reporting and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for self-service reporting and being externally credible is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-19"></a>
##### DATA-19 — Requirements gathering & stakeholder translation

*Type:* Behavioral — Elicits business questions and translates them into well-scoped analytical deliverables.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Captures stated requirements accurately under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Capturing stated requirements accurately under guidance is supervised elicitation against a defined ask -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Elicits and documents routine requirements independently, clarifying obvious gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Eliciting and documenting routine requirements independently, clarifying obvious gaps, applies BABOK's standard elicitation techniques to a routine ask -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Surfaces unstated needs and translates ambiguous asks into clear specs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Surfacing unstated needs and translating ambiguous asks into clear specs autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band; BABOK's elicitation-and-analysis knowledge area names exactly this -- moving from stated to underlying need -- as the core skill above basic requirements-capture. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines elicitation and translation approaches others adopt across teams.
  — *Why this level:* Defining elicitation and translation approaches others adopt across teams is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the BABOK-aligned elicitation approach other analysts standardize on, not eliciting one set of requirements. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for requirements practice and anticipates evolving stakeholder needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting standards for requirements practice and anticipating evolving stakeholder needs is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for stakeholder translation in analytics and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for stakeholder translation in analytics and being externally recognized is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="data-20"></a>
##### DATA-20 — Business & domain acumen

*Type:* Behavioral — Applies understanding of the business context to frame data work around real value.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Learns core domain concepts and applies them to tasks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Learning core domain concepts and applying them to tasks under guidance is supervised, guided domain learning -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies solid domain understanding to routine analytical work independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying solid domain understanding to routine analytical work independently uses BABOK's business-context and stakeholder-analysis concepts unsupervised on familiar work -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Connects data work to business outcomes and frames hard domain questions autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Connecting data work to business outcomes and framing hard domain questions autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band; BABOK's Value and Need core concepts (linking a solution back to business value) are exactly what this level operationalizes without guidance. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines how domain context shapes analytics approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how domain context shapes analytics approaches others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying domain judgment into an approach others follow, not applying it oneself. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets direction linking data capability to business strategy and anticipates domain shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting direction linking data capability to business strategy and anticipating domain shifts is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Recognized externally for shaping how the domain and data discipline intersect.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized externally for shaping how the domain and data discipline intersect is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- practice-shaping beyond the organization. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

### AI & ML Engineering (AI)

#### LLM Systems

<a id="ai-01"></a>
##### AI-01 — LLM Integration & Prompt Engineering

*Type:* Technical — Builds reliable features on top of language models.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands LLM basics (tokens, context windows, temperature, system prompts); calls model APIs correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Calling documented APIs correctly under review, without yet judging prompt design trade-offs, is Dreyfus's novice band: following supplied rules (token limits, parameter defaults) without weighing context. SFIA Level 2 Assist matches: supervised use of a defined tool. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Writes effective prompts; uses structured outputs, function calling and streaming; understands model differences and pricing.
  — *Why this level:* Applying the standard few-shot prompting technique Brown et al. demonstrated (in-context examples, structured completions) independently for routine tasks is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- recognized prompt patterns matched to known situations, not yet designed from first principles. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, NeurIPS 2020.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Expert prompt/context design (few-shot, decomposition, chaining); knows when fine-tuning beats prompting (rarely); designs for model swappability.
  — *Why this level:* Decomposing a problem into intermediate reasoning steps and chaining prompts autonomously is the deliberate chain-of-thought practice Wei et al. show is not automatic below a capability threshold -- applying it unaided for ambiguous problems is Dreyfus's competent band, the go-to for prompt design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wei et al., Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models, NeurIPS 2022.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Mastery of model behavior across providers and versions; designs upgrade-migration strategies; squeezes capability others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining migration strategies across model providers and versions requires the cross-model behavioral fluency Bommasani et al. describe as the differentiator once practice moves beyond a single foundation model; codifying that fluency into patterns others adopt is SFIA's higher responsibility band of setting technical direction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bommasani et al., On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models, Stanford CRFM (2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Deep expertise; anticipates capability shifts (new modalities, reasoning models) and repositions ahead of them.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating shifts such as new modalities or reasoning models before they land in production is the "opportunities and risks ahead of deployment" framing Bommasani et al. establish for foundation-model strategy; SFIA's authority band grounds this as org-wide, not team-local, foresight. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bommasani et al., On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models, Stanford CRFM (2021).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Authority on applied LLM engineering; may influence industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider industry applies LLMs -- beyond any one org -- is the Dreyfus master band and SFIA's highest responsibility level, where the individual's own practice becomes a reference point others (including foundation-model researchers like Bommasani et al.) cite. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bommasani et al., On the Opportunities and Risks of Foundation Models, Stanford CRFM (2021).

<a id="ai-02"></a>
##### AI-02 — Context & Retrieval Engineering

*Type:* Technical — Grounds models in the right knowledge.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands embeddings, similarity search and why grounding reduces hallucination.
  — *Why this level:* Grasping why retrieval grounds generation -- without yet building a pipeline -- is Dreyfus's novice band: conceptual understanding of a supplied rationale, work reviewed before it is applied. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard RAG pipelines (chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking); manages context budgets deliberately.
  — *Why this level:* Building the chunk-embed-retrieve-generate pipeline Lewis et al. defined, independently and for routine cases, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- applying a named architecture as given rather than adapting it to novel constraints. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lewis et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, NeurIPS 2020.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs retrieval quality systems (hybrid search, reranking, freshness, citation, memory for multi-turn).
  — *Why this level:* Combining hybrid search, reranking and freshness handling autonomously for ambiguous retrieval needs is the competent-level synthesis Gao et al.'s survey identifies as the layer of RAG practice built atop the base Lewis et al. recipe, not covered by any single fixed pipeline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gao et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in retrieval at scale (index strategy, multi-source federation, permission-aware retrieval).
  — *Why this level:* Designing index strategy for retrieval at scale is the problem Johnson et al.'s billion-scale similarity search work exists to solve; defining that index architecture as a pattern others reuse across sources is SFIA's expert band of setting direction beyond one's own pipeline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Johnson, Douze & Jegou, Billion-Scale Similarity Search with GPUs, IEEE Transactions on Big Data (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Deep expertise; anticipates how longer context and new architectures change retrieval economics.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating how longer context windows shift the cost/benefit of retrieval versus stuffing context is a forward-looking judgment the RAG survey literature (Gao et al.) frames as an open, evolving trade-off -- SFIA's authority band is the org-wide anticipation of that shift, not merely reacting to it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gao et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Mastery of the discipline; defines how AI systems access knowledge.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how AI systems access knowledge industry-wide is the master/pioneer band in Dreyfus's model and SFIA's top responsibility level -- the individual's retrieval architecture choices, informed by foundational work like Lewis et al. and Johnson et al., become the reference others build on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-03"></a>
##### AI-03 — Agentic Systems & Orchestration

*Type:* Technical — Designs systems where models plan and act through tools.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands tool calling and the agent loop (plan, act, observe); knows why agents need constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Understanding the plan-act-observe loop that Yao et al.'s ReAct formalized, without yet building it, is Dreyfus's novice band -- conceptual grasp of a supplied structure under review. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models, ICLR 2023.
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs good tool interfaces; builds single-agent workflows with sensible termination and confirmation points.
  — *Why this level:* Building a single-agent ReAct-style loop independently for routine workflows, with standard termination conditions, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- applying the named reasoning-acting pattern to recognized situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models, ICLR 2023.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reliable multi-step agents (state, recovery, sandboxing, permissions, human-in-the-loop); knows when an agent is the wrong answer.
  — *Why this level:* Handling state, recovery and permissioning for ambiguous multi-step tasks autonomously -- and judging when an agent is the wrong tool -- is the competent band's ownership of a non-routine design space that single-agent ReAct loops do not resolve on their own. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wu et al., AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in complex orchestration (multi-agent, long-running workflows, MCP-style standards) and safe constraint at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Operating multi-agent conversation frameworks like AutoGen and adopting interoperability standards such as Anthropic's Model Context Protocol is defining the emerging orchestration patterns SFIA's higher responsibility bands describe as setting technical direction others follow, not merely using a single agent. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wu et al., AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation (2023); Anthropic, Model Context Protocol Specification (2025-11-25).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Deep expertise; anticipates how increasing model autonomy changes system design.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating how rising model autonomy reshapes system design -- ahead of standards like MCP being widely adopted -- is SFIA's authority band: org-wide anticipation of direction, grounded in the same autonomy-safety tension the ReAct line of work was built to manage. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models, ICLR 2023.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Authority on agentic systems; may influence emerging industry standards.
  — *Why this level:* Influencing emerging industry standards for agentic systems -- the kind of protocol work MCP represents -- is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA's top responsibility level: shaping the discipline rather than applying its current state of the art. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Anthropic, Model Context Protocol Specification (2025-11-25).

#### AI Quality & Safety

<a id="ai-04"></a>
##### AI-04 — AI Evaluation

*Type:* Technical — Proves AI behavior is good enough to ship.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands why 'it looked right in testing' is insufficient; runs existing evals and labels carefully.
  — *Why this level:* Executing an existing eval suite carefully under review, without yet designing one, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct execution of a supplied procedure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds basic eval sets from real usage; measures changes before shipping prompt/model updates.
  — *Why this level:* Building a basic eval set from real usage and measuring changes independently is the advanced-beginner application of a recognized practice -- routine before/after measurement -- not yet the systematic, multi-metric methodology HELM demonstrates. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Liang et al., Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM), Stanford CRFM (2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs eval methodology (golden sets, LLM-as-judge with validation, human review, helpfulness/groundedness/safety metrics).
  — *Why this level:* Designing LLM-as-judge evaluation with validation against human review is precisely the calibration problem Zheng et al. solved (showing GPT-4 judgments reach human-level agreement only once validated); doing this autonomously for a golden-set methodology is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zheng et al., Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, NeurIPS 2023.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in eval at scale (continuous eval, A/B testing AI features, drift detection).
  — *Why this level:* Running continuous, multi-scenario evaluation at scale is the taxonomize-and-measure-everywhere approach HELM operationalized across dozens of models and metrics; codifying that as the org's standard eval infrastructure is SFIA's expert band of defining patterns others adopt. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Liang et al., Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM), Stanford CRFM (2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Deep expertise in measuring AI quality where ground truth is contested.
  — *Why this level:* Measuring quality where ground truth is contested -- the exact problem LLM-as-judge exists to approximate, per Zheng et al.'s finding that even strong judges carry position and verbosity biases -- is the authority-level judgment SFIA places above routine methodology application: recognizing and correcting for the judge's own limits. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Zheng et al., Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, NeurIPS 2023.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Mastery of the discipline; sets the bar for what 'proven to work' means.
  — *Why this level:* Setting industry-wide standards for what "proven to work" means in AI evaluation is the master/pioneer band -- the individual's methodology, building on foundational holistic-evaluation work like HELM, becomes the reference the field cites. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Liang et al., Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM), Stanford CRFM (2022).

<a id="ai-05"></a>
##### AI-05 — Responsible AI & Guardrails

*Type:* Technical — Keeps AI behavior safe, honest and within bounds.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands that models can be harmful, biased or confidently wrong; flags concerning behavior.
  — *Why this level:* Recognizing and flagging concerning model behavior against known risk categories -- without yet implementing controls -- is Dreyfus's novice band, matching OWASP's own framing of its Top 10 as an awareness document for practitioners new to LLM-specific risks. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications (2025).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements guardrails (filtering, refusal handling, grounding checks); designs honest UX.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing filtering and refusal handling against the named risk categories in the OWASP LLM Top 10 independently, for routine cases, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- applying documented mitigations to recognized threats. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications (2025).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs layered safety proportional to stakes; evaluates for bias/misuse before launch.
  — *Why this level:* Designing layered, stakes-proportional safety autonomously is the MAP/MEASURE discipline NIST's AI RMF defines as contextualizing risk to the specific system rather than applying a fixed checklist; doing this unaided for ambiguous, high-stakes launches is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1 (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in safety system design at scale; defines oversight and escalation frameworks.
  — *Why this level:* Defining oversight and escalation frameworks that others adopt is the GOVERN function NIST's AI RMF places above system-level MEASURE/MANAGE activity; codifying self-critique-and-revision techniques like those Bai et al. describe as reusable safety infrastructure is SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1 (2023); Bai et al., Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback, Anthropic (2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Deep expertise balancing capability and safety under real product pressure.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing capability against safety under real product pressure, across many teams, is SFIA's authority band applied to the GOVERN function of the NIST AI RMF -- setting org-wide policy trade-offs rather than a single system's controls. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1 (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Recognized authority; establishes responsible AI as a value; externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing responsible AI as a value recognized outside one's own org is the master/pioneer band -- externally credible practice that itself shapes documents like NIST's AI RMF and the OWASP Top 10 rather than merely applying them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Data Preparation for ML

<a id="ai-06"></a>
##### AI-06 — Feature engineering

*Type:* Technical — Transforms raw data into informative features that improve model learning and performance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements specified features and transformations under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing specified transformations under review, without choosing which features to build, is Dreyfus's novice band -- following a supplied specification. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Engineers standard features independently for routine modeling tasks.
  — *Why this level:* Applying the standard transformation techniques (binning, scaling, encoding) Zheng & Casari catalog independently for routine tasks is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- known techniques matched to recognized data types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zheng & Casari, Feature Engineering for Machine Learning: Principles and Techniques for Data Scientists (O'Reilly, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Derives high-signal features for ambiguous problems and avoids leakage autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Avoiding leakage autonomously in ambiguous cases is exactly the training/serving-skew failure mode Zinkevich's Rules of ML names as a recurring, hard-to-spot production bug; catching it unaided for novel problems is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zinkevich, Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering, Google (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines feature-engineering patterns and leakage-prevention standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leakage-prevention standards that other teams adopt is codifying the practice Zinkevich's rules describe at the level of an org-wide checklist rather than one engineer's vigilance -- SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Zinkevich, Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering, Google (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets feature strategy and anticipates advances in representation techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating advances in representation techniques (e.g., learned embeddings displacing hand-built features) ahead of the org needing them is SFIA's authority band -- strategic foresight beyond any single pipeline's feature set, extending the domain Zheng & Casari catalog. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Zheng & Casari, Feature Engineering for Machine Learning: Principles and Techniques for Data Scientists (O'Reilly, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for feature engineering across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized for defining best practice is the master/pioneer band -- the individual's work becomes a reference alongside catalogs like Zheng & Casari and practice guides like Zinkevich's rules, not merely a consumer of them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-07"></a>
##### AI-07 — Data labeling & dataset curation

*Type:* Technical — Assembles, labels, and curates representative datasets suitable for model training.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Labels data to clear guidelines and flags ambiguities under review.
  — *Why this level:* Labeling to clear guidelines and flagging ambiguities under review, without authoring the guidelines, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct execution of a supplied rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Curates and labels routine datasets independently, applying consistent guidelines.
  — *Why this level:* Applying labeling guidelines consistently and independently for routine datasets is the advanced-beginner band; it does not yet address the systemic data-quality risks Sambasivan et al. found in 92% of high-stakes AI projects, which require designing the guidelines rather than following them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sambasivan et al., "Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work": Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI, CHI 2021.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs labeling schemes and resolves ambiguity and quality issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a labeling scheme and resolving quality issues autonomously is the documentation-and-provenance discipline Gebru et al.'s Datasheets for Datasets formalizes (motivation, collection process, recommended uses); doing this unaided for ambiguous cases is Dreyfus's competent band, directly preventing the data cascades Sambasivan et al. document. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gebru et al., Datasheets for Datasets, Communications of the ACM 64(12), 86-92 (2021); Sambasivan et al., "Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work": Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI, CHI 2021.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines curation and annotation-quality standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining annotation-quality standards other teams adopt is institutionalizing the datasheet practice Gebru et al. propose as a norm, not a one-off document; SFIA's expert band names this as setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gebru et al., Datasheets for Datasets, Communications of the ACM 64(12), 86-92 (2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets dataset strategy and anticipates shifts in labeling and curation practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide dataset strategy and anticipating shifts in curation practice is SFIA's authority band -- addressing the root causes of data cascades (Sambasivan et al.) at a strategic level rather than per-project mitigation. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sambasivan et al., "Everyone wants to do the model work, not the data work": Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI, CHI 2021.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry best practice for dataset curation and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible for defining industry best practice in dataset curation is the master/pioneer band -- work that extends foundational documentation frameworks like Gebru et al.'s datasheets into the field's reference standard. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-08"></a>
##### AI-08 — Feature stores & reuse

*Type:* Technical — Manages consistent, shareable feature definitions across training and serving.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Registers and retrieves features from a feature store under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Registering and retrieving features from an existing store under guidance, without designing the store, is Dreyfus's novice band -- operating a supplied system. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Publishes and consumes reusable features independently for routine use.
  — *Why this level:* Publishing and consuming reusable features independently is applying the shared-feature-registry pattern Hermann & Del Balso describe as Michelangelo's core value proposition, for routine, already-modeled use cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hermann & Del Balso, Meet Michelangelo: Uber's Machine Learning Platform, Uber Engineering Blog (2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs feature definitions ensuring consistency and freshness across uses autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Ensuring training/serving consistency and freshness autonomously is the exact cross-team correctness problem Hermann & Del Balso built Michelangelo's feature store to solve; doing this unaided for a new, ambiguous use case is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hermann & Del Balso, Meet Michelangelo: Uber's Machine Learning Platform, Uber Engineering Blog (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines feature-store patterns and reuse governance others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining feature-store governance patterns other teams adopt is platform-level work of the kind Hermann & Del Balso describe scaling Michelangelo across all of Uber's ML teams; SFIA's expert band names this as setting direction others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hermann & Del Balso, Meet Michelangelo: Uber's Machine Learning Platform, Uber Engineering Blog (2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets feature-reuse strategy and anticipates shifts in feature management.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide feature-reuse strategy and anticipating shifts in feature management (e.g., toward real-time or embedding-based features) is SFIA's authority band -- strategic direction beyond any single platform's roadmap. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for feature reuse across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized for defining feature-reuse best practice across the discipline is the master/pioneer band -- the kind of influence the Michelangelo platform itself had industry-wide once its design was published. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hermann & Del Balso, Meet Michelangelo: Uber's Machine Learning Platform, Uber Engineering Blog (2017).

#### Modeling & Training

<a id="ai-09"></a>
##### AI-09 — Classical model training & selection

*Type:* Technical — Trains and compares supervised and unsupervised models to fit the problem at hand.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Trains models with given settings and reports metrics under review.
  — *Why this level:* Training a model with given settings and reporting metrics under review, without choosing the model family, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Trains and selects standard models independently for routine problems.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting among the standard supervised/unsupervised model families Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman catalog, independently for routine problems, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- matching a known technique to a recognized problem shape. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition (Springer, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Chooses and trains appropriate models for ambiguous problems and avoids overfitting autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Avoiding overfitting autonomously for ambiguous problems is the bias-variance trade-off Hastie et al. treat as the central, non-mechanical judgment call in model selection; making that judgment unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition (Springer, 2009).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines model-selection approaches others adopt and solves intractable modeling cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining model-selection approaches other teams adopt, and resolving cases where standard bias-variance reasoning from Hastie et al. breaks down, is SFIA's expert band of setting an approach others follow rather than applying an existing one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition (Springer, 2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets modeling strategy and anticipates shifts in classical technique relevance.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating when classical techniques remain the right choice versus being displaced by newer methods is SFIA's authority-band strategic judgment, applied to the trade-off space Hastie et al. formalize. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition (Springer, 2009).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for model selection across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized for defining model-selection best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing to the same body of reference work Hastie et al. represent, not merely applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-10"></a>
##### AI-10 — Deep learning & neural architectures

*Type:* Technical — Designs and trains neural networks for complex perception, sequence, and representation tasks.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Trains predefined network architectures under review.
  — *Why this level:* Training a predefined architecture under review, without designing it, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Adapts standard architectures independently for routine tasks.
  — *Why this level:* Adapting the standard architecture families Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville catalog (CNNs, RNNs, feedforward nets) independently for routine tasks is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- applying known architectural patterns to recognized problem types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville, Deep Learning (MIT Press, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs and debugs architectures for hard problems and convergence issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Debugging convergence issues autonomously for hard problems is the deep, non-formulaic optimization judgment Goodfellow et al. treat as the difficult part of training deep networks; resolving it unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville, Deep Learning (MIT Press, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines architectural patterns others adopt and solves problems others cannot.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a new architectural pattern others adopt across the field is the kind of contribution Vaswani et al.'s transformer made -- a named design others build on, not an adaptation of an existing one -- which is SFIA's expert band of setting direction others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, NeurIPS 2017.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets neural-architecture strategy and anticipates emerging model designs.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating emerging model designs before they're established (the way attention-based architectures were anticipated before displacing recurrence, per Vaswani et al.) is SFIA's authority band -- org-wide strategic foresight, not one project's design choice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, NeurIPS 2017.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for neural architecture and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping industry practice for neural architecture -- the influence Vaswani et al.'s transformer paper itself had -- is the master/pioneer band: defining the discipline rather than working within it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need, NeurIPS 2017.

<a id="ai-11"></a>
##### AI-11 — Hyperparameter tuning & optimization

*Type:* Technical — Systematically searches model configurations to maximize performance and generalization.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs prescribed tuning sweeps and reports results under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Running a prescribed sweep and reporting results under guidance, without designing the search strategy, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tunes standard hyperparameters independently for routine models.
  — *Why this level:* Running the standard grid- or random-search sweeps Bergstra & Bengio benchmark, independently for routine models, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- applying a known search method to a recognized tuning problem. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bergstra & Bengio, Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization, Journal of Machine Learning Research 13, 281-305 (2012).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs efficient search strategies for hard, high-dimensional spaces autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing an efficient search strategy for a hard, high-dimensional space autonomously is the problem Snoek et al.'s Bayesian optimization approach was built to solve, beyond what random search reliably handles; doing this unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Snoek, Larochelle & Adams, Practical Bayesian Optimization of Machine Learning Algorithms, NeurIPS 2012.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines tuning methodologies others adopt and solves stubborn optimization cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a tuning methodology other teams adopt, and resolving optimization cases where standard Bayesian or random search struggles, is SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Snoek, Larochelle & Adams, Practical Bayesian Optimization of Machine Learning Algorithms, NeurIPS 2012.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets optimization strategy and anticipates advances in search techniques.
