  — *Why this level:* Anticipating advances in search techniques -- as Bayesian optimization itself displaced grid search, per Bergstra & Bengio's and Snoek et al.'s findings -- ahead of the org needing them is SFIA's authority band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bergstra & Bengio, Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization, Journal of Machine Learning Research 13, 281-305 (2012).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for hyperparameter optimization and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized for defining hyperparameter-optimization best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing methods at the level Bergstra & Bengio and Snoek et al. did, not applying theirs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-12"></a>
##### AI-12 — Mathematical & statistical foundations

*Type:* Technical — Applies linear algebra, calculus, and probability to reason about model behavior.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies basic mathematical and statistical concepts to tasks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Applying basic, supplied mathematical concepts under guidance, without independently choosing which tool fits a problem, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies foundational math and statistics correctly to routine modeling independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying the standard linear-algebra machinery Strang's text covers (matrix decompositions, eigenvectors) correctly and independently for routine modeling is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- known tools matched to recognized problems. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Strang, Introduction to Linear Algebra, 5th Edition (Wellesley-Cambridge Press, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Reasons rigorously about hard mathematical and statistical aspects of problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Reasoning rigorously and autonomously about hard statistical aspects -- the hypothesis-testing and estimation theory Casella & Berger formalize -- for ambiguous problems is Dreyfus's competent band, applying graduate-level inference unaided. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Casella & Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd Edition (Duxbury Press, 2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines how foundational theory informs practice others adopt and corrects subtle errors.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how foundational theory of the kind Casella & Berger and Strang formalize informs team practice, and catching subtle statistical errors others miss, is SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Casella & Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd Edition (Duxbury Press, 2002).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets standards for mathematical rigor and anticipates relevant theoretical advances.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide standards for mathematical rigor and anticipating relevant theoretical advances is SFIA's authority band -- strategic stewardship of the foundational discipline rather than one team's correctness. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Casella & Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd Edition (Duxbury Press, 2002).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Recognized externally for advancing applied mathematical practice in the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* External recognition for advancing applied mathematical practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing new theory at the level of reference texts like Strang's or Casella & Berger's, not applying them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Evaluation & Experimentation

<a id="ai-13"></a>
##### AI-13 — Model evaluation & validation

*Type:* Technical — Assesses model accuracy, robustness, and generalization with sound validation methods.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Computes prescribed evaluation metrics under review.
  — *Why this level:* Computing a prescribed metric under review, without choosing the validation scheme, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects appropriate metrics and validation splits independently for routine cases.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting an appropriate cross-validation split independently for routine cases is applying Kohavi's well-established finding that ten-fold cross-validation is the right default for most model-selection problems -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, a known technique matched to a recognized situation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kohavi, A Study of Cross-Validation and Bootstrap for Accuracy Estimation and Model Selection, IJCAI 14, 1137-1145 (1995).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs sound evaluation for ambiguous, leakage-prone, or imbalanced cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing sound evaluation for leakage-prone or imbalanced cases autonomously goes beyond Kohavi's default cross-validation recommendation into the bias-variance-aware validation design Hastie et al. treat as a judgment call, not a fixed recipe; doing this unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition (Springer, 2009).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines evaluation methodologies and validation standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining validation standards other teams adopt -- codifying when Kohavi's cross-validation defaults do and don't apply -- is SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kohavi, A Study of Cross-Validation and Bootstrap for Accuracy Estimation and Model Selection, IJCAI 14, 1137-1145 (1995).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets evaluation strategy and anticipates advances in validation practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide evaluation strategy and anticipating advances in validation practice is SFIA's authority band, extending the estimation-theory foundations Hastie et al. and Kohavi established to new problem classes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning: Data Mining, Inference, and Prediction, 2nd Edition (Springer, 2009).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for model evaluation across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* External recognition for defining model-evaluation best practice is the master/pioneer band -- work that stands alongside foundational validation methodology like Kohavi's and Hastie et al.'s, not derived from applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-14"></a>
##### AI-14 — Experimentation & A/B testing (ML)

*Type:* Technical — Designs controlled experiments to measure real-world impact of models and changes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes designed experiments and reports outcomes under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Executing an experiment someone else designed, under guidance, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and runs standard experiments independently with correct basic analysis.
  — *Why this level:* Designing and running a standard controlled experiment independently, with correct basic statistical analysis, is applying the core online-controlled-experiment recipe Kohavi, Tang & Xu lay out for routine cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs rigorous experiments handling confounds and tricky readouts autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Handling confounds and tricky readouts (novelty effects, sample ratio mismatch, network interference) autonomously is exactly the set of pitfalls Kohavi, Tang & Xu devote their book to; resolving them unaided for ambiguous cases is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines experimentation frameworks and guardrails others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining experimentation frameworks and guardrail metrics other teams adopt is institutionalizing the trustworthy-experimentation practices Kohavi, Tang & Xu describe scaling across Microsoft, Google and LinkedIn; SFIA's expert band names this as setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets experimentation strategy and anticipates advances in causal and online testing.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating advances in causal and online testing methodology, ahead of the org needing them, is SFIA's authority band -- strategic direction for the experimentation platform, not one experiment's design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for ML experimentation and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* External credibility for defining ML experimentation best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing at the level Kohavi, Tang & Xu's reference text does, not applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-15"></a>
##### AI-15 — Bias, fairness & error analysis

*Type:* Behavioral — Investigates model errors and disparate outcomes to guide responsible improvement.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs prescribed bias and error checks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Running a prescribed fairness check under review, without choosing the fairness criterion, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Performs standard fairness and error analysis independently for routine models.
  — *Why this level:* Applying a standard fairness metric independently for a routine model is matching a recognized situation to one of the statistical fairness criteria Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan catalog -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, not yet weighing which criterion fits which context. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning: Limitations and Opportunities (MIT Press, 2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses subtle bias and failure modes in ambiguous cases and proposes remedies autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing subtle bias autonomously in ambiguous cases requires the impossibility-result literalness Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan formalize -- most fairness criteria conflict, so the choice of which to satisfy is a judgment call, not a lookup; making that call unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning: Limitations and Opportunities (MIT Press, 2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines fairness and error-analysis frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a fairness framework other teams adopt -- choosing and justifying which of Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan's criteria the org applies where -- is SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning: Limitations and Opportunities (MIT Press, 2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets fairness strategy and anticipates evolving ethical and regulatory expectations.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating evolving ethical and regulatory expectations around fairness, ahead of the org needing to respond, is SFIA's authority band -- strategic foresight beyond any one model's fairness audit. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning: Limitations and Opportunities (MIT Press, 2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes industry practice for fairness and error analysis and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized for shaping industry fairness practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing to the same body of foundational work Barocas, Hardt & Narayanan represent, not applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### ML Operations & Lifecycle

<a id="ai-16"></a>
##### AI-16 — ML pipeline & deployment (MLOps)

*Type:* Technical — Automates training, packaging, and deployment of models into reliable production services.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs predefined training and deployment steps under review.
  — *Why this level:* Running predefined pipeline steps under review, without designing the pipeline, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and deploys routine ML pipelines independently with normal automation.
  — *Why this level:* Building and deploying a routine pipeline independently, following the automation levels Kreuzberger et al. define (manual, automated training, full CI/CD), is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- a known architecture applied to a recognized case. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kreuzberger, Kuhl & Hirschl, Machine Learning Operations (MLOps): Overview, Definition, and Architecture, IEEE Access 11, 31866-31879 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reliable, reproducible deployment pipelines for hard cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing reliable, reproducible pipelines for hard cases autonomously means resolving the entanglement, hidden feedback loops and pipeline jungles Sculley et al. document as ML systems' distinctive technical debt; doing this unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sculley et al., Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems, NeurIPS 2015.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines MLOps patterns and deployment standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining MLOps patterns and deployment standards other teams adopt is operating at Kreuzberger et al.'s highest automation maturity level as an org-wide template; SFIA's expert band names this as setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kreuzberger, Kuhl & Hirschl, Machine Learning Operations (MLOps): Overview, Definition, and Architecture, IEEE Access 11, 31866-31879 (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets MLOps strategy and anticipates shifts in lifecycle automation.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide MLOps strategy and anticipating shifts in lifecycle automation is SFIA's authority band -- strategic direction for how the org avoids the systemic technical debt Sculley et al. describe, not one pipeline's design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sculley et al., Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems, NeurIPS 2015.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for ML operations across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* External recognition for defining ML-operations best practice across the discipline is the master/pioneer band -- contributing reference architecture at the level Kreuzberger et al.'s survey and Sculley et al.'s debt analysis represent. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-17"></a>
##### AI-17 — Model monitoring & drift detection

*Type:* Technical — Tracks live model quality and data drift to trigger retraining or rollback.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Watches configured monitors and reports alerts under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Watching a configured monitor and reporting alerts under guidance, without designing the monitor, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Sets up standard performance and drift monitoring independently.
  — *Why this level:* Setting up standard drift detection independently, using one of the established detection strategies Gama et al. survey (e.g., statistical process control on error rate), is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- a known technique applied to a recognized monitoring need. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gama et al., A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation, ACM Computing Surveys 46(4) (2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs monitoring that catches subtle drift and degradation autonomously and triages causes.
  — *Why this level:* Catching subtle drift and triaging its cause autonomously requires distinguishing the different drift types (sudden, gradual, recurring) Gama et al. categorize, each needing a different detection and adaptation strategy; doing this unaided for ambiguous cases is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gama et al., A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation, ACM Computing Surveys 46(4) (2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines monitoring and drift-detection patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining drift-detection patterns other teams adopt is codifying the adaptation strategies Gama et al. survey into an org-wide standard rather than one model's monitor; SFIA's expert band names this as setting direction others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gama et al., A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation, ACM Computing Surveys 46(4) (2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets monitoring strategy and anticipates advances in drift detection.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide monitoring strategy and anticipating advances in drift-detection technique is SFIA's authority band, extending the survey landscape Gama et al. establish to the org's evolving needs. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gama et al., A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation, ACM Computing Surveys 46(4) (2014).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for model monitoring and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* External credibility for defining model-monitoring best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing to the same body of reference work Gama et al.'s survey represents, not applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-18"></a>
##### AI-18 — Model & experiment versioning

*Type:* Technical — Tracks datasets, models, and experiments for reproducibility and auditability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records model and experiment versions per process under review.
  — *Why this level:* Recording versions per an existing process under review, without designing the versioning scheme, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard versioning of models, data, and experiments independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard versioning independently using a tracking system like the one Zaharia et al. describe (logging parameters, metrics, and artifacts per run) is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- a known tool applied to a recognized need. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zaharia et al., Accelerating the Machine Learning Lifecycle with MLflow, IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin 41(4), 39-45 (2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reproducible versioning across complex experiment lineages autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing reproducible versioning across complex lineages autonomously is solving the reproducibility challenge Zaharia et al. built MLflow specifically to address -- tracking not just a model but the full chain of data, code and parameters that produced it; doing this unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zaharia et al., Accelerating the Machine Learning Lifecycle with MLflow, IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin 41(4), 39-45 (2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines versioning and reproducibility standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reproducibility standards other teams adopt is institutionalizing the lineage-tracking practice Zaharia et al. describe as an org-wide requirement rather than one team's discipline; SFIA's expert band names this as setting the approach others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Zaharia et al., Accelerating the Machine Learning Lifecycle with MLflow, IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin 41(4), 39-45 (2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets versioning strategy and anticipates shifts in reproducibility practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide versioning strategy and anticipating shifts in reproducibility practice is SFIA's authority band -- strategic direction for the org's experiment-tracking infrastructure, not one project's lineage. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Zaharia et al., Accelerating the Machine Learning Lifecycle with MLflow, IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin 41(4), 39-45 (2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for model and experiment versioning and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* External recognition for defining versioning best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing reference infrastructure at the level Zaharia et al.'s MLflow work represents. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-19"></a>
##### AI-19 — Model serving & inference optimization

*Type:* Technical — Exposes models for low-latency, scalable inference across batch and real-time use.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Deploys models to a serving setup with given configs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Deploying to a serving setup with given configs under review, without tuning it, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Serves models independently and applies standard latency and throughput tuning.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard latency and throughput tuning (caching, batching) independently is using the techniques Crankshaw et al.'s Clipper system operationalized for routine serving needs -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Crankshaw et al., Clipper: A Low-Latency Online Prediction Serving System, NSDI 2017.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Optimizes serving for hard latency, scale, and cost constraints autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing serving for hard latency and cost constraints autonomously goes beyond Clipper's general-purpose caching/batching into the model-specific partitioning trade-offs Pope et al. analyze for large-scale inference; resolving these unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Pope et al., Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference (2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines serving and inference-optimization patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining serving patterns other teams adopt is codifying the partitioning and batching techniques Crankshaw et al. and Pope et al. describe into an org-wide serving architecture; SFIA's expert band names this as setting direction others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Pope et al., Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference (2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets serving strategy and anticipates advances in inference efficiency.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating advances in inference efficiency -- the kind of multi-dimensional partitioning frontier Pope et al. establish for large models -- ahead of the org needing them is SFIA's authority band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Pope et al., Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference (2022).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for model serving across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* External recognition for defining model-serving best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing reference systems at the level Crankshaw et al.'s Clipper and Pope et al.'s scaling work represent. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ai-20"></a>
##### AI-20 — Problem framing & ML solution design

*Type:* Behavioral — Translates ambiguous business problems into well-posed, feasible ML approaches.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Translates a clearly scoped problem into a defined ML task under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Translating an already-scoped problem into a defined ML task under guidance, without doing the scoping, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Frames routine problems as appropriate ML solutions independently.
  — *Why this level:* Framing a routine business problem as an ML task independently is applying the data-analytic-thinking process Provost & Fawcett formalize for recognized problem shapes -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Provost & Fawcett, Data Science for Business: What You Need to Know about Data Mining and Data-Analytic Thinking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Frames ambiguous business problems into sound ML or non-ML approaches autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Judging when an ML approach is or isn't warranted for an ambiguous business problem -- including recommending against ML -- is precisely Zinkevich's Rule #1 ("don't be afraid to launch without machine learning") applied autonomously; doing this unaided is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zinkevich, Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering, Google (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines solution-design patterns others adopt and reframes intractable problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining solution-design patterns other teams adopt, and reframing problems that resist standard framing, is SFIA's expert band of setting the approach others follow, extending the data-analytic-thinking framework Provost & Fawcett establish. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Provost & Fawcett, Data Science for Business: What You Need to Know about Data Mining and Data-Analytic Thinking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets ML solution strategy and anticipates where applicable techniques are heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide ML solution strategy and anticipating where applicable techniques are heading is SFIA's authority band -- strategic foresight beyond any single problem's framing. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Provost & Fawcett, Data Science for Business: What You Need to Know about Data Mining and Data-Analytic Thinking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for ML problem framing across the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* External recognition for defining ML problem-framing best practice is the master/pioneer band -- contributing to the same body of reference work Provost & Fawcett's text and Zinkevich's rules represent, not applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### AI Quality & Safety

<a id="ai-21"></a>
##### AI-21 — AI risk governance

*Type:* Behavioral — Assesses and governs the risk of AI systems through their lifecycle - classifying systems against recognized risk frameworks, converting findings into engineering requirements with owners, and keeping the evidence trail (evals, controls, incidents) audit-ready as systems and regulation change.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Completes the risk checklist for their change accurately - identifying who is affected if the model is wrong - and escalates anything the checklist doesn't cover.
  — *Why this level:* Completing a supplied risk checklist accurately and escalating gaps, without yet designing the checklist, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct execution of a predefined MAP-function artifact per NIST's AI RMF. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1 (2023).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Assesses a feature's failure impact before build (misuse, error harm, disparate performance across user groups) and documents mitigations and residual risk unprompted.
  — *Why this level:* Assessing failure impact and documenting residual risk unprompted, for a routine feature, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- independently applying the MAP/MEASURE steps of NIST's AI RMF to a recognized situation without redesigning the framework. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Classifies a domain against the applicable risk framework, keeps its evidence pack (evals, controls, incidents) audit-ready, converts findings into engineering requirements with owners, and flags when a product change alters the risk class.
  — *Why this level:* Classifying a system against a risk framework and keeping an audit-ready evidence pack autonomously maps directly onto the EU AI Act's risk-tiering scheme (minimal/limited/high/unacceptable) and NIST's MEASURE function; doing this unaided for an ambiguous, evolving domain is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act) (2024); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1 (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Operates a cross-team AI risk-review process - fast enough that teams use it honestly, rigorous enough to catch real issues - and builds governance tooling that makes compliance a byproduct of normal engineering.
  — *Why this level:* Operating a cross-team review process and building tooling that embeds compliance into normal engineering is the organizational-scale implementation ISO/IEC 42001 specifies for an AI management system; defining that process as the pattern other teams adopt is SFIA's expert band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO/IEC, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns an organization's AI governance program jointly with legal and risk functions, translating regulation into engineering requirements without freezing delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Owning a governance program that translates regulation such as the EU AI Act into engineering requirements, jointly with legal and risk functions, is SFIA's authority band applied to ISO/IEC 42001's top-level management-system ownership -- org-wide accountability, not a single domain's compliance. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act) (2024); ISO/IEC, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Information technology - Artificial intelligence - Management system (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Positions a company ahead of AI regulation; accountable to executives, boards, and regulators for where the risk lines are drawn.
  — *Why this level:* Being accountable to boards and regulators for where risk lines are drawn -- ahead of where regulation like the EU AI Act currently sits -- is the master/pioneer band: shaping how the discipline of AI governance itself develops, not just complying with its current state. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act) (2024).

### Systems, Infrastructure & Operations (OPS)

#### Infrastructure

<a id="ops-01"></a>
##### OPS-01 — Cloud & Infrastructure Engineering

*Type:* Technical — Engineers compute, network, storage and IaC.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Makes guided changes to existing infra; understands core cloud services.
  — *Why this level:* Guided modification of existing infrastructure with conceptual understanding of core services maps to Dreyfus's advanced-beginner stage, where rules are followed but situational judgment is not yet independent. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds and manages standard resources using IaC.
  — *Why this level:* Independent ownership of standard IaC-provisioned resources matches SFIA level 3 (autonomy within a defined area); AWS Well-Architected's Operational Excellence pillar frames this as the baseline of managing infrastructure as code without oversight. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Amazon Web Services, AWS Well-Architected Framework (AWS, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs infra for scale, cost and resilience across a domain.
  — *Why this level:* Designing across scale, cost and resilience is exactly the intersection of AWS Well-Architected's Reliability, Performance Efficiency and Cost Optimization pillars applied to a whole domain, the level at which the framework expects deliberate architectural trade-offs rather than resource-by-resource fixes. *Sources:* Amazon Web Services, AWS Well-Architected Framework (AWS, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in infra platforms used by many teams; owns major cost strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Owning a platform consumed by many teams is Team Topologies' platform-team pattern -- a team providing infrastructure as an internal product -- combined with SFIA level 5's expectation of accountability for a significant sphere of technical work. *Sources:* Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets org infrastructure direction.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide infrastructure direction corresponds to SFIA level 6, where the individual has authority over strategy and policy across the organization, beyond any single platform or domain. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Trusted with company-level platform bets; defines infra strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Company-level platform bets and strategy-setting sit at SFIA level 7, the top responsibility band reserved for individuals who shape organization-wide direction and are accountable for its long-term technical bets. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ops-02"></a>
##### OPS-02 — CI/CD & Delivery Engineering

*Type:* Technical — Builds the build, test, release and deploy pipeline.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses and makes guided fixes to existing pipelines.
  — *Why this level:* Fixing existing pipelines under guidance without yet designing the deployment pipeline itself is the advanced-beginner stage in Dreyfus's model, applied to Humble & Farley's deployment-pipeline discipline where the pipeline stages already exist and are being operated, not authored. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds and improves pipelines for their area.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and improving pipelines for one's own area is SFIA level 3 autonomy applied to Humble & Farley's pipeline-authoring practice -- the individual now owns pipeline construction, not just its use. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs deployment safety (progressive delivery, rollback) for a domain.
  — *Why this level:* Progressive delivery and rollback design are Continuous Delivery's core deployment-safety patterns; Accelerate's DORA research ties these practices to lower change-fail rate and faster MTTR, the empirical signature of proficient-level delivery engineering across a domain. *Sources:* Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in delivery engineering at scale; sets standards across teams.
  — *Why this level:* Setting delivery standards across teams while driving elite DORA metrics (deploy frequency, lead time) at scale is the empirical high-performer band in Accelerate, matched to SFIA level 5's cross-team standard-setting responsibility. *Sources:* Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Defines the org's delivery/release philosophy.
  — *Why this level:* Defining delivery/release philosophy for the whole organization is SFIA level 6 authority -- setting policy and strategy that other teams' standards must follow, beyond any single delivery domain. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances release engineering practice company-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing release engineering practice company-wide and shaping how the discipline itself evolves is SFIA level 7's field-shaping remit, the same band Accelerate's research places at the frontier that generates new DORA-class practice rather than adopting it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).

<a id="ops-03"></a>
##### OPS-03 — Distributed Systems

*Type:* Technical — Reasons about systems spanning many machines.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands the basics (timeouts, retries, idempotency) conceptually.
  — *Why this level:* Conceptual-only grasp of timeouts, retries and idempotency -- Release It!'s baseline stability vocabulary -- without yet applying it under real failure is Dreyfus's novice/advanced-beginner band, where rules are known but not yet exercised in context. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Correctly applies distributed patterns in scoped work.
  — *Why this level:* Correctly applying Release It!'s stability patterns (timeouts, retries, circuit breakers) within scoped work is SFIA level 3 autonomy: competent independent execution inside a bounded area, not yet system-wide design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs for distributed failure modes (consistency, partitioning, backpressure).
  — *Why this level:* Designing for consistency and partitioning trade-offs is a direct application of the CAP theorem (Gilbert & Lynch), and backpressure/replication design is Kleppmann's core reliable-system material -- proficiency here means reasoning from the formal trade-off space, not just applying individual patterns. *Sources:* Gilbert & Lynch, Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services, ACM SIGACT News 33(2), 51-59 (2002); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in distributed systems at scale; anticipates emergent failure.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating emergent failure across a large distributed system is Designing Data-Intensive Applications' expert-level concern with cascading failure and partial-failure interactions at scale, paired with SFIA level 5's expectation of technical authority over complex, high-consequence systems. *Sources:* Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Shapes how the org builds at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the whole organization builds distributed systems is SFIA level 6 authority over engineering strategy and standards, extending beyond any single system's design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Authority on distributed design; influences the field.
  — *Why this level:* Influencing the field of distributed design is the standard set by foundational contributions like Lamport's logical-clocks paper, which redefined how the discipline itself reasons about ordering and causality -- the field-shaping band SFIA level 7 reserves for its highest responsibility tier. *Sources:* Lamport, Time, Clocks, and the Ordering of Events in a Distributed System, Communications of the ACM 21(7), 558-565 (1978); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Operations

<a id="ops-04"></a>
##### OPS-04 — Reliability & Production Operations

*Type:* Technical — Keeps services healthy; designs for failure.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands SLOs and common failure modes; keeps components healthy with guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Understanding SLOs and failure modes without yet owning their design is the advanced-beginner stage applied to the SRE book's SLO discipline -- the vocabulary is known and used under supervision, not yet set independently. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds retries, timeouts and fallbacks; understands blast radius.
  — *Why this level:* Retries, timeouts, fallbacks and blast-radius awareness are Release It!'s named stability patterns for containing failure -- independent, correct application of them is exactly the practitioner band the book targets, one step past conceptual understanding. *Sources:* Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs for graceful degradation; defines SLOs; accountable for a domain's reliability.
  — *Why this level:* Defining SLOs and owning graceful degradation for a domain is the SRE book's core practice of an SRE accountable for a service's error budget -- the level where reliability engineering becomes a design discipline rather than a reactive one. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in resilience and capacity planning at scale; drives down incidents systemically.
  — *Why this level:* Capacity planning and systemic incident reduction at scale are the SRE book's toil-elimination and capacity-planning chapters, which explicitly target root-cause elimination across a fleet -- paired with SFIA level 5's expert-level accountability for a large technical area. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns org-level reliability; fixes risk in process and org design.
  — *Why this level:* Fixing reliability risk in process and org design, not just systems, is the SRE book's premise that reliability is an organizational property; doing this at org scope is SFIA level 6's authority over policy and structure. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Sets the company's reliability philosophy.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the company's reliability philosophy -- the values and trade-offs other teams inherit -- is SFIA level 7's top responsibility band, reserved for individuals who define organization-wide direction rather than execute within it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ops-05"></a>
##### OPS-05 — Observability & Instrumentation

*Type:* Technical — Makes system behavior visible.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands logs/metrics/traces; reads existing dashboards.
  — *Why this level:* Understanding the three pillars (logs, metrics, traces) and reading dashboards others built, without yet instrumenting anything, is the advanced-beginner stage applied to Sridharan's observability taxonomy -- consumption of signals, not production of them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sridharan, Distributed Systems Observability: A Guide to Building Robust Systems (O'Reilly, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Instruments their services; builds dashboards; tunes alerts to limit noise.
  — *Why this level:* Independently instrumenting one's own services and tuning alert noise is SFIA level 3 autonomy applied to Sridharan's instrumentation practice -- the individual now produces the signals, not just reads them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sridharan, Distributed Systems Observability: A Guide to Building Robust Systems (O'Reilly, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs observability for complex systems (end-to-end traces, quality signals, cost attribution).
  — *Why this level:* End-to-end tracing across a complex system and moving beyond raw signals to quality/cost attribution is the harder integration problem Sridharan identifies once logs, metrics and traces must work together -- the proficient band where observability becomes a designed system property. *Sources:* Sridharan, Distributed Systems Observability: A Guide to Building Robust Systems (O'Reilly, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in instrumentation trade-offs at scale, incl. privacy-safe logging.
  — *Why this level:* Trading off cardinality, cost and privacy in instrumentation at scale is the advanced concern Sridharan flags once naive full-fidelity logging breaks down, matched to SFIA level 5's expert accountability for a large, high-consequence technical area. *Sources:* Sridharan, Distributed Systems Observability: A Guide to Building Robust Systems (O'Reilly, 2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Defines org observability strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Defining observability strategy for the whole org -- standards, tooling, budget -- is SFIA level 6 policy-setting authority, beyond instrumenting or designing observability for any one system. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes company-wide operational visibility; advances practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping company-wide operational visibility and advancing the practice itself is SFIA level 7's field-shaping remit, the band reserved for individuals whose work changes how the whole organization -- not just their team -- sees its systems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ops-06"></a>
##### OPS-06 — Incident Response

*Type:* Technical — Responds to and learns from production incidents.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Responds to alerts with support; follows runbooks; escalates appropriately.
  — *Why this level:* Following runbooks and escalating with support, without yet leading response, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner stage applied to the SRE book's on-call practice -- rules (runbooks) are executed, judgment calls are still supported. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Triages and resolves routine incidents; clear notes; takes on-call.
  — *Why this level:* Independently triaging and resolving routine incidents while carrying on-call is SFIA level 3 autonomy applied to the SRE book's on-call rotation model -- competent solo execution within known incident classes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Leads response to complex failures; blameless postmortems; same failure never recurs.
  — *Why this level:* Leading response and running blameless postmortems that prevent recurrence is Allspaw's named blameless-postmortem practice -- treating incidents as organizational learning rather than blame -- combined with the SRE book's postmortem discipline; this is the level where incident response becomes a systemic-learning practice, not just resolution. *Sources:* Allspaw, Blameless PostMortems and a Just Culture, Code as Craft (Etsy Engineering Blog, 2012); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in incident-management design (rotations, severity, escalation).
  — *Why this level:* Designing rotations, severity classification and escalation paths is precisely PagerDuty's Incident Response Documentation's structural content (Incident Commander role, severity levels, on-call design) -- expertise here means designing the incident-management system itself, matched to SFIA level 5's expert accountability. *Sources:* PagerDuty, Incident Response Documentation (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Commands the highest-severity incidents; sets incident process org-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Commanding the highest-severity incidents (PagerDuty's top severity/Incident Commander tier) and setting incident process for the whole org is SFIA level 6 authority -- process ownership beyond any single team's incident handling. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); PagerDuty, Incident Response Documentation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Sets the company's incident philosophy; calm authority in the worst moments.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the company's incident philosophy -- how the organization as a whole relates to failure -- is SFIA level 7's top responsibility band, the field-shaping tier beyond commanding individual incidents. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ops-07"></a>
##### OPS-07 — Cost & Performance Optimization

*Type:* Technical — Keeps systems fast and economical.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands cost/latency drivers of what they build.
  — *Why this level:* Understanding cost and latency drivers without yet acting on them independently is the advanced-beginner stage mapped to the FinOps Framework's Inform phase, where cost visibility precedes cost accountability. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); FinOps Foundation, FinOps Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard optimizations; stays within cost/latency budgets.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard optimizations and staying within budgets independently is SFIA level 3 autonomy mapped to the FinOps Framework's Optimize phase -- executing known cost-reduction levers within a defined budget. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); FinOps Foundation, FinOps Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs cost-aware architectures; defines and tracks unit economics for a domain.
  — *Why this level:* Defining and tracking unit economics for a domain is the FinOps Framework's Operate phase married to AWS Well-Architected's Cost Optimization pillar -- cost becomes a designed architectural property with owned metrics, not a constraint applied after the fact. *Sources:* FinOps Foundation, FinOps Framework (accessed 2026-07); Amazon Web Services, AWS Well-Architected Framework (AWS, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in economics at scale (fleet optimization, build-vs-buy).
  — *Why this level:* Fleet-wide optimization and build-vs-buy decisions are the FinOps Framework's organizational-maturity end-state, where cost practice spans the whole technology fleet rather than one domain, matched to SFIA level 5's expert accountability for a large technical area. *Sources:* FinOps Foundation, FinOps Framework (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns org-level spend strategy; cost decisions change margins.
  — *Why this level:* Owning spend strategy that moves company margins is SFIA level 6 authority over organization-wide policy and resourcing, beyond any single fleet or domain's cost practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes the company economics of the products.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping the economics of the company's products -- pricing and margin structure via technical decisions -- is SFIA level 7's top responsibility band, the field-shaping tier reserved for organization-defining strategic influence. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Security

<a id="ops-08"></a>
##### OPS-08 — Application & Systems Security

*Type:* Technical — Builds secure-by-default systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Understands core appsec; follows practices and flags concerns.
  — *Why this level:* Recognizing and flagging concerns from a known list (the OWASP Top 10) without yet independently remediating them is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner stage -- named risks are known, judgment about how to fix them is still supported. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Top 10 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies least privilege; validates/sanitizes inputs; knows common attacks.
  — *Why this level:* Independently applying least privilege and input validation against known OWASP Top 10 attack classes (injection, broken access control) is SFIA level 3 autonomy -- competent solo defense against well-characterized threats. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Top 10 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs defense in depth; thinks in abuse cases; owns a domain's posture.
  — *Why this level:* Designing defense in depth and reasoning in abuse cases for a whole domain is OWASP ASVS Level 2's verification bar -- multiple independent control layers and threat-model-driven design, beyond the single-control checks of ASVS Level 1. *Sources:* OWASP Foundation, OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert in securing systems at scale; leads red-teaming and remediation.
  — *Why this level:* Leading red-teaming and remediation at scale corresponds to OWASP ASVS Level 3's advanced/high-assurance verification tier and NIST SP 800-53's expert-level control catalog for defense-in-depth at an organizational scale, well past domain-level design. *Sources:* NIST, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, SP 800-53 Revision 5 (2020, updated 2021); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Defines security strategy for the org's surface area.
  — *Why this level:* Defining security strategy across the org's whole surface area -- e.g. adopting a zero-trust architecture per NIST SP 800-207 -- is SFIA level 6 authority over organization-wide security policy, beyond securing any one domain. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Company-level accountability; authority on the field.
  — *Why this level:* Company-level security accountability and field-wide authority is SFIA level 7's top responsibility band -- the tier reserved for individuals whose decisions define organizational direction and are recognized authorities beyond the company itself. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ops-09"></a>
##### OPS-09 — Privacy & Compliance Engineering

*Type:* Technical — Bakes privacy, audit and regulatory controls into systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Knows data handling has privacy implications; follows rules.
  — *Why this level:* Following predefined data-handling rules without yet applying independent judgment is supervised execution of someone else's compliance policy -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies PII handling, redaction, residency and retention correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Correctly applying PII handling, redaction, residency and retention to routine cases independently is executing GDPR's own operative rules (data minimization, storage limitation, cross-border transfer restrictions) without inventing new controls -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) (2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs for compliance (consent, audit trails, regional rules); owns readiness for a domain.
  — *Why this level:* Designing consent, audit-trail and regional-rule mechanisms for a domain is building the Control and Protect functions of NIST's Privacy Framework rather than just applying existing ones -- Dreyfus's competent band, where the practitioner owns a bounded but non-routine design space. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Expert at translating regulation into controls; represents engineering in audits.
  — *Why this level:* Translating regulation into controls and representing engineering in audits is exactly the exercise NIST SP 800-53's control catalog formalizes -- turning abstract regulatory obligations into concrete, auditable technical controls is Dreyfus's proficient band, where practice is codified for others to rely on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, SP 800-53 Revision 5 (2020, updated 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets org compliance strategy; anticipates regulation.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide compliance strategy and anticipating regulatory change goes beyond any single control -- it is org-level, forward-looking accountability in GDPR's own sense (Article 5's accountability principle), matching Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); European Parliament and Council, Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) (2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Authoritative on the landscape; trusted interface to regulators.
  — *Why this level:* Being the authoritative, trusted interface to regulators is the register NIST's own Privacy Framework aspires to occupy as a cross-sector reference standard -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire, external credibility beyond one organization. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020).

#### Provisioning & Configuration

<a id="ops-10"></a>
##### OPS-10 — Infrastructure as code & provisioning

*Type:* Technical — Define and version infrastructure declaratively to provision repeatable environments.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes simple declarative resource definitions from templates, applying them under review in non-production environments.
  — *Why this level:* Writing simple declarative resource definitions from templates under review is supervised use of an existing IaC pattern, not yet independent design -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently provisions standard infrastructure stacks, manages state and variables, and handles routine drift with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently provisioning standard stacks and managing state/variables for routine drift applies Morris's core infrastructure-as-code practice (declarative definitions plus managed state) to known cases without redesigning it -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reusable modules for ambiguous needs, structures state safely, and is the go-to for tricky provisioning failures.
  — *Why this level:* Designing reusable modules for ambiguous needs and structuring state safely is Morris's stack-design and state-management maturity practice applied to non-routine cases -- Dreyfus's competent band, the go-to for provisioning failures the standard module catalog doesn't cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the provisioning patterns and module conventions others adopt, solving thorny dependency and idempotency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the provisioning patterns and module conventions others adopt, and solving deep dependency/idempotency problems, is codifying Morris's infrastructure-design principles into reusable organizational practice -- Dreyfus's proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization-wide IaC strategy, governance, and standards, anticipating shifts in declarative provisioning practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide IaC strategy and anticipating shifts in declarative provisioning is org-level standard-setting around the version-controlled-infrastructure capability Forsgren et al. identify as a driver of delivery performance -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good infrastructure-as-code means for the field, shaping provisioning practices recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good infrastructure-as-code means for the field and shaping industry practice is the register Morris's own book occupies as the widely cited reference defining the discipline -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).

<a id="ops-11"></a>
##### OPS-11 — Configuration management & desired-state enforcement

*Type:* Technical — Automate system configuration and continuously converge hosts to a defined target state.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies predefined configuration policies to hosts under supervision, verifying convergence against the declared desired state.
  — *Why this level:* Applying predefined configuration policies under supervision and verifying convergence against a declared desired state is supervised use of Burgess's convergent-operator concept, not yet authoring it -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Burgess, Cfengine: A Site Configuration Engine, USENIX Computing Systems 8(3) (1995).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Authors and maintains standard configuration definitions independently, remediating routine drift with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring and maintaining standard configuration definitions independently, remediating routine drift, is independent operation of Burgess's convergence model on known cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Burgess, Cfengine: A Site Configuration Engine, USENIX Computing Systems 8(3) (1995).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs idempotent configuration for ambiguous cases, manages secrets and ordering, and resolves hard convergence failures.
  — *Why this level:* Designing idempotent configuration for ambiguous cases and resolving hard convergence failures directly engages the idempotency property Burgess names as the defining requirement of a convergent operator -- Dreyfus's competent band, ownership of judgment calls the standard playbook doesn't answer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Burgess, Cfengine: A Site Configuration Engine, USENIX Computing Systems 8(3) (1995).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the configuration architecture and enforcement model others adopt, solving deep drift and idempotency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the configuration architecture and enforcement model others adopt, solving deep drift and idempotency problems at scale, is codifying convergence practice into reusable organizational architecture the way Morris frames infrastructure-design conventions -- Dreyfus's proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Morris, Infrastructure as Code: Dynamic Systems for the Cloud Age, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets strategy for desired-state enforcement across the estate, anticipating where configuration management is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting desired-state enforcement strategy across the estate and anticipating where configuration management is heading is org-level, forward-looking application of the autonomous, decentralized convergence model Burgess's theory anticipated -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Burgess, Cfengine: A Site Configuration Engine, USENIX Computing Systems 8(3) (1995).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry standards for desired-state enforcement, externally credible in shaping configuration practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry standards for desired-state enforcement and being externally credible in shaping the practice is the role Burgess's founding CFEngine paper itself occupies as the origin of the convergent configuration-management discipline -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Burgess, Cfengine: A Site Configuration Engine, USENIX Computing Systems 8(3) (1995).

<a id="ops-12"></a>
##### OPS-12 — Image & artifact building / golden baselines

*Type:* Technical — Produce hardened, reproducible machine and application images for consistent deployment.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds images from existing recipes under review, verifying contents match the documented baseline.
  — *Why this level:* Building images from existing recipes under review and verifying contents against a documented baseline is supervised use of a consensus baseline like a CIS Benchmark, not yet authoring one -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently maintains image build pipelines and updates baselines for routine patches and version changes.
  — *Why this level:* Independently maintaining image build pipelines and updating baselines for routine patches and version changes is independently keeping images aligned to published benchmark revisions -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs hardened, minimal golden images for ambiguous needs and resolves tricky reproducibility and provenance issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing hardened, minimal golden images for ambiguous needs and resolving tricky reproducibility/provenance issues applies NIST SP 800-190's minimal-attack-surface and image-hardening guidance to non-routine cases -- Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Application Container Security Guide, SP 800-190 (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the baseline strategy and build conventions others adopt, solving layering, supply-chain, and drift problems.
