  — *Why this level:* Defining the baseline strategy and build conventions others adopt, solving supply-chain and drift problems, is establishing the build-provenance practices SLSA's own levels (L1-L3) formalize -- Dreyfus's proficient band, where practice is codified for others to rely on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenSSF, SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), Version 1.0 (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide standards for image lifecycle and provenance, anticipating shifts in artifact-building practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide standards for image lifecycle and provenance, anticipating shifts in artifact-building practice, is org-level adoption of higher SLSA build levels ahead of where the estate currently sits -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OpenSSF, SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), Version 1.0 (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what a trustworthy golden baseline means for the discipline, shaping industry artifact-integrity practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what a trustworthy golden baseline means for the discipline and shaping industry artifact-integrity practice is the role the SLSA framework itself plays as the named cross-industry supply-chain trust standard -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OpenSSF, SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), Version 1.0 (2023).

<a id="ops-13"></a>
##### OPS-13 — Environment & release promotion strategy

*Type:* Technical — Design promotion paths and parity across dev, staging, and production environments.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Promotes builds through predefined environment stages under review, following the documented gating checklist.
  — *Why this level:* Promoting builds through predefined stages under review, following a documented gating checklist, is supervised execution of Humble & Farley's deployment-pipeline stages without yet designing them -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard promotion flows across environments, handling routine approvals and rollbacks with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing standard promotion flows and handling routine approvals/rollbacks applies Humble & Farley's standard deployment-pipeline model to known cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs promotion paths and gates for ambiguous release scenarios, resolving hard environment-parity and rollback issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing promotion paths and gates for ambiguous release scenarios and resolving hard environment-parity issues is applying Humble & Farley's environment-parity principle to non-routine cases the standard pipeline doesn't cleanly cover -- Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the promotion model and gating strategy others adopt, solving complex multi-stage and dependency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the promotion model and gating strategy others adopt, solving complex multi-stage dependency problems, is codifying deployment-automation practice into an organizational standard -- the shift Forsgren et al. tie to lower change-fail rate and faster lead time -- Dreyfus's proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide release-promotion strategy, anticipating how environment progression and gating should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide release-promotion strategy and anticipating how gating should evolve is org-level, forward-looking application of the deployment-automation capability Forsgren et al. identify as predicting delivery performance -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what disciplined release promotion means for the field, shaping industry environment-strategy practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what disciplined release promotion means for the field and shaping industry practice is the role Humble & Farley's own book occupies as the canonical reference that named continuous delivery as a discipline -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).

#### Compute & Workload Orchestration

<a id="ops-14"></a>
##### OPS-14 — Container orchestration & scheduling

*Type:* Technical — Schedule, place, and manage containerized workloads across a cluster of compute nodes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Deploys workloads to an existing orchestrator under review, adjusting basic scheduling settings from examples.
  — *Why this level:* Deploying workloads to an existing orchestrator under review and adjusting basic scheduling settings from examples is supervised use of documented Kubernetes scheduling constructs, not yet independent design -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Burns, Beda, Hightower & Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running, 3rd Edition (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently operates orchestrated workloads, manages routine scaling, placement, and health checks with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently operating orchestrated workloads and managing routine scaling, placement and health checks is independent use of the standard orchestration operations the book covers -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Burns, Beda, Hightower & Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running, 3rd Edition (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs scheduling, affinity, and resource policies for ambiguous workloads and resolves hard orchestration failures.
  — *Why this level:* Designing scheduling, affinity and resource policies for ambiguous workloads and resolving hard orchestration failures applies the advanced affinity/anti-affinity and resource-management constructs to non-routine cases -- Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Burns, Beda, Hightower & Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running, 3rd Edition (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines cluster topology and scheduling patterns others adopt, solving deep placement, contention, and lifecycle problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining cluster topology and scheduling patterns others adopt, solving deep placement and contention problems, is codifying cluster-architecture practice into an organizational standard -- Dreyfus's proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Burns, Beda, Hightower & Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running, 3rd Edition (O'Reilly, 2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide orchestration strategy and standards, anticipating where workload scheduling is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide orchestration strategy and anticipating where workload scheduling is heading is org-level, forward-looking application of the automated-operations-at-scale principles the SRE book establishes for running production systems -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what effective orchestration means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping scheduling practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what effective orchestration means for the discipline and being externally credible is the register occupied by a book authored by Kubernetes' own co-founders, shaping how the industry understands scheduling -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Burns, Beda, Hightower & Evenson, Kubernetes: Up and Running, 3rd Edition (O'Reilly, 2022).

<a id="ops-15"></a>
##### OPS-15 — Containerization & workload packaging

*Type:* Technical — Package applications and dependencies into portable, isolated runtime units.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Packages applications into containers from existing recipes under review, verifying they run as expected.
  — *Why this level:* Packaging applications into containers from existing recipes under review and verifying they run as expected is supervised production of images that conform to the OCI Image Format without altering its structure -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Open Container Initiative, OCI Image Format Specification (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds and maintains container images, managing dependencies and layers for routine workloads with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and maintaining container images, managing dependencies and layers for routine workloads, is independently authoring images against the standard layered OCI format -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Open Container Initiative, OCI Image Format Specification (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs minimal, secure, reproducible packaging for ambiguous workloads and resolves tricky runtime and size issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing minimal, secure, reproducible packaging for ambiguous workloads and resolving tricky runtime/size issues applies NIST SP 800-190's minimal-image and runtime-isolation guidance to non-routine cases -- Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Application Container Security Guide, SP 800-190 (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines packaging conventions and base-image strategy others adopt, solving deep build-efficiency and isolation problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining packaging conventions and base-image strategy others adopt, solving deep build-efficiency and isolation problems, is codifying organization-wide conventions on top of the OCI spec's manifest/layer model -- Dreyfus's proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Open Container Initiative, OCI Image Format Specification (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide containerization standards, anticipating shifts in workload packaging and runtime practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide containerization standards and anticipating shifts in runtime practice is org-level, forward-looking application of container-security guidance across the estate -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Application Container Security Guide, SP 800-190 (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good workload packaging means for the field, shaping industry containerization practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good workload packaging means for the field and shaping industry practice is the role the OCI Image Format itself plays as the cross-industry standard for container packaging -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Open Container Initiative, OCI Image Format Specification (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="ops-16"></a>
##### OPS-16 — Capacity & autoscaling design

*Type:* Technical — Plan compute capacity and design elastic scaling to meet variable demand.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adjusts capacity settings within defined limits under review, monitoring basic utilization against thresholds.
  — *Why this level:* Adjusting capacity settings within defined limits under review and monitoring utilization against thresholds is supervised application of the capacity-planning thresholds the SRE book describes, not yet setting them -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently configures standard autoscaling rules and capacity buffers, tuning routine thresholds with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently configuring standard autoscaling rules and capacity buffers, tuning routine thresholds, is independently applying standard capacity-planning practice to known demand patterns -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs scaling policies and capacity models for ambiguous, bursty demand and resolves hard scaling-stability issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing scaling policies and capacity models for ambiguous, bursty demand and resolving hard scaling-stability issues combines SRE demand forecasting with Nygard's stability patterns for containing cascading failure under load spikes -- Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the capacity-planning and autoscaling approach others adopt, solving complex demand-prediction and cost-tradeoff problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the capacity-planning and autoscaling approach others adopt, solving complex demand-prediction and cost-tradeoff problems, is codifying the elasticity and cost/performance tradeoff guidance the AWS Well-Architected performance-efficiency pillar sets out into organizational practice -- Dreyfus's proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); AWS, Performance Efficiency Pillar -- AWS Well-Architected Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide capacity strategy, anticipating demand shifts and how scaling design should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide capacity strategy and anticipating demand shifts is org-level, forward-looking application of the continuous workload-review discipline the performance-efficiency pillar prescribes -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); AWS, Performance Efficiency Pillar -- AWS Well-Architected Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what sound capacity and autoscaling design means for the discipline, shaping industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what sound capacity and autoscaling design means for the discipline and shaping industry practice is the register the SRE book's capacity-planning chapter itself occupies as the widely cited industry reference -- Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

<a id="ops-17"></a>
##### OPS-17 — Operating system & host administration

*Type:* Technical — Administer, harden, and tune host operating systems and their runtime services.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs routine host tasks like updates and user setup under review, following documented procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Executing patching and account-setup procedures under review against a documented runbook is supervised execution of a known interface -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently administers hosts, manages packages, services, and permissions, troubleshooting routine issues with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running package, service, and permission administration for routine faults applies Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan's standard operational-procedures playbook without redesigning it -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Tunes and hardens hosts for ambiguous workloads and diagnoses hard kernel, resource, and performance problems.
  — *Why this level:* Hardening and tuning hosts for ambiguous workloads and diagnosing hard kernel/performance problems is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner adapts CIS Benchmarks' consensus baselines to cases the checklist doesn't cover, owning judgment the standard leaves open. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines host-administration standards and hardening baselines others adopt, solving deep OS-level and tuning problems.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the hardening baseline and administration standard other teams adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- the shift from applying CIS Benchmarks to writing the organization's own equivalent, codifying practice the way Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan describe as the mark of a mature operations function. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07); Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide host-management strategy, anticipating shifts in operating-system administration practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting host-management strategy and anticipating shifts in OS administration practice is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting beyond any one host or fleet -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent host administration means for the field, externally credible in shaping OS practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent host administration means and being externally credible in shaping practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by practitioner-authored references like Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan's book, cited across the industry as the field's own standard. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016).

<a id="ops-18"></a>
##### OPS-18 — Storage & data persistence design

*Type:* Technical — Design block, object, and file storage for durability, performance, and access patterns.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Provisions and attaches storage from defined options under review, verifying capacity and access settings.
  — *Why this level:* Provisioning storage from a defined menu and verifying capacity/access settings under review is supervised execution of a known configuration -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages storage volumes, snapshots, and routine persistence configuration with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing volumes, snapshots, and routine persistence configuration for standard cases applies established storage-engine and replication patterns without redesigning them -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs persistence schemes balancing durability, performance, and cost for ambiguous needs, resolving hard data-integrity issues.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing durability, performance, and cost for ambiguous needs and resolving hard data-integrity issues is Dreyfus's competent band -- Kleppmann frames these as continuous engineering trade-offs rather than a fixed recipe, and full autonomous ownership of that trade-off space is what separates P3 from applying a template. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines storage architecture and persistence patterns others adopt, solving deep consistency, replication, and performance problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reusable persistence architecture and solving deep consistency/replication problems others cannot is Dreyfus's proficient band, where practice is codified for reuse; Kleppmann names replication consistency and partitioning as the genuinely hard, still-debated problems, so resolving them for others is P4-grade. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide storage and persistence strategy, anticipating where data-durability design is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting storage strategy and anticipating where durability design is heading is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting beyond any one system's persistence design -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what sound data-persistence design means for the discipline, shaping industry storage practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what sound persistence design means and shaping industry storage practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Kleppmann's own synthesis of the field occupies as a widely cited reference model for the discipline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems (O'Reilly, 2017).

#### Networking & Connectivity

<a id="ops-19"></a>
##### OPS-19 — Network design & routing

*Type:* Technical — Architect network topologies, subnets, and routing for connectivity and segmentation.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures basic network segments and routes from designs under review, verifying connectivity.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring segments and routes from a given design and verifying connectivity under review is supervised execution of someone else's topology -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds standard network topologies, manages routing and segmentation for routine needs with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard topologies and managing routine routing/segmentation applies the layered addressing and routing models Kurose & Ross treat as foundational network-layer mechanics, without needing to design new ones -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kurose & Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8th ed. (Pearson, 2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs routing and addressing schemes for ambiguous topologies and diagnoses hard reachability and routing failures.
  — *Why this level:* Designing addressing and routing schemes for ambiguous topologies and diagnosing hard reachability failures is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner autonomously applies routing-protocol convergence behavior, the mechanics Kurose & Ross dedicate a full network-layer treatment to, to cases with no template. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kurose & Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8th ed. (Pearson, 2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines network architecture and routing patterns others adopt, solving deep segmentation, scale, and convergence problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining routing and segmentation patterns others adopt and solving deep convergence problems is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying network-layer design decisions into an architecture others build against, rather than solving one topology at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kurose & Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8th ed. (Pearson, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide network strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in network design and routing.
  — *Why this level:* Setting network strategy and standards and anticipating shifts in design and routing practice is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good network design means for the field, externally credible in shaping routing practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good network design means for the field and being externally credible in shaping routing practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by foundational references like Kurose & Ross that set how the discipline itself is taught and practiced. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kurose & Ross, Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach, 8th ed. (Pearson, 2020).

<a id="ops-20"></a>
##### OPS-20 — Load balancing & traffic management

*Type:* Technical — Distribute and shape traffic across endpoints for availability and performance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures basic load-balancing rules from templates under review, verifying traffic reaches healthy targets.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring load-balancing rules from a template and verifying traffic reaches healthy targets under review is supervised execution of a known configuration -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard balancing, health checks, and routing rules for routine traffic with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing health checks and standard balancing rules for routine traffic applies named algorithms like NGINX's round-robin, least-connections, and IP-hash methods without inventing new distribution logic -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NGINX, Inc., NGINX HTTP Load Balancing (Admin Guide, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs traffic-distribution and failover policies for ambiguous patterns and resolves hard balancing and session issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing distribution and failover policy for ambiguous traffic patterns and resolving hard session-affinity issues is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner owns the trade-offs Google's SRE book frames as load-balancing-at-the-frontend design decisions, not just applying a stock algorithm. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines traffic-management patterns others adopt, solving deep distribution, affinity, and graceful-degradation problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining traffic-management patterns others adopt and solving deep graceful-degradation problems is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying the SRE book's graceful-degradation and load-shedding practices into an org-wide pattern rather than handling one incident at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide traffic-management strategy, anticipating how load distribution and routing should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting traffic-management strategy and anticipating how distribution and routing should evolve is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what effective traffic management means for the discipline, shaping industry load-balancing practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what effective traffic management means for the discipline and shaping industry practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by publicly authored references like Google's SRE book that set how the wider industry reasons about load balancing. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

<a id="ops-21"></a>
##### OPS-21 — DNS & service discovery

*Type:* Technical — Resolve names and dynamically locate services across distributed systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Creates and edits basic name records under review, verifying resolution behaves as documented.
  — *Why this level:* Creating and editing basic records under review and verifying documented resolution behavior is supervised execution of a known record format -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages zones, records, and standard service-registration for routine needs with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing zones and standard service registration for routine needs applies RFC 1035's defined resource-record types and zone-transfer mechanics without deviating from them -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Mockapetris, Domain Names - Implementation and Specification, RFC 1035 (IETF, 1987).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs resolution and discovery schemes for ambiguous, dynamic environments and resolves hard propagation and caching issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing resolution schemes for ambiguous, dynamic environments and resolving hard propagation/caching issues is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner reasons about TTL, negative-caching, and zone-transfer behavior that RFC 1035 specifies but leaves the practitioner to apply correctly under real propagation delay. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mockapetris, Domain Names - Implementation and Specification, RFC 1035 (IETF, 1987).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines naming and discovery architecture others adopt, solving deep resolution, failover, and registration problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining naming and discovery architecture others adopt and solving deep failover/registration problems is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying resolution and registration design into a reusable architecture rather than fixing one propagation incident at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mockapetris, Domain Names - Implementation and Specification, RFC 1035 (IETF, 1987).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide naming and discovery strategy, anticipating shifts in service-discovery practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting naming and discovery strategy and anticipating shifts in service-discovery practice is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what robust naming and discovery means for the field, shaping industry DNS and discovery practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what robust naming and discovery means for the field and shaping industry practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by the foundational specification (RFC 1035) that has itself shaped how the entire industry implements name resolution. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Mockapetris, Domain Names - Implementation and Specification, RFC 1035 (IETF, 1987).

<a id="ops-22"></a>
##### OPS-22 — Network protocols & packet-level troubleshooting

*Type:* Technical — Diagnose connectivity using knowledge of layered protocols and packet behavior.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Captures traffic and reads basic protocol fields under guidance to confirm expected behavior.
  — *Why this level:* Capturing traffic and reading basic protocol fields under guidance to confirm expected behavior is supervised use of a known capture tool -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently traces standard protocol exchanges and diagnoses routine connectivity faults from captures with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently tracing standard exchanges (TCP handshake, ARP, DHCP) and diagnosing routine faults from captures applies the layered protocol mechanics Stevens documents in exhaustive, named detail, without needing to reason beyond the textbook case -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Stevens, TCP/IP Illustrated, Volume 1: The Protocols (Addison-Wesley, 1994).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Dissects complex multi-layer exchanges for ambiguous faults and resolves hard latency, fragmentation, and handshake issues.
  — *Why this level:* Dissecting complex multi-layer exchanges for ambiguous faults and resolving hard fragmentation/handshake issues is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner autonomously applies Stevens's protocol-internals detail to failures the reference material doesn't spell out as a worked example. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Stevens, TCP/IP Illustrated, Volume 1: The Protocols (Addison-Wesley, 1994).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines packet-analysis methods others adopt, solving deep protocol-interaction and elusive intermittent-failure problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining packet-analysis methods others adopt and solving elusive intermittent-failure problems is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying diagnostic method into a reusable practice rather than resolving one capture at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Stevens, TCP/IP Illustrated, Volume 1: The Protocols (Addison-Wesley, 1994).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide troubleshooting standards and tooling direction, anticipating protocol-behavior challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Setting troubleshooting standards and tooling direction and anticipating protocol-behavior challenges is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what rigorous packet-level diagnosis means for the discipline, externally credible in protocol practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what rigorous packet-level diagnosis means for the discipline and being externally credible in protocol practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by Stevens's own volume, still the reference the field measures protocol-internals writing against. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Stevens, TCP/IP Illustrated, Volume 1: The Protocols (Addison-Wesley, 1994).

<a id="ops-23"></a>
##### OPS-23 — Edge, CDN & content delivery

*Type:* Technical — Cache and serve content near users to reduce latency and origin load.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures basic caching and delivery rules from templates under review, verifying content serves correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring caching and delivery rules from a template and verifying correct serving under review is supervised execution of a known configuration -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages edge caching, invalidation, and routing for routine content with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing caching, invalidation, and routing for routine content applies the HTTP caching semantics and connection-reuse behavior Grigorik documents as standard browser/CDN mechanics, without redesigning delivery strategy -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs delivery and caching strategies for ambiguous traffic and resolves hard cache-coherence and edge-routing issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing delivery strategy for ambiguous traffic and resolving hard cache-coherence issues is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner autonomously applies the latency and protocol trade-offs Grigorik frames (TCP/TLS handshake cost, HTTP/2 multiplexing) to cases with no standard playbook. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines edge-delivery architecture others adopt, solving deep caching, origin-offload, and latency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining edge-delivery architecture others adopt and solving deep origin-offload problems is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying delivery and caching design into a reusable architecture rather than tuning one traffic pattern at a time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide content-delivery strategy, anticipating shifts in edge and distribution practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting content-delivery strategy and anticipating shifts in edge and distribution practice is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent content delivery means for the field, shaping industry edge and CDN practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent content delivery means for the field and shaping industry practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by Grigorik's own book, written as and cited as the field's reference for network-performance practice. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grigorik, High Performance Browser Networking (O'Reilly, 2013).

<a id="ops-24"></a>
##### OPS-24 — Secure connectivity & network perimeter

*Type:* Technical — Establish encrypted tunnels, gateways, and boundaries between trust zones.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies predefined firewall and tunnel rules under review, verifying allowed and blocked paths behave correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Applying predefined firewall and tunnel rules under review and verifying allowed/blocked paths is supervised execution of a known ruleset -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard perimeter controls, secure tunnels, and segmentation rules with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing standard perimeter controls and secure tunnels for routine needs applies established segmentation and encrypted-tunnel patterns without redesigning the trust model -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs perimeter and encrypted-connectivity schemes for ambiguous needs and resolves hard isolation and access issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing perimeter and encrypted-connectivity schemes for ambiguous needs and resolving hard isolation issues is Dreyfus's competent band -- the practitioner applies NIST SP 800-207's zero-trust tenets (per-request, identity-based authorization rather than static network location) to cases the reference architecture only sketches. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines perimeter architecture and secure-connectivity patterns others adopt, solving deep segmentation and trust problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining perimeter architecture others adopt and solving deep trust-model problems is Dreyfus's proficient band -- this is the same move Google made in BeyondCorp: retiring the trusted-network perimeter for a device/identity-based access architecture that other teams then adopt wholesale. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ward & Beyer, BeyondCorp: A New Approach to Enterprise Security, ;login: 39(6), 6-11 (USENIX, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide perimeter and secure-connectivity strategy, anticipating shifts in network-security practice.
  — *Why this level:* Setting perimeter and secure-connectivity strategy and anticipating shifts in network-security practice is org-wide, forward-looking standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what strong network perimeter design means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what strong perimeter design means for the discipline and being externally credible in shaping practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register occupied by NIST SP 800-207 and the BeyondCorp papers, both of which moved from one organization's practice to the field's reference architecture for zero trust. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020); Ward & Beyer, BeyondCorp: A New Approach to Enterprise Security, ;login: 39(6), 6-11 (USENIX, 2014).

#### Resilience & Continuity

<a id="ops-25"></a>
##### OPS-25 — Backup, DR & business continuity

*Type:* Technical — Plan backups, recovery objectives, and failover to survive disruptive events.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs scheduled backups and restore tests under review, verifying jobs complete and data is recoverable.
  — *Why this level:* Executing SP 800-34's testing/training/exercise (TT&E) activities under supervision -- verifying backup jobs and restore success -- is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA9 Level 2 Assist, where correctness is checked externally rather than reasoned about. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Revision 1 (2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages backup schedules, retention, and routine restores, validating recovery points with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running the routine backup-schedule and restore-validation portions of an SP 800-34 contingency plan, with review, is the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band and SFIA9 Level 3 Apply: recurring recovery-point checks handled without case-by-case coaching. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Revision 1 (2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs backup and recovery schemes for ambiguous needs, meeting recovery objectives and resolving hard restore issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a backup and recovery scheme for ambiguous needs is SP 800-34's Strategy Development phase -- setting RTOs/RPOs and choosing a recovery strategy with no template to follow -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Revision 1 (2010).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines continuity architecture and recovery patterns others adopt, solving deep cross-failure and dependency problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining continuity architecture and recovery patterns other teams adopt extends SP 800-34's Plan Development phase across systems and dependencies rather than one plan, matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise and Dreyfus's expert band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Revision 1 (2010).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide continuity strategy and recovery objectives, anticipating evolving business-continuity needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide continuity strategy and recovery objectives is owning SP 800-34's contingency-planning program at the senior-management tier the standard specifies -- SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Revision 1 (2010).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what credible business continuity means for the discipline, shaping industry disaster-recovery practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what credible business continuity means for the discipline goes beyond applying SP 800-34 to shaping standards like it -- SFIA9 Level 7 Set Strategy/Inspire and Dreyfus's master band, authoring frameworks others follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems, SP 800-34 Revision 1 (2010).

<a id="ops-26"></a>
##### OPS-26 — High availability & fault-tolerance design

*Type:* Technical — Eliminate single points of failure through redundancy and graceful degradation.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures basic redundancy and failover from designs under review, verifying standby paths activate.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring basic redundancy and failover from someone else's design, with standby-path activation verified in review, is Dreyfus's novice band applying one of Nygard's stability patterns (e.g. a supplied circuit breaker) exactly as specified. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds standard redundant setups and failover behavior for routine services with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard redundant setups and failover behavior for routine services is SFIA9 Level 3 Apply and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band: recognized Release It! patterns (bulkheads, timeouts) applied to familiar service shapes without novel tradeoffs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs availability schemes for ambiguous failure modes and resolves hard split-brain, quorum, and failover issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing availability schemes for ambiguous failure modes and resolving split-brain and quorum issues means reasoning directly about Gilbert & Lynch's consistency/availability/partition-tolerance tradeoff rather than a documented pattern -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gilbert & Lynch, Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services, ACM SIGACT News 33(2), 51-59 (2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines fault-tolerance patterns others adopt, solving deep redundancy, isolation, and graceful-degradation problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining fault-tolerance patterns that other teams adopt is authoring new entries in Nygard's stability-pattern catalog rather than applying existing ones, matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise and Dreyfus's expert band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nygard, Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd Edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide availability strategy and targets, anticipating where resilience design is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide availability strategy and targets moves CAP-theorem and stability-pattern tradeoffs from one system's design into governing policy across many systems -- the SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what genuine fault tolerance means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping availability practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what genuine fault tolerance means for the discipline is the register Gilbert & Lynch themselves operate in -- proving the theorem that reshaped how the field reasons about availability -- Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gilbert & Lynch, Brewer's Conjecture and the Feasibility of Consistent, Available, Partition-Tolerant Web Services, ACM SIGACT News 33(2), 51-59 (2002).

<a id="ops-27"></a>
##### OPS-27 — Platform & developer-experience engineering

*Type:* Technical — Build self-service internal platforms and paved paths that streamline delivery.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains existing self-service platform components under review, addressing documented user requests.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining existing self-service platform components under review, addressing documented requests, is Dreyfus's novice band: operating inside a platform team's existing paved path (Skelton & Pais's Team Topologies) without yet shaping it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds and supports standard platform capabilities and templates for routine developer needs with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and supporting standard platform capabilities and templates for routine needs matches the Initial/Managed tier of the CNCF Platform Engineering Maturity Model -- documented, repeatable capability delivery -- and SFIA9 Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); CNCF TAG App Delivery, Platform Engineering Maturity Model (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs self-service workflows for ambiguous needs, reducing friction and resolving hard abstraction and adoption issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing self-service workflows for ambiguous needs is Team Topologies' platform-as-a-product principle applied end to end -- reducing a stream-aligned team's cognitive load with no template -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines platform architecture and golden paths others adopt, solving deep developer-experience and leverage problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining platform architecture and golden paths other teams adopt is the CNCF maturity model's Scaled tier, where platform investment becomes deliberate cross-team leverage rather than one team's tooling, matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); CNCF TAG App Delivery, Platform Engineering Maturity Model (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide platform strategy, anticipating how developer-experience engineering should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide platform strategy is owning the CNCF maturity model's people/process/policy/technology investment as a portfolio, not a single platform -- SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); CNCF TAG App Delivery, Platform Engineering Maturity Model (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent platform engineering means for the field, shaping industry developer-experience practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent platform engineering means for the field is the register the Team Topologies and CNCF-whitepaper authors themselves operate in -- shaping the vocabulary the discipline uses -- Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).

#### Operating Mindset

<a id="ops-28"></a>
##### OPS-28 — Automation-first operations

*Type:* Behavioral — Default to eliminating toil by automating repetitive operational work.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs and lightly edits existing automation under review, flagging tasks that remain manual.
  — *Why this level:* Running and lightly editing existing automation under review, flagging remaining manual tasks, is Dreyfus's novice band: recognizing toil, per the SRE book's definition, without yet being trusted to remove it unsupervised. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently automates routine operational tasks and integrates them into standard workflows with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently automating routine operational tasks and integrating them into standard workflows is applying the SRE book's toil-elimination practice to well-understood, bounded work -- SFIA9 Level 3 Apply and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs automation for ambiguous, error-prone toil and resolves hard reliability and orchestration issues in pipelines.
  — *Why this level:* Designing automation for ambiguous, error-prone toil and resolving hard reliability and orchestration issues in pipelines goes beyond the SRE book's routine toil-reduction cases into engineering judgment under uncertainty -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines automation patterns and toil-elimination practices others adopt, solving deep workflow and safety problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining automation patterns and toil-elimination practices other teams adopt is generalizing the SRE book's toil-budget discipline beyond one team's on-call rotation, matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise and Dreyfus's expert band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide automation strategy, anticipating where automation-first operations should head.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide automation strategy is codifying the SRE book's toil-budget policy (e.g. the 50% operational-work cap) as governance across every SRE-adjacent team -- the SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what automation-first operations means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping the practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what automation-first operations means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping the practice, is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7 Set Strategy/Inspire -- authoring the next reference work rather than applying an existing one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="ops-29"></a>
##### OPS-29 — Systems thinking & failure-mode reasoning

*Type:* Behavioral — Reason about emergent behavior and cascading failures across interdependent systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Traces simple cause-and-effect across components under guidance, identifying obvious failure points.
  — *Why this level:* Tracing simple cause-and-effect across components under guidance is Dreyfus's novice band applying Meadows's basic stock-and-flow reasoning to an obvious, single-loop failure, with the mapping checked by a supervisor. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Meadows (ed. Wright), Thinking in Systems: A Primer (Chelsea Green, 2008).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently maps standard system interactions and reasons through routine failure modes with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently mapping standard system interactions and reasoning through routine failure modes is applying Meadows's system-archetype patterns to familiar systems without coaching -- SFIA9 Level 3 Apply and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Meadows (ed. Wright), Thinking in Systems: A Primer (Chelsea Green, 2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Analyzes emergent behavior and cascading failures in ambiguous systems, anticipating non-obvious failure interactions.
  — *Why this level:* Analyzing emergent behavior and cascading failures in ambiguous systems, anticipating non-obvious interactions, is reasoning about Perrow's normal accidents -- failures that emerge from tight coupling and complex interaction rather than a single broken part -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Perrow, Normal Accidents: Living with High-Risk Technologies (Basic Books, 1984).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines failure-mode reasoning methods others adopt, solving deep systemic and feedback-loop problems others miss.
  — *Why this level:* Defining failure-mode reasoning methods other teams adopt, solving systemic and feedback-loop problems others miss, is Dekker's shift from hunting broken components to understanding drift -- authoring the investigative method itself -- matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise and Dreyfus's expert band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dekker, Drift into Failure: From Hunting Broken Components to Understanding Complex Systems (Ashgate, 2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organization-wide approaches to systems reasoning, anticipating where complex-failure analysis is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide approaches to systems reasoning is applying Dekker's drift-into-failure lens as standing governance -- how the whole organization investigates and anticipates gradual risk normalization -- the SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dekker, Drift into Failure: From Hunting Broken Components to Understanding Complex Systems (Ashgate, 2011).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what rigorous systems thinking means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping the practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what rigorous systems thinking means for the discipline, externally credible in shaping the practice, is the register Perrow, Meadows and Dekker themselves operate in -- authoring the theory the field now reasons with -- Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Perrow, Normal Accidents: Living with High-Risk Technologies (Basic Books, 1984).

#### Operations

<a id="ops-30"></a>
##### OPS-30 — Progressive Delivery & Release Safety

*Type:* Technical — Manages how change reaches production safely — decoupling deploy from release with feature flags, staged and canary rollouts, rollback readiness, and migration sequencing that bounds the blast radius of every change.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Follows the release process exactly — flags, staged rollout steps, verification checklists — verifies their change in production, and rolls back with guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Following the release process exactly -- flags, staged rollout steps, verification checklists -- and rolling back with guidance is Dreyfus's novice band: executing Humble & Farley's deployment-pipeline discipline as a fixed checklist rather than reasoning about it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Ships behind flags with a rollback plan by default, monitors rollouts and reverts on their own judgment when signals degrade, and writes changes that tolerate both versions running during rollout.
  — *Why this level:* Shipping behind flags with a rollback plan by default and reverting on their own judgment is independently applying Hodgson's release-toggle pattern to a known rollout, without escalation -- SFIA9 Level 3 Apply and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hodgson, Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags) (martinfowler.com, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs the rollout for risky changes — canary criteria, migration sequencing, flag lifecycle, kill switches — and reviews others' rollout plans for blast radius; the person teams ask how to ship something safely.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the rollout for risky changes -- canary criteria, migration sequencing, flag lifecycle, kill switches -- and reviewing others' blast-radius plans requires managing Hodgson's full toggle lifecycle and Humble & Farley's pipeline design for cases with no template -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hodgson, Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags) (martinfowler.com, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds progressive-delivery machinery multiple teams release through (flag platforms, automated canary analysis, automated rollback), retiring deploy patterns that cause repeat incidents and measurably raising deploy frequency.
  — *Why this level:* Building progressive-delivery machinery multiple teams release through and measurably raising deploy frequency is moving the organization's DORA metrics (Forsgren, Humble & Kim) -- deploy frequency, lead time, change-fail rate, MTTR -- SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise and Dreyfus's expert band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns release policy for an organization and its delivery metrics — rollout standards, freeze rules, environment strategy — dismantling ceremony that adds no safety.
