  — *Why this level:* Owning release policy and its delivery metrics for an organization, dismantling ceremony that adds no safety, is governing DORA's capability metrics as organizational policy rather than one team's practice -- the SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Sets how an entire company's software reaches customers — the risk posture products ship under — and defends it to executives, auditors, and regulators.
  — *Why this level:* Setting how an entire company's software reaches customers and defending that risk posture to executives, auditors and regulators is authoring release doctrine at the register Humble & Farley wrote Continuous Delivery in -- Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7 Set Strategy/Inspire. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).

#### Operating Mindset

<a id="ops-31"></a>
##### OPS-31 — Thinnest viable platform scoping

*Type:* Behavioral — Scopes an internal platform to the smallest set of APIs, tools, docs, and services that accelerates its consumers - making explicit build-buy-adopt decisions and retiring surface area that no longer earns its maintenance cost.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Checks for an existing tool, service, or open-source option before writing new code and raises what they find; asks whether a proposed task serves a real user need.
  — *Why this level:* Checking for an existing tool or service before writing new code and asking whether a task serves a real need is Dreyfus's novice band applying Team Topologies' build-buy-adopt awareness as a supplied checklist, not yet defending the decision. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Proposes wrapping or configuring an existing service instead of building new when it meets the need, writing the comparison down and defending removal of unused features in their own component.
  — *Why this level:* Proposing wrapping or configuring an existing service and defending removal of unused features in their own component is independently applying Skelton & Pais's Thinnest Viable Platform principle to a bounded piece of work -- SFIA9 Level 3 Apply and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Keeps a whole capability at its thinnest viable size - makes explicit, documented build-buy-adopt decisions, ships the thinnest version that serves proven demand, and retires surface area whose maintenance cost exceeds its value.
  — *Why this level:* Keeping a whole capability at its thinnest viable size, with documented build-buy-adopt decisions and retirement of surface area that no longer earns its cost, is Team Topologies' Thinnest Viable Platform concept applied at capability scope rather than one component -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Arbitrates overlap and sprawl across teams - merges duplicate offerings, cuts under-used surface, and sets the bar for what deserves to be shared platform at all.
  — *Why this level:* Arbitrating overlap and sprawl across teams -- merging duplicate offerings, cutting under-used surface, setting the bar for shared platform -- extends the Thinnest Viable Platform principle across team boundaries, the judgment call Team Topologies assigns to platform leadership, matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Shapes the organization's platform boundary - what the platform owns versus product teams versus vendors - and drives the organization to shed what it should not own.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping the organization's platform boundary -- what the platform owns versus product teams versus vendors -- is Team Topologies' team-boundary design applied as standing organizational policy -- the SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Sets the build-buy-adopt principles an entire company references, keeping company-scale platform investment proportional to the delivery it unlocks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the build-buy-adopt principles an entire company references, keeping platform investment proportional to the delivery it unlocks, is the register Skelton & Pais themselves wrote Team Topologies in -- authoring doctrine rather than applying it -- Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).

<a id="ops-32"></a>
##### OPS-32 — Cognitive-load management & abstraction design

*Type:* Behavioral — Designs tooling, interfaces, and abstractions to minimize the extraneous cognitive load imposed on the teams that consume them - deciding deliberately what consumers must and must not need to know, and measuring the load imposed.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Names the exact docs, errors, and setup steps that forced them to understand internals a consumer should not need, and files concrete simplification issues.
  — *Why this level:* Naming the exact docs, errors, and setup steps that forced understanding of internals a consumer should not need, and filing concrete simplification issues, is Dreyfus's novice band: identifying instances of Sweller's extraneous cognitive load under guidance, not yet designing them out. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sweller, Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning, Cognitive Science 12(2), 257-285 (1988).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Reduces the concepts and steps a consumer must hold to use their component - collapsing configuration, defaulting decisions, rewriting errors to say what to do next - and shows the before/after.
  — *Why this level:* Reducing the concepts and steps a consumer must hold -- collapsing configuration, defaulting decisions, rewriting errors -- and showing the before/after is independently cutting Sweller's extraneous load for a bounded component -- SFIA9 Level 3 Apply and Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sweller, Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning, Cognitive Science 12(2), 257-285 (1988).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs a capability's abstractions around what consumers must not have to know, so a first-time user succeeds without reading internals; measures load with time-to-first-success and support-ticket themes and treats regressions as defects.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a capability's abstractions around what consumers must not know, and measuring load with time-to-first-success and support-ticket themes, is applying Team Topologies' team-cognitive-load fit test to a whole capability with no template -- Dreyfus's competent/proficient band and SFIA9 Level 4 Enable. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Audits cognitive load across team boundaries - quantifying onboarding time, concepts-to-learn, and ticket themes - and drives the cross-boundary simplifications no single team could make.
  — *Why this level:* Auditing cognitive load across team boundaries -- quantifying onboarding time, concepts-to-learn, ticket themes -- and driving cross-boundary simplifications no single team could make is Team Topologies' cognitive-load assessment extended across multiple teams, matching SFIA9 Level 5 Ensure/Advise and Dreyfus's expert band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Makes cognitive load a first-class organizational measure with explicit load budgets, vetoing designs that externalize complexity onto consuming teams.
  — *Why this level:* Making cognitive load a first-class organizational measure with explicit load budgets, and vetoing designs that externalize complexity onto consuming teams, is Team Topologies' team-cognitive-load principle enforced as standing organizational policy -- the SFIA9 Level 6 Initiate/Influence tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes company-level technology and team-boundary choices explicitly around team cognitive load, arguing for fewer, deeper abstractions over sprawling optionality.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping company-level technology and team-boundary choices explicitly around cognitive load, arguing for fewer, deeper abstractions over sprawling optionality, is applying Sweller's cognitive-load theory at the register its own authors intended it to reshape instructional and system design -- Dreyfus's master band and SFIA9 Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Sweller, Cognitive Load During Problem Solving: Effects on Learning, Cognitive Science 12(2), 257-285 (1988).

### Security Engineering (SEC)

#### Identity & Access

<a id="sec-01"></a>
##### SEC-01 — Identity & access management

*Type:* Technical — Govern identities, authentication, and least-privilege authorization across systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Provisions and deprovisions accounts from documented procedures, with approvals and access reviewed before activation.
  — *Why this level:* Provisioning/deprovisioning from documented procedure with review is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist -- supervised execution of someone else's identity-lifecycle procedure, not yet judgment over access design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Configures roles, group membership, and authentication factors independently for standard joiners, movers, and leavers.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring roles, group membership, and auth factors independently for standard joiner/mover/leaver flows applies NIST 800-63's baseline assurance-level requirements to routine cases without redesigning them -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, SP 800-63, Revision 4 (2025).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex entitlement conflicts and designs least-privilege role models for ambiguous, cross-system access needs.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex entitlement conflicts and designing least-privilege role models for ambiguous cross-system needs is Dreyfus's competent band -- exactly the risk-based assurance-level selection NIST 800-63's 2025 revision requires organizations to judge case-by-case rather than follow a checklist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, SP 800-63, Revision 4 (2025).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the identity lifecycle and authorization architecture that other engineers adopt across the organization.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the identity lifecycle and authorization architecture other engineers adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying identity practice into reusable architecture rather than resolving one access model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets identity strategy, governs federation and privileged-access standards, and anticipates emerging access risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting identity strategy, governing federation/privileged-access standards, and anticipating emerging access risks is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what sound identity practice means for the field and shapes how others govern access.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what sound identity practice means for the field and shaping how others govern access is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register NIST's own Digital Identity Guidelines occupy as the reference federal identity standard. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Digital Identity Guidelines, SP 800-63, Revision 4 (2025).

<a id="sec-02"></a>
##### SEC-02 — Secrets & key management

*Type:* Technical — Securely generate, store, rotate, and distribute credentials and keys.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Stores and retrieves secrets using approved vaults, following rotation and handling procedures under review.
  — *Why this level:* Storing/retrieving secrets via approved vaults following documented rotation procedure under review is supervised execution of someone else's key-handling procedure -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Configures secret storage, rotation schedules, and access scoping independently for routine services.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring secret storage, rotation schedules, and access scoping independently for routine services applies NIST 800-57's key-lifecycle states (generation, activation, rotation) to a familiar service without redesigning the hierarchy -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Recommendation for Key Management: Part 1 - General, SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5 (2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs key hierarchies and rotation strategies for complex systems with conflicting availability and security constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Designing key hierarchies and rotation strategies for systems with conflicting availability and security constraints is Dreyfus's competent band -- resolving exactly the key-management trade-offs NIST 800-57 documents as requiring case-specific judgment, not a fixed schedule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Recommendation for Key Management: Part 1 - General, SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5 (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the secrets and key-management architecture and lifecycle others implement organization-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the secrets and key-management architecture and lifecycle others implement organization-wide is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the architecture other teams' key handling must conform to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets cryptographic-key governance and custody strategy and anticipates risks from emerging key threats.
  — *Why this level:* Setting cryptographic-key governance and custody strategy and anticipating emerging key threats is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative practice for secret and key stewardship that practitioners across the field adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative practice for secret and key stewardship that practitioners across the field adopt is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- practice recognized beyond one organization. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-03"></a>
##### SEC-03 — Cryptography & data protection

*Type:* Technical — Apply encryption, hashing, and key practices to protect data at rest and in transit.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies approved encryption settings and protects data following documented schemes, with choices reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Applying approved encryption settings from a documented scheme with choices reviewed is supervised execution of someone else's cryptographic design -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Selects and configures standard cryptographic primitives and data-protection controls independently for common cases.
  — *Why this level:* Selecting and configuring standard cryptographic primitives and controls independently for common cases applies FIPS 140-3's validated-module catalog to routine choices without evaluating module security itself -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules, FIPS PUB 140-3 (2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs encryption schemes and key-usage patterns for ambiguous threat and compliance trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing encryption schemes and key-usage patterns for ambiguous threat and compliance trade-offs is Dreyfus's competent band -- reasoning across FIPS 140-3's four security levels to fit a specific, non-routine risk and compliance posture. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules, FIPS PUB 140-3 (2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the cryptographic and data-protection patterns others reuse and resolves problems they cannot.
  — *Why this level:* Defining cryptographic and data-protection patterns others reuse, and resolving problems they cannot, is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying applied-cryptography judgment into patterns rather than solving one scheme. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets cryptographic standards and migration strategy and anticipates shifts such as quantum-resistant needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting cryptographic standards and migration strategy and anticipating quantum-resistant needs is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6, tracking exactly the migration NIST's 2024 post-quantum standards (FIPS 203) now require organizations to plan for. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard, FIPS 203 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what sound applied cryptography means for the discipline and influences industry data-protection norms.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what sound applied cryptography means for the discipline and influencing industry data-protection norms is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-04"></a>
##### SEC-04 — Zero-trust & policy-based access control

*Type:* Technical — Enforce continuous, context-aware authorization rather than implicit network trust.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements access policies from defined rules, verifying identity and context before granting under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing access policies from defined rules, verifying identity and context before granting under review, is supervised execution of someone else's policy set -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Authors and tests policy rules for standard resources, enforcing context-aware checks independently.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring and testing policy rules for standard resources, enforcing context-aware checks independently, applies NIST 800-207's core zero-trust tenets (per-request evaluation, least privilege) to a familiar resource without redesigning the architecture -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs segmentation and policy models that resolve ambiguous trust boundaries and hard exceptions.
  — *Why this level:* Designing segmentation and policy models that resolve ambiguous trust boundaries and hard exceptions is Dreyfus's competent band -- the architecture judgment NIST 800-207 leaves to the implementer once its logical components are understood. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the zero-trust architecture and policy framework other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the zero-trust architecture and policy framework other teams adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- moving from enforcing policy to authoring the framework others' policies must conform to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's zero-trust strategy and anticipates how trust models must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's zero-trust strategy and anticipating how trust models must evolve is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what mature zero-trust means for the field and shapes how the industry approaches it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what mature zero-trust means for the field and shaping how the industry approaches it is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register NIST's own zero-trust publication occupies as the field's reference architecture. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020).

#### Defensive Security

<a id="sec-05"></a>
##### SEC-05 — Threat modeling

*Type:* Technical — Systematically identify assets, threats, and attack surfaces to guide defenses.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Documents assets, entry points, and obvious threats for a component using a guided method, reviewed by others.
  — *Why this level:* Documenting assets, entry points, and obvious threats using a guided method, reviewed by others, is supervised application of someone else's method -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces complete threat models for standard systems independently, identifying realistic threats and mitigations.
  — *Why this level:* Producing complete threat models for standard systems independently applies Shostack's four-question STRIDE-based framing to a familiar system without adapting the method -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Shostack, Threat Modeling: Designing for Security (Wiley, 2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models complex, ambiguous architectures and prioritizes subtle, chained threats others miss.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling complex, ambiguous architectures and prioritizing subtle, chained threats others miss is Dreyfus's competent band -- exactly the skill Shostack distinguishes from mechanical STRIDE application: seeing threats the checklist doesn't surface. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Shostack, Threat Modeling: Designing for Security (Wiley, 2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the threat-modeling methodology and reusable patterns others adopt across teams.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the threat-modeling methodology and reusable patterns other teams adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the team-level methodology Shostack frames as the maturation from doing threat modeling to institutionalizing it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Shostack, Threat Modeling: Designing for Security (Wiley, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets threat-modeling strategy and anticipates classes of threats before they become prevalent.
  — *Why this level:* Setting threat-modeling strategy and anticipating classes of threats before they become prevalent is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative threat-modeling practice that shapes how the discipline reasons about risk.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative threat-modeling practice that shapes how the discipline reasons about risk is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register Shostack's own book occupies as the field's standard reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Shostack, Threat Modeling: Designing for Security (Wiley, 2014).

<a id="sec-06"></a>
##### SEC-06 — Vulnerability management & remediation

*Type:* Technical — Discover, prioritize, and drive remediation of weaknesses across the estate.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Triages and tracks scanner findings, verifying fixes against documented severity and remediation steps.
  — *Why this level:* Triaging and tracking scanner findings against documented severity and remediation steps is supervised execution of someone else's triage rules -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently validates, prioritizes, and coordinates remediation for routine vulnerabilities through closure.
  — *Why this level:* Independently validating, prioritizing, and coordinating remediation for routine vulnerabilities through closure applies CVSS 3.1's standard severity scoring to prioritize familiar findings without adapting the scoring model -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); FIRST.org, Common Vulnerability Scoring System version 3.1: Specification Document (2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous, hard-to-reproduce, or high-impact vulnerabilities and sets local remediation standards.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous, hard-to-reproduce, or high-impact vulnerabilities and setting local remediation standards is Dreyfus's competent band -- the enterprise-specific prioritization judgment NIST 800-40 requires beyond following a generic patch cadence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning: Preventive Maintenance for Technology, SP 800-40 Revision 4 (2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the vulnerability-management lifecycle and prioritization approach others follow.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the vulnerability-management lifecycle and prioritization approach others follow is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the enterprise patch-management strategy NIST 800-40 frames as a program others execute, not one remediation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Guide to Enterprise Patch Management Planning: Preventive Maintenance for Technology, SP 800-40 Revision 4 (2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise remediation strategy and anticipates exposure trends across the portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise remediation strategy and anticipating exposure trends across the portfolio is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what effective vulnerability management means for the field and influences its practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what effective vulnerability management means for the field and influencing its practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-07"></a>
##### SEC-07 — Security monitoring & detection

*Type:* Technical — Collect, correlate, and alert on signals to detect malicious activity.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Monitors alerts and triages events against documented playbooks, escalating uncertain cases for review.
  — *Why this level:* Monitoring alerts and triaging events against documented playbooks, escalating uncertain cases, is supervised execution of someone else's playbook -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tunes detections and investigates standard alerts independently, reducing routine false positives.
  — *Why this level:* Tuning detections and investigating standard alerts independently, reducing routine false positives, works at the easy-to-change, low-pain layers of Bianco's pyramid (hashes, IPs) without yet targeting adversary behavior -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bianco, The Pyramid of Pain (Enterprise Detection & Response blog, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Authors high-fidelity detections for novel and ambiguous adversary behavior across noisy signals.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring high-fidelity detections for novel and ambiguous adversary behavior across noisy signals is Dreyfus's competent band -- detecting at MITRE ATT&CK's TTP layer, the top of Bianco's pyramid that imposes the most cost on an adversary and requires independent judgment to build. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); MITRE, ATT&CK: Adversarial Tactics, Techniques and Common Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); Bianco, The Pyramid of Pain (Enterprise Detection & Response blog, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines detection engineering methods and coverage strategy that other analysts adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining detection engineering methods and coverage strategy other analysts adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying ATT&CK-mapped coverage into a reusable strategy rather than writing one detection. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); MITRE, ATT&CK: Adversarial Tactics, Techniques and Common Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets monitoring and detection strategy and anticipates evasion techniques before they appear.
  — *Why this level:* Setting monitoring and detection strategy and anticipating evasion techniques before they appear is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative detection practice and shapes how the discipline approaches monitoring.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative detection practice and shaping how the discipline approaches monitoring is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the register MITRE's own ATT&CK knowledge base occupies as the field's shared reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); MITRE, ATT&CK: Adversarial Tactics, Techniques and Common Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="sec-08"></a>
##### SEC-08 — Security hardening & baseline configuration

*Type:* Technical — Reduce attack surface by applying secure configuration standards to systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies hardening baselines from checklists and verifies configurations against documented standards.
  — *Why this level:* Applying hardening baselines from checklists and verifying configurations against documented standards is supervised checklist execution -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Hardens standard systems independently and adapts baselines to routine configuration variation.
  — *Why this level:* Hardening standard systems independently and adapting baselines to routine configuration variation applies a CIS Benchmark to a familiar platform without redesigning the baseline -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs hardening baselines for complex systems, balancing security against operational constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Designing hardening baselines for complex systems, balancing security against operational constraints, is Dreyfus's competent band -- the Level-1-versus-Level-2 trade-off CIS Benchmarks leave to the implementer's judgment for non-standard systems. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the hardening standards and reusable baselines other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the hardening standards and reusable baselines other teams adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the organization's own benchmark rather than applying a published one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets configuration-security strategy and anticipates hardening needs for emerging platforms.
  — *Why this level:* Setting configuration-security strategy and anticipating hardening needs for emerging platforms is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what authoritative hardening practice means for the field and influences accepted baselines.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what authoritative hardening practice means for the field and influencing accepted baselines is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- the consensus-setting register CIS's own benchmark process occupies. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Center for Internet Security, CIS Benchmarks (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="sec-09"></a>
##### SEC-09 — Supply-chain & artifact security

*Type:* Technical — Verify provenance and integrity of dependencies, builds, and deployed artifacts.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Verifies artifact provenance and signatures following documented checks, escalating anomalies for review.
  — *Why this level:* Verifying artifact provenance and signatures against documented checks, escalating anomalies for review, is supervised execution of someone else's verification checklist -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Configures signing, dependency scanning, and provenance controls independently for standard pipelines.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring signing, dependency scanning, and provenance controls independently for standard pipelines applies SLSA's lower build-integrity levels to a familiar pipeline without designing new controls -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenSSF, SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), Version 1.0 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs artifact-integrity and dependency-trust controls for complex, ambiguous supply chains.
  — *Why this level:* Designing artifact-integrity and dependency-trust controls for complex, ambiguous supply chains is Dreyfus's competent band -- reaching SLSA's higher build levels (hermetic, verified provenance) requires exactly the non-routine design judgment this level names. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenSSF, SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), Version 1.0 (2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the supply-chain security architecture and verification patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the supply-chain security architecture and verification patterns others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying an SLSA-aligned architecture other teams' pipelines must conform to, not securing one pipeline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenSSF, SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts), Version 1.0 (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets supply-chain assurance strategy and anticipates emerging artifact and dependency threats.
  — *Why this level:* Setting supply-chain assurance strategy and anticipating emerging artifact and dependency threats is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative supply-chain security practice that shapes industry expectations.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative supply-chain security practice that shapes industry expectations is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-10"></a>
##### SEC-10 — Digital forensics & malware analysis

*Type:* Technical — Investigate compromises by analyzing artifacts, evidence, and malicious code.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Collects and preserves evidence following chain-of-custody procedures, with analysis reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Collecting and preserving evidence following chain-of-custody procedures, with analysis reviewed, is supervised execution of a defined procedure -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Conducts standard forensic examinations and basic malware triage independently, documenting findings.
  — *Why this level:* Conducting standard forensic examinations and basic malware triage independently applies NIST 800-86's data-source examination process (files, OS, network, applications) to a routine case without adapting the method -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response, SP 800-86 (2006).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Reconstructs complex incidents and reverse-engineers obfuscated samples others cannot interpret.
  — *Why this level:* Reconstructing complex incidents and reverse-engineering obfuscated samples others cannot interpret is Dreyfus's competent band -- the static/dynamic reverse-engineering judgment Sikorski & Honig treat as the hard, non-recipe part separating triage from real analysis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sikorski & Honig, Practical Malware Analysis: The Hands-On Guide to Dissecting Malicious Software (No Starch Press, 2012).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines forensic and analysis methodologies and tooling approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining forensic and analysis methodologies and tooling approaches others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying the analysis techniques Sikorski & Honig catalog into a team methodology rather than analyzing one sample. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Sikorski & Honig, Practical Malware Analysis: The Hands-On Guide to Dissecting Malicious Software (No Starch Press, 2012).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets investigative strategy and anticipates evolving anti-forensic and malware techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting investigative strategy and anticipating evolving anti-forensic and malware techniques is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative forensic and malware-analysis practice that shapes the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative forensic and malware-analysis practice that shapes the discipline is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Offensive Security

<a id="sec-11"></a>
##### SEC-11 — Penetration testing & offensive security

*Type:* Technical — Emulate adversaries to find and demonstrate exploitable weaknesses.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes scoped test cases under guidance, documenting findings against an approved methodology.
  — *Why this level:* Executing scoped test cases under guidance against an approved methodology is supervised execution of someone else's test plan -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Conducts standard penetration tests independently and reports exploitable findings with clear evidence.
  — *Why this level:* Conducting standard penetration tests independently and reporting exploitable findings with clear evidence applies NIST 800-115's five-phase testing process to a familiar target without adapting the methodology -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment, SP 800-115 (2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Chains subtle weaknesses into impactful attacks in ambiguous, well-defended environments.
  — *Why this level:* Chaining subtle weaknesses into impactful attacks in ambiguous, well-defended environments is Dreyfus's competent band -- the exploitation-phase judgment NIST 800-115 names as requiring skilled, non-mechanical adaptation to the target. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment, SP 800-115 (2008).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines testing methodology and tradecraft that other testers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining testing methodology and tradecraft other testers adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the methodology other testers execute rather than executing one test. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets offensive-testing strategy and anticipates attack surfaces before they are widely understood.
  — *Why this level:* Setting offensive-testing strategy and anticipating attack surfaces before they are widely understood is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what rigorous offensive testing means for the field and influences its practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what rigorous offensive testing means for the field and influencing its practice is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-12"></a>
##### SEC-12 — Adversarial testing of AI systems / red teaming

*Type:* Technical — Probe AI systems for jailbreaks, prompt injection, and unsafe or harmful behavior.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs predefined adversarial prompts and probes, recording model failures under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Running predefined adversarial prompts and probes, recording model failures under guidance, is supervised execution of someone else's test set -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and executes standard adversarial tests independently, documenting reproducible weaknesses.
  — *Why this level:* Designing and executing standard adversarial tests independently, documenting reproducible weaknesses, applies OWASP's cataloged LLM risk classes (prompt injection, insecure output handling) to a familiar system without discovering new failure modes -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications (2025).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Discovers novel, ambiguous failure modes and bypasses in well-guarded AI systems.
  — *Why this level:* Discovering novel, ambiguous failure modes and bypasses in well-guarded AI systems is Dreyfus's competent band -- surfacing risks NIST AI 600-1's twelve generative-AI risk categories name as novel-to-GenAI, not yet covered by a known probe. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile, NIST AI 600-1 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines AI red-teaming methodology and evaluation patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining AI red-teaming methodology and evaluation patterns others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying probing technique into a reusable evaluation pattern others apply, rather than testing one system. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications (2025).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets adversarial-AI testing strategy and anticipates emerging model attack classes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting adversarial-AI testing strategy and anticipating emerging model attack classes is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative AI red-teaming practice that shapes how the field tests AI safety.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative AI red-teaming practice that shapes how the field tests AI safety is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-13"></a>
##### SEC-13 — Exploit development & weakness research

*Type:* Technical — Research and weaponize flaws to validate real-world exploitability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Reproduces known weaknesses and adapts existing proof-of-concepts under close review.
  — *Why this level:* Reproducing known weaknesses and adapting existing proof-of-concepts under close review is supervised adaptation of someone else's exploit -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Develops reliable exploits for standard, documented weakness classes independently.
  — *Why this level:* Developing reliable exploits for standard, documented weakness classes independently applies MITRE's cataloged CWE weakness classes to a familiar target without discovering a new class -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); MITRE, Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Discovers and weaponizes novel weaknesses in hardened targets others cannot crack.
  — *Why this level:* Discovering and weaponizing novel weaknesses in hardened targets others cannot crack is Dreyfus's competent band -- exactly the primary-research skill the Shellcoder's Handbook teaches beyond applying a known technique: finding and reliably triggering a new bug class. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Anley, Heasman, Lindner & Richarte, The Shellcoder's Handbook: Discovering and Exploiting Security Holes, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2007).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines research techniques and exploitation primitives other researchers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining research techniques and exploitation primitives other researchers adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring reusable primitives of the kind the Handbook's own later chapters teach as craft, not solving one bug. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Anley, Heasman, Lindner & Richarte, The Shellcoder's Handbook: Discovering and Exploiting Security Holes, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2007).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets weakness-research direction and anticipates new exploitation classes ahead of the field.
  — *Why this level:* Setting weakness-research direction and anticipating new exploitation classes ahead of the field is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative exploit-research practice and shapes the discipline's frontier.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative exploit-research practice and shaping the discipline's frontier is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-14"></a>
##### SEC-14 — Social engineering & human-factor testing

*Type:* Technical — Assess susceptibility to manipulation through pretexting and phishing simulations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes approved phishing or pretext scripts under supervision and records target responses.
  — *Why this level:* Executing approved phishing or pretext scripts under supervision and recording target responses is supervised execution of someone else's script -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and runs standard social-engineering campaigns independently within agreed rules of engagement.
  — *Why this level:* Designing and running standard social-engineering campaigns independently within agreed rules of engagement applies Hadnagy's cataloged elicitation and pretexting techniques to a familiar scenario without inventing new tradecraft -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hadnagy, Social Engineering: The Science of Human Hacking, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Crafts convincing, context-aware pretexts that succeed against security-aware, ambiguous targets.
  — *Why this level:* Crafting convincing, context-aware pretexts that succeed against security-aware, ambiguous targets is Dreyfus's competent band -- the psychological tailoring Hadnagy treats as the science above scripted pretexting, requiring an independent read of a specific target. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hadnagy, Social Engineering: The Science of Human Hacking, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines human-factor testing methodology and ethical guardrails others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining human-factor testing methodology and ethical guardrails others adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the methodology and rules of engagement other testers follow, the professionalization Hadnagy's own framework represents. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hadnagy, Social Engineering: The Science of Human Hacking, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets human-factor testing strategy and anticipates evolving manipulation techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting human-factor testing strategy and anticipating evolving manipulation techniques is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative human-factor testing practice that shapes the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative human-factor testing practice that shapes the discipline is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Governance & Mindset

<a id="sec-15"></a>
##### SEC-15 — Security governance, risk & policy

*Type:* Technical — Frame risk, controls, and policy to align security with organizational obligations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains policy documents and risk-register entries following templates, reviewed before publication.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining policy documents and risk-register entries from templates, reviewed before publication, is supervised documentation against a defined template -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Drafts standard policies and assesses routine risks independently against established frameworks.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting standard policies and assessing routine risks independently against established frameworks applies NIST CSF 2.0's Identify/Protect/Detect/Respond/Recover functions to routine assessment without designing new governance -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, NIST CSWP 29 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous risk trade-offs and tailors governance for complex, contested contexts.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous risk trade-offs and tailoring governance for complex, contested contexts is Dreyfus's competent band -- the risk-based tailoring judgment ISO/IEC 27001:2022's ISMS requires for a specific organization's context, not checklist compliance. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC, Information Security, Cybersecurity and Privacy Protection - Information Security Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 27001:2022.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the governance and risk frameworks other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the governance and risk frameworks other teams adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the organization-wide ISMS other teams must conform to rather than assessing one risk. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC, Information Security, Cybersecurity and Privacy Protection - Information Security Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 27001:2022.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise security governance strategy and anticipates regulatory and risk shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise security governance strategy and anticipating regulatory and risk shifts is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6, exercising exactly the Govern function CSF 2.0 added to name this strategic layer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, NIST CSWP 29 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what sound security governance means for the field and influences external standards.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what sound security governance means for the field and influencing external standards is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-16"></a>
##### SEC-16 — Adversarial mindset & ethical conduct

*Type:* Behavioral — Think like an attacker while operating within legal and ethical boundaries.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Questions assumptions on prompting and follows ethical and authorization rules under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Questioning assumptions on prompting and following ethical and authorization rules under guidance is supervised, rule-following conduct -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently spots realistic abuse cases and consistently operates within ethical boundaries.
  — *Why this level:* Independently spotting realistic abuse cases and consistently operating within ethical boundaries applies ISC2's Code of Ethics canons (act honorably, provide diligent service) unsupervised in familiar situations -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISC2, Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Anticipates subtle attacker reasoning in ambiguous situations while modeling sound ethical judgment.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating subtle attacker reasoning in ambiguous situations while modeling sound ethical judgment is Dreyfus's competent band -- resolving cases the Code of Ethics' canons don't explicitly answer, which is exactly where independent ethical judgment is required. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISC2, Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Teaches adversarial thinking and ethical decision-making that others adopt as their model.
  — *Why this level:* Teaching adversarial thinking and ethical decision-making that others adopt as their model is Dreyfus's proficient band -- becoming the practical exemplar of the Code's 'advance and protect the profession' canon for a team. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISC2, Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the standard for ethical adversarial practice and anticipates emerging ethical dilemmas.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the standard for ethical adversarial practice and anticipating emerging ethical dilemmas is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what principled adversarial conduct means for the discipline and shapes its norms.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what principled adversarial conduct means for the discipline and shaping its norms is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sec-17"></a>
##### SEC-17 — Security awareness & shift-left advocacy

*Type:* Behavioral — Champion secure practices early and embed security into everyday engineering.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Delivers prepared awareness material and flags security concerns early under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering prepared awareness material and flagging security concerns early under guidance is supervised delivery of someone else's material -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tailors awareness content and embeds standard secure practices into routine team workflows independently.
  — *Why this level:* Tailoring awareness content and embedding standard secure practices into routine team workflows independently applies SAMM's foundational practice activities to a familiar team without designing a maturity program -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP, Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM) v2 (2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Drives security adoption in resistant, ambiguous contexts and sets the local shift-left standard.
  — *Why this level:* Driving security adoption in resistant, ambiguous contexts and setting the local shift-left standard is Dreyfus's competent band -- pushing a team from SAMM's foundational activities toward its higher maturity levels through judgment, not a script. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP, Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM) v2 (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines awareness and shift-left programs other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining awareness and shift-left programs other teams adopt is Dreyfus's proficient band -- authoring the SAMM-aligned program other teams execute rather than running one campaign. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP, Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM) v2 (2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's security-culture strategy and anticipates shifts in developer behavior.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's security-culture strategy and anticipating shifts in developer behavior is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what effective security culture means for the field and influences how it is fostered.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what effective security culture means for the field and influencing how it is fostered is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Defensive Security

<a id="sec-18"></a>
##### SEC-18 — Guardrails & policy as code

*Type:* Technical — Encodes preventive controls as versioned, tested, automatically enforced policy - admission checks, pipeline gates, configuration rules - with actionable violation messages and governed exception paths, so the safe way is the default way.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Works within existing guardrails, reads a policy violation to its cause instead of requesting an exception, and explains what each guardrail protects against.
  — *Why this level:* Working within existing guardrails and reading a violation to its cause instead of requesting an exception is supervised, rule-abiding use of someone else's controls -- Dreyfus novice, SFIA Level 2. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Writes and tests policy rules for a component - admission checks, pipeline gates - with low false-positive rates and violation messages that tell the user how to comply.
  — *Why this level:* Writing and testing policy rules for a component with low false-positive rates and actionable violation messages applies Open Policy Agent's Rego policy-as-code model to a bounded component without designing the overall guardrail architecture -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Open Policy Agent, Documentation (CNCF graduated project, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs the guardrail architecture for a capability - what is blocked, warned, or audited, with documented threat reasoning - tuned so the safe path is the fast path, and runs an audited exception workflow without becoming the bottleneck.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the guardrail architecture for a capability -- what is blocked, warned, or audited, tuned so the safe path is the fast path -- and running an audited exception workflow is Dreyfus's competent band -- exactly the policy-design judgment a policy engine like OPA enforces but does not make for you. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Open Policy Agent, Documentation (CNCF graduated project, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Harmonizes policy across teams into a coherent, versioned policy library with a governed exception process, and adjudicates escalated safety-versus-velocity disputes.
  — *Why this level:* Harmonizing policy across teams into a coherent, versioned policy library with a governed exception process, and adjudicating safety-versus-velocity disputes, is Dreyfus's proficient band -- codifying guardrail judgment into a library and adjudication process others use, not writing one policy. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns an organization's preventive-control strategy with security partners - the control catalog, its coverage, and the evidence it works - moving enforcement from review-time to platform-time.
  — *Why this level:* Owning an organization's preventive-control strategy with security partners -- the control catalog, its coverage, and the evidence it works -- is org-wide anticipatory standard-setting -- Dreyfus's expert band, SFIA Level 6, operating the Govern function CSF 2.0 names at portfolio scale. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, NIST CSWP 29 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Sets an organization-defining balance of enablement and control, accountable for guardrails that hold under audit and attack without throttling delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Setting an organization-defining balance of enablement and control, accountable for guardrails that hold under audit and attack without throttling delivery, is Dreyfus's master band, SFIA Level 7 -- ultimate organizational accountability for the preventive-control system, matching this capability's own framing of the top level as organization-defining rather than externally field-shaping. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

### Quality Engineering & Test (QA)

#### Test Strategy & Design

<a id="qa-01"></a>
##### QA-01 — Test strategy & planning

*Type:* Technical — Defining test scope, levels, priorities, and coverage goals aligned to risk and product objectives.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts test plans from templates for defined features, reviewed before execution.
  — *Why this level:* Filling in a prescribed test-plan template for a defined feature under review is exactly ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1's documented test-planning process followed as given rules, not yet adapted to context -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC/IEEE, Software and Systems Engineering — Software Testing — Part 1: General Concepts, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-1:2022.
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces complete test strategies for standard projects independently, scoping coverage and risk.
