  — *Why this level:* Independently scoping coverage and risk for a standard, well-understood project is the ISTQB Foundation syllabus's bar for applying the standard test process without guidance -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, where routine variation no longer needs escalation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISTQB, Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus, Version 4.0 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Devises test strategies for ambiguous, high-risk programs balancing coverage, time, and cost.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing coverage, time, and cost for ambiguous, high-risk programs is the judgment call Craig & Jaskiel's systematic risk-based strategy method exists to teach, not a checklist -- the Dreyfus competent band, autonomous and setting the local standard. *Sources:* Craig & Jaskiel, Systematic Software Testing (Artech House, 2002); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the test-strategy approach and planning patterns other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the strategy template other teams reuse is the same level of contribution Craig & Jaskiel's own book makes to the field, formalized as SFIA9's 'ensure/advise' responsibility band: defining method, not just applying it. *Sources:* Craig & Jaskiel, Systematic Software Testing (Artech House, 2002); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organizational quality strategy and anticipates how testing must evolve with delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide quality strategy and anticipating how testing must change as delivery evolves is SFIA9's strategy-setting/influence band applied to the empirical link DORA's research draws between test-strategy maturity and elite delivery performance. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what effective test strategy means for the discipline and influences its practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what effective test strategy means for the discipline, beyond one org, is SFIA9's highest originate/set-policy band matched to IEEE SWEBOK's practitioner-to-discipline-shaper transition -- the Dreyfus master band, externally credible. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="qa-02"></a>
##### QA-02 — Test case design & techniques

*Type:* Technical — Deriving effective test cases using equivalence, boundary, decision-table, and state-based techniques.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes test cases from clear requirements using prescribed techniques, reviewed for coverage.
  — *Why this level:* Applying a named technique (equivalence partitioning, boundary analysis) to clear requirements under review, without judging which technique fits, is exactly the rule-following Myers' foundational catalog was written to teach novices -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Myers, Sandler & Badgett, The Art of Software Testing, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs effective test cases independently, applying standard techniques to cover routine variation.
  — *Why this level:* Independently selecting and applying Myers' standard techniques to cover routine variation, without a reviewer choosing the technique, is the advanced-beginner band: recognized situations matched to known methods. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Myers, Sandler & Badgett, The Art of Software Testing, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs minimal, high-yield cases for ambiguous requirements and complex condition combinations.
  — *Why this level:* Designing minimal, high-yield cases for ambiguous requirements and complex decision-table combinations is Myers' technique catalog applied with judgment where no single named technique alone resolves the case -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Myers, Sandler & Badgett, The Art of Software Testing, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2011).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines case-design techniques and reusable patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring reusable case-design patterns other testers adopt moves beyond applying the ISTQB syllabus's named techniques to contributing to how they're taught internally -- SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISTQB, Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus, Version 4.0 (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets case-design standards and anticipates techniques needed for new system classes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's case-design standard and anticipating which techniques new system classes (e.g. ML, event-driven) will need is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- direction-setting, not local practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative test-design practice that shapes how the discipline designs tests.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline designs tests, beyond a single employer, is SFIA9's highest originate band matched to IEEE SWEBOK's testing-techniques knowledge area -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); IEEE Computer Society, Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge (SWEBOK), Version 3.0 (2014).

<a id="qa-03"></a>
##### QA-03 — Exploratory & manual testing

*Type:* Technical — Unscripted investigative testing to uncover defects, usability issues, and unspecified behaviors.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes guided exploratory sessions and reports defects clearly under review.
  — *Why this level:* Executing a guided exploratory session against someone else's charter and reporting findings for review is Kaner, Bach & Pettichord's context-driven school describing this as testing under close direction -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kaner, Bach & Pettichord, Lessons Learned in Software Testing: A Context-Driven Approach (Wiley, 2001).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs self-directed exploratory sessions independently, uncovering issues beyond scripted cases.
  — *Why this level:* Running self-directed sessions from a standard charter independently is Hendrickson's session-based exploratory-testing practice applied without a coach setting the charter -- the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hendrickson, Explore It!: Reduce Risk and Increase Confidence with Exploratory Testing (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Uncovers subtle, high-impact defects in ambiguous areas through skilled exploratory charters.
  — *Why this level:* Writing one's own charters to find subtle, high-impact defects in ambiguous, unfamiliar areas is the skilled, autonomous investigative judgment Kaner, Bach & Pettichord's 'lessons learned' explicitly distinguish from scripted execution -- Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Kaner, Bach & Pettichord, Lessons Learned in Software Testing: A Context-Driven Approach (Wiley, 2001); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines exploratory methods and charters others adopt to find what scripts miss.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the charter templates and exploratory methods a team reuses is Hendrickson's own contribution to the field, formalized as SFIA9's method-defining band -- teaching the skilled-but-still-local practice of P3. *Sources:* Hendrickson, Explore It!: Reduce Risk and Increase Confidence with Exploratory Testing (Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2013); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets exploratory-testing strategy and anticipates where investigative effort yields most value.
  — *Why this level:* Deciding where exploratory investment yields the most value across a whole org's portfolio, not one team's backlog, is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- anticipating direction rather than reacting to it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative exploratory practice that shapes how the discipline explores quality.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline practices exploratory testing, externally credible beyond one employer, extends the context-driven school Kaner, Bach & Pettichord founded to SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kaner, Bach & Pettichord, Lessons Learned in Software Testing: A Context-Driven Approach (Wiley, 2001).

<a id="qa-04"></a>
##### QA-04 — Risk-based & shift-left quality

*Type:* Behavioral — Prioritizing quality effort by risk and embedding testing early across the delivery lifecycle.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Identifies obvious quality risks and contributes early-stage checks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Contributing early-stage checks that someone else designed, under guidance, is following Smith's shift-left prescription as a given rule rather than judging where risk actually concentrates -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Smith, Shift-Left Testing, Dr. Dobb's Journal 26(9) (2001).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Prioritizes routine testing by risk and embeds standard quality checks early independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently embedding Smith's 'catch bugs when they're cheap' shift-left checks into routine, well-understood work is the advanced-beginner band: a known practice applied without a coach. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Smith, Shift-Left Testing, Dr. Dobb's Journal 26(9) (2001).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Drives risk-based focus across ambiguous, high-stakes work and sets the local shift-left standard.
  — *Why this level:* Driving risk-based focus across ambiguous, high-stakes work and setting the local shift-left standard is where Smith's original prescription meets DORA's empirical finding that shift-left/continuous-testing capability predicts elite delivery performance -- the Dreyfus competent band, autonomous and standard-setting. *Sources:* Smith, Shift-Left Testing, Dr. Dobb's Journal 26(9) (2001); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the risk-based and shift-left approach other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the risk-based, shift-left approach other teams adopt is turning DORA's capability into a locally-defined method -- SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band, beyond applying the practice to teaching it. *Sources:* DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organizational risk-based quality strategy and anticipates where quality must move earlier.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide risk-based quality strategy and anticipating where quality must move earlier as delivery changes is SFIA9's strategy-setting band applied at the scale DORA measures across whole organizations. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what mature shift-left quality means for the field and influences its adoption.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what mature shift-left quality means for the field, the way Smith's 2001 article originated the term itself, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band, shaping industry vocabulary and practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Smith, Shift-Left Testing, Dr. Dobb's Journal 26(9) (2001).

#### Test Automation

<a id="qa-05"></a>
##### QA-05 — Test automation architecture

*Type:* Technical — Designing maintainable, layered automation frameworks and reusable test infrastructure.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds tests to an existing automation framework following established patterns under review.
  — *Why this level:* Adding tests that follow an existing framework's established fixture and pattern conventions, reviewed before merge, is applying Meszaros' xUnit patterns as given rules -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Meszaros, xUnit Test Patterns: Refactoring Test Code (Addison-Wesley, 2007).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and extends automation suites independently using sound, maintainable structure.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and extending suites using Meszaros' maintainable-structure patterns (without a reviewer choosing them) on standard work is the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Meszaros, xUnit Test Patterns: Refactoring Test Code (Addison-Wesley, 2007).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs resilient automation frameworks for complex, ambiguous systems and flaky conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a resilient framework from scratch for complex, ambiguous systems is applying Meszaros' pattern catalog and Cohn's testing-pyramid layering judgment to a novel case with no established precedent -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Meszaros, xUnit Test Patterns: Refactoring Test Code (Addison-Wesley, 2007); Cohn, Succeeding with Agile: Software Development Using Scrum (Addison-Wesley, 2009).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the automation architecture and patterns other engineers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the automation architecture and pattern set other engineers reuse is the same contribution Meszaros' own catalog makes to the field, formalized as SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Meszaros, xUnit Test Patterns: Refactoring Test Code (Addison-Wesley, 2007); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets automation strategy and anticipates architectural needs as systems and pipelines evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide automation strategy and anticipating how pyramid-layer needs shift as systems and pipelines evolve is SFIA9's strategy-setting band applied to Cohn's pyramid model at organizational scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cohn, Succeeding with Agile: Software Development Using Scrum (Addison-Wesley, 2009).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative test-automation architecture that shapes how the discipline builds it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline builds test-automation architecture, externally credible the way Meszaros' patterns became an industry reference, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Meszaros, xUnit Test Patterns: Refactoring Test Code (Addison-Wesley, 2007).

<a id="qa-06"></a>
##### QA-06 — UI & end-to-end automation

*Type:* Technical — Automating user-facing flows reliably across interfaces while minimizing flakiness.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Automates defined UI flows using existing patterns, with scripts reviewed for reliability.
  — *Why this level:* Automating a defined flow through the WebDriver protocol using existing locator patterns, reviewed for reliability, is executing a given rule rather than judging why a locator is fragile -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C, WebDriver, Level 2 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and maintains stable end-to-end UI tests independently for standard journeys.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and maintaining stable WebDriver-based tests for standard, well-understood journeys is the advanced-beginner band: routine variation handled without escalation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C, WebDriver, Level 2 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Stabilizes flaky, complex end-to-end flows and designs resilient locator and wait strategies.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and eliminating flakiness in complex flows is exactly the systematic non-determinism triage Fowler's article describes -- isolation, waits, and environment causes -- applied autonomously to ambiguous, hard-to-reproduce failures: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Fowler, Eradicating Non-Determinism in Tests (martinfowler.com, 2011); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines UI and end-to-end automation patterns others adopt for reliability at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the locator and wait-strategy patterns a team reuses to prevent Fowler's non-determinism failure modes at scale is SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band, beyond fixing one's own flaky tests. *Sources:* Fowler, Eradicating Non-Determinism in Tests (martinfowler.com, 2011); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets end-to-end automation strategy and anticipates challenges from evolving interfaces.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide end-to-end strategy and anticipating how evolving interfaces (new frameworks, shadow DOM, WebDriver BiDi) will strain automation is SFIA9's strategic-influence band, anticipating direction rather than reacting to breakage. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); W3C, WebDriver, Level 2 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative end-to-end automation practice that shapes the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline treats end-to-end reliability, the way Fowler's article became the field's reference on non-determinism, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fowler, Eradicating Non-Determinism in Tests (martinfowler.com, 2011).

<a id="qa-07"></a>
##### QA-07 — API & service-level testing

*Type:* Technical — Validating contracts, integrations, and service behavior below the user interface.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes and extends API tests from examples, validating responses under review.
  — *Why this level:* Extending API tests from given examples and validating responses against a documented OpenAPI contract, under review, is following the contract's rules without judging what the contract should say -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenAPI Initiative, OpenAPI Specification v3.1.0 (2021).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and automates service-level tests independently for standard contracts and flows.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing tests against standard, well-specified OpenAPI contracts and flows is the advanced-beginner band: applying the standard without a reviewer's guidance. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenAPI Initiative, OpenAPI Specification v3.1.0 (2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Tests complex service interactions, contracts, and edge behaviors in ambiguous integrations.
  — *Why this level:* Testing complex, ambiguous multi-service interactions and edge behaviors is the consumer-driven-contract judgment Robinson's pattern was written to formalize where a static spec alone doesn't resolve provider/consumer expectations -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Robinson, Consumer-Driven Contracts: A Service Evolution Pattern (martinfowler.com, 2006); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines service-testing and contract-verification patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the contract-verification pattern a team adopts is the same contribution Robinson's own pattern made to the field, formalized as SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Robinson, Consumer-Driven Contracts: A Service Evolution Pattern (martinfowler.com, 2006); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets service-level testing strategy and anticipates needs as service architectures evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide service-testing strategy and anticipating how contract testing must evolve as the service architecture grows is SFIA9's strategy-setting band applied to Robinson's contract-evolution pattern at organizational scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Robinson, Consumer-Driven Contracts: A Service Evolution Pattern (martinfowler.com, 2006).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative service-testing practice that shapes how the discipline tests services.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline validates services against machine-readable contracts, the way the OpenAPI standard itself became the industry's shared contract language, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OpenAPI Initiative, OpenAPI Specification v3.1.0 (2021).

<a id="qa-08"></a>
##### QA-08 — Continuous testing in delivery pipelines

*Type:* Technical — Integrating automated quality gates into build and deployment pipelines for fast feedback.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds tests to existing pipeline stages following defined configuration, reviewed before merge.
  — *Why this level:* Adding a test to an existing pipeline stage by following defined configuration, reviewed before merge, is executing Humble & Farley's deployment-pipeline structure as a given rule -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Integrates and maintains automated test stages independently within standard pipelines.
  — *Why this level:* Independently integrating and maintaining test stages within a standard, already-designed pipeline is the advanced-beginner band: applying Humble & Farley's pipeline discipline without redesigning it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs fast, reliable test gating for complex pipelines balancing speed and confidence.
  — *Why this level:* Designing gating that balances speed and confidence for a complex pipeline is the deployment-pipeline design judgment Humble & Farley's book centers on, validated by DORA's empirical finding that this balance predicts delivery performance -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines continuous-testing patterns and gating strategy other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the gating strategy other teams adopt is contributing at the level Humble & Farley's own book does for the field, formalized as SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets continuous-testing strategy and anticipates how quality gates must evolve with delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide continuous-testing strategy and anticipating how gates must evolve as delivery practice changes is SFIA9's strategy-setting band applied to DORA's org-scale delivery-capability research. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative continuous-testing practice that shapes the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline gates delivery pipelines, the way Humble & Farley's book became the field's reference on continuous delivery, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).

#### Specialized Testing

<a id="qa-09"></a>
##### QA-09 — Performance & load testing

*Type:* Technical — Assessing responsiveness, throughput, and stability under expected and peak demand.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs predefined performance scenarios and records results against documented thresholds.
  — *Why this level:* Running a predefined scenario and checking results against documented thresholds (e.g. Core Web Vitals' fixed LCP/INP/CLS budgets) without judging what threshold fits the product is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Core Web Vitals, built on the Chrome User Experience Report (2020-).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and executes standard load tests independently, identifying obvious bottlenecks.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing standard load tests and spotting obvious bottlenecks is Molyneaux's baseline performance-testing methodology applied without a mentor's guidance -- the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Molyneaux, The Art of Application Performance Testing, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses subtle performance issues under realistic, ambiguous load and contention conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing subtle, non-obvious performance issues under realistic, ambiguous contention is Molyneaux's strategy-to-tools methodology applied autonomously to hard cases a checklist doesn't resolve -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Molyneaux, The Art of Application Performance Testing, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2014); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines performance-testing methodology and modeling approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the performance-modeling approach other engineers adopt is the same contribution Molyneaux's own book makes to the field, formalized as SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Molyneaux, The Art of Application Performance Testing, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2014); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets performance-engineering strategy and anticipates scaling limits before they bite.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide performance-engineering strategy and anticipating scaling limits before they bite -- rather than reacting once a Core Web Vitals field threshold is breached -- is SFIA9's strategic-influence band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Core Web Vitals, built on the Chrome User Experience Report (2020-).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative performance-testing practice that shapes how the discipline measures it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline measures performance, externally credible beyond one employer, is SFIA9's highest originate band applied to Molyneaux's strategy-to-tools methodology -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Molyneaux, The Art of Application Performance Testing, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2014).

<a id="qa-10"></a>
##### QA-10 — Security & vulnerability testing

*Type:* Technical — Probing systems for weaknesses, misconfigurations, and exploitable flaws.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs prescribed security test cases and reports findings against documented criteria under review.
  — *Why this level:* Running a prescribed OWASP WSTG test case against documented criteria, with findings reviewed, is following a named methodology's steps as given rules -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG) v4.2 (2020).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Conducts standard security and vulnerability tests independently, validating common weaknesses.
  — *Why this level:* Independently conducting standard OWASP WSTG tests for common, well-catalogued weaknesses is the advanced-beginner band: applying the guide's standard test cases without escalation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG) v4.2 (2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Uncovers subtle security defects in ambiguous flows and chains them into meaningful risk.
  — *Why this level:* Uncovering subtle defects in ambiguous flows and chaining them into meaningful risk is the assessment judgment NIST SP 800-115 distinguishes from mechanical scanning -- autonomous technique selection and interpretation, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* NIST, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment, SP 800-115 (2008); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines security-testing methods integrated into quality practice that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the security-testing method a QA team integrates into its practice, adapting NIST SP 800-115's assessment framework locally, is SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* NIST, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment, SP 800-115 (2008); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets security-testing strategy within quality and anticipates emerging weakness classes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide security-testing strategy and anticipating emerging weakness classes ahead of the next OWASP guide revision is SFIA9's strategic-influence band, not just executing the current guide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OWASP Foundation, OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG) v4.2 (2020).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative security-in-quality practice that shapes the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline integrates security assessment into quality practice, externally credible the way NIST's own framework shapes federal and industry assessment practice, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment, SP 800-115 (2008).

<a id="qa-11"></a>
##### QA-11 — Accessibility & compatibility testing

*Type:* Technical — Verifying inclusive usability and consistent behavior across devices, platforms, and assistive tech.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs prescribed accessibility and compatibility checks, reporting issues against standards under review.
  — *Why this level:* Checking a page against prescribed WCAG 2.2 success criteria and reporting deviations for review, without judging which criteria matter most, is applying a standard's rules as given -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tests standard accessibility and cross-environment compatibility independently against guidelines.
  — *Why this level:* Independently testing standard flows against WCAG 2.2 and WAI-ARIA 1.2 guidelines for common assistive-technology patterns is the advanced-beginner band: applying published guidelines without a reviewer's interpretation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023); W3C, Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses subtle accessibility and compatibility defects across ambiguous, diverse contexts.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing subtle ARIA-semantics defects and cross-engine compatibility gaps across diverse, ambiguous contexts is the judgment WAI-ARIA's role/state model requires beyond checklist conformance, matched to the kind of interoperability gap the Web Platform Tests Interop Project exists to surface -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* W3C, Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 (2023); WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines accessibility and compatibility testing approaches other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the accessibility-testing approach other teams adopt, translating WCAG 2.2 conformance into a reusable internal method, is SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets inclusive-quality strategy and anticipates accessibility needs across emerging contexts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide inclusive-quality strategy and anticipating accessibility/compatibility needs in emerging contexts (new form factors, assistive tech) is SFIA9's strategic-influence band, tracking the same forward-looking gap-closing the Interop Project pursues across browser engines. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); WebKit, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft et al., Web Platform Tests Interop Project (2026).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative accessibility-testing practice that shapes how the discipline approaches it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline approaches accessibility testing, externally credible the way W3C's own WCAG working group shapes global practice, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023).

#### Quality Operations

<a id="qa-12"></a>
##### QA-12 — Test data & environment management

*Type:* Technical — Provisioning, masking, and maintaining realistic data and stable environments for testing.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Provisions test data and environments from documented procedures under review.
  — *Why this level:* Provisioning test data by following a documented masking procedure under review, without judging re-identification risk, is applying NIST's de-identification guidance as a given rule -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, De-Identification of Personal Information, NISTIR 8053 (2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard test data and environments independently, ensuring consistent, valid conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing standard, already-defined environments to ensure consistent, valid conditions is Humble & Farley's production-like-environment discipline applied without redesigning it -- the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs reliable, representative data and environment strategies for complex, ambiguous needs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a data and environment strategy for complex, ambiguous needs -- realistic-but-safe data, reproducible infrastructure -- is combining NIST's de-identification risk judgment with Humble & Farley's environment-management discipline where no documented procedure already covers the case: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* NIST, De-Identification of Personal Information, NISTIR 8053 (2015); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines test-data and environment-management patterns other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the data and environment-management pattern other teams adopt is contributing at the level Humble & Farley's own book does for the field, formalized as SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets data and environment strategy and anticipates needs as systems and privacy demands evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide data and environment strategy and anticipating how privacy demands will tighten beyond today's NIST de-identification guidance is SFIA9's strategic-influence band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, De-Identification of Personal Information, NISTIR 8053 (2015).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative test-data and environment practice that shapes the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline manages test data and environments, externally credible beyond one employer, is SFIA9's highest originate band applied to the practice Humble & Farley's book helped establish industry-wide -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Humble & Farley, Continuous Delivery: Reliable Software Releases through Build Test and Deployment Automation (Addison-Wesley, 2010).

<a id="qa-13"></a>
##### QA-13 — Defect lifecycle management

*Type:* Behavioral — Tracking, triaging, prioritizing, and driving defects to resolution with clear reporting.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Logs and updates defects with clear detail following the defined workflow under review.
  — *Why this level:* Logging and updating defects by following the defined workflow ISTQB's syllabus formalizes (report, confirm, assign, fix, retest, close), with output reviewed, is applying a given process rather than judging it -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISTQB, Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus, Version 4.0 (2023).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages defects independently through triage, prioritization, and verification for routine cases.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running the ISTQB defect life cycle -- triage, prioritization, verification -- for routine, well-understood cases without escalation is the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISTQB, Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus, Version 4.0 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Drives resolution of ambiguous, cross-team defects and sets the local quality bar for reporting.
  — *Why this level:* Driving resolution of ambiguous, cross-team defects with urgency proportional to cost-of-escape is the prioritization judgment Boehm's empirically grounded defect-cost curve exists to justify -- autonomous, standard-setting, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Boehm, Software Engineering Economics (Prentice-Hall, 1981); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the defect-management workflow and triage approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the triage workflow other teams adopt, encoding Boehm's cost-of-escape reasoning into policy rather than applying it case-by-case, is SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Boehm, Software Engineering Economics (Prentice-Hall, 1981); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets defect-management strategy and anticipates trends from defect patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide defect-management strategy and anticipating trends from aggregate defect patterns -- where the cost curve is trending worse -- is SFIA9's strategic-influence band, forward-looking rather than case-by-case. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Boehm, Software Engineering Economics (Prentice-Hall, 1981).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative defect-lifecycle practice that shapes how the discipline manages defects.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the wider discipline manages the defect lifecycle, at the level a certification body's syllabus itself is written, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISTQB, Certified Tester Foundation Level Syllabus, Version 4.0 (2023).

<a id="qa-14"></a>
##### QA-14 — Quality metrics & reporting

*Type:* Behavioral — Measuring coverage, escape rates, and quality trends to inform release decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compiles defined quality metrics into standard reports under review.
  — *Why this level:* Compiling defined metrics (e.g. DORA's four keys) into a standard report format, reviewed before distribution, without judging which metric to trust, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces meaningful quality reports independently, selecting relevant metrics for routine needs.
  — *Why this level:* Independently selecting which of DORA's or similar standard metrics are relevant for a routine reporting need is the advanced-beginner band: recognized situations matched to known measures. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs metrics that reveal real quality signals in ambiguous, contested contexts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing metrics that reveal a real signal in ambiguous, contested contexts -- resisting the gaming and dysfunction Austin's study documents in measurement systems -- while grounding choices in DORA's validated delivery metrics is the Dreyfus competent band, autonomous and judgment-driven. *Sources:* Austin, Measuring and Managing Performance in Organizations (Dorset House, 1996); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the quality-metrics framework and reporting patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring the metrics framework other teams adopt, building in the gaming-resistance Austin's research shows naive metrics lack, is SFIA9's method-defining responsibility band. *Sources:* Austin, Measuring and Managing Performance in Organizations (Dorset House, 1996); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets quality-measurement strategy and anticipates which signals will matter as delivery evolves.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide quality-measurement strategy and anticipating which signals will matter as delivery practice evolves (the way DORA's own metric set has evolved across report years) is SFIA9's strategic-influence band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DORA (Google Cloud), Accelerate State of DevOps Report 2024 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what meaningful quality measurement means for the field and influences its practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what meaningful quality measurement means for the field, extending Austin's foundational critique of measurement dysfunction to shape industry practice, is SFIA9's highest originate band -- Dreyfus's master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Austin, Measuring and Managing Performance in Organizations (Dorset House, 1996).

### Game Development (GAME)

#### Engine & Runtime

<a id="game-01"></a>
##### GAME-01 — Game loop & real-time simulation

*Type:* Technical — Structuring frame-driven update, timing, and state progression for real-time interactivity.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements update steps within an existing loop on guided, well-scoped tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Coding a fixed slice of Gregory's game-loop/real-time-simulation chapter under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band: rule-following on decomposed tasks, no situational judgment yet asked of the engineer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard fixed/variable timestep loops independently, handling routine frame-timing variation.
  — *Why this level:* Independently applying Gregory's fixed/variable-timestep loop patterns to routine timing cases is the advanced-beginner band -- situational recognition without yet weighing competing tradeoffs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns the simulation loop autonomously, resolving timing, ordering, and determinism edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving determinism and update-order edge cases is the Dreyfus competent stage: the engineer plans deliberately and owns outcomes rather than following a template loop. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the loop architecture and update model others adopt across systems.
  — *Why this level:* Originating a loop/update-model architecture that other systems and teams adopt is the codification step Nystrom's Game Programming Patterns names explicitly as a reusable pattern -- authoring the pattern, not merely applying it, is what separates P4 from P3. *Sources:* Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018); Nystrom, Game Programming Patterns (Genever Benning, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets simulation-timing strategy and standards, anticipating scaling and platform shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting timing strategy across an org and anticipating platform shifts (variable refresh, cross-platform frame budgets) matches SFIA9's Level 6 'set strategy' responsibility band, applied to the engine-architecture layer Gregory scopes as engine-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what robust real-time simulation means for the field and influences industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* Gregory's and Nystrom's texts are themselves the field-defining artifacts for this capability -- authoring reference work that becomes how the industry teaches real-time simulation is the Dreyfus master/P6 band, beyond any single org's strategy. *Sources:* Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018); Nystrom, Game Programming Patterns (Genever Benning, 2014).

<a id="game-02"></a>
##### GAME-02 — Physics & collision systems

*Type:* Technical — Modeling motion, forces, and collision detection and response for believable interaction.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Adds colliders and tunes parameters on defined tasks with reviewed results.
  — *Why this level:* Tuning collider parameters from Ericson's intersection/response toolkit on assigned tasks under review is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct use of provided primitives, not yet independent problem framing. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2004).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard collision detection and response independently for routine cases.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing Ericson's standard broadphase/narrowphase detection and response independently for routine geometry is the advanced-beginner band: situational but not yet the numerically unstable cases his robustness chapters cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2004).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves tunneling, stacking, and stability issues autonomously across hard scenarios.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing tunneling and stacking instability autonomously is exactly the numerical-robustness problem class Ericson treats as the hard case in Real-Time Collision Detection; owning it without escalation is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2004).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the physics solver and broadphase approach others build on.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the solver/broadphase approach -- the architectural layer both Ericson's and Gregory's texts treat as a distinct subsystem others build on top of -- is the P4 pattern-authoring step, not case-by-case resolution. *Sources:* Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2004); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets physics-fidelity and performance strategy, anticipating new simulation demands.
  — *Why this level:* Setting fidelity/performance strategy and anticipating new simulation demands (destructible or soft-body content) is SFIA9's Level 6 'set strategy, inspire' responsibility, scoped to the physics subsystem Gregory places under engine-wide ownership. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for game physics recognized beyond their organization.
  — *Why this level:* Ericson's Real-Time Collision Detection is itself the cross-industry reference the field cites as best practice; producing work at that reference-text level, recognized outside one's own studio, is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Ericson, Real-Time Collision Detection (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2004).

<a id="game-03"></a>
##### GAME-03 — Graphics & rendering fundamentals

*Type:* Technical — Translating scenes into rendered frames via pipelines, shading, lighting, and cameras.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements basic draw calls and material settings on guided tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Setting material parameters and issuing draw calls per guided spec, drawn from Real-Time Rendering's pipeline-stage primitives, is Dreyfus's novice band -- rule application without independent diagnosis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard render passes and shading independently for routine scenes.
  — *Why this level:* Independently assembling standard render passes and shading models from Akenine-Moller et al.'s pipeline chapters for routine scenes is the advanced-beginner band: recognized situations, not yet the artifact-diagnosis skill the book treats as advanced. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and fixes rendering artifacts and pipeline issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously diagnosing rendering artifacts (aliasing, z-fighting, banding) that Real-Time Rendering catalogs as pipeline failure modes is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate diagnosis without a senior engineer's sign-off. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects the rendering pipeline and techniques others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Originating pipeline techniques that other teams adopt is the same authorial act Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman perform in codifying techniques into the field's standard reference -- the P4 pattern-authoring step. *Sources:* Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets rendering strategy and quality standards, anticipating hardware and technique shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting rendering strategy across projects and anticipating hardware shifts (new GPU architectures, ray-tracing adoption) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategic-influence band applied to the rendering subsystem. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines rendering best practice and advances the discipline externally.
  — *Why this level:* Real-Time Rendering is the reference text the graphics field treats as defining best practice; contributing work recognized at that discipline-shaping level, beyond one employer, is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).

<a id="game-04"></a>
##### GAME-04 — Spatial math & geometry

*Type:* Technical — Applying vectors, matrices, and transforms for movement, orientation, and spatial reasoning.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided vector and matrix operations to well-defined tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying the vector/matrix operations Lengyel's Foundations Vol. 1 sets out to well-scoped tasks under review is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct execution of given formulas. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lengyel, Foundations of Game Engine Development, Volume 1: Mathematics (Terathon Software, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently solves standard transform, projection, and intersection problems.
  — *Why this level:* Independently solving standard transform and projection problems from Lengyel's treatment is the advanced-beginner band -- competent with situational cases, not yet the numerically fragile ones. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lengyel, Foundations of Game Engine Development, Volume 1: Mathematics (Terathon Software, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles tricky spatial math—quaternions, edge cases, numerical stability—autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning quaternion interpolation and numerical-stability edge cases -- the advanced material Lengyel introduces via Grassmann/geometric algebra -- without escalation is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lengyel, Foundations of Game Engine Development, Volume 1: Mathematics (Terathon Software, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Devises geometric algorithms and conventions others reuse.
  — *Why this level:* Devising new geometric algorithms and conventions that other engineers reuse is the same pattern-authoring act Lengyel performs in extending conventional linear algebra into a reusable engine-math foundation -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Lengyel, Foundations of Game Engine Development, Volume 1: Mathematics (Terathon Software, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets spatial-math standards and anticipates emerging geometric techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting spatial-math conventions org-wide and anticipating emerging techniques (geometric-algebra adoption, precision strategies for large worlds) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy-setting band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Lengyel, Foundations of Game Engine Development, Volume 1: Mathematics (Terathon Software, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the field reasons about spatial math and geometry.
  — *Why this level:* Lengyel's own move to reframe engine math around geometric algebra, now referenced across the field, is the P6 marker: originating a reasoning framework the discipline adopts, not just applying an existing one. *Sources:* Lengyel, Foundations of Game Engine Development, Volume 1: Mathematics (Terathon Software, 2016).

#### Gameplay & Design

<a id="game-05"></a>
##### GAME-05 — Gameplay systems & mechanics design

*Type:* Technical — Designing and implementing rules, controls, and feedback loops that drive player experience.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements specified mechanics within an existing system under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing a specified mechanic against an existing system, with feel/balance left to review, is Dreyfus's novice band -- executing a defined lens from Schell's framework rather than choosing it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard gameplay systems independently with normal iteration.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard systems through normal iteration cycles is the advanced-beginner band -- applying Schell's lenses situationally without yet resolving ambiguity between competing lenses autonomously. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs and tunes cohesive mechanics autonomously, resolving balance and feel ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving balance and feel ambiguity -- weighing Schell's competing lenses against each other and committing -- is the Dreyfus competent stage: deliberate tradeoff judgment, not rule-following. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines systemic design patterns and frameworks other designers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Originating systemic patterns other designers adopt is the authorial step Schell's own book performs in codifying design lenses into a shared vocabulary -- P4 authors the framework rather than applying one. *Sources:* Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets gameplay-design direction and standards, anticipating player and genre shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting design direction across a studio's slate and anticipating genre/player shifts is SFIA9's Level 6 'set strategy, inspire' responsibility band applied to creative direction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what great mechanics design means and influences the craft broadly.
  — *Why this level:* Schell's Book of Lenses is itself the text the discipline cites for what mechanics design means; work recognized at that craft-defining level, beyond one studio's output, is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).

<a id="game-06"></a>
##### GAME-06 — Game AI & behavior systems

*Type:* Technical — Building agent decision-making, pathfinding, and reactive behaviors for non-player entities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Wires up provided behaviors and parameters on guided tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Wiring provided behavior-tree nodes and tuning exposed parameters per Millington's AI for Games primitives under review is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Millington, AI for Games, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard behavior trees or state machines independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently implementing standard behavior trees or FSMs from Millington's catalog for routine agents is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence without yet the believability tuning P3 requires. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Millington, AI for Games, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Crafts believable, performant agent behavior autonomously across hard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously balancing believability against performance budgets -- the tradeoff Millington frames as the core decision-making design problem -- across hard cases is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Millington, AI for Games, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects the AI behavior framework others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting a behavior framework other teams adopt mirrors the authorial act Millington performs in systematizing decision-making techniques into a reusable framework -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Millington, AI for Games, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets game-AI strategy and standards, anticipating new behavioral techniques.
  — *Why this level:* Setting AI strategy across projects and anticipating new techniques (learning-based agents, utility-AI adoption) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategic band applied to the AI subsystem. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Millington, AI for Games, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for game AI recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Millington's AI for Games is the reference the industry treats as defining game-AI best practice; contributing at that industry-recognized, cross-studio level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Millington, AI for Games, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2019).

<a id="game-07"></a>
##### GAME-07 — Audio & feedback integration

*Type:* Technical — Integrating sound, music, and sensory feedback to reinforce gameplay and immersion.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Hooks up provided sounds and feedback cues on defined tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Hooking up provided sound/feedback cues per spec under review is Dreyfus's novice band -- executing sensation elements Swink catalogs (juice, hit-stop, screen shake) without yet judging their combination. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Swink, Game Feel: A Game Designer's Guide to Virtual Sensation (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2008).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard audio triggers and feedback layers independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently layering standard triggers for routine actions is the advanced-beginner band -- applying Swink's individual feel components situationally without yet composing them into a cohesive system. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Swink, Game Feel: A Game Designer's Guide to Virtual Sensation (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs cohesive audio-feedback systems autonomously, resolving timing and mix edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously composing Swink's feel components into a cohesive, well-timed system and resolving mix edge cases is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate synthesis, not isolated hookups. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Swink, Game Feel: A Game Designer's Guide to Virtual Sensation (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2008).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the feedback and audio integration approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a feedback-integration approach other designers adopt is the same pattern-naming act Swink performs in identifying and naming feel's atomic components -- the P4 authorial marker. *Sources:* Swink, Game Feel: A Game Designer's Guide to Virtual Sensation (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2008).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets audio-feedback strategy and standards, anticipating immersion trends.
  — *Why this level:* Setting feedback strategy across a studio's titles and anticipating immersion trends (haptics, adaptive audio) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy-setting responsibility band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines excellence in game audio-feedback integration for the field.
  — *Why this level:* Swink's Game Feel is the text the field cites for what feedback excellence means; producing work recognized at that field-defining level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band, beyond any single title's polish. *Sources:* Swink, Game Feel: A Game Designer's Guide to Virtual Sensation (Morgan Kaufmann/CRC Press, 2008).

#### Content & Production

<a id="game-08"></a>
##### GAME-08 — Game asset pipeline

*Type:* Technical — Authoring, importing, and optimizing art, models, and animation through production workflows.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Imports and configures assets through an existing pipeline under review.
  — *Why this level:* Importing and configuring assets through an existing pipeline per instructions, reviewed before merge, is Dreyfus's novice band applied to the resource/asset-conditioning chapter Gregory scopes as its own engine subsystem. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and maintains standard pipeline steps independently for routine assets.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and maintaining standard conditioning steps for routine assets is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence with the pipeline as given, not yet redesigning it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and optimizes pipeline bottlenecks and edge-case assets autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously diagnosing bottlenecks and edge-case assets (huge meshes, malformed data) without escalation is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate root-causing of the pipeline Gregory treats as engine infrastructure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects the asset pipeline and conventions others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting the pipeline and conventions other teams adopt is the infrastructure-ownership role Gregory assigns to engine architects, not content producers -- the P4 marker separating design from execution. *Sources:* Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets pipeline strategy and standards, anticipating tooling and scale shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting pipeline strategy across a studio and anticipating tooling/scale shifts (cloud builds, larger asset counts) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy band applied to production infrastructure. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines asset-pipeline best practice recognized beyond their organization.
  — *Why this level:* Producing pipeline practice recognized industry-wide -- the level Gregory's own reference text operates at -- rather than just within one studio's tooling is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).

<a id="game-09"></a>
##### GAME-09 — Level design & content authoring

*Type:* Technical — Crafting spaces, pacing, and encounters that shape player progression and challenge.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds level sections to spec using existing tools under review.
  — *Why this level:* Building a level section to spec with existing tools, reviewed for correctness, is Dreyfus's novice band -- executing a design brief rather than the spatial-composition judgment Totten's architectural lenses require. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Totten, An Architectural Approach to Level Design (CRC Press, 2014; 2nd ed. 2019).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Authors complete standard levels independently with normal iteration.
  — *Why this level:* Independently authoring a complete standard level through normal iteration is the advanced-beginner band -- applying Totten's spatial-sequencing principles situationally without yet the pacing mastery P3 demands. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Totten, An Architectural Approach to Level Design (CRC Press, 2014; 2nd ed. 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs compelling pacing, flow, and layout autonomously across hard content.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously designing pacing and flow across hard content -- the architectural-experience judgment Totten frames as evoking emotion through gamespace -- is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Totten, An Architectural Approach to Level Design (CRC Press, 2014; 2nd ed. 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines level-design patterns and authoring standards others follow.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoring patterns other designers follow is the same codification act Totten performs in translating architectural theory into reusable level-design principles -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Totten, An Architectural Approach to Level Design (CRC Press, 2014; 2nd ed. 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets content-design direction, anticipating player-experience and tooling shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting content direction across a title's levels and anticipating player-experience/tooling shifts is SFIA9's Level 6 strategic-direction band applied to content design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what great level design means and influences the craft widely.
  — *Why this level:* Totten's Architectural Approach is itself one of the field's defining texts on what level design is; contributing at that craft-defining, cross-studio level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Totten, An Architectural Approach to Level Design (CRC Press, 2014; 2nd ed. 2019).

#### Online & Backend

<a id="game-10"></a>
##### GAME-10 — Multiplayer networking & netcode

*Type:* Technical — Synchronizing state across clients with replication, prediction, and latency compensation.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements specified replication on an existing netcode layer under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing specified replication logic on top of an existing netcode layer, reviewed before merge, is Dreyfus's novice band -- applying Glazer & Madhav's socket/serialization primitives to a scoped task. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard state sync and messaging independently for routine cases.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard state-sync and messaging for routine cases from Glazer & Madhav's architecture is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence short of the latency-compensation problems P3 owns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves latency, prediction, and reconciliation problems autonomously.
