  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving prediction and reconciliation under latency/jitter -- the core problem Glazer & Madhav devote their networking-topology chapters to -- is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects the netcode model others adopt for synchronization.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting a synchronization model other teams adopt is the same authorial act the book performs in codifying networked-game architecture into reusable engine-level systems -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets networking strategy and standards, anticipating scale and topology shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting networking strategy across titles and anticipating scale/topology shifts (peer-to-peer to dedicated servers, rollback adoption) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy band applied to the netcode subsystem. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines netcode best practice recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Producing netcode practice recognized industry-wide, at the reference level this book itself occupies, rather than one studio's internal convention is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).

<a id="game-11"></a>
##### GAME-11 — Game server & live operations

*Type:* Technical — Running authoritative servers, matchmaking, sessions, and persistent live-service backends.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs defined live-ops and server tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Performing defined server/live-ops tasks (config changes, scripted deploys) under review is Dreyfus's novice band, applied to the cloud game-server operations Glazer & Madhav scope as distinct from client-side netcode. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Operates and maintains game servers independently for routine events.
  — *Why this level:* Independently operating and maintaining servers through routine events (patch rollouts, scheduled matchmaking load) is the advanced-beginner band -- situational operation without yet incident diagnosis under pressure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses live incidents and scales services autonomously under pressure.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously diagnosing live incidents and scaling services under pressure -- the operational judgment beyond the book's baseline server architecture -- is the Dreyfus competent stage: deliberate triage without a senior sign-off. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects the live-service and operations approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting the live-service and matchmaking approach other teams adopt is the authorial step the book performs in codifying cloud-hosted server architecture into a reusable pattern -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets live-ops strategy and reliability standards, anticipating demand shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting reliability standards and anticipating demand shifts (launch spikes, seasonal events) across a live-service portfolio is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy-and-standards band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines live-operations best practice recognized beyond their organization.
  — *Why this level:* Contributing live-ops practice recognized beyond one's own studio -- at the industry-reference level this book operates at for networked-game operations -- is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Glazer & Madhav, Multiplayer Game Programming: Architecting Networked Games (Addison-Wesley, 2015).

<a id="game-12"></a>
##### GAME-12 — Performance optimization & profiling

*Type:* Technical — Diagnosing and tuning frame rate, memory, and resource use for target platforms.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies suggested optimizations and reads profiles on guided tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying suggested fixes and reading profiler output from Gregory's debugging/development-tools chapter on guided tasks under review is Dreyfus's novice band -- execution, not independent diagnosis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Profiles and fixes standard bottlenecks independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently profiling and fixing standard bottlenecks (draw-call counts, allocation spikes) is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence with well-known bottleneck classes, short of cross-system diagnosis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses and resolves complex performance issues autonomously across systems.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously tracing a complex issue across rendering, physics, and gameplay systems -- correlating symptoms the way Real-Time Rendering's performance chapters and Gregory's engine-wide profiling both require -- is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018); Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines profiling methodology and optimization patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a profiling methodology other engineers adopt is the same authorial move Gregory performs in codifying debugging/optimization tooling into an engine-wide discipline -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets performance strategy and budgets, anticipating platform constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Setting frame/memory budgets across a title and anticipating platform constraints (console generations, mobile thermal limits) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy-and-standards band applied to performance engineering. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines performance-engineering best practice for the field.
  — *Why this level:* Producing performance-engineering practice recognized at the reference-text level these books occupy for the field, rather than one studio's internal guidance, is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Gregory, Game Engine Architecture, 3rd Edition (CRC Press, 2018); Akenine-Moller, Haines & Hoffman, Real-Time Rendering, 4th Edition (CRC Press, 2018).

### Blockchain & Web3 (WEB3)

#### Protocol Foundations

<a id="web3-01"></a>
##### WEB3-01 — Consensus & protocol fundamentals

*Type:* Technical — Understanding distributed agreement, block production, and protocol-level trust mechanisms.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Explains and configures protocol parameters on defined tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring protocol parameters (block time, difficulty target) per spec under review, without yet reasoning about the consensus guarantees Nakamoto's proof-of-work design provides, is Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (2008).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard protocol logic independently for routine changes.
  — *Why this level:* Independently implementing standard protocol logic (block validation, chain selection) from Nakamoto's design for routine changes is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence short of safety/liveness reasoning. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Reasons about consensus safety, liveness, and edge cases autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously reasoning about safety and liveness under adversarial or faulty participants is precisely the Byzantine Generals problem Lamport, Shostak & Pease formalize; owning that reasoning without escalation is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lamport, Shostak & Pease, The Byzantine Generals Problem, ACM TOPLAS 4(3), 382-401 (1982).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs consensus mechanisms and protocol approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a consensus mechanism other systems adopt is the same act Nakamoto performed in applying Byzantine-fault-tolerant reasoning to produce a new, widely adopted protocol -- the P4 pattern-authoring step, not case-by-case implementation. *Sources:* Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (2008); Lamport, Shostak & Pease, The Byzantine Generals Problem, ACM TOPLAS 4(3), 382-401 (1982).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets protocol-design strategy and standards, anticipating emerging models.
  — *Why this level:* Setting protocol strategy across a system and anticipating emerging consensus models (BFT variants, proof-of-stake evolution) is SFIA9's Level 6 'set strategy, inspire' responsibility band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines consensus best practice and shapes protocol research broadly.
  — *Why this level:* Nakamoto's and Lamport et al.'s papers are themselves the field-defining artifacts consensus research still cites as the baseline; contributing research recognized at that discipline-shaping level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (2008); Lamport, Shostak & Pease, The Byzantine Generals Problem, ACM TOPLAS 4(3), 382-401 (1982).

<a id="web3-02"></a>
##### WEB3-02 — Applied cryptography & key management

*Type:* Technical — Applying hashing, signatures, and asymmetric cryptography to secure on-chain identity and data.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses provided cryptographic primitives correctly on guided tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Correctly invoking a FIPS 186-5-approved signature primitive (ECDSA/EdDSA) as provided, on a scoped task under review, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct usage, not scheme selection. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, FIPS 186-5: Digital Signature Standard (DSS) (2023).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard signing, hashing, and key handling independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently implementing standard signing and hashing flows from the Handbook of Applied Cryptography's protocol catalog for routine cases is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence with known-good constructions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Menezes, van Oorschot & Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography (CRC Press, 1996).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves subtle cryptographic and key-lifecycle issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving key-lifecycle issues (rotation, compromise recovery, cryptoperiod expiry) against NIST SP 800-57's key-management lifecycle model is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate lifecycle judgment, not a checklist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5: Recommendation for Key Management (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs cryptographic schemes and key-management approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a key-management approach other teams adopt is the applied-synthesis step the Handbook and SP 800-57 both scope as scheme design, distinct from correctly using an existing scheme -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Menezes, van Oorschot & Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography (CRC Press, 1996); NIST, SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5: Recommendation for Key Management (2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets applied-crypto strategy and standards, anticipating threat shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting cryptographic standards org-wide and anticipating threat shifts (algorithm deprecation, as FIPS 186-5 itself did in retiring DSA) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy band applied to applied cryptography. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, FIPS 186-5: Digital Signature Standard (DSS) (2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines applied cryptography best practice recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* The Handbook of Applied Cryptography is itself the cross-industry reference the field cites for applied-crypto best practice; producing work recognized at that reference level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Menezes, van Oorschot & Vanstone, Handbook of Applied Cryptography (CRC Press, 1996).

<a id="web3-03"></a>
##### WEB3-03 — Scalability & interoperability design

*Type:* Technical — Designing layered scaling and cross-chain communication to extend throughput and reach.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements specified scaling or bridging components under review.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing a specified payment-channel or bridge component from the Lightning Network design, under review, is Dreyfus's novice band -- execution of a specified sub-piece. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Poon & Dryja, The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments (2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard scaling and interoperability features independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard channel-management or off-chain settlement features from Poon & Dryja's design for routine cases is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence short of cross-system trust reasoning. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Poon & Dryja, The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments (2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves throughput, finality, and cross-system trust trade-offs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously weighing finality and trust trade-offs across systems is the exact classification problem Zamyatin et al.'s SoK formalizes as inherent to cross-chain communication; owning that trade-off judgment is the Dreyfus competent stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Zamyatin, Al-Bassam, Zindros, Kokoris-Kogias, Moreno-Sanchez, Kiayias & Knottenbelt, SoK: Communication Across Distributed Ledgers, Financial Cryptography and Data Security 2021 (LNCS 12675), 3-36.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects scalability and interoperability designs others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting a scaling or interoperability design other systems adopt is the same act Poon & Dryja performed in producing Lightning as a widely-implemented off-chain protocol -- the P4 pattern-authoring step Zamyatin et al. classify as a distinct CCC-protocol design choice. *Sources:* Poon & Dryja, The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments (2016); Zamyatin, Al-Bassam, Zindros, Kokoris-Kogias, Moreno-Sanchez, Kiayias & Knottenbelt, SoK: Communication Across Distributed Ledgers, Financial Cryptography and Data Security 2021 (LNCS 12675), 3-36.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets scaling and interoperability strategy, anticipating ecosystem shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting scaling strategy across a protocol's roadmap and anticipating ecosystem shifts (rollup-centric scaling, new bridge trust models) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategic-direction band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for scalable, interoperable systems across the field.
  — *Why this level:* Zamyatin et al.'s systematization and Lightning's protocol design are themselves the reference points the field cites for scalable, interoperable system design; contributing at that field-defining level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Zamyatin, Al-Bassam, Zindros, Kokoris-Kogias, Moreno-Sanchez, Kiayias & Knottenbelt, SoK: Communication Across Distributed Ledgers, Financial Cryptography and Data Security 2021 (LNCS 12675), 3-36; Poon & Dryja, The Bitcoin Lightning Network: Scalable Off-Chain Instant Payments (2016).

#### Smart Contracts

<a id="web3-04"></a>
##### WEB3-04 — Smart contract design

*Type:* Technical — Architecting deterministic on-chain logic with correct state, upgrade, and gas considerations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements specified contract logic with reviewed results.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing specified contract logic against a given standard interface (ERC-20's transfer/approve functions), with results reviewed, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct execution of a defined spec. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Vogelsteller & Buterin, EIP-20: Token Standard (Ethereum Improvement Proposals, 2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard contracts independently, handling routine requirements.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard token or interface contracts compliant with EIP-20-class specifications for routine requirements is the advanced-beginner band -- situational compliance without yet novel architecture. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Vogelsteller & Buterin, EIP-20: Token Standard (Ethereum Improvement Proposals, 2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs robust, gas-aware contract architectures autonomously across hard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously designing gas-aware architectures against the EVM's formally specified execution and gas-accounting model (the Yellow Paper) for hard cases is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate resource-tradeoff reasoning. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wood, Ethereum: A Secure Decentralised Generalised Transaction Ledger (Ethereum Yellow Paper, 2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines contract design patterns and standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a contract pattern or standard other developers adopt is the same authorial act Vogelsteller & Buterin performed in proposing EIP-20 as a reusable interface grounded in the Yellow Paper's execution semantics -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Vogelsteller & Buterin, EIP-20: Token Standard (Ethereum Improvement Proposals, 2015); Wood, Ethereum: A Secure Decentralised Generalised Transaction Ledger (Ethereum Yellow Paper, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets smart-contract design strategy, anticipating language and pattern shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting contract-design strategy across a protocol's contract suite and anticipating language/pattern shifts (upgradeability patterns, account abstraction) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines smart-contract design best practice recognized industry-wide.
  — *Why this level:* EIP-20 and the Yellow Paper are themselves the industry-wide references smart-contract design is measured against; producing new standards recognized at that level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Vogelsteller & Buterin, EIP-20: Token Standard (Ethereum Improvement Proposals, 2015); Wood, Ethereum: A Secure Decentralised Generalised Transaction Ledger (Ethereum Yellow Paper, 2014).

<a id="web3-05"></a>
##### WEB3-05 — On-chain security & auditing

*Type:* Technical — Identifying and mitigating contract vulnerabilities through review, testing, and formal analysis.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs provided checks and flags obvious issues under review.
  — *Why this level:* Running provided checks against the SWC Registry's catalogued weakness classes and flagging obvious matches, under review, is Dreyfus's novice band -- pattern-matching against a given list. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SmartContractSecurity, SWC Registry: Smart Contract Weakness Classification and Test Cases (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Audits standard contracts independently, identifying common vulnerabilities.
  — *Why this level:* Independently auditing standard contracts for the SWC Registry's common weakness classes (reentrancy, integer issues) is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence with cataloged patterns, short of novel exploit construction. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SmartContractSecurity, SWC Registry: Smart Contract Weakness Classification and Test Cases (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Uncovers subtle, novel vulnerabilities and exploit paths autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Uncovering subtle, novel exploit paths beyond the taxonomy Atzei, Bartoletti & Cimoli's survey catalogs is the Dreyfus competent stage -- autonomous vulnerability research past known patterns, not checklist auditing. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Atzei, Bartoletti & Cimoli, A Survey of Attacks on Ethereum Smart Contracts (SoK), Principles of Security and Trust (POST) 2017, LNCS 10204, 164-186.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines audit methodology and threat models others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining an audit methodology and threat model other auditors adopt is the same standard-setting act OWASP performs in the SCSVS's verification levels, building on taxonomies like Atzei et al.'s -- the P4 marker of authoring the methodology, not applying one. *Sources:* OWASP Foundation, Smart Contract Security Verification Standard (SCSVS) (accessed 2026-07); Atzei, Bartoletti & Cimoli, A Survey of Attacks on Ethereum Smart Contracts (SoK), Principles of Security and Trust (POST) 2017, LNCS 10204, 164-186.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets on-chain security strategy and standards, anticipating attack trends.
  — *Why this level:* Setting security strategy across a protocol's contract portfolio and anticipating attack trends, at the level OWASP's SCSVS Level 3 'mission-critical' tier targets, is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy-and-standards band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); OWASP Foundation, Smart Contract Security Verification Standard (SCSVS) (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines on-chain security best practice recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* The SWC Registry and OWASP's SCSVS are themselves the industry-recognized references on-chain security is measured against; contributing new standards at that recognized level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* OWASP Foundation, Smart Contract Security Verification Standard (SCSVS) (accessed 2026-07); SmartContractSecurity, SWC Registry: Smart Contract Weakness Classification and Test Cases (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="web3-06"></a>
##### WEB3-06 — Decentralized application integration

*Type:* Technical — Connecting interfaces and off-chain services to on-chain logic via nodes, wallets, and oracles.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Wires up provided on-chain calls in an app under review.
  — *Why this level:* Wiring a provided contract call (e.g. an ERC-20 transfer) into an app per spec, reviewed before merge, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct use of a given interface. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Vogelsteller & Buterin, EIP-20: Token Standard (Ethereum Improvement Proposals, 2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Integrates standard contract interactions and wallets independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently integrating standard wallet connections against EIP-1193's provider API for routine flows is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence with a standardized interface, short of failure-mode handling. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ethereum Provider JavaScript API (EIP-1193, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves state-sync, signing, and failure-mode issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving signing and chain/account-change failure modes -- the accountsChanged/chainChanged event handling EIP-1193 specifies as provider-consumer obligations -- is the Dreyfus competent stage: deliberate edge-case ownership, not a checklist integration. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ethereum Provider JavaScript API (EIP-1193, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects dApp integration patterns others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting an integration pattern other teams adopt -- spanning wallet providers and oracle connectivity the way Chainlink's whitepaper formalizes for external data -- is the P4 pattern-authoring step, not case-by-case wiring. *Sources:* Ethereum Provider JavaScript API (EIP-1193, 2018); Ellis, Juels & Nazarov, ChainLink: A Decentralized Oracle Network, Whitepaper v1.0 (2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets integration strategy and standards, anticipating ecosystem shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting integration strategy across an app portfolio and anticipating ecosystem shifts (account abstraction, new provider standards) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines decentralized-app integration best practice for the field.
  — *Why this level:* Chainlink's oracle-network design and EIP-1193's provider standard are themselves the references dApp integration is measured against; contributing new standards recognized at that field level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Ellis, Juels & Nazarov, ChainLink: A Decentralized Oracle Network, Whitepaper v1.0 (2017); Ethereum Provider JavaScript API (EIP-1193, 2018).

#### Economics & Custody

<a id="web3-07"></a>
##### WEB3-07 — Tokenomics & on-chain economics

*Type:* Technical — Designing token incentives, supply mechanics, and economic models for sustainable networks.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Models specified token parameters under review.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling specified supply/emission parameters per a given design brief, under review, is Dreyfus's novice band -- applying Catalini & Gans's cost-of-verification/cost-of-networking framework rather than choosing it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Catalini & Gans, Some Simple Economics of the Blockchain, NBER Working Paper No. 22952 (2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs standard token mechanics and incentives independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing standard incentive mechanics (staking rewards, fee splits) using Catalini & Gans's economic framework for routine cases is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence, not yet systemic risk analysis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Catalini & Gans, Some Simple Economics of the Blockchain, NBER Working Paper No. 22952 (2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs sound incentive and supply systems autonomously, resolving economic edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving economic edge cases (reflexive collateral, liquidation cascades) that Werner et al.'s SoK catalogs as DeFi's systemic risk classes is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate mechanism-design judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Werner, Perez, Gudgeon, Klages-Mundt, Harz & Knottenbelt, SoK: Decentralized Finance (DeFi), Proc. 4th ACM Conference on Advances in Financial Technologies (AFT 2022), 30-46.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines tokenomic frameworks and modeling approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a tokenomic framework other designers adopt is the same synthesis act Catalini & Gans and Werner et al. perform in systematizing blockchain economics into reusable analytic categories -- the P4 marker. *Sources:* Catalini & Gans, Some Simple Economics of the Blockchain, NBER Working Paper No. 22952 (2016); Werner, Perez, Gudgeon, Klages-Mundt, Harz & Knottenbelt, SoK: Decentralized Finance (DeFi), Proc. 4th ACM Conference on Advances in Financial Technologies (AFT 2022), 30-46.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets on-chain economic strategy, anticipating market and mechanism shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting economic strategy across a protocol's token design and anticipating market/mechanism shifts (real-world-asset collateral, new AMM curves) is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines tokenomics best practice recognized across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Werner et al.'s SoK and Catalini & Gans's economic framework are themselves the references tokenomics research is measured against; producing work recognized at that industry level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* Werner, Perez, Gudgeon, Klages-Mundt, Harz & Knottenbelt, SoK: Decentralized Finance (DeFi), Proc. 4th ACM Conference on Advances in Financial Technologies (AFT 2022), 30-46; Catalini & Gans, Some Simple Economics of the Blockchain, NBER Working Paper No. 22952 (2016).

<a id="web3-08"></a>
##### WEB3-08 — Wallet & key custody

*Type:* Technical — Securing private keys, signing flows, and asset custody for users and institutions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures provided custody and wallet flows under review.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring a provided mnemonic-seed wallet flow per BIP-39's specification, under review, is Dreyfus's novice band -- correct use of a given standard, not custody design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bitcoin Core contributors, BIP-39: Mnemonic Code for Generating Deterministic Keys (Bitcoin Improvement Proposals, 2013).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Implements standard custody and signing flows independently.
  — *Why this level:* Independently implementing standard HD-wallet derivation and signing flows from BIP-32's tree-derivation scheme for routine cases is the advanced-beginner band -- situational competence with a given key hierarchy. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wuille, BIP-32: Hierarchical Deterministic Wallets (Bitcoin Improvement Proposals, 2012).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves recovery, multi-party, and key-lifecycle challenges autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously resolving recovery and key-lifecycle challenges (compromise, rotation, multi-party approval) against NIST SP 800-57's lifecycle model is the Dreyfus competent stage -- deliberate lifecycle judgment beyond routine key generation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5: Recommendation for Key Management (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs custody architectures and policies others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a custody architecture other teams adopt -- e.g. threshold-signature custody per Gennaro & Goldfeder's MPC protocol, assessed against CCSS's ten security aspects -- is the P4 architectural-authorship step, not flow implementation. *Sources:* Gennaro & Goldfeder, Fast Multiparty Threshold ECDSA with Fast Trustless Setup, Proc. ACM CCS 2018, 1179-1194; CryptoCurrency Certification Consortium (C4), CryptoCurrency Security Standard (CCSS), v9.0 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets custody strategy and security standards, anticipating threat shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting custody strategy across an institution's holdings and anticipating threat shifts, at the level CCSS's Level III 'comprehensive security' tier targets, is SFIA9's Level 6 strategy-and-standards band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); CryptoCurrency Certification Consortium (C4), CryptoCurrency Security Standard (CCSS), v9.0 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines key-custody best practice recognized beyond their organization.
  — *Why this level:* The CCSS and Gennaro & Goldfeder's threshold-ECDSA protocol are themselves the references custody practice is measured against industry-wide; contributing new standards recognized at that level is the Dreyfus master/P6 band. *Sources:* CryptoCurrency Certification Consortium (C4), CryptoCurrency Security Standard (CCSS), v9.0 (2024); Gennaro & Goldfeder, Fast Multiparty Threshold ECDSA with Fast Trustless Setup, Proc. ACM CCS 2018, 1179-1194.

## Product, Design & Cross-functional

### UX & Product Design (UX)

#### User Research & Insight

<a id="ux-01"></a>
##### UX-01 — User research & usability evaluation

*Type:* Behavioral — Planning and conducting research and usability testing to uncover user needs and validate designs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs scripted sessions and notes observations under review.
  — *Why this level:* Dreyfus's novice band performs well-defined tasks under review; Rubin & Chisnell's moderation protocol is written to be run by a facilitator following a fixed script rather than designing the study, matching P1's reviewed execution. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rubin & Chisnell, Handbook of Usability Testing: How to Plan, Design, and Conduct Effective Tests, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2008).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Plans and conducts standard studies independently, synthesizing routine findings.
  — *Why this level:* Rubin & Chisnell's handbook targets practitioners who plan and run a standard usability test end-to-end without oversight -- the advanced-beginner threshold of independent, standard-variation execution. *Sources:* Rubin & Chisnell, Handbook of Usability Testing: How to Plan, Design, and Conduct Effective Tests, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2008).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs rigorous research and extracts hard insights autonomously across ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* ISO 9241-210's human-centred design process requires autonomously selecting and iterating methods against ambiguous user needs, not following a fixed protocol -- Dreyfus's competent band of handling ambiguity and hard cases without guidance. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 9241-210:2019 Ergonomics of Human-System Interaction — Part 210: Human-Centred Design for Interactive Systems (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines research methods and evaluation frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Nielsen's heuristic set was derived and published specifically so other practitioners could adopt it as an evaluation method -- the defining-the-approach-others-use behavior of the expert band. *Sources:* Nielsen, Enhancing the Explanatory Power of Usability Heuristics, Proc. ACM CHI'94, 152-158 (1994).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets research strategy and standards, anticipating where inquiry must head.
  — *Why this level:* NN/g's career-progression research identifies a senior tier that sets research strategy and standards across an org rather than executing studies -- the authority band's org-wide, direction-anticipating scope. *Sources:* Nielsen Norman Group, User Experience Careers: What a Career in UX Looks Like Today (survey, focus groups, and interviews with UX professionals, 2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines user-research best practice recognized across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* ISO 9241-11 is the globally adopted definitional standard for usability itself -- the pioneer band's discipline-defining, externally credible reach, beyond any single organization's practice. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 9241-11:2018 Ergonomics of Human-System Interaction — Part 11: Usability: Definitions and Concepts (2018).

<a id="ux-02"></a>
##### UX-02 — Information architecture & content structuring

*Type:* Technical — Organizing content and navigation into coherent structures that match user mental models.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Organizes content into provided structures under review.
  — *Why this level:* The Polar Bear Book's introductory IA structure types (hierarchy, sequence, matrix) are taught as templates a novice applies to given content -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task, reviewed-work band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rosenfeld, Morville & Arango, Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond, 4th Edition (O'Reilly, 2015).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds standard navigation and taxonomies independently.
  — *Why this level:* Spencer's card-sorting method is written for practitioners running standard categorization studies unsupervised -- independent execution of routine-variation IA work, the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Spencer, Card Sorting: Designing Usable Categories (Rosenfeld Media, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Structures complex, ambiguous content domains autonomously into coherent models.
  — *Why this level:* Rosenfeld & Morville frame IA's hard problems as 'ill-defined' domains requiring judgment, not lookup -- Dreyfus's competent band of autonomous, ambiguity-handling execution. *Sources:* Rosenfeld, Morville & Arango, Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond, 4th Edition (O'Reilly, 2015); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines IA patterns and structuring methods others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* The book's own pattern catalog (organization/labeling/navigation/search systems) is the reference other practitioners build from -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-adopt behavior, distinct from P3's per-project autonomy. *Sources:* Rosenfeld, Morville & Arango, Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond, 4th Edition (O'Reilly, 2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets information-architecture strategy, anticipating content and scale shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Resmini & Rosati's Pervasive IA framework explicitly targets anticipating cross-channel and scale shifts (device, context, growth) at a strategic level -- the authority band's direction-anticipating scope, beyond single-product structuring. *Sources:* Resmini & Rosati, Pervasive Information Architecture: Designing Cross-Channel User Experiences (Morgan Kaufmann, 2011).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines IA best practice recognized across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Rosenfeld & Morville's text is credited with naming and founding the information-architecture discipline itself -- the pioneer band's externally credible, field-defining reach. *Sources:* Rosenfeld, Morville & Arango, Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond, 4th Edition (O'Reilly, 2015).

#### Interaction & Visual Design

<a id="ux-03"></a>
##### UX-03 — Interaction & flow design

*Type:* Technical — Designing task flows, states, and interaction patterns that make products intuitive and efficient.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds specified flows and interactions under review.
  — *Why this level:* About Face's goal-directed workflows are given to novice designers as templates to implement under review -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cooper, Reimann, Cronin & Noessel, About Face: The Essentials of Interaction Design, 4th Edition (Wiley, 2014).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs standard end-to-end flows independently with normal iteration.
  — *Why this level:* Cooper et al.'s standard interaction patterns are executed by practitioners running normal flows independently -- the advanced-beginner band's routine-variation, low-oversight work. *Sources:* Cooper, Reimann, Cronin & Noessel, About Face: The Essentials of Interaction Design, 4th Edition (Wiley, 2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex, ambiguous interaction problems autonomously with strong judgment.
  — *Why this level:* About Face's goal-directed design method is aimed at resolving genuinely ambiguous interaction trade-offs without a template -- Dreyfus's competent band of autonomous judgment on hard cases. *Sources:* Cooper, Reimann, Cronin & Noessel, About Face: The Essentials of Interaction Design, 4th Edition (Wiley, 2014); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines interaction patterns and flow frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Apple's Human Interface Guidelines are a published interaction-pattern framework built precisely so other teams adopt its flows and gestures -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-use behavior. *Sources:* Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets interaction-design direction, anticipating behavioral and modality shifts.
  — *Why this level:* About Face's chapters on cross-platform and emerging-modality (touch, gesture, voice) design set direction ahead of the shift rather than reacting to it -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* Cooper, Reimann, Cronin & Noessel, About Face: The Essentials of Interaction Design, 4th Edition (Wiley, 2014).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines interaction-design best practice recognized across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Nielsen's heuristic framework is the most-cited interaction/usability evaluation standard in the discipline -- the pioneer band's externally credible, field-shaping reach. *Sources:* Nielsen, Enhancing the Explanatory Power of Usability Heuristics, Proc. ACM CHI'94, 152-158 (1994).

<a id="ux-04"></a>
##### UX-04 — Visual & layout design

*Type:* Technical — Applying typography, color, spacing, and composition to create clear, appealing visual hierarchy.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided styles and layouts to defined screens under review.
  — *Why this level:* White's four elements (dominance, scale, space, type) are taught as rules a novice applies to a given screen under review -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); White, The Elements of Graphic Design, 2nd Edition (Allworth Press, 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces standard, consistent visual layouts independently.
  — *Why this level:* White's framework for consistent hierarchy and rhythm is applied by practitioners producing standard layouts unsupervised -- the advanced-beginner band's independent, routine execution. *Sources:* White, The Elements of Graphic Design, 2nd Edition (Allworth Press, 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Crafts strong hierarchy, rhythm, and polish autonomously across hard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Wertheimer's grouping laws (proximity, similarity, closure) require judgment to apply to non-obvious layouts, not rule-following -- Dreyfus's competent band of autonomous handling of hard visual cases. *Sources:* Wertheimer, Laws of Organization in Perceptual Forms, Psychologische Forschung 4, 301-350 (1923); trans. in Ellis (Ed.), A Source Book of Gestalt Psychology (1938); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines visual language and layout systems others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Lupton's typographic system approach is built for defining a visual language other designers then work within -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-adopt behavior, beyond executing one's own layouts. *Sources:* Lupton, Thinking with Type, 2nd Edition (Princeton Architectural Press, 2010).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets visual-design direction and standards, anticipating aesthetic shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Material Design's periodic system-wide redesigns set visual direction ahead of shifting aesthetic and platform expectations across many product teams -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* Google, Material Design 3 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines visual-design excellence recognized across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Apple's Human Interface Guidelines function as an externally credible, industry-wide visual-design reference cited well beyond Apple's own products -- the pioneer band's discipline-shaping reach. *Sources:* Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).

<a id="ux-05"></a>
##### UX-05 — Prototyping & design validation

*Type:* Technical — Creating prototypes at varied fidelity to explore, communicate, and test design concepts.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds simple prototypes from specs under review.
  — *Why this level:* Buxton distinguishes low-cost sketches built to spec from validating prototypes; a novice building simple prototypes under review sits at Buxton's sketch end of the fidelity spectrum -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Buxton, Sketching User Experiences: Getting the Design Right and the Right Design (Morgan Kaufmann, 2007).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Creates standard interactive prototypes and runs basic validation independently.
  — *Why this level:* Buxton's fidelity-spectrum method is applied independently by practitioners building standard interactive prototypes for routine validation -- the advanced-beginner band's unsupervised, routine-variation work. *Sources:* Buxton, Sketching User Experiences: Getting the Design Right and the Right Design (Morgan Kaufmann, 2007).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs prototypes that answer hard questions and validates rigorously autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Buxton's central argument -- choosing the right fidelity to answer a specific hard design question -- requires autonomous judgment absent from templated prototyping, matching Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Buxton, Sketching User Experiences: Getting the Design Right and the Right Design (Morgan Kaufmann, 2007); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines prototyping and validation methods others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Rubin & Chisnell's evaluation methodology is the reference other practitioners adopt to structure their own validation process -- the expert band's defines-the-method-others-use behavior. *Sources:* Rubin & Chisnell, Handbook of Usability Testing: How to Plan, Design, and Conduct Effective Tests, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2008).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets validation strategy and standards, anticipating new fidelity needs.
  — *Why this level:* NN/g's career-progression research places setting validation strategy and standards across an org, ahead of emerging tooling and fidelity needs, at its senior tier -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* Nielsen Norman Group, User Experience Careers: What a Career in UX Looks Like Today (survey, focus groups, and interviews with UX professionals, 2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines prototyping-and-validation best practice for the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Buxton's sketch-versus-prototype distinction became the field's standard vocabulary for fidelity and validation practice -- the pioneer band's externally credible, discipline-defining reach. *Sources:* Buxton, Sketching User Experiences: Getting the Design Right and the Right Design (Morgan Kaufmann, 2007).

<a id="ux-06"></a>
##### UX-06 — Inclusive & accessible design

*Type:* Technical — Designing experiences usable by people with diverse abilities, contexts, and assistive needs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies provided accessibility guidelines on defined tasks under review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying specific WCAG 2.2 success criteria to a defined task under review is the entry point into the standard -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task, reviewed-work band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs to standard accessibility requirements independently.
  — *Why this level:* Meeting WCAG 2.2's AA conformance criteria independently across routine screens is the standard practitioner threshold the guideline itself defines -- the advanced-beginner band's independent, standard-variation work. *Sources:* W3C, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex inclusion and accessibility trade-offs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* WAI-ARIA's roles and states require autonomous judgment to resolve conflicting semantics in complex custom widgets, beyond checklist conformance -- Dreyfus's competent band of ambiguity-handling execution. *Sources:* W3C, Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2 (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines inclusive-design practices and standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Holmes (Microsoft's former Principal Director of Inclusive Design) defines inclusive-design practice that goes beyond compliance and is built for other teams to adopt -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-use behavior. *Sources:* Holmes, Mismatch: How Inclusion Shapes Design (MIT Press, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets accessibility strategy, anticipating regulatory and inclusion shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Section 508 is a regulatory code that is periodically revised, and organizations must set strategy ahead of it rather than merely comply reactively -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* U.S. General Services Administration, Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act — IT Accessibility Standards (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines inclusive-design best practice recognized across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Microsoft's Inclusive Design Toolkit is an externally credible framework cited and adopted across the industry well beyond its originating company -- the pioneer band's discipline-shaping reach. *Sources:* Microsoft, Inclusive Design Toolkit and Principles (Microsoft Design, accessed 2026-07).

#### Design Systems

<a id="ux-07"></a>
##### UX-07 — Design tokens & system governance

*Type:* Technical — Defining tokenized design foundations and governing a shared system for consistency at scale.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies existing tokens and follows governance rules under review.
  — *Why this level:* Using an established token vocabulary under someone else's governance rules is the entry-level, reviewed-work application of the token format standard -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Design Tokens Format Module (draft).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Maintains and extends token sets independently within standard governance.
  — *Why this level:* Extending a token set to fit the DTCG format while staying inside existing governance is independent, routine-variation execution within an established structure -- the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Design Tokens Format Module (draft).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves token-architecture and governance conflicts autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Kholmatova's account of design-system governance centers on resolving conflicting stakeholder needs and pattern ownership autonomously -- Dreyfus's competent band of ambiguity-handling execution. *Sources:* Kholmatova, Design Systems: A Practical Guide to Creating Design Languages for Digital Products (Smashing Magazine, 2017); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines token structures and governance models others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Atomic Design's foundational hierarchy is a token/structure framework built specifically to be adopted by other teams' systems -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-use behavior. *Sources:* Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets token and governance strategy, anticipating scale and theming needs.
  — *Why this level:* Material Design's token system is built to anticipate multi-brand theming and platform scale ahead of need, serving as the strategic reference other orgs plan against -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* Google, Material Design 3 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines design-token and governance best practice across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* The W3C Design Tokens Community Group format is the cross-vendor, discipline-wide standard for token interchange -- the pioneer band's externally credible, field-defining reach, beyond any single company's system. *Sources:* W3C Design Tokens Community Group, Design Tokens Format Module (draft).

<a id="ux-08"></a>
##### UX-08 — Component library & pattern curation

*Type:* Technical — Curating reusable design components and patterns with usage guidance and maintenance over time.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Uses and documents existing components under review.
  — *Why this level:* Using and documenting existing atoms/molecules from an established system under review is Atomic Design's own entry-level task -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and maintains standard components and patterns independently.
  — *Why this level:* Building standard components at the atom/molecule/organism levels independently is the routine, unsupervised application of Atomic Design's hierarchy -- the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Curates a coherent, reusable library autonomously, resolving pattern conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Kholmatova's central practice -- reconciling competing pattern variants into one coherent, reusable library -- requires autonomous judgment on ambiguous cases, Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Kholmatova, Design Systems: A Practical Guide to Creating Design Languages for Digital Products (Smashing Magazine, 2017); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines component and pattern standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Atomic Design's own vocabulary and hierarchy became the standard other teams' component libraries are built against -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-adopt behavior, distinct from P3's per-library curation. *Sources:* Frost, Atomic Design (Brad Frost, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets library strategy and curation standards, anticipating product needs.
  — *Why this level:* Material Design's component library is maintained to anticipate new product surfaces and platforms ahead of demand, serving as the strategic reference other orgs plan their own libraries against -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* Google, Material Design 3 (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines component-library best practice recognized across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Apple's Human Interface Guidelines component standards are cited and adopted as best practice well beyond Apple's own platforms -- the pioneer band's externally credible, discipline-shaping reach. *Sources:* Apple Inc., Human Interface Guidelines (Apple Developer, accessed 2026-07).

<a id="ux-09"></a>
##### UX-09 — Design-to-development handoff

*Type:* Behavioral — Translating design intent into clear specifications and collaborating with engineering on faithful implementation.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares specified handoff artifacts under review.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing a specified handoff artifact to a given template under review is producing a boundary object without yet authoring its translation rules -- Dreyfus's well-defined-task band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Star & Griesemer, Institutional Ecology, 'Translations,' and Boundary Objects: Amateurs and Professionals in Berkeley's Museum of Vertebrate Zoology, 1907-39, Social Studies of Science 19(3), 387-420 (1989).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces complete, standard handoffs independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Kaplan's DesignOps baseline describes practitioners running the standard handoff process independently with routine review -- the advanced-beginner band's independent, standard-variation execution. *Sources:* Kaplan, DesignOps 101, Nielsen Norman Group (2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous handoff and implementation-fidelity issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Star & Griesemer's boundary-object theory describes artifacts that must be actively translated between differing professional viewpoints when standardization breaks down -- resolving that ambiguity autonomously is Dreyfus's competent band. *Sources:* Star & Griesemer, Institutional Ecology, 'Translations,' and Boundary Objects: Amateurs and Professionals in Berkeley's Museum of Vertebrate Zoology, 1907-39, Social Studies of Science 19(3), 387-420 (1989); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines handoff processes and artifacts others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* DesignOps as Kaplan defines it is the org-level orchestration of process and artifacts that other teams then adopt -- the expert band's defines-the-approach-others-use behavior, beyond running one's own handoffs. *Sources:* Kaplan, DesignOps 101, Nielsen Norman Group (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets handoff strategy and standards, anticipating workflow and tooling shifts.
  — *Why this level:* GOV.UK's Design System codifies a cross-team handoff and delivery standard maintained ahead of tooling and workflow change across many government services -- the authority band's anticipatory, org-wide scope. *Sources:* UK Government Digital Service, GOV.UK Design System (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines design-to-development handoff best practice for the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Boundary-object theory is the most-cited framework in Social Studies of Science for how artifacts mediate across professional communities, and now underpins how the design discipline talks about handoff -- the pioneer band's externally credible, field-shaping reach. *Sources:* Star & Griesemer, Institutional Ecology, 'Translations,' and Boundary Objects: Amateurs and Professionals in Berkeley's Museum of Vertebrate Zoology, 1907-39, Social Studies of Science 19(3), 387-420 (1989).

### Product Management (PM)

#### Discovery & Research

<a id="pm-01"></a>
##### PM-01 — Product discovery & customer research

*Type:* Behavioral — Uncovering user needs and validating problems through interviews, observation, and experimentation.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs scripted customer interviews and notes findings under a senior researcher's guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Running a scripted interview and logging notes under a senior researcher's guidance is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist; Fitzpatrick's Mom Test names exactly this failure mode -- leading, biased questions -- as what a script and review catch before a researcher can trust their own judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fitzpatrick, The Mom Test: How to Talk to Customers and Learn If Your Business Is a Good Idea When Everyone Is Lying to You (self-published, 2013).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Plans and conducts standard discovery for a feature, synthesizing themes with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Planning and running discovery for one feature with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band and SFIA Level 3 Apply; it matches Torres's baseline weekly customer-touchpoint habit -- a repeatable cadence run without redesigning the method each time. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently frames ambiguous problems, selects fitting methods, and separates signal from noise.
  — *Why this level:* Choosing which discovery method fits an ambiguous problem and separating signal from noise is Dreyfus's competent band; Cagan frames this method judgment against the four discovery risks (value, usability, feasibility, viability) as the skill separating a proficient PM from one following a fixed script. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cagan, INSPIRED: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the team's discovery approach and untangles findings others find contradictory.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a discovery approach a whole team adopts and untangling contradictory findings is Dreyfus's proficient band, where practice becomes codified for reuse; this is the register Torres's opportunity-solution-tree method occupies -- a structure one person designs and a team runs against. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's research strategy and anticipates emerging customer needs before they surface.
  — *Why this level:* Setting research strategy across an organization and anticipating unstated needs before they surface is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- standard-setting beyond any single product's discovery process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what rigorous product discovery means and shapes the discipline's practice externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what rigorous discovery means for the field and shaping practice externally is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the same register Cagan's own discovery framework occupies as an externally cited reference model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cagan, INSPIRED: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).

<a id="pm-02"></a>
##### PM-02 — User persona & journey modeling

*Type:* Behavioral — Mapping target segments and their end-to-end experiences to ground product decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Documents personas and journey steps from supplied data under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Documenting personas and journey steps from supplied data under direction is supervised execution of a known template -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds usable personas and maps journeys for a product area with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Building usable personas and mapping journeys for one product area with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it reproduces Kalbach's standard alignment-diagram structure without needing to redesign the artifact -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kalbach, Mapping Experiences: A Complete Guide to Creating Value through Journeys, Blueprints, and Diagrams, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently models complex multi-actor journeys and resolves conflicting user signals.
  — *Why this level:* Independently modeling complex multi-actor journeys and resolving conflicting user signals is Dreyfus's competent band; Kalbach frames alignment diagrams as diagnostic tools for exactly this -- reconciling conflicting inputs into one coherent map, a judgment call with no fixed procedure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kalbach, Mapping Experiences: A Complete Guide to Creating Value through Journeys, Blueprints, and Diagrams, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines modeling standards others adopt and reconciles personas across overlapping segments.
  — *Why this level:* Defining modeling standards others adopt and reconciling personas across overlapping segments is Dreyfus's proficient band, where one person's method becomes the team's codified artifact standard -- the organizational use Kalbach's own alignment-diagram practice is built for. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kalbach, Mapping Experiences: A Complete Guide to Creating Value through Journeys, Blueprints, and Diagrams, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets persona and journey strategy across the portfolio and predicts shifting behavior patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Setting persona and journey strategy across a portfolio and predicting shifting behavior patterns is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single product's user model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes industry-recognized methods for journey modeling and teaches them widely.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing industry-recognized journey-modeling methods and teaching them widely is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the exact register Kalbach's own book occupies as a widely taught, externally cited method. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kalbach, Mapping Experiences: A Complete Guide to Creating Value through Journeys, Blueprints, and Diagrams, 2nd Edition (O'Reilly, 2021).

<a id="pm-03"></a>
##### PM-03 — Competitive & product-market analysis

*Type:* Behavioral — Assessing market trends, competitors, and whitespace to inform positioning and opportunity sizing.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers competitor facts and populates comparison grids under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering competitor facts and populating comparison grids under guidance is supervised execution of a defined template -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces a sound competitive analysis for a product with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Producing a sound competitive analysis for one product with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Porter's Five Forces framework as given, without adapting it to an ambiguous or unusual market structure -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Porter, Competitive Strategy: Techniques for Analyzing Industries and Competitors (Free Press, 1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently reads ambiguous markets and frames defensible positioning implications.
  — *Why this level:* Independently reading ambiguous markets and framing defensible positioning implications is Dreyfus's competent band; Moore's technology-adoption-lifecycle model requires exactly this judgment -- placing a market correctly relative to the chasm when the evidence is not clear-cut. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Moore, Crossing the Chasm: Marketing and Selling High-Tech Products to Mainstream Customers, 3rd Edition (HarperBusiness, 2014; orig. 1991).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the analytical approach others follow and decodes confusing competitive dynamics.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the analytical approach others follow and decoding confusing competitive dynamics is Dreyfus's proficient band, where a framework is adapted and codified for a team -- extending Porter's structural analysis beyond its textbook application to a team's specific market. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Porter, Competitive Strategy: Techniques for Analyzing Industries and Competitors (Free Press, 1980).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets market-analysis strategy and anticipates structural shifts before competitors react.
  — *Why this level:* Setting market-analysis strategy and anticipating structural shifts before competitors react is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- foresight beyond any single product's competitive set. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the field interprets product-market fit and is cited externally on it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the field interprets product-market fit and being cited externally is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register both Porter's and Moore's own frameworks occupy as canonical, externally cited references. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Porter, Competitive Strategy: Techniques for Analyzing Industries and Competitors (Free Press, 1980); Moore, Crossing the Chasm: Marketing and Selling High-Tech Products to Mainstream Customers, 3rd Edition (HarperBusiness, 2014; orig. 1991).

#### Strategy & Planning

<a id="pm-04"></a>
##### PM-04 — Product strategy & positioning

*Type:* Behavioral — Defining target markets, value propositions, and differentiation that guide what to build and why.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts positioning statements from a given strategy under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting positioning statements from a given strategy under direction is supervised execution of someone else's strategic decisions -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Articulates strategy and positioning for one product with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Articulating strategy and positioning for one product with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it fills in Dunford's positioning canvas (competitive alternatives, unique attributes, target market) as a standard template -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dunford, Obviously Awesome: How to Nail Product Positioning (Ambient Press, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently sets coherent strategy amid ambiguity and defends hard trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Independently setting coherent strategy amid ambiguity and defending hard trade-offs is Dreyfus's competent band; Rumelt's strategy kernel -- diagnosis, guiding policy, coherent action -- names defending real trade-offs as exactly what separates strategy from the vague goal-setting he calls bad strategy. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rumelt, Good Strategy Bad Strategy: The Difference and Why It Matters (Crown Business, 2011).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the strategy framework teams adopt and resolves conflicting strategic bets.
