  — *Why this level:* Defining the strategy framework teams adopt and resolving conflicting strategic bets is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Rumelt's kernel stops being one person's private discipline and becomes the team's shared framework for arbitrating competing bets. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rumelt, Good Strategy Bad Strategy: The Difference and Why It Matters (Crown Business, 2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns portfolio-level strategy and anticipates where the market is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Owning portfolio-level strategy and anticipating where the market is heading is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- strategic reach beyond any single product. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good product strategy means for the discipline and influences practice externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good product strategy means for the discipline and influencing practice externally is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Rumelt's and Dunford's own books occupy as externally cited definitions of good strategy and good positioning. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Rumelt, Good Strategy Bad Strategy: The Difference and Why It Matters (Crown Business, 2011); Dunford, Obviously Awesome: How to Nail Product Positioning (Ambient Press, 2019).

<a id="pm-05"></a>
##### PM-05 — Roadmap & portfolio planning

*Type:* Behavioral — Sequencing initiatives across products and horizons against goals, capacity, and dependencies.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains roadmap items and updates status under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining roadmap items and updating status under guidance is supervised upkeep of an existing artifact -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and sequences a credible roadmap for one product with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Building and sequencing a credible roadmap for one product with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it reproduces Lombardo et al.'s theme-based roadmap format as a standard artifact -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Lombardo, McCarthy, Ryan & Connors, Product Roadmaps Relaunched: How to Set Direction while Embracing Uncertainty (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently balances competing priorities and replans confidently under shifting constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Independently balancing competing priorities and replanning confidently under shifting constraints is Dreyfus's competent band; Lombardo et al. frame the roadmap as a living communication tool rather than a fixed plan, which requires exactly this judgment to re-sequence under uncertainty. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lombardo, McCarthy, Ryan & Connors, Product Roadmaps Relaunched: How to Set Direction while Embracing Uncertainty (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the planning approach others use and resolves cross-team portfolio conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the planning approach others use and resolving cross-team portfolio conflicts is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Lombardo et al.'s guidance on 'relaunching' an organization's roadmap process becomes one person's codified approach for the whole team. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lombardo, McCarthy, Ryan & Connors, Product Roadmaps Relaunched: How to Set Direction while Embracing Uncertainty (O'Reilly, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets portfolio planning strategy and foresees where investment should shift next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting portfolio planning strategy and foreseeing where investment should shift next is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach across the whole portfolio, not one roadmap. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines portfolio-planning best practice for the field and is recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining portfolio-planning best practice for the field and being recognized for it is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- externally referenced practice, not an internal artifact. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="pm-06"></a>
##### PM-06 — Vision & goal setting

*Type:* Behavioral — Articulating product vision and outcome-based objectives that align teams over time.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Translates a stated vision into concrete goals under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Translating a stated vision into concrete goals under direction is supervised decomposition of someone else's vision -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Sets clear, measurable goals for a product area with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Setting clear, measurable goals for one product area with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Doerr's OKR format -- an objective with two to five measurable key results -- as a standard structure, not an invented one -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Doerr, Measure What Matters (Portfolio/Penguin, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently crafts a compelling vision and cascades aligned goals through ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Independently crafting a compelling vision and cascading aligned goals through ambiguity is Dreyfus's competent band; Grove's original cascading management-by-objectives model requires this judgment -- aligning goals down through an org when the path is not already mapped. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines goal-setting frameworks others adopt and aligns competing visions.
  — *Why this level:* Defining goal-setting frameworks others adopt and aligning competing visions is Dreyfus's proficient band; it mirrors Doerr's own account of OKRs moving from one leader's private practice to a codified, org-wide framework other teams adopt wholesale. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Doerr, Measure What Matters (Portfolio/Penguin, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enduring vision across the portfolio and anticipates long-horizon shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enduring vision across a portfolio and anticipating long-horizon shifts is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- vision reach beyond any single product's goals. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline frames product vision and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the discipline frames product vision and being externally credible on it is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Grove's and Doerr's own frameworks occupy as originals cited industry-wide. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983); Doerr, Measure What Matters (Portfolio/Penguin, 2018).

#### Definition & Delivery

<a id="pm-07"></a>
##### PM-07 — Requirement & specification definition

*Type:* Behavioral — Translating problems into clear, testable requirements, specs, and acceptance criteria.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes requirements from supplied input and refines them under review.
  — *Why this level:* Writing requirements from supplied input and refining them under review is supervised drafting against someone else's problem framing -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Authors complete, testable specs for standard features with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring complete, testable specs for standard features with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies BABOK's requirements elicitation and life-cycle-management practices as given -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently specifies ambiguous, cross-cutting features and resolves edge cases cleanly.
  — *Why this level:* Independently specifying ambiguous, cross-cutting features and resolving edge cases cleanly is Dreyfus's competent band; ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148's requirement-quality characteristics -- unambiguous, verifiable, necessary -- are judgment criteria applied to genuinely hard cases, not a checklist for routine ones. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC/IEEE, Systems and Software Engineering -- Life Cycle Processes -- Requirements Engineering, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines specification standards others adopt and untangles the hardest requirement conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Defining specification standards others adopt and untangling the hardest requirement conflicts is Dreyfus's proficient band, where BABOK's competency areas stop being individually applied and become one person's codified standard for a team. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IIBA, A Guide to the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge (BABOK Guide), Version 3 (2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets specification strategy across teams and anticipates downstream definition needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting specification strategy across teams and anticipating downstream definition needs is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single feature's requirements. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent product specification means and influences the practice externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent product specification means and influencing practice externally is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register a body-of-knowledge standard like ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 itself occupies as an externally adopted reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO/IEC/IEEE, Systems and Software Engineering -- Life Cycle Processes -- Requirements Engineering, ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018.

<a id="pm-08"></a>
##### PM-08 — Product backlog management

*Type:* Behavioral — Curating, refining, and grooming a backlog so the team always works on the highest-value items.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates and grooms backlog items under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Updating and grooming backlog items under direction is supervised maintenance of an existing artifact -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Prioritizes and maintains a healthy backlog for one team with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Prioritizing and maintaining a healthy backlog for one team with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it performs the Scrum Guide's formally defined Product Backlog refinement practice as specified -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Schwaber & Sutherland, The Scrum Guide (scrumguides.org, 2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently sequences contested work and keeps the backlog coherent under churn.
  — *Why this level:* Independently sequencing contested work and keeping the backlog coherent under churn is Dreyfus's competent band; Pichler's value/risk/cost prioritization techniques require exactly this judgment under contested, ambiguous conditions the Scrum Guide does not resolve. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Pichler, Agile Product Management with Scrum: Creating Products that Customers Love (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines backlog practices others follow and resolves cross-team prioritization disputes.
  — *Why this level:* Defining backlog practices others follow and resolving cross-team prioritization disputes is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Pichler's guidance on scaling product ownership across multiple teams becomes one person's codified standard for the group. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Pichler, Agile Product Management with Scrum: Creating Products that Customers Love (Addison-Wesley, 2010).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets backlog-management strategy across products and anticipates capacity tensions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting backlog-management strategy across products and anticipating capacity tensions is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single team's backlog. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines backlog-management best practice for the discipline and is recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining backlog-management best practice for the discipline and being recognized for it is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- externally referenced practice, not one team's process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="pm-09"></a>
##### PM-09 — Go-to-market coordination

*Type:* Behavioral — Orchestrating launch readiness across engineering, marketing, sales, and support.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes assigned launch tasks and tracks checklist items under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Executing assigned launch tasks and tracking checklist items under guidance is supervised execution of someone else's launch plan -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Coordinates a standard product launch across functions with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Coordinating a standard product launch across functions with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it runs Bush's product-led launch motion as a given playbook, not an invented one -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bush, Product-Led Growth: How to Build a Product That Sells Itself (Product-Led Institute, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently orchestrates complex launches and recovers when plans go sideways.
  — *Why this level:* Independently orchestrating complex launches and recovering when plans go sideways is Dreyfus's competent band; Moore's chasm-crossing guidance on adapting a launch when it does not land in the intended beachhead segment requires exactly this recovery judgment under ambiguity. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Moore, Crossing the Chasm: Marketing and Selling High-Tech Products to Mainstream Customers, 3rd Edition (HarperBusiness, 2014; orig. 1991).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the go-to-market playbook others adopt and rescues high-stakes launches.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the go-to-market playbook others adopt and rescuing high-stakes launches is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Bush's launch motion moves from one launch's execution to a codified playbook a team reuses. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bush, Product-Led Growth: How to Build a Product That Sells Itself (Product-Led Institute, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets go-to-market strategy across the portfolio and anticipates market-timing risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting go-to-market strategy across the portfolio and anticipating market-timing risks is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single launch. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what great go-to-market means for the field and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what great go-to-market means for the field and shaping external practice is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Moore's own chasm-crossing model occupies as an externally cited go-to-market reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Moore, Crossing the Chasm: Marketing and Selling High-Tech Products to Mainstream Customers, 3rd Edition (HarperBusiness, 2014; orig. 1991).

#### Measurement & Insight

<a id="pm-10"></a>
##### PM-10 — Metrics & product analytics

*Type:* Technical — Defining success metrics and interpreting product data to evaluate impact and guide iteration.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Pulls and reports defined product metrics under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Pulling and reporting defined product metrics under direction is supervised execution against someone else's metric definitions -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and interprets metric dashboards for a product with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Building and interpreting metric dashboards for one product with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Croll & Yoskovitz's One Metric That Matters framework as given -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Croll & Yoskovitz, Lean Analytics: Use Data to Build a Better Startup Faster (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently designs metric frameworks and draws sound conclusions from messy data.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing metric frameworks and drawing sound conclusions from messy data is Dreyfus's competent band; Croll & Yoskovitz's stage-based metrics model requires exactly this judgment -- selecting the right metric for an ambiguous, noisy business stage rather than a prescribed one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Croll & Yoskovitz, Lean Analytics: Use Data to Build a Better Startup Faster (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the measurement model teams adopt and diagnoses misleading metrics others trust.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the measurement model teams adopt and diagnosing misleading metrics others trust is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Croll & Yoskovitz's vanity-metric diagnosis becomes one person's codified practice enforced across a team. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Croll & Yoskovitz, Lean Analytics: Use Data to Build a Better Startup Faster (O'Reilly, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets product-analytics strategy across the org and anticipates which signals will matter.
  — *Why this level:* Setting product-analytics strategy across the org and anticipating which signals will matter is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single product's dashboards. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines rigorous product measurement for the discipline and is cited externally on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining rigorous product measurement for the discipline and being cited externally on it is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Croll & Yoskovitz's own book occupies as an externally cited measurement reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Croll & Yoskovitz, Lean Analytics: Use Data to Build a Better Startup Faster (O'Reilly, 2013).

<a id="pm-11"></a>
##### PM-11 — Product experimentation & A/B testing

*Type:* Technical — Designing and reading controlled experiments to validate hypotheses and de-risk decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs predefined experiments and records results under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Running predefined experiments and recording results under supervision is supervised execution of someone else's test design -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and analyzes a standard A/B test with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Designing and analyzing a standard A/B test with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Kohavi, Tang & Xu's core randomization and overall-evaluation-criterion design as given -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently designs valid experiments and interprets ambiguous or conflicting results.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing valid experiments and interpreting ambiguous or conflicting results is Dreyfus's competent band; Kohavi et al. document exactly this class of judgment call -- diagnosing novelty effects, sample-ratio mismatch, or Simpson's paradox in results a routine reading would miss. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines experimentation standards others adopt and rescues flawed test designs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining experimentation standards others adopt and rescuing flawed test designs is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Kohavi et al.'s guardrail-metric and trustworthiness checks become one person's codified standard a team is held to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's experimentation strategy and anticipates where testing should expand.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's experimentation strategy and anticipating where testing should expand is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single test. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines experimentation rigor for the discipline and influences external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining experimentation rigor for the discipline and influencing external practice is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the exact register Kohavi et al.'s book occupies as the canonical external reference on trustworthy experimentation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kohavi, Tang & Xu, Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments: A Practical Guide to A/B Testing (Cambridge University Press, 2020).

<a id="pm-12"></a>
##### PM-12 — Pricing & business modeling

*Type:* Behavioral — Reasoning about pricing, packaging, and unit economics to sustain a viable product.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Populates pricing models with supplied assumptions under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Populating pricing models with supplied assumptions under direction is supervised execution against someone else's assumptions -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds a sound business model for one product with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Building a sound business model for one product with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it fills in Osterwalder & Pigneur's Business Model Canvas as a standard template, not an invented structure -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Osterwalder & Pigneur, Business Model Generation (Wiley, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently structures pricing under uncertainty and defends margin trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Independently structuring pricing under uncertainty and defending margin trade-offs is Dreyfus's competent band; Nagle et al.'s value-based pricing approach requires exactly this judgment to defend a trade-off rather than defaulting to cost-plus math. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nagle, Muller & Gruyaert, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 7th Edition (Routledge, 2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the modeling approach others adopt and untangles complex monetization questions.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the modeling approach others adopt and untangling complex monetization questions is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Nagle et al.'s value cascade moves from one pricing decision to a codified approach a team reuses. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nagle, Muller & Gruyaert, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 7th Edition (Routledge, 2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets pricing strategy across the portfolio and anticipates market and cost shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting pricing strategy across the portfolio and anticipating market and cost shifts is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single product's price. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines pricing and business-modeling best practice for the field and is recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining pricing and business-modeling best practice for the field and being recognized for it is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Osterwalder's and Nagle et al.'s own books occupy as canonical, externally cited references. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Osterwalder & Pigneur, Business Model Generation (Wiley, 2010); Nagle, Muller & Gruyaert, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 7th Edition (Routledge, 2023).

#### Stakeholder Engagement

<a id="pm-13"></a>
##### PM-13 — Stakeholder & executive management

*Type:* Behavioral — Aligning leadership and cross-functional stakeholders around product direction and trade-offs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares updates and gathers input for stakeholders under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing updates and gathering input for stakeholders under direction is supervised support of someone else's stakeholder relationship -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine stakeholder relationships and communications with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine stakeholder relationships and communications with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Fisher & Ury's basic principled-negotiation posture -- separating people from the problem -- to low-stakes, routine interactions -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fisher & Ury, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Penguin, 1981).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently aligns conflicting stakeholders and navigates tense executive conversations.
  — *Why this level:* Independently aligning conflicting stakeholders and navigating tense executive conversations is Dreyfus's competent band; Fisher & Ury's interests-versus-positions framing requires exactly this judgment under real, high-stakes conflict rather than routine coordination. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fisher & Ury, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Penguin, 1981).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines stakeholder-engagement approaches others adopt and brokers the hardest alignment.
  — *Why this level:* Defining stakeholder-engagement approaches others adopt and brokering the hardest alignment is Dreyfus's proficient band; Cagan & Jones describe this as the product leader's codified practice for building executive trust that other PMs in the org are taught to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cagan & Jones, EMPOWERED: Ordinary People, Extraordinary Products (Wiley, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets executive-engagement strategy and anticipates leadership concerns before they arise.
  — *Why this level:* Setting executive-engagement strategy and anticipating leadership concerns before they arise is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single stakeholder relationship. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines exemplary stakeholder management for the discipline and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining exemplary stakeholder management for the discipline and being externally credible on it is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- externally referenced practice, not one org's internal habit. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="pm-14"></a>
##### PM-14 — Customer & partner relationship management

*Type:* Behavioral — Building trust with customers and external partners to inform and advance the product.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Logs interactions and handles routine customer requests under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Logging interactions and handling routine customer requests under guidance is supervised execution of a defined support process -- Dreyfus's novice band, SFIA Level 2 Assist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard customer and partner relationships with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard customer and partner relationships with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it runs Mehta, Steinman & Murphy's customer-success playbook on routine accounts as given -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently nurtures key accounts and resolves difficult relationship conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Independently nurturing key accounts and resolving difficult relationship conflicts is Dreyfus's competent band; Mehta et al.'s guidance on rescuing at-risk accounts requires judgment beyond the standard playbook -- reading and repairing a relationship the playbook alone does not fix. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines relationship-management practices others adopt and salvages strained partnerships.
  — *Why this level:* Defining relationship-management practices others adopt and salvaging strained partnerships is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Mehta et al.'s function-design guidance becomes one person's codified practice for how a whole team runs customer success. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets relationship strategy across the portfolio and anticipates partner-ecosystem shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting relationship strategy across the portfolio and anticipating partner-ecosystem shifts is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- reach beyond any single account. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent partner relationship management means and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent partner relationship management means and shaping external practice is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- externally referenced practice, not one company's account playbook. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Discovery & Research

<a id="pm-15"></a>
##### PM-15 — Opportunity mapping & framing

*Type:* Behavioral — Structures discovered customer needs into an explicit opportunity space — mapped, sized, and compared — so solution choices trace to the most valuable problem rather than the first idea.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Places research findings onto an existing opportunity map correctly, distinguishing opportunities from solutions with coaching.
  — *Why this level:* Placing research findings onto an existing opportunity map correctly, with coaching to distinguish opportunities from solutions, is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist -- exactly the opportunity/solution distinction Torres names as the foundational skill a coach must first correct. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and maintains the opportunity map for their area, sizing and pruning branches against evidence without prompting.
  — *Why this level:* Building and maintaining the opportunity map for their area, sizing and pruning branches against evidence without prompting, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it runs Torres's opportunity-solution-tree maintenance as a standard, repeatable practice -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Structures messy, contested problem spaces into maps that make trade-offs explicit, and defends why one opportunity is pursued over its siblings.
  — *Why this level:* Structuring messy, contested problem spaces into maps that make trade-offs explicit, and defending why one opportunity is pursued over its siblings, is Dreyfus's competent band; this is Torres's own description of tree-pruning under ambiguity -- a judgment call, not a mechanical sizing exercise. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Reconciles overlapping opportunity maps across teams, exposing duplicate bets and orphaned opportunities no single team could see.
  — *Why this level:* Reconciling overlapping opportunity maps across teams and exposing duplicate or orphaned opportunities no single team could see is Dreyfus's proficient band, where one person's mapping method is applied across multiple teams' trees -- the cross-team synthesis Torres describes as a senior discovery practice. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Makes opportunity mapping an organization's default synthesis method; investment reviews open from the mapped opportunity space.
  — *Why this level:* Making opportunity mapping an organization's default synthesis method, so investment reviews open from the mapped opportunity space, is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- the method now shapes how the org allocates investment, not just how one team plans. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how organizations represent customer opportunity at portfolio level; their framing methods are cited and reused beyond their own organization.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how organizations represent customer opportunity at portfolio level, with methods cited and reused beyond their own organization, is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the exact register Torres's own opportunity-solution-tree occupies as an externally adopted method. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Torres, Continuous Discovery Habits: Discover Products that Create Customer Value and Business Value (Product Talk LLC, 2021).

<a id="pm-16"></a>
##### PM-16 — Problem framing & outcome definition

*Type:* Behavioral — Frames incoming requests and observations as customer problems tied to measurable outcomes — separating the problem from the proposed solution before work is committed.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes a one-page problem statement naming the user, the struggle, and the evidence, with review; separates problem from requested feature when prompted.
  — *Why this level:* Writing a one-page problem statement naming the user, struggle, and evidence, with review, and separating problem from feature only when prompted, is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist -- the basic problem/solution separation performed under coaching. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Frames work as outcomes the team can move rather than outputs to ship, and rewrites incoming feature requests into the underlying problem before triage.
  — *Why this level:* Framing work as outcomes the team can move rather than outputs to ship, and rewriting incoming feature requests into the underlying problem before triage, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Seiden's outcome-versus-output distinction as a standard reframing habit -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Seiden, Outcomes Over Output: Why Customer Behavior Is the Key Metric for Business Success (Sense & Respond Press, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Sets the outcome a product is accountable for and keeps the team pointed at it, publicly re-framing efforts that drift into output-counting.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the outcome a product is accountable for and publicly re-framing efforts that drift into output-counting is Dreyfus's competent band; Seiden frames holding a team to an outcome under drift and ambiguity as the harder, judgment-driven half of outcome-based work. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Seiden, Outcomes Over Output: Why Customer Behavior Is the Key Metric for Business Success (Sense & Respond Press, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Arbitrates problem framing across teams — spotting duplicated or conflicting framings — and re-cuts problem boundaries drawn along org lines instead of customer lines.
  — *Why this level:* Arbitrating problem framing across teams and re-cutting problem boundaries drawn along org lines instead of customer lines is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Seiden's outcome-based team design -- organizing around outcomes, not org charts -- becomes a codified practice applied across multiple teams. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Seiden, Outcomes Over Output: Why Customer Behavior Is the Key Metric for Business Success (Sense & Respond Press, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Defines an organization's outcome architecture — how team-level outcomes ladder to organizational results — and retires vanity outcomes.
  — *Why this level:* Defining an organization's outcome architecture -- how team-level outcomes ladder to organizational results -- and retiring vanity outcomes is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- architecture spanning the whole org's outcome structure, not one team's. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Frames an organization's hardest, ownerless problems into tractable outcome statements executives fund; their framing practice shapes the discipline externally.
  — *Why this level:* Framing an organization's hardest, ownerless problems into tractable outcome statements executives fund is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Seiden's own book occupies as an externally cited outcome-framing doctrine. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Seiden, Outcomes Over Output: Why Customer Behavior Is the Key Metric for Business Success (Sense & Respond Press, 2019).

<a id="pm-17"></a>
##### PM-17 — Jobs-to-be-done analysis

*Type:* Behavioral — Models what customers hire products to accomplish — the circumstance, the progress sought, and the competing alternatives (including workarounds and non-consumption) — to predict adoption and define product boundaries.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Restates a feature request as the job the customer is hiring it for — circumstance and progress sought — with coaching.
  — *Why this level:* Restating a feature request as the job the customer is hiring it for -- circumstance and progress sought -- with coaching is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist -- applying Christensen et al.'s core JTBD vocabulary under supervision before it becomes an independent lens. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Christensen, Hall, Dillon & Duncan, Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice (HarperBusiness, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Maps the main jobs in their area from interview evidence, identifying what customers currently hire and where those hires fail.
  — *Why this level:* Mapping the main jobs in their area from interview evidence, and identifying what customers currently hire and where those hires fail, is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Christensen et al.'s hiring/firing metaphor independently but to standard, well-bounded cases -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Christensen, Hall, Dillon & Duncan, Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice (HarperBusiness, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Anchors a product's definition and boundaries in its core job, using the job to rule scope in or out and to identify non-obvious competitors.
  — *Why this level:* Anchoring a product's definition and boundaries in its core job, and using it to identify non-obvious competitors, is Dreyfus's competent band; this is Christensen et al.'s own milkshake-study move -- spotting a job's true competing alternatives when they are not obviously products at all. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Christensen, Hall, Dillon & Duncan, Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice (HarperBusiness, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Aligns job maps across teams into one view of customer progress, exposing where customers must stitch products together to finish one job.
  — *Why this level:* Aligning job maps across teams into one view of customer progress, exposing where customers must stitch products together to finish one job, is Dreyfus's proficient band, where a single-product JTBD lens becomes a codified, portfolio-spanning map others build on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Christensen, Hall, Dillon & Duncan, Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice (HarperBusiness, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Uses jobs analysis to shape organization-level portfolio choices — which jobs are served end-to-end, which are exited.
  — *Why this level:* Using jobs analysis to shape organization-level portfolio choices -- which jobs are served end-to-end, which are exited -- is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- portfolio reach beyond any single product's job. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Frames markets and strategy in jobs terms that reveal disruption threats early; their jobs analyses influence practice beyond their organization.
  — *Why this level:* Framing markets and strategy in jobs terms that reveal disruption threats early, with analyses that influence practice beyond their organization, is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Christensen's own disruption and jobs theory occupies as an externally cited doctrine. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Christensen, Hall, Dillon & Duncan, Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice (HarperBusiness, 2016).

<a id="pm-18"></a>
##### PM-18 — Assumption mapping & discovery testing

*Type:* Behavioral — Names and ranks the assumptions behind a product bet — desirability, viability, feasibility, usability — and designs the cheapest decisive pre-build tests (prototypes, fake doors, concierge runs) to validate or kill them.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Lists the assumptions behind a proposed feature, sorts them by risk with coaching, and runs a prescribed simple test, logging what was learned.
  — *Why this level:* Listing assumptions behind a proposed feature, sorting them by risk with coaching, and running a prescribed simple test is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist -- a supervised first pass through Ries's build-measure-learn loop. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ries, The Lean Startup: How Today's Entrepreneurs Use Continuous Innovation to Create Radically Successful Businesses (Crown Business, 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Identifies the riskiest assumption before build and matches the test type to it — prototype, painted door, concierge — with pass/fail defined in advance.
  — *Why this level:* Identifying the riskiest assumption before build and matching the test type to it -- prototype, painted door, concierge -- with pass/fail defined in advance is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Bland & Osterwalder's experiment library as a standard lookup, matching test type to assumption -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bland & Osterwalder, Testing Business Ideas: A Field Guide for Rapid Experimentation (Wiley, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Surfaces assumptions others treat as facts, designs test sequences that retire the most risk per unit effort, and kills initiatives whose load-bearing assumptions fail.
  — *Why this level:* Surfacing assumptions others treat as facts and designing test sequences that retire the most risk per unit effort is Dreyfus's competent band; this is Bland & Osterwalder's assumptions mapping -- ranking by importance times evidence -- applied with judgment to sequence tests for maximum risk retirement, not a fixed checklist. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bland & Osterwalder, Testing Business Ideas: A Field Guide for Rapid Experimentation (Wiley, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Standardizes how multiple teams express and rank risk, and rejects validation theater — tests that can only confirm, never falsify — before major commitments.
  — *Why this level:* Standardizing how multiple teams express and rank risk, and rejecting validation theater -- tests that can only confirm, never falsify -- is Dreyfus's proficient band, where Bland & Osterwalder's explicit warning against non-falsifiable tests becomes one person's codified standard enforced across teams. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bland & Osterwalder, Testing Business Ideas: A Field Guide for Rapid Experimentation (Wiley, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Builds discovery-testing capability into an organization's investment process — funding follows tested assumptions, and the cost of a first test drops to hours.
  — *Why this level:* Building discovery-testing capability into an organization's investment process, so funding follows tested assumptions and a first test costs hours, is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- capability built into the org's process, not one team's habit. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Structures bets too big to A/B as staged, falsifiable commitments; their validation doctrine is cited and adopted beyond their organization.
  — *Why this level:* Structuring bets too big to A/B as staged, falsifiable commitments, with a validation doctrine cited and adopted beyond their organization, is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- the register Ries's original validated-learning doctrine occupies as an externally cited reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ries, The Lean Startup: How Today's Entrepreneurs Use Continuous Innovation to Create Radically Successful Businesses (Crown Business, 2011).

#### Strategy & Planning

<a id="pm-19"></a>
##### PM-19 — Domain & industry fluency

*Type:* Behavioral — Builds and maintains deep working knowledge of the product's domain — its industry structure, customer workflows, constraints, and trajectory — deeply enough to be a credible reference for customers and colleagues.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Learns the domain deliberately — shadows customers, reads industry sources, asks how the system actually works — and uses domain vocabulary correctly.
  — *Why this level:* Learning the domain deliberately -- shadowing customers, reading industry sources, asking how the system actually works -- and using domain vocabulary correctly is Dreyfus's novice band and SFIA Level 2 Assist -- the supervised, deliberate acquisition phase before independent fluency. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Answers most domain questions without deferring and corrects domain errors in specs and designs.
  — *Why this level:* Answering most domain questions without deferring and correcting domain errors in specs and designs is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; it applies Cagan's framing of market/domain knowledge as a core, day-to-day PM competency without yet catching risks others miss -- SFIA Level 3 Apply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cagan, INSPIRED: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Is the recognized domain reference for a product — customers, field teams, and engineers check facts with them — and spots domain-driven risks others miss.
  — *Why this level:* Being the recognized domain reference for a product, whom others check facts with, and spotting domain-driven risks others miss is Dreyfus's competent band; this is Cagan's value risk in practice -- domain judgment about what will actually work for the customer that a less fluent PM cannot supply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cagan, INSPIRED: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Connects domain knowledge across teams, catching where one roadmap violates another domain's constraints (regulatory, workflow, ecosystem).
  — *Why this level:* Connecting domain knowledge across teams and catching where one roadmap violates another domain's constraints is Dreyfus's proficient band, where individual domain expertise scales into cross-team risk-catching -- Cagan's discussion of domain fluency extending beyond a single product's boundary. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cagan, INSPIRED: How to Create Tech Products Customers Love, 2nd Edition (Wiley, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Represents an organization's domain understanding externally — industry forums, advisory boards, analyst briefings.
  — *Why this level:* Representing an organization's domain understanding externally -- industry forums, advisory boards, analyst briefings -- is Dreyfus's expert band and SFIA Level 6 Initiate/Influence -- external representation on the org's behalf, not internal reference status alone. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Anticipates domain evolution — where the industry's workflows and rules are heading — and positions portfolios for it before consensus forms.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating domain evolution and positioning portfolios for it before consensus forms is Dreyfus's master band and SFIA Level 7 Set strategy/Inspire -- foresight that shapes the discipline's direction, not just fluency with its current state. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

### Engineering Management (EM)

#### People Management

<a id="em-01"></a>
##### EM-01 — Performance management & accountability

*Type:* Behavioral — Setting expectations, evaluating performance, and addressing under-performance fairly and clearly.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers performance inputs and drafts feedback under a manager's guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting feedback under a manager's guidance before it is delivered is Dreyfus's novice stage -- following someone else's judgment rather than exercising their own; Grove's High Output Management ties review quality directly to the reviewer's own calibration, which a novice has not yet built. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard performance cycles and holds direct reports accountable with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard review cycles independently with normal oversight is Grove's baseline one-on-one/appraisal cadence applied at Dreyfus's advanced-beginner level -- routine cases handled alone, calibration still checked by a manager. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently manages underperformance and difficult cases through to clear resolution.
  — *Why this level:* Independently resolving underperformance through to a clear outcome is Grove's task-relevant-maturity judgment exercised without a backstop -- the Dreyfus competent band, where ambiguous, high-stakes cases are owned end to end. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines accountability practices other managers adopt and coaches them through hard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining accountability practices other managers adopt and coaching them through hard cases turns Grove's individual practice into a taught method -- the shift Project Oxygen found separates good managers from ones whose approach scales to others. *Sources:* Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983); Google re:Work, Following the Data: The Research Behind Great Managers (Project Oxygen research, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's performance philosophy and anticipates systemic accountability gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's performance philosophy and anticipating systemic accountability gaps is SFIA's Initiate/Influence responsibility band -- authority over policy across the organization, not application of someone else's. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google re:Work, Following the Data: The Research Behind Great Managers (Project Oxygen research, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what fair, effective performance management means and influences the field externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what fair, effective performance management means for the field is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level; Grove's own book is a large part of why Silicon Valley performance practice looks the way it does -- a definition that shaped an industry's standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).

<a id="em-02"></a>
##### EM-02 — Career development & sponsorship

*Type:* Behavioral — Growing engineers through development plans, advancement opportunities, and active sponsorship.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports growth conversations and tracks development goals under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting growth conversations under guidance is Dreyfus's novice band; Fournier's Manager's Path treats coaching as a skill a new manager must be taught before running it solo. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fournier, The Manager's Path (O'Reilly Media, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Coaches direct reports on standard career growth with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Coaching direct reports on standard growth with normal review is the mentoring-adjacent competency Fournier describes as the first rung of the management path -- routine cases, still checked. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fournier, The Manager's Path (O'Reilly Media, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently sponsors people into stretch roles and navigates complex growth paths.
  — *Why this level:* Independently sponsoring people into stretch roles is Hewlett's sponsorship act specifically -- putting one's own credibility on the line for someone else's advancement, distinct from mentoring -- requiring the Dreyfus competent band's autonomous judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hewlett, Forget a Mentor, Find a Sponsor: The New Way to Fast-Track Your Career (Harvard Business Review Press, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines career-development practices others adopt and unblocks the toughest growth cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining career-development practices others adopt and unblocking the toughest growth cases is Fournier's senior-manager layer, where sponsorship becomes a repeatable organizational practice rather than one relationship. *Sources:* Fournier, The Manager's Path (O'Reilly Media, 2017); Hewlett, Forget a Mentor, Find a Sponsor: The New Way to Fast-Track Your Career (Harvard Business Review Press, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's talent-development strategy and anticipates future capability needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's talent-development strategy and anticipating future capability needs is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level applied to the sponsorship pipeline Hewlett describes at organizational scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hewlett, Forget a Mentor, Find a Sponsor: The New Way to Fast-Track Your Career (Harvard Business Review Press, 2013).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines exemplary career sponsorship for the discipline and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized for exemplary career sponsorship is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the practice becomes a model cited outside the org, the way Hewlett's own research became a field reference on sponsorship. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hewlett, Forget a Mentor, Find a Sponsor: The New Way to Fast-Track Your Career (Harvard Business Review Press, 2013).

<a id="em-03"></a>
##### EM-03 — Psychological safety & team health

*Type:* Behavioral — Creates the conditions where people raise problems, dissent, and admit mistakes without penalty; reads and repairs team-health signals (conflict, burnout risk, on-call load).

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** With guidance, runs meetings where quieter members are heard; escalates team-health concerns they notice.
  — *Why this level:* Running meetings where quieter members are heard under guidance is applying Edmondson's psychological-safety behaviors without yet owning the diagnosis -- Dreyfus's novice band, escalating rather than resolving. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Edmondson, Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams, Administrative Science Quarterly 44(2), 350-383 (1999).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Creates safety on their own team — models fallibility, protects dissent, surfaces and resolves conflict early; monitors basic health signals.
  — *Why this level:* Creating safety on one's own team -- modeling fallibility, protecting dissent -- is Edmondson's team-level psychological-safety climate built independently, at the point in Tuckman's cycle where norms are actively forming. *Sources:* Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965); Edmondson, Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams, Administrative Science Quarterly 44(2), 350-383 (1999).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Sustains safety through pressure (incidents, deadlines, change); repairs damaged trust; the team measurably speaks up (postmortems name real causes).
  — *Why this level:* Sustaining safety through incidents and deadlines and repairing damaged trust is Edmondson's finding that psychological safety must survive pressure to enable real learning behavior -- the Dreyfus competent band, holding the climate up without external support. *Sources:* Edmondson, Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams, Administrative Science Quarterly 44(2), 350-383 (1999); Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Diagnoses and fixes systemic safety failures across teams; other leaders seek their help on entrenched conflict and burnout patterns.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing and fixing systemic safety failures across teams, sought out by other leaders, extends Edmondson's construct beyond a single team -- the same factor Project Aristotle found was the single strongest predictor of effectiveness across Google's 180 teams. *Sources:* Edmondson, Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams, Administrative Science Quarterly 44(2), 350-383 (1999); Google re:Work, Guide: Understand Team Effectiveness (Project Aristotle research, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's team-health bar and mechanisms; safety practices they designed are adopted org-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's team-health bar and mechanisms so they're adopted org-wide is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- the Aristotle findings turned into a mandated practice rather than a discovered one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google re:Work, Guide: Understand Team Effectiveness (Project Aristotle research, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the industry thinks about team health; published practices others implement.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the industry thinks about team health, with published practices others implement, is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- Edmondson's own research is why 'psychological safety' is now the field's vocabulary for this. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Edmondson, Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams, Administrative Science Quarterly 44(2), 350-383 (1999).

#### Organizational Design

<a id="em-04"></a>
##### EM-04 — Team design & org structuring

*Type:* Behavioral — Shaping team topologies, roles, and reporting lines to fit the work and scale.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains team charts and documents structure under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining team charts and documenting structure under direction is Dreyfus's novice band -- recording Katzenbach & Smith's team-type distinctions without yet applying them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Katzenbach & Smith, The Wisdom of Teams: Creating the High-Performance Organization (Harvard Business School Press, 1993).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs a sound structure for one team with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Designing a sound structure for one team with normal review is Katzenbach & Smith's 'real team' formation criteria (complementary skills, common purpose, mutual accountability) applied to a single unit, still checked. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Katzenbach & Smith, The Wisdom of Teams: Creating the High-Performance Organization (Harvard Business School Press, 1993).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently restructures teams to fit changing work and resolves boundary conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Independently restructuring teams to fit changing work and resolving boundary conflicts is Team Topologies' dynamic reteaming applied without oversight -- the Dreyfus competent band, owning structural trade-offs end to end. *Sources:* Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019); Katzenbach & Smith, The Wisdom of Teams: Creating the High-Performance Organization (Harvard Business School Press, 1993).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines org-design approaches others adopt and reshapes the most tangled structures.
  — *Why this level:* Defining org-design approaches others adopt and reshaping the most tangled structures is Team Topologies' team-interaction patterns codified into a playbook others follow -- Nadler & Tushman's architecture-as-lever applied across multiple teams, not one. *Sources:* Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019); Nadler, Tushman & Nadler, Competing by Design: The Power of Organizational Architecture (Oxford University Press, 1997).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets org-structuring strategy across the org and anticipates scaling inflection points.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-structuring strategy and anticipating scaling inflection points is Nadler & Tushman's congruence model exercised at organization-wide scale -- SFIA's Initiate/Influence responsibility. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nadler, Tushman & Nadler, Competing by Design: The Power of Organizational Architecture (Oxford University Press, 1997).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines effective engineering-org design for the discipline and is cited externally on it.
  — *Why this level:* Being cited externally for defining effective engineering-org design is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same discipline-shaping role Skelton & Pais' own book plays for team-topology practice industry-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).

<a id="em-05"></a>
##### EM-05 — Headcount & resource planning

*Type:* Behavioral — Forecasting staffing needs and allocating people across initiatives and priorities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks headcount and updates plans under direction.
