  — *Why this level:* Tracking headcount and updating plans under direction is SFIA's Follow level and Dreyfus's novice band -- executing a plan someone else designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds a credible headcount plan for one team with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Building a credible headcount plan for one team with normal review is SFIA's Apply level -- routine resourcing work performed independently but still checked. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently plans resourcing under uncertainty and defends staffing trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Independently planning resourcing under uncertainty and defending trade-offs is Cappelli's 'talent on demand' just-in-time forecasting discipline exercised without a backstop -- SFIA's Enable level, owning ambiguous resourcing calls. *Sources:* Cappelli, Talent on Demand: Managing Talent in an Age of Uncertainty (Harvard Business Press, 2008); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines resource-planning practices others adopt and resolves cross-team allocation conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Defining resource-planning practices others adopt and resolving cross-team allocation conflicts is Cappelli's make-versus-buy framework codified into an org-wide method -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Cappelli, Talent on Demand: Managing Talent in an Age of Uncertainty (Harvard Business Press, 2008); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets org-wide resourcing strategy and anticipates future capacity demand.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide resourcing strategy and anticipating future capacity demand is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- Cappelli's demand-forecasting principles applied at the scale the book itself targets. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cappelli, Talent on Demand: Managing Talent in an Age of Uncertainty (Harvard Business Press, 2008).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines headcount-planning best practice for the discipline and is recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized for headcount-planning best practice for the discipline is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same field-defining role Cappelli's framework occupies in workforce-planning literature. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cappelli, Talent on Demand: Managing Talent in an Age of Uncertainty (Harvard Business Press, 2008).

<a id="em-06"></a>
##### EM-06 — Budget & vendor management

*Type:* Behavioral — Managing budgets, costs, and external vendor or contractor relationships.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks spend and processes vendor invoices under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking spend and processing vendor invoices under guidance is SFIA's Follow level -- mechanical execution of someone else's budget and supplier decisions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages a team budget and standard vendor relationships with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing a team budget and standard vendor relationships with normal review is SFIA's Apply level -- routine cases handled independently, still checked. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently controls budgets under pressure and negotiates difficult vendor terms.
  — *Why this level:* Independently controlling budgets under pressure and negotiating difficult vendor terms is Kraljic's strategic/leverage supplier categories in practice -- negotiation posture set by risk and spend impact, not habit -- SFIA's Enable level. *Sources:* Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines budget and vendor practices others adopt and rescues failing vendor relationships.
  — *Why this level:* Defining budget and vendor practices others adopt and rescuing failing vendor relationships is the Kraljic matrix applied as an org-wide sourcing method rather than a single negotiation -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets org-wide budget and vendor strategy and anticipates cost and supplier risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org-wide budget and vendor strategy and anticipating cost and supplier risk is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- Kraljic's portfolio approach exercised across the full supplier base. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines exemplary budget and vendor management for the field and influences practice.
  — *Why this level:* Influencing the field's practice on budget and vendor management is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same status Kraljic's 1983 matrix still holds as the reference model for supplier-relationship strategy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983).

#### Execution & Operations

<a id="em-07"></a>
##### EM-07 — Delivery & program management

*Type:* Behavioral — Driving cross-team execution, dependencies, and predictable delivery of programs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks tasks and updates delivery status under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking tasks and updating delivery status under direction is Dreyfus's novice band -- following PMBOK's basic status-reporting practice rather than owning it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Drives delivery of a standard program with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Driving delivery of a standard program with normal review is PMBOK's project-performance-domain practice applied to one program, with review -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently runs complex multi-team programs and recovers slipping delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running complex multi-team programs and recovering slipping delivery is exactly what PMI's Standard for Program Management defines as distinct from single-project management -- coordinating multiple related projects toward a shared benefit, owned without a backstop. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines delivery practices others adopt and rescues the most troubled programs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining delivery practices others adopt and rescuing the most troubled programs is the program manager's benefits-realization and governance role from PMI's standard, taught to and adopted by other program managers -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's delivery strategy and anticipates systemic delivery risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's delivery strategy and anticipating systemic delivery risk is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level, applied at the portfolio tier PMI's program standard sits below. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent program delivery means and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping external practice on what excellent program delivery means is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the role PMI's own PMBOK plays as the globally adopted certification-body standard for the discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).

<a id="em-08"></a>
##### EM-08 — Process & operating-cadence design

*Type:* Behavioral — Designing rituals, workflows, and cadences that keep teams effective and aligned.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Follows and documents established processes under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Following and documenting established processes under guidance is Dreyfus's novice band -- executing someone else's meeting and cadence design rather than shaping it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs and tunes a team's operating cadence with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Running and tuning a team's operating cadence with normal review is Grove's principle that every meeting needs a purpose, applied to one team's existing rituals with a manager still checking the result. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently designs processes that fit the work and removes friction others miss.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing processes that fit the work and removing friction others miss is Grove's cadence design exercised without a backstop, matched to the DevOps Handbook's First Way (flow) principle of surfacing and removing local friction -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983); Kim, Humble, Debois & Willis, The DevOps Handbook (IT Revolution Press, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines operating-cadence patterns others adopt and fixes broken processes across teams.
  — *Why this level:* Defining operating-cadence patterns others adopt and fixing broken processes across teams is the DevOps Handbook's Second and Third Way practices (fast feedback, continual learning) codified into a cross-team playbook -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Kim, Humble, Debois & Willis, The DevOps Handbook (IT Revolution Press, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's operating model and anticipates where cadence must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's operating model and anticipating where cadence must evolve is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- the DevOps Handbook's flow/feedback/learning principles applied at organizational scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kim, Humble, Debois & Willis, The DevOps Handbook (IT Revolution Press, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines effective engineering operating cadence for the discipline and is recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized for defining effective engineering operating cadence for the discipline is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same discipline-shaping role the DevOps Handbook itself has played since 2016. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kim, Humble, Debois & Willis, The DevOps Handbook (IT Revolution Press, 2016).

<a id="em-09"></a>
##### EM-09 — Engineering metrics & productivity

*Type:* Technical — Using delivery and health metrics to diagnose and improve team effectiveness.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Collects and reports defined engineering metrics under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Collecting and reporting defined engineering metrics under direction is Dreyfus's novice band -- running someone else's DORA-style measurement pipeline rather than designing it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Interprets productivity metrics for one team with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Interpreting productivity metrics for one team with normal review is applying Accelerate's four key metrics to a single team's data, with a manager still checking the read -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently designs metric systems and distinguishes real signal from vanity numbers.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing metric systems and distinguishing real signal from vanity numbers is Accelerate's own rigorous, causally validated measurement methodology exercised without a backstop -- SFIA's Enable level. *Sources:* Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the productivity-measurement model others adopt and debunks misleading metrics.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the productivity-measurement model others adopt and debunking misleading metrics is becoming the internal authority on Accelerate's methodology, taught to and adopted by other teams -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's engineering-metrics strategy and anticipates which signals will matter.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's engineering-metrics strategy and anticipating which signals will matter is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- DORA-style measurement applied as organizational policy, not team practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines rigorous engineering productivity measurement and influences the field externally.
  — *Why this level:* Influencing the field externally on rigorous productivity measurement is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same role Forsgren, Humble & Kim's DORA research plays as the industry's reference standard for engineering-productivity measurement. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018).

<a id="em-10"></a>
##### EM-10 — Incident & operational risk management

*Type:* Behavioral — Establishing on-call, incident response, and risk practices that protect reliability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Follows incident runbooks and logs actions under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Following incident runbooks and logging actions under guidance is the SRE book's description of a new responder shadowing before they carry the pager -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard incidents and routine operational risk with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard incidents and routine operational risk with normal review is carrying primary on-call for well-understood incidents under the SRE book's incident-command structure, with review still in place -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently leads severe incidents and drives durable remediation of risk.
  — *Why this level:* Independently leading severe incidents and driving durable remediation is the SRE book's incident-commander role exercised without a backstop, plus the postmortem-to-fix follow-through that keeps risk from recurring -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines incident and risk practices others adopt and commands the worst crises calmly.
  — *Why this level:* Defining incident and risk practices others adopt and commanding the worst crises calmly is the SRE book's error-budget policy and incident-command training turned into a practice other teams are taught -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's operational-risk strategy and anticipates systemic failure modes.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's operational-risk strategy and anticipating systemic failure modes is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- SRE practice applied as organization-wide policy rather than one team's runbook. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent operational risk management means and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent operational risk management means and shaping external practice is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same discipline-defining role Google's own SRE book has played industry-wide since publication. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).

#### Culture & Change

<a id="em-11"></a>
##### EM-11 — Engineering culture & values stewardship

*Type:* Behavioral — Shaping norms, standards, and culture that define how the team builds and behaves.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Models stated values and reinforces them within a team under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling stated values within a team under guidance is Schein's 'artifacts' level of culture -- visible behavior without yet owning the underlying assumptions driving it -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Sustains a healthy team culture aligned to values with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Sustaining a healthy team culture aligned to values with normal review is maintaining Schein's 'espoused values' consistency on one team, independently but still checked. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently strengthens culture and addresses values violations decisively.
  — *Why this level:* Independently strengthening culture and addressing values violations decisively is intervening at Schein's 'basic underlying assumptions' level within a team -- the Dreyfus competent band, resolving culture breaks without external support. *Sources:* Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010); Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines cultural practices others adopt and repairs damaged team cultures.
  — *Why this level:* Defining cultural practices others adopt and repairing damaged team cultures is Schein's culture-change methodology applied across multiple teams as a taught intervention -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's culture strategy and anticipates where values must be reinforced.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's culture strategy and anticipating where values must be reinforced is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- Schein's model of culture as a leadership lever exercised at organizational scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what a strong engineering culture looks like and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible on what a strong engineering culture looks like is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same field-defining status Schein's own framework holds in organizational-culture literature. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010).

<a id="em-12"></a>
##### EM-12 — Change & transformation management

*Type:* Behavioral — Leading teams through reorganization, process change, and shifting priorities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports rollout of defined changes and tracks adoption under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting the rollout of defined changes and tracking adoption under direction is helping individuals through ADKAR's Awareness and Desire stages without owning the change design -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hiatt, ADKAR: A Model for Change in Business, Government and Our Community (Prosci Learning Center, 2006).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Leads a contained team change with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Leading a contained team change with normal review is applying Kotter's early steps (urgency, a clear vision) at team scale, with a manager still checking the result -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kotter, Leading Change (Harvard Business School Press, 1996).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently drives significant change through resistance to durable adoption.
  — *Why this level:* Independently driving significant change through resistance to durable adoption is Kotter's consolidating-gains and anchoring-in-culture steps executed without a backstop, reaching ADKAR's Reinforcement stage unaided -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Kotter, Leading Change (Harvard Business School Press, 1996); Hiatt, ADKAR: A Model for Change in Business, Government and Our Community (Prosci Learning Center, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines change approaches others adopt and rescues stalled transformations.
  — *Why this level:* Defining change approaches others adopt and rescuing stalled transformations is Kotter's eight-step model codified into an org playbook other leaders are taught to run -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Kotter, Leading Change (Harvard Business School Press, 1996); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's transformation strategy and anticipates where change is needed next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's transformation strategy and anticipating where change is needed next is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- Kotter's model applied as standing organizational capability rather than a single campaign. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kotter, Leading Change (Harvard Business School Press, 1996).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines effective engineering transformation for the discipline and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping external practice on effective engineering transformation is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same discipline-defining role Kotter's eight-step model has held in change-management literature since 1996. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kotter, Leading Change (Harvard Business School Press, 1996).

#### People Management

<a id="em-13"></a>
##### EM-13 — Onboarding & team formation

*Type:* Behavioral — Ramps new people to productivity fast and leads teams through formation stages — launches, merges, and resets — deliberately rather than enduring them.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Follows an existing onboarding checklist for new hires; escalates ramp problems.
  — *Why this level:* Executing someone else's onboarding checklist and escalating problems is Bauer's passive/compliance onboarding level — rule-following without adaptation, the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Bauer, Onboarding New Employees: Maximizing Success, SHRM Foundation Effective Practice Guidelines (2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs a 30/60/90 onboarding with named buddies and early wins; new hires ship in their first weeks and say so in check-ins.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running a structured 30/60/90 with buddies and early wins is Bauer's proactive-onboarding practice and Watkins' standard line-manager transition toolkit, applied to one team without needing design authority. *Sources:* Bauer, Onboarding New Employees: Maximizing Success, SHRM Foundation Effective Practice Guidelines (2010); Watkins, The First 90 Days (Harvard Business Review Press, 2003).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Reads a team's formation stage and intervenes on it — resets norms after a merge, names storming in the room instead of managing it by email.
  — *Why this level:* Reading a team's formation stage and intervening live (resetting norms post-merge, naming storming) is applying Tuckman's stage model to real group dynamics — situational judgment beyond procedure. *Sources:* Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds the onboarding and team-launch playbook multiple teams use; teams start faster because of materials and rituals they created, and stands up whole new teams repeatedly.
  — *Why this level:* Building the onboarding/team-launch playbook other teams adopt and repeatedly standing up new teams is codified, transferable expertise — the shift from doing to defining the approach. *Sources:* Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965); Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Designs how an organization absorbs step-change growth — acquisitions, new sites, doubled headcount — without culture dilution; integration plans carry named cultural mechanisms.
  — *Why this level:* Designing how an organization absorbs step-change growth without culture dilution is acquisition-integration design per Haspeslagh & Jemison — organization-level authority over formation. *Sources:* Haspeslagh & Jemison, Managing Acquisitions: Creating Value Through Corporate Renewal (Free Press, 1991).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Makes team formation an organization-wide capability — new groups spin up predictably without heroics — and audits that the machinery still works.
  — *Why this level:* Making team formation a predictable org-wide capability with audited machinery is defining the discipline's operating model across a company — pioneer-level practice shaping. *Sources:* Skelton & Pais, Team Topologies (IT Revolution, 2019).

<a id="em-14"></a>
##### EM-14 — Delegation & empowerment

*Type:* Behavioral — Hands over whole outcomes with context and calibrated support, pushes decision rights to where the information lives, and builds organizations that run on intent rather than presence.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assigns tasks with instructions and checks completion; keeps consequential work for themselves.
  — *Why this level:* Assigning tasks with instructions and keeping consequential work for oneself is Oncken & Wass's classic failure mode -- the 'monkey' never leaving the manager's back -- Dreyfus's novice band, not yet trusting outcomes to others. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Oncken & Wass, Management Time: Who's Got the Monkey?, Harvard Business Review (Nov-Dec 1974; HBR Classic reprint 1999).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Delegates whole outcomes with context and check-in contracts matched to each person's readiness — and resists snatching work back when it wobbles.
  — *Why this level:* Delegating whole outcomes with context and check-in contracts, resisting the urge to snatch work back, is Oncken & Wass's proper delegation levels in practice, applied with normal review -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Oncken & Wass, Management Time: Who's Got the Monkey?, Harvard Business Review (Nov-Dec 1974; HBR Classic reprint 1999).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Hands ownership of critical, visible work to someone not yet proven and scaffolds them to success, letting them keep the credit; the team runs a week without them and nothing stalls.
  — *Why this level:* Handing critical, visible work to someone not yet proven and scaffolding them to success is Grove's task-relevant-maturity model calibrated for deliberate stretch, keeping the monkey on the subordinate's back even under real stakes -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983); Oncken & Wass, Management Time: Who's Got the Monkey?, Harvard Business Review (Nov-Dec 1974; HBR Classic reprint 1999).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Pushes decisions down across multiple teams — publishes decision rights so teams stop escalating what they can decide themselves; involvement is exception-based, and everyone knows which is which.
  — *Why this level:* Publishing decision rights across multiple teams so escalation becomes exception-based is Grove's peer-plus-one decision principle scaled from one relationship into a structural org design -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Builds organizations that run on mechanisms rather than presence — delegated authorities with audit trails, pre-declared tripwires — and grants leaders consequential authority held to outcomes, not methods.
  — *Why this level:* Building organizations that run on mechanisms -- audit trails, pre-declared tripwires -- rather than presence is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level, delegation turned into designed organizational infrastructure. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Runs an organization on intent — direction and guardrails clear enough that leaders act correctly without asking — and treats every upward escalation as a design flaw to fix.
  — *Why this level:* Running an organization on intent, where every escalation is treated as a design flaw, is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the natural extreme of Grove's management-by-objectives lineage that shaped how the tech industry delegates at scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).

#### Execution & Operations

<a id="em-15"></a>
##### EM-15 — Technical debt & risk stewardship

*Type:* Behavioral — Surfaces, prices, and manages technical debt and technical risk as an economic portfolio — funding paydown structurally and setting the speed-versus-soundness posture explicitly.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records known shortcuts and defects when directed; raises debt concerns in planning.
  — *Why this level:* Recording known shortcuts and defects when directed is recognizing Cunningham's debt metaphor exists without yet managing it -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cunningham, The WyCash Portfolio Management System, OOPSLA 1992 Experience Report.
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Keeps a visible debt register with the cost of carry noted and defends a steady paydown allocation in planning rather than begging quarter by quarter.
  — *Why this level:* Keeping a visible debt register with the cost of carry noted and defending a steady paydown allocation is tracking Cunningham's 'interest' concept and acting on it independently, with normal review -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cunningham, The WyCash Portfolio Management System, OOPSLA 1992 Experience Report.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Distinguishes debt worth carrying from debt that will detonate, sequences remediation by risk, and prices debt in incident and velocity terms stakeholders accept.
  — *Why this level:* Distinguishing debt worth carrying from debt that will detonate and sequencing remediation by risk is literally Fowler's reckless/prudent, deliberate/inadvertent quadrant applied without a backstop -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Fowler, Technical Debt Quadrant, martinfowler.com bliki (2009); Cunningham, The WyCash Portfolio Management System, OOPSLA 1992 Experience Report.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Makes debt legible across multiple teams — shared taxonomy, reporting rhythm — and gets cross-team risk (the shared library nobody owns, the half-finished migration) owned and funded.
  — *Why this level:* Making debt legible across multiple teams with a shared taxonomy and reporting rhythm is Fowler's quadrant codified into an org-wide method others are taught to use -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Fowler, Technical Debt Quadrant, martinfowler.com bliki (2009); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Carries technical risk onto the executive risk register — top exposures known, sized, owned, trending — and lands multi-quarter remediation programs against feature pressure.
  — *Why this level:* Carrying technical risk onto the executive risk register and landing multi-quarter remediation programs is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- debt management exercised as enterprise risk policy, not a team register. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fowler, Technical Debt Quadrant, martinfowler.com bliki (2009).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Sets an organization's speed-versus-soundness posture explicitly — where debt is accepted for velocity and where it never is — and holds it under growth pressure.
  — *Why this level:* Setting an organization's speed-versus-soundness posture explicitly and holding it under growth pressure is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same field-defining status Cunningham's 1992 metaphor still holds as the industry's shared vocabulary for this discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cunningham, The WyCash Portfolio Management System, OOPSLA 1992 Experience Report.

#### Personal Effectiveness

<a id="em-16"></a>
##### EM-16 — Managerial leverage & focus

*Type:* Behavioral — Spends leadership time where it multiplies — deliberate calendar design, high-leverage intervention choice, and systematic abandonment of low-value work.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Keeps commitments manageable with help; recognizes when their calendar no longer matches priorities.
  — *Why this level:* Keeping commitments manageable with help and recognizing when a calendar no longer matches priorities is Dreyfus's novice band -- noticing the leverage problem Grove describes without yet correcting it independently. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs a deliberate calendar that matches stated priorities — protected one-on-ones, deep work, and team time; declines low-leverage meetings with alternatives offered.
  — *Why this level:* Running a deliberate calendar that matches stated priorities is Grove's output-equals-leverage-times-activities principle applied to one's own schedule, with the discipline still emerging -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Prunes their own involvement ruthlessly as complexity grows — automates, delegates, or kills recurring work every quarter — and models sustainable pace through crunch.
  — *Why this level:* Pruning one's own involvement ruthlessly as complexity grows -- automating, delegating, or killing recurring work -- is Newport's deliberate elimination of low-value shallow work combined with Grove's delegation-as-multiplier, exercised without a backstop -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Newport, Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World (Grand Central Publishing, 2016); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Chooses interventions by multiplier across many teams — the review that shapes ten decisions, the document that aligns three roadmaps — declining the rest by policy; audits their time and publishes the changes.
  — *Why this level:* Choosing interventions by multiplier across many teams and declining the rest by published policy is Grove's managerial-leverage concept extended from one manager's calendar to a codified cross-team practice -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Allocates attention like a portfolio at organizational scale — deep on the few places they are the unique unlock, delegated on the rest — and says which is which out loud.
  — *Why this level:* Allocating attention like a portfolio at organizational scale, naming where one is the unique unlock, is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- Grove's leverage principle applied as an executive resource-allocation strategy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Spends presence deliberately as an organizational signal — where they show up moves priorities — and guards the organization's focus by limiting concurrent top priorities and abandoning stale initiatives by name.
  — *Why this level:* Spending presence deliberately as an organizational signal and guarding the org's focus is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the discipline-shaping extreme of the leverage concept Grove's own book originated for the field. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Grove, High Output Management (Random House, 1983).

#### People Management

<a id="em-17"></a>
##### EM-17 — Motivation & engagement

*Type:* Behavioral — Builds durable intrinsic motivation: removes dissatisfiers, feeds autonomy/mastery/purpose, recognizes well.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Recognizes teammates' good work; flags demotivating friction to their manager.
  — *Why this level:* Recognizing teammates' good work and flagging demotivating friction to a manager is noticing Herzberg's hygiene factors and motivators without yet owning their removal or design -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Herzberg, One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?, Harvard Business Review 46(1), 53-62 (1968; HBR Classic reprint 2003).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Knows what drives each person on their team; removes hygiene friction and matches work to intrinsic drivers; recognition is specific and timely.
  — *Why this level:* Knowing what drives each person, removing hygiene friction, and matching work to intrinsic drivers is literally Herzberg's hygiene-factor removal paired with Pink's autonomy/mastery/purpose framework, applied to one team with normal review. *Sources:* Herzberg, One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?, Harvard Business Review 46(1), 53-62 (1968; HBR Classic reprint 2003); Pink, Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us (Riverhead Books, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Sustains engagement through hard stretches; diagnoses systemic motivation problems (not just individuals) and fixes the conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing systemic motivation problems -- not just individuals -- and fixing the conditions is Herzberg's job-enrichment redesign applied at the team-conditions level rather than the individual level, exercised without a backstop -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Pink, Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us (Riverhead Books, 2009); Herzberg, One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?, Harvard Business Review 46(1), 53-62 (1968; HBR Classic reprint 2003).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds engagement mechanisms other teams adopt; reverses disengagement trends beyond their own span.
  — *Why this level:* Building engagement mechanisms other teams adopt and reversing disengagement trends beyond one's own span is Pink's autonomy/mastery/purpose framework codified into a repeatable mechanism taught to other managers -- SFIA's Ensure/Advise responsibility. *Sources:* Pink, Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us (Riverhead Books, 2009); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Owns the engagement strategy for a function; conditions they designed show up in retention and survey trends.
  — *Why this level:* Owning the engagement strategy for a function, with designed conditions showing up in retention and survey trends, is SFIA's Initiate/Influence level -- intrinsic-motivation design exercised as organizational policy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Pink, Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us (Riverhead Books, 2009).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Advances the practice of engagement in the field; frameworks others cite and use.
  — *Why this level:* Advancing the practice of engagement in the field, with frameworks others cite and use, is SFIA's Set-strategy/Inspire level -- the same field-defining status Herzberg's two-factor theory has held in motivation literature for over five decades. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Herzberg, One More Time: How Do You Motivate Employees?, Harvard Business Review 46(1), 53-62 (1968; HBR Classic reprint 2003).

### Developer Relations & Technical Communication (DR)

#### Community & Advocacy

<a id="dr-01"></a>
##### DR-01 — Developer advocacy & community building

*Type:* Behavioral — Growing and nurturing developer communities and representing their needs internally.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Engages community channels and answers routine questions under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Engaging community channels under guidance with reviewed answers is Dreyfus's novice band; routine tasks bounded by rules, not yet judgment calls about community health. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Grows and supports a developer community segment with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently growing a community segment under normal review is the advanced-beginner band; it maps to Tuckman's forming/storming stages, which a P2 advocate can run without redesigning group structure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Tuckman, Developmental Sequence in Small Groups, Psychological Bulletin 63(6), 384-399 (1965).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently builds thriving communities and defuses tense community conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Building thriving communities and defusing conflict unsupervised is Dreyfus's competent band and matches Thengvall's account of community managers who independently own a program's health -- the shift from following playbooks to owning outcomes. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Thengvall, The Business Value of Developer Relations: How and Why Technical Communities Are Key To Your Success (Apress, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines community-building practices others adopt and revives flagging communities.
  — *Why this level:* Defining community-building practices others adopt and reviving flagging communities is Thengvall's account of DevRel leads who set organizational advocacy strategy, beyond running one's own community; SFIA9's higher bands mark this as setting direction for others. *Sources:* Thengvall, The Business Value of Developer Relations: How and Why Technical Communities Are Key To Your Success (Apress, 2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's community strategy and anticipates where developer interest is shifting.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org community strategy and anticipating shifts in developer interest is SFIA9's highest autonomy/influence descriptor -- strategic accountability across the organization, not a single community. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what great developer advocacy means and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what great developer advocacy means, externally recognized, is Dreyfus's master band combined with Thengvall's portrait of DevRel thought leaders who shape the field beyond their employer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Thengvall, The Business Value of Developer Relations: How and Why Technical Communities Are Key To Your Success (Apress, 2018).

<a id="dr-02"></a>
##### DR-02 — Developer experience & feedback loops

*Type:* Behavioral — Gathering developer feedback and championing improvements to the developer experience.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Collects developer feedback and logs friction points under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Collecting feedback and logging friction points under direction is the novice band -- following a defined intake process rather than diagnosing DX problems. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard feedback loops and surfaces DX issues with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard feedback loops and surfacing DX issues with normal review is the advanced-beginner band; it covers the Activity and Communication dimensions of the SPACE framework without yet synthesizing across all five. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck & Butler, The SPACE of Developer Productivity, ACM Queue 19(1) (2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently diagnoses deep DX problems and closes the loop to real fixes.
  — *Why this level:* Independently diagnosing deep DX problems and closing the loop to real fixes is the competent band and requires triangulating across SPACE's five dimensions rather than reading a single metric. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck & Butler, The SPACE of Developer Productivity, ACM Queue 19(1) (2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines DX-feedback practices others adopt and untangles the hardest experience gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Defining DX-feedback practices others adopt and untangling the hardest experience gaps is what SPACE's authors describe as building the measurement system itself -- moving from using the framework to instituting it for other teams. *Sources:* Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck & Butler, The SPACE of Developer Productivity, ACM Queue 19(1) (2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's developer-experience strategy and anticipates emerging friction.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org DX strategy and anticipating emerging friction is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- DX ownership at the scale of an organization's whole developer population, not one product's users. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent developer experience means and shapes the field's practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent developer experience means and shaping the field's practice is Dreyfus's master band, externally credible the way SPACE's authors became reference points for DX measurement industry-wide. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck & Butler, The SPACE of Developer Productivity, ACM Queue 19(1) (2021).

<a id="dr-03"></a>
##### DR-03 — Developer marketing & evangelism

*Type:* Behavioral — Raising awareness and adoption through authentic, technically credible outreach.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes assigned evangelism tasks and amplifies messages under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Executing assigned evangelism tasks and amplifying messages under guidance is the novice band -- applying someone else's messaging, not yet crafting persuasive narrative. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs a standard developer-marketing campaign with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Running a standard developer-marketing campaign with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying established persuasion patterns rather than adapting them to a skeptical audience. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cialdini, Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion (William Morrow, 1984).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently crafts resonant developer narratives and adapts to skeptical audiences.
  — *Why this level:* Independently crafting resonant narratives and adapting to skeptical audiences is the competent band and requires applying Cialdini's persuasion principles -- social proof, authority, consistency -- to a technically literate audience that discounts marketing framing. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cialdini, Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion (William Morrow, 1984).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines evangelism approaches others adopt and turns around messaging that fell flat.
  — *Why this level:* Defining evangelism approaches others adopt and turning around messaging that fell flat is Thengvall's description of DevRel leads who set the org's advocacy playbook, beyond running one's own campaign. *Sources:* Thengvall, The Business Value of Developer Relations: How and Why Technical Communities Are Key To Your Success (Apress, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets developer-marketing strategy and anticipates which narratives will land next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting developer-marketing strategy and anticipating which narratives will land next is SFIA9's strategic-influence band applied to messaging direction across the whole developer audience. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what authentic developer evangelism means and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authentic developer evangelism and being externally credible on it is Dreyfus's master band; Thengvall's field describes this as becoming a reference point other DevRel practitioners study. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Thengvall, The Business Value of Developer Relations: How and Why Technical Communities Are Key To Your Success (Apress, 2018).

#### Content & Documentation

<a id="dr-04"></a>
##### DR-04 — Technical content creation

*Type:* Behavioral — Producing tutorials, samples, posts, and reference material that help developers succeed.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts technical content from outlines and revises under review.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting content from outlines and revising under review is the novice band -- following a given structure, not yet making content decisions independently. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces accurate, clear technical content independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Producing accurate, clear technical content independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying the drafting-and-review lifecycle Docs for Developers lays out without yet owning ambiguous scope. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bhatti, Corleissen, Lambourne, Nunez & Waterhouse, Docs for Developers: An Engineer's Field Guide to Technical Writing (Apress, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently creates content for complex topics and ambiguous audiences.
  — *Why this level:* Independently creating content for complex topics and ambiguous audiences is the competent band and matches Docs for Developers' account of writers who scope and structure content for users they must first understand. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bhatti, Corleissen, Lambourne, Nunez & Waterhouse, Docs for Developers: An Engineer's Field Guide to Technical Writing (Apress, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines content standards others adopt and elevates the hardest technical pieces.
  — *Why this level:* Defining content standards others adopt and elevating the hardest technical pieces moves beyond producing content to setting the org's content craft bar -- SFIA9's higher responsibility bands describe this shift from execution to standard-setting. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's content strategy and anticipates which topics developers will need.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org content strategy and anticipating which topics developers will need is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- planning content coverage ahead of demand, not responding to a backlog. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent technical content looks like and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent technical content looks like and shaping external practice is Dreyfus's master band -- the discipline-shaping level Docs for Developers' authors themselves occupy as widely cited practitioners. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bhatti, Corleissen, Lambourne, Nunez & Waterhouse, Docs for Developers: An Engineer's Field Guide to Technical Writing (Apress, 2021).

<a id="dr-05"></a>
##### DR-05 — Developer documentation & information architecture

*Type:* Behavioral — Structuring, writing, and organizing docs so information is findable and usable.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes and updates doc pages within an existing structure under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Writing and updating doc pages within an existing structure under guidance is the novice band -- working inside an information architecture someone else designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Authors and organizes documentation for a product area with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Authoring and organizing documentation for a product area with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying Diataxis's tutorial/how-to/reference/explanation categories to known content rather than resolving structural ambiguity. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Procida, Diataxis: A Systematic Framework for Technical Documentation (diataxis.fr, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently architects coherent doc structures for complex, evolving products.
  — *Why this level:* Independently architecting coherent doc structures for complex, evolving products is the competent band and requires the structural judgment Rosenfeld & Morville describe as information architecture proper -- organizing for findability, not just writing pages. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rosenfeld, Morville & Arango, Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond, 4th Edition (O'Reilly, 2015).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines information-architecture standards others adopt and restructures tangled doc sets.
  — *Why this level:* Defining information-architecture standards others adopt and restructuring tangled doc sets is Rosenfeld & Morville's account of IA practitioners who redesign systems, not just organize one product's docs. *Sources:* Rosenfeld, Morville & Arango, Information Architecture: For the Web and Beyond, 4th Edition (O'Reilly, 2015).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's documentation strategy and anticipates structural scaling needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org documentation strategy and anticipating structural scaling needs is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- planning IA ahead of the org's growth, not reacting to it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines great developer documentation and information architecture for the field.
  — *Why this level:* Defining great developer documentation and information architecture for the field is Dreyfus's master band; Diataxis itself is an example of a practitioner-built framework that reshaped industry practice. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Procida, Diataxis: A Systematic Framework for Technical Documentation (diataxis.fr, accessed 2026-07).

<a id="dr-06"></a>
##### DR-06 — Editing & content governance

*Type:* Behavioral — Upholding style, quality, accuracy, and consistency across published content.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies style rules and fixes errors under an editor's guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Applying style rules and fixing errors under an editor's guidance is the novice band -- following a style guide's rules, not yet adjudicating ambiguous cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); University of Chicago Press, The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th Edition (2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Edits content to standard and enforces routine governance with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Editing content to standard and enforcing routine governance with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying an established house style to typical cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Google Developer Documentation Style Guide (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently edits complex material and adjudicates ambiguous style and quality calls.
  — *Why this level:* Independently editing complex material and adjudicating ambiguous style and quality calls is the competent band -- resolving the cases a style guide doesn't explicitly cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); University of Chicago Press, The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th Edition (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines editorial standards others adopt and resolves the hardest governance disputes.
  — *Why this level:* Defining editorial standards others adopt and resolving the hardest governance disputes is what large developer platforms formalize as their own style guide -- writing the rules rather than applying someone else's. *Sources:* Google, Google Developer Documentation Style Guide (accessed 2026-07); Microsoft, Microsoft Writing Style Guide (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's content-governance strategy and anticipates quality risks at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Setting org content-governance strategy and anticipating quality risks at scale is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- governance as a system, not a queue of edits. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines editorial excellence and content governance for the discipline externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining editorial excellence and content governance for the discipline externally is Dreyfus's master band -- the level at which a practitioner's style guide becomes an industry reference, as Chicago's has for a century of publishing. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); University of Chicago Press, The Chicago Manual of Style, 17th Edition (2017).

<a id="dr-07"></a>
##### DR-07 — Content strategy & localization

*Type:* Behavioral — Planning content coverage, lifecycle, and adaptation for diverse audiences and locales.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tags content for localization and tracks coverage under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Tagging content for localization and tracking coverage under direction is the novice band -- mechanical application of a localization checklist, not strategy. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Executes a content and localization plan for an area with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Executing a content and localization plan for an area with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying W3C's internationalization practices to a defined scope. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); W3C, Internationalization (i18n) Activity (W3C, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently shapes content strategy and resolves complex localization trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Independently shaping content strategy and resolving complex localization trade-offs is the competent band and matches Halvorson & Rach's account of content strategists who make lifecycle and locale trade-offs, not just produce content. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Halvorson & Rach, Content Strategy for the Web, 2nd Edition (New Riders, 2012).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines content-strategy and localization practices others adopt across teams.
  — *Why this level:* Defining content-strategy and localization practices others adopt across teams is Halvorson & Rach's higher-order content strategy -- governance frameworks other teams inherit -- combined with locale-data standardization at scale. *Sources:* Halvorson & Rach, Content Strategy for the Web, 2nd Edition (New Riders, 2012); Unicode Consortium, Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's global content strategy and anticipates emerging audience needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's global content strategy and anticipating emerging audience needs is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- planning content and locale coverage ahead of expansion. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what world-class content strategy and localization mean for the field.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what world-class content strategy and localization mean for the field is Dreyfus's master band; Halvorson is herself cited as the practitioner who set this field's terms. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Halvorson & Rach, Content Strategy for the Web, 2nd Edition (New Riders, 2012).

#### Education & Enablement

<a id="dr-08"></a>
##### DR-08 — Developer education & enablement

*Type:* Behavioral — Designing learning paths, workshops, and resources that build developer competence.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Delivers prepared training material and supports learners under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering prepared training material and supporting learners under guidance is the novice band -- running someone else's curriculum. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and runs standard enablement for a topic with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Building and running standard enablement for a topic with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying Dirksen's instructional-design patterns to a known topic. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Dirksen, Design for How People Learn, 2nd Edition (New Riders, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently designs learning paths for complex topics and varied skill levels.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing learning paths for complex topics and varied skill levels is the competent band and requires the learner-modeling judgment Dirksen describes for open-ended instructional design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Dirksen, Design for How People Learn, 2nd Edition (New Riders, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines enablement approaches others adopt and rescues ineffective programs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining enablement approaches others adopt and rescuing ineffective programs requires evaluating training outcomes the way Kirkpatrick's four levels prescribe -- reaction, learning, behavior, and results -- not just running sessions. *Sources:* Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's developer-education strategy and anticipates future learning needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's developer-education strategy and anticipating future learning needs is SFIA9's strategic-influence band, planning enablement investment ahead of need. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what effective developer education means and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what effective developer education means and shaping external practice is Dreyfus's master band -- the level at which an educator's evaluation model, like Kirkpatrick's, becomes the field's standard. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994).

<a id="dr-09"></a>
##### DR-09 — Public speaking & demos

*Type:* Behavioral — Delivering compelling talks, live demos, and presentations to technical audiences.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Delivers a prepared talk or demo with coaching and review.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering a prepared talk or demo with coaching and review is the novice band -- executing a rehearsed script with a coach present. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Presents standard talks and demos independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Presenting standard talks and demos independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying learned presentation structure without yet handling the room's unpredictability. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gallo, Talk Like TED: The 9 Public-Speaking Secrets of the World's Top Minds (St. Martin's Press, 2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently commands tough rooms and recovers gracefully when demos break.
  — *Why this level:* Independently commanding tough rooms and recovering gracefully when demos break is the competent band and is exactly the improvisational skill Gallo documents across top technical presenters -- composure when the plan fails. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gallo, Talk Like TED: The 9 Public-Speaking Secrets of the World's Top Minds (St. Martin's Press, 2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines presentation and demo craft others adopt and coaches them to improve.
  — *Why this level:* Defining presentation and demo craft others adopt and coaching them to improve moves from performing to teaching Gallo's techniques to others -- the coach, not just the presenter. *Sources:* Gallo, Talk Like TED: The 9 Public-Speaking Secrets of the World's Top Minds (St. Martin's Press, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's speaking strategy and anticipates which stages and stories matter.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's speaking strategy and anticipating which stages and stories matter is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- choosing where the org shows up, not just how one talk goes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what compelling technical speaking looks like and is externally renowned for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what compelling technical speaking looks like and being externally renowned for it is Dreyfus's master band -- the level of the speakers Gallo studied to write the book in the first place. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Gallo, Talk Like TED: The 9 Public-Speaking Secrets of the World's Top Minds (St. Martin's Press, 2014).

<a id="dr-10"></a>
##### DR-10 — Sample code & API storytelling

*Type:* Technical — Building example projects and narratives that show how to apply interfaces and tools effectively.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Writes basic sample snippets from specs under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Writing basic sample snippets from specs under guidance is the novice band -- translating a given spec into example calls, not yet composing a narrative. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces clear, working samples that illustrate an API with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Producing clear, working samples that illustrate an API with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, accurately reflecting a documented interface without yet making it intuitive for a first-time user. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); OpenAPI Initiative, OpenAPI Specification v3.1.0 (2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Independently crafts samples that make complex APIs intuitive and tell a clear story.
  — *Why this level:* Independently crafting samples that make complex APIs intuitive and telling a clear story is the competent band and matches Docs for Developers' treatment of code samples as narrative devices, not just correctness demos. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bhatti, Corleissen, Lambourne, Nunez & Waterhouse, Docs for Developers: An Engineer's Field Guide to Technical Writing (Apress, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines sample-and-storytelling standards others adopt and reworks confusing examples.
  — *Why this level:* Defining sample-and-storytelling standards others adopt and reworking confusing examples is setting the sample-code conventions a whole platform's docs follow -- the kind of house standard Google's developer style guide formalizes for code examples. *Sources:* Google, Google Developer Documentation Style Guide (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the org's API-storytelling strategy and anticipates which patterns developers need.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the org's API-storytelling strategy and anticipating which patterns developers need is SFIA9's strategic-influence band -- planning sample coverage ahead of what developers will ask for. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent API storytelling through code means and shapes external practice.
