  — *Why this level:* Deliberately building mechanisms to counter the feedback vacuum Eurich's research shows worsens with seniority and power -- cultivating truth-tellers rather than waiting for volunteers -- is SFIA's authority band: engineering the org-level conditions for self-awareness, not just practicing it personally. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Eurich, What Self-Awareness Really Is (and How to Cultivate It), Harvard Business Review (2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Institutionalizes challenge to their own judgment — red teams, protected dissent — and manages how their moods and offhand comments get amplified across an organization.
  — *Why this level:* Institutionalizing red teams and protected dissent against one's own judgment, and managing how offhand comments get amplified organization-wide, is Dreyfus's master band turned inward -- expertise mature enough to build structural checks on itself, at SFIA's highest responsibility level. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="li-10"></a>
##### LI-10 — Resilience & Sustainable Pace

*Type:* Behavioral — Sustains effectiveness under prolonged pressure, recovers from setbacks, and designs sustainable pace into how teams operate rather than modeling heroics.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains composure through normal setbacks; recognizes their own overload and asks for help.
  — *Why this level:* Recognizing one's own overload and asking for help, rather than pushing through silently, is the early-warning behavior Maslach & Leiter identify as protective against the exhaustion dimension of burnout -- Dreyfus's novice band, seeking help appropriately. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Maslach & Leiter, The Truth About Burnout: How Organizations Cause Personal Stress and What to Do About It (Jossey-Bass, 1997).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Stays effective and steady under pressure — recovers from setbacks, manages their own energy, and models a sustainable pace others learn from watching.
  — *Why this level:* Managing one's own energy and recovering from setbacks independently, such that others learn a sustainable pace just from observation, is self-management of the workload-mismatch factor Maslach & Leiter identify as the top driver of burnout -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band of unaided, routine-case competence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Maslach & Leiter, The Truth About Burnout: How Organizations Cause Personal Stress and What to Do About It (Jossey-Bass, 1997).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Holds up through prolonged pressure — incident sieges, crunch, organizational turbulence — helping the team stay resilient and refusing burnout-driven decisions.
  — *Why this level:* Refusing burnout-driven decisions during prolonged incident sieges is the on-call sustainability discipline Google's SRE book prescribes as a first-class practice, not an afterthought; holding the team together through it without a script is the competent band's handling of ambiguous, high-stakes situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Maslach & Leiter, The Truth About Burnout: How Organizations Cause Personal Stress and What to Do About It (Jossey-Bass, 1997); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds resilience into how multiple teams operate — on-call health, recovery after pushes, load balancing — and repairs burnout risk at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Building on-call health and load-balancing into how multiple teams operate is exactly the SRE book's toil-reduction and error-budget practices applied across teams rather than one; SFIA's higher band captures the shift from personal resilience to defining the operating model others adopt. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Stewards organizational resilience — capacity buffers, crisis rotation, energy management for senior leaders — and holds the line when business pressure argues for permanent crunch.
  — *Why this level:* Holding the line against permanent crunch when business pressure argues for it, at the scale of senior-leader energy management and org-wide capacity buffers, is stewardship against the occupational phenomenon WHO's ICD-11 formally recognizes -- SFIA's authority band of setting organizational standards, not managing one's own or one team's load. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); World Health Organization, ICD-11 QD85 Burn-out, an occupational phenomenon (2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes a resilient, sustainable culture across an organization; the organization absorbs shocks without breaking people, and the practice is referenced beyond it.
  — *Why this level:* A culture that absorbs organizational shocks without breaking people, and is referenced by other organizations, is Dreyfus's master band -- practice so mature it becomes doctrine -- operating at SFIA's highest responsibility level of externally visible influence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="li-11"></a>
##### LI-11 — Integrity & Trust

*Type:* Behavioral — Earns and keeps trust through consistency and courage — keeping commitments, telling unwelcome truths, and holding the ethical line when it is costly.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Keeps commitments with reminders; is honest when asked directly; escalates ethical concerns to others.
  — *Why this level:* Being honest when asked and escalating concerns rather than resolving them independently maps to the 'ability' and reactive-'integrity' cues Mayer, Davis & Schoorman's trust model identifies as a trustee's earliest, most observable signals -- Dreyfus's novice band, needing reminders and structure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mayer, Davis & Schoorman, An Integrative Model of Organizational Trust, Academy of Management Review 20(3), 709-734 (1995).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Keeps commitments or renegotiates before the deadline, never after; says the same thing in the room and out of it, owns mistakes unprompted, and reports true status when the truth is unwelcome.
  — *Why this level:* Renegotiating before a deadline rather than missing it silently, and owning mistakes unprompted, are exactly the behavioral 'trust taxes vs. dividends' Covey's Speed of Trust catalogs as the daily-transaction level of trust-building; doing them consistently and independently is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mayer, Davis & Schoorman, An Integrative Model of Organizational Trust, Academy of Management Review 20(3), 709-734 (1995); Covey, The Speed of Trust: The One Thing That Changes Everything (Free Press, 2006).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Makes the unpopular-but-right call under pressure and absorbs the cost personally; protects the person who raised the flag and handles sensitive information impeccably.
  — *Why this level:* Absorbing personal cost for the right call and protecting a whistleblower are the 'integrity' dimension of Mayer, Davis & Schoorman's model under real pressure -- exercised autonomously in ambiguous, high-stakes situations, this is the competent band, not the routine-case honesty of the levels below it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Mayer, Davis & Schoorman, An Integrative Model of Organizational Trust, Academy of Management Review 20(3), 709-734 (1995); Covey, The Speed of Trust: The One Thing That Changes Everything (Free Press, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Serves as the honest broker across teams — disputing parties accept their account of the facts — and carries uncomfortable systemic truths to the room that can fix them.
  — *Why this level:* Being the honest broker whose factual account disputing parties accept, across teams, is trustworthiness operating as an organizational resource rather than a personal trait -- Mayer, Davis & Schoorman's model scaled to multi-party trust; SFIA's higher band matches the shift from personal integrity to a role others rely on. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Mayer, Davis & Schoorman, An Integrative Model of Organizational Trust, Academy of Management Review 20(3), 709-734 (1995).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Builds mechanisms that make integrity cheap at scale — ethics review in design, safe escalation with follow-through, fairness systems whose losers affirm the process — and stops launches on ethical grounds with the business case for trust.
  — *Why this level:* Building fairness systems whose losers still affirm the process is precisely Kim & Mauborgne's Fair Process framework -- engagement, explanation, expectation clarity -- engineered into organizational mechanisms rather than exercised case by case; SFIA's authority band is this shift from personal conduct to organizational design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kim & Mauborgne, Fair Process: Managing in the Knowledge Economy, Harvard Business Review 75(4), 65-75 (1997).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Holds an organization's line when the profitable path and the right path diverge — the hard disclosure, the walked-away revenue — and those moments become the story the culture tells about itself.
  — *Why this level:* Walking away from revenue rather than crossing the ethical line, in a way that becomes the story an organization tells about itself, is Dreyfus's master band of judgment so integrated it defines the culture -- SFIA's highest responsibility level, where the individual's choices set organizational identity. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

## Business & Corporate Functions

### Marketing & Communications (MKT)

#### Brand & Creative

<a id="mkt-01"></a>
##### MKT-01 — Brand strategy & management

*Type:* Behavioral — Define and steward brand identity, positioning, voice, and consistency across touchpoints.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies existing brand guidelines to assets under review, flagging obvious off-brand usage.
  — *Why this level:* Applying supplied brand guidelines and flagging obvious violations is executing Keller's customer-based brand equity rules as given, without yet judging positioning trade-offs -- Dreyfus's novice band, work reviewed before it counts. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Keller, Strategic Brand Management: Building, Measuring, and Managing Brand Equity, 4th ed. (Pearson, 2013).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Maintains brand consistency across standard channels independently, handling routine positioning questions.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining consistency across standard channels and answering routine positioning questions unaided is applying Keller's brand-equity framework to known situations -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, competent without yet handling ambiguity. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Keller, Strategic Brand Management: Building, Measuring, and Managing Brand Equity, 4th ed. (Pearson, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns brand positioning for a product or segment, resolving ambiguous identity and messaging trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous identity and messaging trade-offs for a segment -- not applying a rule but deciding what the brand means there -- is Aaker's brand-identity-system judgment exercised autonomously; the competent band's hallmark of handling what the guidelines don't cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Keller, Strategic Brand Management: Building, Measuring, and Managing Brand Equity, 4th ed. (Pearson, 2013); Aaker, Building Strong Brands (Free Press, 1996).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the brand architecture and positioning approach other marketers adopt across the portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the brand architecture -- how a portfolio's sub-brands relate -- that other marketers then adopt is Aaker's brand-architecture theory applied at the level SFIA's higher band describes: setting the approach rather than executing within one segment. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Aaker, Building Strong Brands (Free Press, 1996).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets multi-year brand strategy and equity standards, anticipating shifts in market perception.
  — *Why this level:* Setting multi-year brand-equity standards and anticipating perception shifts is Keller's strategic, not tactical, brand-management layer -- SFIA's authority band of anticipating direction for an organization rather than managing one portfolio's positioning. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Keller, Strategic Brand Management: Building, Measuring, and Managing Brand Equity, 4th ed. (Pearson, 2013).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the field defines brand value, externally cited as a reference on brand building.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally cited as a reference on brand building, shaping how the field itself measures brand value, is the master-band altitude Dreyfus describes -- the same altitude Interbrand's Best Global Brands methodology occupies as an industry-referenced valuation standard rather than one company's practice. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Interbrand, Best Global Brands Methodology (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="mkt-02"></a>
##### MKT-02 — Content & editorial strategy

*Type:* Behavioral — Plan, produce, and govern editorial content aligned to audience needs and brand narrative.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts and formats content pieces to a brief, with edits reviewed before publishing.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting to a brief with edits reviewed before publishing is executing Halvorson & Rach's content-production process as given, without yet owning the strategy behind the brief -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Halvorson & Rach, Content Strategy for the Web, 2nd ed. (New Riders, 2012).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Plans and produces a content calendar independently, adapting tone for routine audiences.
  — *Why this level:* Planning a calendar and adapting tone for routine, known audiences independently is applying Halvorson & Rach's content-strategy workflow to standard cases -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Halvorson & Rach, Content Strategy for the Web, 2nd ed. (New Riders, 2012).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns editorial strategy for a domain, balancing competing topics, formats, and audience needs.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing competing topics, formats, and audience needs for a whole domain -- the editorial trade-offs Halvorson & Rach's strategy layer addresses beyond their production workflow -- exercised autonomously is the competent band; it draws on the same audience/business-goal balancing act the Content Marketing Institute's framework names its 'sweet spot.' *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Halvorson & Rach, Content Strategy for the Web, 2nd ed. (New Riders, 2012); Content Marketing Institute (Pulizzi), Content Marketing Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the content model and governance that other writers and teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a content model and governance other teams adopt is the Content Marketing Institute's framework operationalized past one domain into an org-wide standard -- SFIA's higher band of defining practice rather than applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Content Marketing Institute (Pulizzi), Content Marketing Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's editorial vision and standards, anticipating audience and format shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating audience and format shifts while setting org-wide editorial vision is SFIA's authority band -- forward-looking standard-setting, beyond even the Content Marketing Institute framework's org-adoption layer, into anticipating what the framework will need to become next. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Content Marketing Institute (Pulizzi), Content Marketing Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what authoritative content means in the field, externally recognized as a thought leader.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what authoritative content means for the field -- not one org's standard -- and being recognized as a thought leader for it is Dreyfus's master band, the same altitude at which the Content Marketing Institute's own framework became an industry reference rather than one company's playbook. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Content Marketing Institute (Pulizzi), Content Marketing Framework (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="mkt-03"></a>
##### MKT-03 — Creative direction & design management

*Type:* Behavioral — Guide visual and creative execution to deliver compelling, on-brand assets.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes design tasks within a defined visual system, with creative choices reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Executing within a defined visual system with choices reviewed is applying someone else's creative direction rather than setting it -- Ogilvy's own apprenticeship model of learning the discipline's fundamentals under review, Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ogilvy, Ogilvy on Advertising (Crown, 1983).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Delivers creative work independently to brief, managing routine revisions and feedback.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering to brief independently and managing routine revisions is executing Ogilvy's discipline of craft -- what sells and what doesn't -- unaided for known briefs; Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ogilvy, Ogilvy on Advertising (Crown, 1983).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Directs creative for whole campaigns, resolving ambiguous briefs into coherent concepts.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving an ambiguous brief into a coherent concept -- not executing a concept someone else resolved -- is the creative-director judgment Ogilvy describes as separating art directors from advertising craftspeople; exercised autonomously across a whole campaign, this is the competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ogilvy, Ogilvy on Advertising (Crown, 1983).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the creative approach and critique standards other designers learn from.
  — *Why this level:* Defining critique standards other designers learn from -- codifying what 'good' looks like -- is Ogilvy's own function at Ogilvy & Mather scaled institutionally; SFIA's higher band of setting the approach rather than practicing within it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ogilvy, Ogilvy on Advertising (Crown, 1983).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the creative vision and aesthetic direction across the organization, anticipating design trends.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating design trends while setting an org's aesthetic direction is the forward-looking judgment SFIA's authority band describes; the trend-anticipation itself is what Cannes Lions' craft-and-strategy judging criteria reward when work is ahead of, not merely current with, the field. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, Lions Awards Criteria (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes creative standards the industry references, externally celebrated for distinctive work.
  — *Why this level:* Externally celebrated, industry-referenced distinctive work is precisely what Cannes Lions' Awards recognize at the top of the field -- Dreyfus's master band, where the individual's work becomes the standard others are judged against. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, Lions Awards Criteria (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="mkt-04"></a>
##### MKT-04 — Public relations & corporate communications

*Type:* Behavioral — Shape public narrative, manage media relationships, and protect reputation through earned channels.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts press materials and media lists from templates, with messaging reviewed before release.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting from templates with messaging reviewed before release is executing supplied press-agentry or public-information tasks -- the least autonomous of Grunig & Hunt's four PR models -- without yet judging when two-way engagement is called for; Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grunig & Hunt, Managing Public Relations (Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1984).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine media relationships and announcements independently, handling standard inquiries.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine media relationships and standard inquiries independently is practicing Grunig & Hunt's two-way asymmetrical model -- persuading based on audience research -- unaided for known situations; Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grunig & Hunt, Managing Public Relations (Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1984).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns communications for sensitive topics, navigating ambiguous narratives and difficult press situations.
  — *Why this level:* Navigating ambiguous, sensitive narratives autonomously is Grunig & Hunt's two-way symmetrical model -- genuine two-way negotiation of meaning, not scripted messaging -- under the ethical judgment PRSA's Code of Ethics requires when advocacy and honesty pull in different directions; the competent band's handling of hard, unscripted cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Grunig & Hunt, Managing Public Relations (Holt, Rinehart and Winston, 1984); Public Relations Society of America, PRSA Member Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the messaging framework and crisis-response playbook other communicators adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a crisis-response playbook other communicators adopt is codifying Coombs' Situational Crisis Communication Theory -- matching response strategy to attributed crisis responsibility -- into a reusable organizational framework, guided by the professional standards PRSA's Code sets; SFIA's higher band of defining practice rather than exercising it case by case. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Coombs, Ongoing Crisis Communication: Planning, Managing, and Responding, 6th ed. (SAGE, 2022); Public Relations Society of America, PRSA Member Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets corporate communications strategy and reputation standards, anticipating narrative and stakeholder risks.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating narrative and stakeholder risk while setting org-wide reputation standards is SFIA's authority band -- forward-looking governance built on the same professional-standards foundation PRSA codifies, applied at organizational rather than individual scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Public Relations Society of America, PRSA Member Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline handles reputation, sought externally as an authority on communications.
  — *Why this level:* Being sought externally as an authority on communications, shaping how the discipline itself handles reputation, is Dreyfus's master band -- the practitioner's judgment becomes a reference point the profession's own standards bodies, like PRSA, draw on. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Public Relations Society of America, PRSA Member Code of Ethics (accessed 2026-07).

#### Demand & Growth

<a id="mkt-05"></a>
##### MKT-05 — Demand generation & growth marketing

*Type:* Behavioral — Drive qualified pipeline through coordinated multi-channel acquisition and growth experiments.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes demand campaigns to spec, with targeting and budget choices reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Executing to spec with targeting and budget reviewed is running someone else's growth experiment rather than designing one -- Ellis & Brown's growth process treats this execution step as the base of their team's workflow, and Dreyfus places supervised execution at the novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ellis & Brown, Hacking Growth: How Today's Fastest-Growing Companies Drive Breakout Success (Currency, 2017).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard acquisition programs independently, optimizing routine funnels toward targets.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing routine funnels toward known targets independently is running Ellis & Brown's test-analyze-optimize loop unaided for familiar acquisition channels -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ellis & Brown, Hacking Growth: How Today's Fastest-Growing Companies Drive Breakout Success (Currency, 2017).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns demand strategy for a segment, diagnosing and fixing underperforming funnels autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing why a funnel underperforms and fixing it, rather than optimizing a known-healthy one, is the hypothesis-generation layer of Ellis & Brown's growth process exercised autonomously on ambiguous, segment-specific problems -- the competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ellis & Brown, Hacking Growth: How Today's Fastest-Growing Companies Drive Breakout Success (Currency, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the growth model and experimentation approach other marketers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the experimentation approach other marketers adopt is installing Ellis & Brown's growth process as organizational infrastructure rather than running it personally -- SFIA's higher band of setting practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ellis & Brown, Hacking Growth: How Today's Fastest-Growing Companies Drive Breakout Success (Currency, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's demand strategy and growth standards, anticipating channel saturation and shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating channel saturation before it happens, while setting org-wide growth standards, is SFIA's authority band -- forecasting direction for the organization rather than diagnosing one segment's current funnel. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines growth-marketing practice the field follows, externally credible on scalable acquisition.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible on scalable acquisition, defining growth-marketing practice the field follows, is Dreyfus's master band at SFIA's highest responsibility level -- the same altitude at which Ellis & Brown's own coined term 'growth hacking' became industry vocabulary. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ellis & Brown, Hacking Growth: How Today's Fastest-Growing Companies Drive Breakout Success (Currency, 2017).

<a id="mkt-06"></a>
##### MKT-06 — Digital & search marketing

*Type:* Behavioral — Acquire and engage audiences through organic, paid, and search-driven digital channels.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Implements digital and search campaigns from a plan, with keywords and bids reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Implementing from a plan with keywords and bids reviewed is applying supplied targeting decisions rather than judging quality signals independently -- Dreyfus's novice band, work checked before it goes live. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Search Quality Rater Guidelines (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages search and digital channels independently, optimizing routine campaigns to targets.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing routine campaigns to targets independently means reading Google Ads' own performance and attribution signals unaided for familiar channels -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, competent within known tools and patterns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, About Data-Driven Attribution, Google Ads Help (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns digital strategy across channels, resolving ambiguous attribution and ranking challenges autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous attribution and ranking challenges across channels -- where Google's own rater guidelines and attribution documentation stop giving a single right answer -- and doing so autonomously is the competent band's defining trait: judgment where the rules run out. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Google, Search Quality Rater Guidelines (accessed 2026-07); Google, About Data-Driven Attribution, Google Ads Help (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the digital and search methodology other practitioners adopt across campaigns.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a search methodology other practitioners adopt across campaigns -- codifying how the org interprets signals like Google's E-E-A-T guidance -- is SFIA's higher band of setting approach rather than applying one campaign's tactics. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Google, Search Quality Rater Guidelines (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets digital marketing strategy and standards, anticipating algorithm and platform shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating algorithm and platform shifts before they land, while setting org-wide digital standards, is SFIA's authority band of forward-looking, organization-scale direction-setting. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes search and digital practice the industry references, externally recognized expert.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally recognized as shaping search and digital practice the industry references is Dreyfus's master band at SFIA's highest responsibility level -- expertise whose judgment about platform shifts becomes a reference point beyond any one practitioner's campaigns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="mkt-07"></a>
##### MKT-07 — Lifecycle & retention marketing

*Type:* Behavioral — Nurture, convert, and retain audiences across the customer lifecycle to maximize value.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds lifecycle messages from defined journeys, with timing and segmentation reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Building messages within a defined, already-designed journey is executing someone else's loyalty-driver diagnosis -- the diagnostic step Reichheld's research treats as the hard part -- rather than performing it; Dreyfus's novice band, work checked before use. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reichheld, The One Number You Need to Grow, Harvard Business Review 81(12), 46-55 (2003).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard retention and nurture programs independently, handling routine segmentation.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard nurture programs and routine segmentation independently is applying Reichheld's loyalty-driver logic to known, familiar cohorts -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reichheld, The One Number You Need to Grow, Harvard Business Review 81(12), 46-55 (2003).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns lifecycle strategy for a cohort, diagnosing churn and engagement problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing why a specific cohort churns or disengages, not applying a known playbook, is using the loyalty-to-growth link Reichheld's research establishes to solve an ambiguous, cohort-specific problem autonomously -- the competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Reichheld, The One Number You Need to Grow, Harvard Business Review 81(12), 46-55 (2003).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the lifecycle model and retention frameworks other marketers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a retention framework other marketers adopt -- turning Reichheld's single-metric insight into a full lifecycle model -- is SFIA's higher band of setting practice rather than diagnosing one cohort. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Reichheld, The One Number You Need to Grow, Harvard Business Review 81(12), 46-55 (2003).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets retention strategy and customer-value standards, anticipating shifts in engagement behavior.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating shifts in engagement behavior while setting org-wide customer-value standards is SFIA's authority band -- forecasting direction for the organization's retention posture, not one cohort's current churn. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines lifecycle-marketing practice the field follows, externally credible on retention and loyalty.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible on retention and loyalty, defining lifecycle practice the field follows, is Dreyfus's master band -- the same altitude at which Reichheld's own metric became a standard other researchers and practitioners cite. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Reichheld, The One Number You Need to Grow, Harvard Business Review 81(12), 46-55 (2003).

<a id="mkt-08"></a>
##### MKT-08 — Campaign planning & management

*Type:* Behavioral — Orchestrate integrated campaigns end-to-end from brief through execution and optimization.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Coordinates campaign tasks and timelines under direction, with the plan reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Coordinating tasks and timelines under direction, with the plan reviewed, is executing someone else's integration decisions rather than making the cross-channel trade-offs Schultz, Tannenbaum & Lauterborn's IMC framework calls for -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schultz, Tannenbaum & Lauterborn, Integrated Marketing Communications: Putting It Together and Making It Work (NTC Business Books, 1993).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Plans and runs standard multi-channel campaigns independently, managing routine dependencies.
  — *Why this level:* Planning and running standard multi-channel campaigns independently is applying Schultz et al.'s integrated-communications discipline -- coordinating channels to a consistent message -- to known, routine dependencies; Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schultz, Tannenbaum & Lauterborn, Integrated Marketing Communications: Putting It Together and Making It Work (NTC Business Books, 1993).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns complex campaigns end-to-end, resolving conflicting priorities and ambiguous briefs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving conflicting priorities and ambiguous briefs end-to-end -- not following an integration plan someone else set -- is Schultz et al.'s IMC judgment exercised autonomously on hard, unscripted trade-offs; the competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Schultz, Tannenbaum & Lauterborn, Integrated Marketing Communications: Putting It Together and Making It Work (NTC Business Books, 1993).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the campaign planning methodology and orchestration approach other marketers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the orchestration methodology other marketers adopt is installing Schultz et al.'s integration principles as organizational process rather than applying them campaign by campaign -- SFIA's higher band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Schultz, Tannenbaum & Lauterborn, Integrated Marketing Communications: Putting It Together and Making It Work (NTC Business Books, 1993).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets integrated campaign strategy and standards, anticipating cross-channel and timing dynamics.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating cross-channel and timing dynamics before they emerge, while setting org-wide campaign standards, is SFIA's authority band of forward-looking, organization-scale direction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes campaign-management practice the industry references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Being an externally recognized authority whose campaign-management practice the industry references is Dreyfus's master band at SFIA's highest responsibility level. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Events & Engagement

<a id="mkt-09"></a>
##### MKT-09 — Event & field marketing

*Type:* Behavioral — Plan and run events and field programs that generate engagement and pipeline.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports event logistics and setup under direction, with arrangements reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting logistics and setup under direction, with arrangements reviewed, is executing the operational layer of Getz's planned-events framework without yet judging the experience design behind it -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Getz, Event Studies: Theory, Research and Policy for Planned Events (Butterworth-Heinemann/Elsevier, 2007).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard events and field programs independently, handling routine vendor and attendee issues.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard events independently and handling routine vendor and attendee issues is applying Getz's event-management operations to known formats -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Getz, Event Studies: Theory, Research and Policy for Planned Events (Butterworth-Heinemann/Elsevier, 2007).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns flagship events end-to-end, resolving ambiguous trade-offs in scope, budget, and experience.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous scope, budget, and experience trade-offs for a flagship event -- the design judgment Getz's framework treats as distinct from execution -- exercised autonomously is the competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Getz, Event Studies: Theory, Research and Policy for Planned Events (Butterworth-Heinemann/Elsevier, 2007).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the event playbook and field-marketing approach other organizers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the event playbook other organizers adopt is codifying Getz's planned-events design principles into reusable organizational practice -- SFIA's higher band of setting approach. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Getz, Event Studies: Theory, Research and Policy for Planned Events (Butterworth-Heinemann/Elsevier, 2007).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets event strategy and experience standards, anticipating shifts in audience engagement.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating shifts in audience engagement while setting org-wide event standards is SFIA's authority band of forward-looking, organization-scale direction-setting. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what great events mean in the field, externally sought to design landmark experiences.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally sought to design landmark experiences, defining what great events mean for the field, is Dreyfus's master band -- practice so mature it becomes the reference the discipline, including researchers like Getz, points to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Getz, Event Studies: Theory, Research and Policy for Planned Events (Butterworth-Heinemann/Elsevier, 2007).

<a id="mkt-10"></a>
##### MKT-10 — Community & advocacy programs

*Type:* Behavioral — Build and nurture communities and advocates that amplify reach and loyalty.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Moderates and supports community activity under direction, with responses reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Moderating and supporting activity under direction, with responses reviewed, is participating in a community of practice at its most peripheral -- Wenger's legitimate peripheral participation -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wenger, Communities of Practice: Learning, Meaning, and Identity (Cambridge University Press, 1998).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard community and advocacy programs independently, handling routine member needs.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard programs and routine member needs independently is moving from peripheral to fuller participation in Wenger's community-of-practice model, applied to known situations -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wenger, Communities of Practice: Learning, Meaning, and Identity (Cambridge University Press, 1998).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns community strategy for a program, resolving ambiguous engagement and conflict situations autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous engagement and conflict situations autonomously is the community-design judgment Fournier & Lee identify as separating brand communities that work from those treated as a marketing channel -- exercised without a script, the competent band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wenger, Communities of Practice: Learning, Meaning, and Identity (Cambridge University Press, 1998); Fournier & Lee, Getting Brand Communities Right, Harvard Business Review 87(4), 105-111 (2009).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the community-building and advocacy model other program leads adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the community-building model other program leads adopt is elevating Fournier & Lee's design principles -- treat the community as corporate strategy, not a channel -- from one program to organizational practice; SFIA's higher band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fournier & Lee, Getting Brand Communities Right, Harvard Business Review 87(4), 105-111 (2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets community strategy and health standards, anticipating shifts in member behavior and sentiment.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating shifts in member behavior and sentiment while setting org-wide community-health standards is SFIA's authority band of forward-looking, organization-scale direction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes community and advocacy practice the field follows, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Being an externally recognized authority whose community practice the field follows is Dreyfus's master band -- the same altitude Fournier & Lee's own research draws on when citing landmark communities as the field's reference cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fournier & Lee, Getting Brand Communities Right, Harvard Business Review 87(4), 105-111 (2009).

#### Marketing Operations & Insight

<a id="mkt-11"></a>
##### MKT-11 — Marketing analytics & attribution

*Type:* Technical — Measure marketing performance and attribute outcomes across channels to guide investment.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Pulls standard marketing reports and metrics, with interpretation reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Pulling standard reports with interpretation reviewed is retrieving the named metrics Farris et al.'s guide catalogs without yet judging what they mean for a decision -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Farris, Bendle, Pfeifer & Reibstein, Marketing Metrics: The Definitive Guide to Measuring Marketing Performance, 2nd ed. (Pearson FT Press, 2010).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds routine dashboards and attribution analyses independently, answering standard performance questions.
  — *Why this level:* Building routine dashboards and answering standard performance questions independently is applying Farris et al.'s metrics definitions to known, well-posed questions -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Farris, Bendle, Pfeifer & Reibstein, Marketing Metrics: The Definitive Guide to Measuring Marketing Performance, 2nd ed. (Pearson FT Press, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns measurement for a domain, resolving ambiguous attribution and data-quality problems autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous multi-touch attribution -- the exact problem Shao & Li's data-driven attribution models were built to address, where no single fixed rule like first-touch or last-touch is defensible -- autonomously for a domain is the competent band's hallmark of judgment where the rules run out. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Shao & Li, Data-driven Multi-touch Attribution Models, KDD 2011; Farris, Bendle, Pfeifer & Reibstein, Marketing Metrics: The Definitive Guide to Measuring Marketing Performance, 2nd ed. (Pearson FT Press, 2010).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the attribution methodology and measurement framework other analysts adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining an attribution methodology other analysts adopt -- choosing and codifying a data-driven model over simpler heuristics, per Shao & Li's comparison -- is SFIA's higher band of setting approach rather than resolving one domain's data-quality problems. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Shao & Li, Data-driven Multi-touch Attribution Models, KDD 2011.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets analytics strategy and measurement standards, anticipating shifts in data and privacy constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating shifts in data and privacy constraints while setting org-wide measurement standards is SFIA's authority band -- forward-looking governance, not one domain's current attribution model. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines marketing-measurement practice the field follows, externally credible on attribution.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible on attribution, defining measurement practice the field follows, is Dreyfus's master band -- the altitude at which a practitioner's approach to the same multi-touch attribution problem Shao & Li formalized becomes the field's reference. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Shao & Li, Data-driven Multi-touch Attribution Models, KDD 2011.

<a id="mkt-12"></a>
##### MKT-12 — Marketing operations & automation

*Type:* Behavioral — Design marketing processes, data flows, and automated programs that scale execution.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes automation tasks and data hygiene under direction, with configuration reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Executing automation tasks and data hygiene under direction, with configuration reviewed, is running someone else's martech process rather than managing it as software -- Brinker's core thesis in Hacking Marketing -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brinker, Hacking Marketing: Agile Practices to Make Marketing Smarter, Faster, and More Innovative (Wiley, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds and maintains standard automation workflows independently, handling routine operational issues.
  — *Why this level:* Building and maintaining standard workflows independently is applying Brinker's agile-marketing-management practices to known, routine operational issues -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brinker, Hacking Marketing: Agile Practices to Make Marketing Smarter, Faster, and More Innovative (Wiley, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns the marketing operations stack for a team, resolving ambiguous process and data challenges autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous process and data challenges across a stack chosen from the thousands of tools chiefmartec's landscape tracks -- with no single right architecture -- autonomously is the competent band's handling of what no vendor playbook covers. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brinker, Hacking Marketing: Agile Practices to Make Marketing Smarter, Faster, and More Innovative (Wiley, 2016); Brinker, Marketing Technology Landscape Supergraphic, chiefmartec.com (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the operations architecture and automation standards other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the operations architecture other practitioners adopt is installing Brinker's agile-marketing-as-software discipline as organizational standard rather than one team's stack -- SFIA's higher band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Brinker, Hacking Marketing: Agile Practices to Make Marketing Smarter, Faster, and More Innovative (Wiley, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets marketing-operations strategy and governance, anticipating scaling and integration needs.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating scaling and integration needs ahead of the market -- in a landscape chiefmartec tracks growing by thousands of new tools yearly -- while setting org-wide governance is SFIA's authority band of forward-looking, organization-scale direction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Brinker, Marketing Technology Landscape Supergraphic, chiefmartec.com (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes marketing-operations practice the industry references, externally recognized expert.
  — *Why this level:* Being an externally recognized expert whose operations practice the industry references is Dreyfus's master band -- the same altitude Brinker himself occupies now that chiefmartec's landscape has become the field's own reference document. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Brinker, Hacking Marketing: Agile Practices to Make Marketing Smarter, Faster, and More Innovative (Wiley, 2016); Brinker, Marketing Technology Landscape Supergraphic, chiefmartec.com (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="mkt-13"></a>
##### MKT-13 — Customer & audience research

*Type:* Technical — Generate audience insight through segmentation, research, and behavioral analysis.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Conducts research tasks to a defined protocol, with analysis reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Conducting research to a defined protocol with analysis reviewed is executing the segmentation and targeting steps Kotler & Keller's STP framework specifies, without yet designing the study -- Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kotler & Keller, Marketing Management, 15th ed. (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard studies and surveys independently, drawing routine insights from data.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard studies and drawing routine insights independently is applying Kotler & Keller's segmentation methodology to known, well-posed questions -- Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kotler & Keller, Marketing Management, 15th ed. (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns research for a question, designing methods and resolving ambiguous findings autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the method itself and resolving ambiguous findings -- under the methodological and ethical rigor ESOMAR's Code requires of professional researchers -- autonomously for a genuinely open question is the competent band, distinct from running a study someone else designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ICC/ESOMAR, International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics (2025); Kotler & Keller, Marketing Management, 15th ed. (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the research methodology and insight frameworks other researchers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining a research methodology other researchers adopt, grounded in the professional standards ESOMAR's Code sets for the discipline, is SFIA's higher band of setting approach rather than designing one study. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ICC/ESOMAR, International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics (2025).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the research agenda and rigor standards, anticipating shifts in audience and method.
  — *Why this level:* Anticipating shifts in audience and method while setting an org's research agenda and rigor standards -- the kind of forward-looking governance ESOMAR's own periodic Code revisions institutionalize at industry scale -- is SFIA's authority band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ICC/ESOMAR, International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics (2025).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines audience-research practice the field follows, externally credible on customer insight.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally credible on customer insight, defining audience-research practice the field follows, is Dreyfus's master band -- the altitude at which a practitioner's methods become as referenced as the standards bodies, like ESOMAR, that govern the discipline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ICC/ESOMAR, International Code on Market, Opinion and Social Research and Data Analytics (2025).

### Sales (SAL)

#### Pipeline Generation

<a id="sal-01"></a>
##### SAL-01 — Prospecting & lead qualification

*Type:* Behavioral — Identify, reach, and qualify prospects to build a healthy top-of-funnel pipeline.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Works defined prospect lists and qualifies leads against a checklist, with outreach reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Working defined prospect lists and qualifying leads against a checklist under review is explicit, rule-following execution -- the Dreyfus novice band; it is also the narrowly scoped SDR role Predictable Revenue's Cold Calling 2.0 model deliberately hands to new specialists before they own a cadence. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ross & Tyler, Predictable Revenue: Turn Your Business Into a Sales Machine with the $100 Million Best Practices of Salesforce.com (PebbleStorm, 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard prospecting independently, qualifying routine opportunities to agreed criteria.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard prospecting independently and qualifying routine opportunities to agreed criteria is Cold Calling 2.0's specialized outbound motion executed without escalation -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Ross & Tyler, Predictable Revenue: Turn Your Business Into a Sales Machine with the $100 Million Best Practices of Salesforce.com (PebbleStorm, 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns prospecting for a territory, qualifying ambiguous and complex opportunities autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning prospecting for a territory and qualifying ambiguous, complex opportunities autonomously is applying MEDDICC's qualification criteria (Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria) with judgment rather than as a checklist -- the Dreyfus competent band, the rep other reps go to. *Sources:* Whyte (with Dunkel & Napoli), MEDDICC: The Ultimate Guide to Staying One Step Ahead in the Complex Sale (self-published, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the prospecting and qualification methodology other reps adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the prospecting and qualification methodology other reps adopt is SFIA's Selling skill at the 'ensure, advise' responsibility level -- authoritative advice that shapes how a team qualifies, not just personal execution. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the pipeline-generation strategy and qualification standards across the organization.
  — *Why this level:* Setting pipeline-generation strategy and qualification standards across the organization is SFIA's Selling skill at the 'initiate, influence' level -- organizational policy-setting beyond any one team's methodology. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes prospecting practice the profession references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Predictable Revenue's role-specialized outbound model became a reference prospecting practice across B2B SaaS (dubbed the 'Sales Bible of Silicon Valley'); shaping prospecting practice the profession references is exactly that discipline-defining, externally credible Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Ross & Tyler, Predictable Revenue: Turn Your Business Into a Sales Machine with the $100 Million Best Practices of Salesforce.com (PebbleStorm, 2011).

<a id="sal-02"></a>
##### SAL-02 — Territory & market coverage planning

*Type:* Behavioral — Segment and prioritize territories and markets to optimize sales coverage and effort.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains territory data and coverage lists under direction, with assignments reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining territory data and coverage lists under direction, with assignments reviewed, is explicit record-keeping without independent design judgment -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Plans coverage for a defined territory independently, handling routine allocation decisions.
  — *Why this level:* Planning coverage for a defined territory independently and handling routine allocation is applying Zoltners, Sinha & Lorimer's territory-alignment method to bounded, routine cases without redesigning the model -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Zoltners, Sinha & Lorimer, Sales Force Design for Strategic Advantage (Palgrave Macmillan, 2004).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns territory design for a region, resolving ambiguous segmentation and capacity trade-offs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning territory design for a region and resolving ambiguous segmentation and capacity trade-offs autonomously is applying the same segmentation-alignment-sizing framework with judgment to the 'overlooked productivity' problems the book addresses -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Zoltners, Sinha & Lorimer, Sales Force Design for Strategic Advantage (Palgrave Macmillan, 2004).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the territory-planning methodology and coverage model other planners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the territory-planning methodology and coverage model other planners adopt is SFIA's Selling skill 'ensure, advise' level -- turning personal design judgment into a method others follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets market-coverage strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in market and capacity.
  — *Why this level:* Setting market-coverage strategy and standards while anticipating shifts in market and capacity is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to coverage strategy across the org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines territory-design practice the field follows, externally credible on coverage strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Zoltners, Sinha & Lorimer's territory-alignment research, drawn from direct work with 300+ sales forces, is the field's standard reference for coverage design; defining practice the field follows at that scale is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Zoltners, Sinha & Lorimer, Sales Force Design for Strategic Advantage (Palgrave Macmillan, 2004).

#### Selling

<a id="sal-03"></a>
##### SAL-03 — Consultative & solution selling

*Type:* Behavioral — Diagnose customer needs and craft tailored solutions that link value to outcomes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Follows a discovery script to surface needs, with solution framing reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Following a discovery script to surface needs, with solution framing reviewed, is explicit rule-following before internalizing SPIN's Situation-Problem-Implication-Need-payoff sequence as judgment -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rackham, SPIN Selling (McGraw-Hill, 1988).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs consultative conversations independently, mapping routine needs to solutions.
  — *Why this level:* Running consultative conversations independently and mapping routine needs to solutions is executing Rackham's SPIN sequence unsupervised on the major-sale conversations it was built from -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Rackham, SPIN Selling (McGraw-Hill, 1988).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns complex consultative deals, diagnosing ambiguous needs and shaping tailored solutions autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning complex consultative deals -- diagnosing ambiguous needs and shaping tailored solutions autonomously -- is the Challenger profile's 'commercial teaching': reframing a customer's own problem for them, the highest-performing profile in CEB's study, and the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Dixon & Adamson, The Challenger Sale: Taking Control of the Customer Conversation (Portfolio/Penguin, 2011).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the consultative selling methodology and discovery approach other sellers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the consultative-selling methodology and discovery approach other sellers adopt is turning Challenger's commercial-teaching insight into a codified internal methodology -- moving from personal skill to a taught approach. *Sources:* Dixon & Adamson, The Challenger Sale: Taking Control of the Customer Conversation (Portfolio/Penguin, 2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the solution-selling strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in buyer needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting solution-selling strategy and standards while anticipating shifts in buyer needs is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to how a whole sales org approaches diagnosis. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes consultative-selling practice the profession references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* SPIN Selling's needs-diagnosis research reshaped how the selling profession itself defines a major sale, cited and taught industry-wide decades on -- shaping practice the profession references is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Rackham, SPIN Selling (McGraw-Hill, 1988).

<a id="sal-04"></a>
##### SAL-04 — Sales presentations & demonstrations

*Type:* Behavioral — Deliver persuasive presentations and demonstrations that advance buyer commitment.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Delivers standard presentations from a deck, with delivery reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering standard presentations from a deck, with delivery reviewed, is explicit script-following without adapting structure -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Tailors and presents independently to routine audiences, handling common questions.
  — *Why this level:* Tailoring and presenting independently to routine audiences, handling common questions, is applying Resonate's narrative-structure techniques (hero, journey, meaningful content) to standard talks without yet reworking the story for hard rooms -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Duarte, Resonate: Present Visual Stories that Transform Audiences (Wiley, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns high-stakes presentations, adapting to ambiguous rooms and tough objections autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning high-stakes presentations and adapting to ambiguous rooms and tough objections autonomously is Resonate's full storytelling method -- structuring content as a persuasive journey in real time -- applied with judgment, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Duarte, Resonate: Present Visual Stories that Transform Audiences (Wiley, 2010).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the presentation and demo approach other sellers learn from.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the presentation and demo approach other sellers learn from is codifying Challenger-style commercial teaching into a reusable narrative others are trained on, not just performing it personally. *Sources:* Dixon & Adamson, The Challenger Sale: Taking Control of the Customer Conversation (Portfolio/Penguin, 2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets presentation strategy and storytelling standards across the sales organization.
  — *Why this level:* Setting presentation strategy and storytelling standards across the sales organization is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to how the whole org communicates value. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what compelling sales presentation means in the field, externally sought to teach it.
  — *Why this level:* Duarte's presentation framework, drawn from decades of coaching Fortune 500 and TED-level speakers, is an industry reference structure for persuasive presenting; defining what compelling sales presentation means at that scale is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Duarte, Resonate: Present Visual Stories that Transform Audiences (Wiley, 2010).

<a id="sal-05"></a>
##### SAL-05 — Negotiation & closing

*Type:* Behavioral — Navigate terms, resolve objections, and close agreements that protect mutual value.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes standard closing steps within set terms, with concessions reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Executing standard closing steps within set terms, with concessions reviewed, is rule-following before internalizing principled negotiation as judgment -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Negotiates and closes routine deals independently within approved guardrails.
  — *Why this level:* Negotiating and closing routine deals independently within approved guardrails is applying Getting to Yes's principled-negotiation method (interests over positions, objective criteria) unsupervised on bounded deals -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns complex negotiations, navigating ambiguous terms and multi-party closes autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning complex negotiations -- ambiguous terms, multi-party closes -- autonomously is running a full Blue Sheet analysis of competing buying influences and red flags without a template, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Miller & Heiman, Strategic Selling: The Unique Sales System Proven Successful by America's Best Companies (William Morrow, 1985).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the negotiation and closing playbook other sellers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the negotiation and closing playbook other sellers adopt is turning personal Blue Sheet discipline into the org's standard multi-stakeholder deal-navigation method. *Sources:* Miller & Heiman, Strategic Selling: The Unique Sales System Proven Successful by America's Best Companies (William Morrow, 1985).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets negotiation strategy and deal-term standards, anticipating buyer tactics.
  — *Why this level:* Setting negotiation strategy and deal-term standards while anticipating buyer tactics is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to negotiation policy across the sales org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes negotiation practice the profession references, externally recognized authority on closing.
  — *Why this level:* Getting to Yes's principled-negotiation framework, from the Harvard Negotiation Project, is among the most widely taught negotiation methods in business and diplomacy alike; shaping practice the profession references at that reach is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).

#### Deal & Account Management

<a id="sal-06"></a>
##### SAL-06 — Sales pipeline & deal management

*Type:* Behavioral — Manage opportunities through stages with rigor, hygiene, and momentum to close.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates deal records and stages under direction, with hygiene reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Updating deal records and stages under direction, with hygiene reviewed, is explicit, checked data entry -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages a personal pipeline independently, advancing routine deals through stages.
  — *Why this level:* Managing a personal pipeline independently and advancing routine deals through stages is tracking MEDDICC's qualification fields (Metrics, Champion, Decision Process) for standard deals without yet using them to diagnose stalls -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Whyte (with Dunkel & Napoli), MEDDICC: The Ultimate Guide to Staying One Step Ahead in the Complex Sale (self-published, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns a complex pipeline, diagnosing stalled deals and prioritizing ambiguous trade-offs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning a complex pipeline -- diagnosing stalled deals and prioritizing ambiguous trade-offs autonomously -- is using MEDDICC's qualification gaps diagnostically to find why a deal is stuck, not just to score it, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Whyte (with Dunkel & Napoli), MEDDICC: The Ultimate Guide to Staying One Step Ahead in the Complex Sale (self-published, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the pipeline-management discipline and deal-review approach other sellers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the pipeline-management discipline and deal-review approach other sellers adopt is turning personal diagnostic skill into the review cadence and hygiene standard CSO Insights ties to 'world-class' forecast win rates. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 2018-2019 Sales Performance Study: Selling in the Age of Ceaseless Change (2018).
