- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets pipeline strategy and deal-management standards, anticipating funnel risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting pipeline strategy and deal-management standards while anticipating funnel risks is applying CSO Insights' world-class-vs-average benchmark data (57% vs 47% forecast win rate) to set org-wide pipeline policy. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 2018-2019 Sales Performance Study: Selling in the Age of Ceaseless Change (2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines pipeline-management practice the profession references, externally credible authority.
  — *Why this level:* Defining pipeline-management practice the profession references, an externally credible authority, is SFIA's Selling skill ceiling of organizational influence extended to cross-company recognition -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sal-07"></a>
##### SAL-07 — Account planning & expansion

*Type:* Behavioral — Develop strategic account plans that retain, grow, and expand key relationships.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains account records and plans under direction, with priorities reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining account records and plans under direction, with priorities reviewed, is explicit record-keeping without independent strategy -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages expansion in assigned accounts independently, pursuing routine upsell opportunities.
  — *Why this level:* Managing expansion in assigned accounts independently and pursuing routine upsell opportunities is applying Challenger-style value-framing to accounts unsupervised on straightforward expansion asks -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dixon & Adamson, The Challenger Sale: Taking Control of the Customer Conversation (Portfolio/Penguin, 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns strategic account plans, navigating ambiguous stakeholder maps and expansion paths autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning strategic account plans -- navigating ambiguous stakeholder maps and expansion paths autonomously -- is Cespedes's account-prioritization discipline applied with judgment to a portfolio's hardest, non-routine cases -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Cespedes, Aligning Strategy and Sales: The Choices, Systems, and Behaviors That Drive Effective Selling (Harvard Business Review Press, 2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the account-planning methodology and expansion approach other sellers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the account-planning methodology and expansion approach other sellers adopt is codifying Aligning Strategy and Sales's account-prioritization framework into the org's own adopted playbook. *Sources:* Cespedes, Aligning Strategy and Sales: The Choices, Systems, and Behaviors That Drive Effective Selling (Harvard Business Review Press, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets account strategy and growth standards, anticipating shifts in customer value.
  — *Why this level:* Setting account strategy and growth standards while anticipating shifts in customer value is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to account strategy across the org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes account-management practice the profession references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Aligning Strategy and Sales, cited as 'a must read' by Gartner and 'perhaps the best sales book ever' by Forbes, is a field reference connecting account strategy to sales execution; shaping practice the profession references at that scope is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Cespedes, Aligning Strategy and Sales: The Choices, Systems, and Behaviors That Drive Effective Selling (Harvard Business Review Press, 2014).

#### Sales Effectiveness

<a id="sal-08"></a>
##### SAL-08 — Sales forecasting & quota management

*Type:* Technical — Forecast revenue and manage quota attainment with predictable, data-grounded rigor.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates forecast inputs and quota tracking under direction, with figures reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Updating forecast inputs and quota tracking under direction, with figures reviewed, is explicit data entry without independent judgment calls -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Produces a personal forecast independently, managing routine quota attainment questions.
  — *Why this level:* Producing a personal forecast independently and managing routine quota-attainment questions is applying the Sales Learning Curve's execution-phase discipline (once the org already knows how to sell the product) to one's own number -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Leslie & Holloway, The Sales Learning Curve, Harvard Business Review 84(7-8), 114-123 (2006).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns forecasting for a team, reconciling ambiguous signals into reliable calls autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning forecasting for a team and reconciling ambiguous signals into reliable calls autonomously is the practice CSO Insights ties to 'world-class' forecast accuracy (57% vs. 47% average forecast win rate) -- judgment under ambiguity, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 2018-2019 Sales Performance Study: Selling in the Age of Ceaseless Change (2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the forecasting methodology and quota-setting approach other leaders adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the forecasting methodology and quota-setting approach other leaders adopt is turning personal forecast discipline into the org's standard practice, the kind CSO Insights' benchmarking identifies as the differentiator between world-class and average sales organizations. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 2018-2019 Sales Performance Study: Selling in the Age of Ceaseless Change (2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets forecasting strategy and quota standards, anticipating market and capacity shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting forecasting strategy and quota standards while anticipating market and capacity shifts is applying the Sales Learning Curve's phase model (initiation/transition/execution) at the portfolio level -- deciding when a whole org is ready for aggressive quota, not just one rep's ramp. *Sources:* Leslie & Holloway, The Sales Learning Curve, Harvard Business Review 84(7-8), 114-123 (2006).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines forecasting practice the field follows, externally credible on predictability and quota design.
  — *Why this level:* Defining forecasting practice the field follows, externally credible on predictability and quota design, is SFIA's Selling skill ceiling of organizational influence extended to external, cross-company recognition -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="sal-09"></a>
##### SAL-09 — Sales enablement & coaching

*Type:* Behavioral — Equip and coach sellers with the skills, content, and tools to perform consistently.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Delivers enablement content and onboarding tasks under direction, with coaching reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering enablement content and onboarding tasks under direction, with coaching reviewed, is running someone else's curriculum, not yet diagnosing skill gaps -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard training and coaching independently, developing routine rep skills.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard training and coaching independently, developing routine rep skills, is executing an established enablement program's content and coaching cadence unsupervised -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band CSO Insights' enablement study treats as baseline program delivery. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 5th Annual Sales Enablement Study (2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns enablement for a team, diagnosing ambiguous performance gaps and coaching autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning enablement for a team -- diagnosing ambiguous performance gaps and coaching autonomously -- is the diagnostic, not just deliverable, practice CSO Insights' 5th Annual Sales Enablement Study links to measurably higher win rates, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 5th Annual Sales Enablement Study (2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the enablement curriculum and coaching model other trainers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the enablement curriculum and coaching model other trainers adopt is building the kind of formalized, cross-team enablement function CSO Insights' study identifies as distinguishing mature programs from ad hoc coaching. *Sources:* CSO Insights (Miller Heiman Group), 5th Annual Sales Enablement Study (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enablement strategy and competency standards, anticipating skill needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enablement strategy and competency standards while anticipating skill needs is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to how a whole sales org builds capability. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes sales-enablement practice the profession references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* CEB's Challenger research on what separates top from average performers reshaped enablement and coaching practice industry-wide (coaching toward commercial teaching, not generic skills); shaping practice the profession references is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Dixon & Adamson, The Challenger Sale: Taking Control of the Customer Conversation (Portfolio/Penguin, 2011).

<a id="sal-10"></a>
##### SAL-10 — Channel & partner sales

*Type:* Behavioral — Drive revenue through indirect channels by enabling and managing selling partners.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports partner deals and registrations under direction, with terms reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting partner deals and registrations under direction, with terms reviewed, is explicit, checked administrative work -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine partner-sourced deals independently, handling standard channel conflict.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine partner-sourced deals independently and handling standard channel conflict is executing The Channel Advantage's multi-channel deal-routing rules on ordinary cases unsupervised -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns channel revenue for a region, resolving ambiguous partner and conflict situations autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning channel revenue for a region and resolving ambiguous partner and conflict situations autonomously is applying the book's channel-mix and conflict-resolution framework with judgment to the non-routine cases it was written to address -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the channel-selling model and partner-engagement approach other reps adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the channel-selling model and partner-engagement approach other reps adopt is codifying Friedman & Furey's channel-design method into the org's own adopted model, moving from applying the framework to authoring it internally. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets channel-sales strategy and standards, anticipating ecosystem and conflict dynamics.
  — *Why this level:* Setting channel-sales strategy and standards while anticipating ecosystem and conflict dynamics is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to indirect-channel strategy across the org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines channel-sales practice the field follows, externally credible on indirect revenue.
  — *Why this level:* The Channel Advantage's channel-mix strategy, endorsed by CEOs of AOL, Lotus, Ocean Spray and Xerox and taught industry-wide, is a field reference for indirect go-to-market; defining practice the field follows at that reach is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).

<a id="sal-11"></a>
##### SAL-11 — Sales operations & process

*Type:* Behavioral — Design and run sales processes, territories, and systems that improve productivity.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes sales-ops tasks and data updates under direction, with changes reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Executing sales-ops tasks and data updates under direction, with changes reviewed, is explicit, checked operational work -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Maintains standard sales processes and tooling independently, handling routine requests.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining standard sales processes and tooling independently, handling routine requests, is running Aligning Strategy and Sales's process/systems layer as designed, without yet redesigning it -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Cespedes, Aligning Strategy and Sales: The Choices, Systems, and Behaviors That Drive Effective Selling (Harvard Business Review Press, 2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns sales process for a team, resolving ambiguous workflow and data challenges autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning sales process for a team and resolving ambiguous workflow and data challenges autonomously is applying sales-force design method (sizing, structuring, aligning) with judgment to a team's specific, non-routine operational problems -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Zoltners, Sinha & Lorimer, Sales Force Design for Strategic Advantage (Palgrave Macmillan, 2004).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the sales-operations architecture and process standards other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the sales-operations architecture and process standards other practitioners adopt is Cespedes's own thesis -- linking strategy to systems, incentives and measurement -- turned from personal practice into the org's adopted operating model. *Sources:* Cespedes, Aligning Strategy and Sales: The Choices, Systems, and Behaviors That Drive Effective Selling (Harvard Business Review Press, 2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets sales-operations strategy and governance, anticipating scaling and tooling needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting sales-operations strategy and governance while anticipating scaling and tooling needs is SFIA's Selling skill 'initiate, influence' level, applied to operational governance across the org. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes sales-operations practice the profession references, externally recognized expert.
  — *Why this level:* Aligning Strategy and Sales, cited as 'a must read' by Gartner and 'the best sales book of the year' by Strategy & Business, is a field reference for how sales operations should connect to strategy; shaping practice the profession references at that scope is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Cespedes, Aligning Strategy and Sales: The Choices, Systems, and Behaviors That Drive Effective Selling (Harvard Business Review Press, 2014).

### Partnerships & Business Development (BD)

#### Partnership Strategy

<a id="bd-01"></a>
##### BD-01 — Partnership strategy & sourcing

*Type:* Behavioral — Identify, evaluate, and source partnerships that advance strategic and revenue goals.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Researches and shortlists potential partners under direction, with the rationale reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Researching and shortlisting potential partners under direction, with the rationale reviewed, is explicit, checked research work -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Sources and screens routine partnership opportunities independently against agreed criteria.
  — *Why this level:* Sourcing and screening routine partnership opportunities independently against agreed criteria is applying Gulati's network-position and resource-complementarity criteria as a fixed checklist, unsupervised, on ordinary cases -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Gulati, Alliances and Networks, Strategic Management Journal 19(4), 293-317 (1998).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns partnership strategy for a domain, prioritizing ambiguous opportunities and fit autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning partnership strategy for a domain and prioritizing ambiguous opportunities and fit autonomously is applying Getting Partnering Right's partner-fit and readiness criteria with judgment to the ambiguous cases the book was written to resolve -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Rackham, Friedman & Ruff, Getting Partnering Right: How Market Leaders Are Creating Long-Term Competitive Advantage (McGraw-Hill, 1996).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the partnership-sourcing methodology and prioritization model others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the partnership-sourcing methodology and prioritization model others adopt is codifying Alliance Advantage's partner-selection and value-creation logic into the org's own adopted sourcing method. *Sources:* Doz & Hamel, Alliance Advantage: The Art of Creating Value through Partnering (Harvard Business School Press, 1998).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the partnership strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in the partner landscape.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the partnership strategy and standards while anticipating shifts in the partner landscape is choosing and defending a keystone/dominator/niche ecosystem position at the strategy-setting level Iansiti & Levien describe. *Sources:* Iansiti & Levien, The Keystone Advantage: What the New Dynamics of Business Ecosystems Mean for Strategy, Innovation, and Sustainability (Harvard Business School Press, 2004).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines partnership-strategy practice the field follows, externally credible on ecosystem strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Defining partnership-strategy practice the field follows, externally credible on ecosystem strategy, is the Dreyfus master band the alliance profession recognizes formally through ASAP's Certified Strategic Alliance Professional credential. *Sources:* Association of Strategic Alliance Professionals, Certified Strategic Alliance Professional (CSAP) Certification (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="bd-02"></a>
##### BD-02 — Ecosystem & channel development

*Type:* Behavioral — Build and grow partner ecosystems and channels that extend reach and capability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports ecosystem and channel tasks under direction, with recruitment steps reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting ecosystem and channel tasks under direction, with recruitment steps reviewed, is explicit, checked execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Develops routine channel relationships independently, onboarding standard partners.
  — *Why this level:* Developing routine channel relationships independently and onboarding standard partners is executing The Channel Advantage's channel-recruitment and onboarding steps unsupervised on ordinary cases -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns ecosystem development for a segment, resolving ambiguous structure and incentive trade-offs autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning ecosystem development for a segment and resolving ambiguous structure and incentive trade-offs autonomously is applying the keystone/dominator/niche framework with judgment to design a segment's actual ecosystem structure -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Iansiti & Levien, The Keystone Advantage: What the New Dynamics of Business Ecosystems Mean for Strategy, Innovation, and Sustainability (Harvard Business School Press, 2004).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the ecosystem-development model and channel-design approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the ecosystem-development model and channel-design approach others adopt is codifying Platform Revolution's two-sided-market design principles into the org's own adopted ecosystem model. *Sources:* Parker, Van Alstyne & Choudary, Platform Revolution: How Networked Markets Are Transforming the Economy and How to Make Them Work for You (W.W. Norton, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets ecosystem strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in channel economics and structure.
  — *Why this level:* Setting ecosystem strategy and standards while anticipating shifts in channel economics and structure is evolving the org's keystone strategy at the level Iansiti & Levien reserve for ecosystem leaders anticipating structural change, not just designing one segment. *Sources:* Iansiti & Levien, The Keystone Advantage: What the New Dynamics of Business Ecosystems Mean for Strategy, Innovation, and Sustainability (Harvard Business School Press, 2004).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes ecosystem-development practice the field references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Platform Revolution's two-sided-market framework, from three of the most-cited platform-strategy researchers, is a field reference model for ecosystem design; shaping practice the field references at that reach is the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Parker, Van Alstyne & Choudary, Platform Revolution: How Networked Markets Are Transforming the Economy and How to Make Them Work for You (W.W. Norton, 2016).

#### Deal Making & Alliances

<a id="bd-03"></a>
##### BD-03 — Deal structuring & negotiation

*Type:* Behavioral — Structure and negotiate partnership and commercial deals balancing risk and value.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares deal terms from templates under direction, with structure reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing deal terms from templates under direction, with structure reviewed, is explicit template-following before internalizing principled-negotiation judgment -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Structures and negotiates routine partnership deals independently within agreed guardrails.
  — *Why this level:* Structuring and negotiating routine partnership deals independently within agreed guardrails is applying Getting to Yes's principled-negotiation method unsupervised to bounded deals -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns complex deal structuring, navigating ambiguous terms and multi-party negotiations autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning complex deal structuring -- navigating ambiguous terms and multi-party negotiations autonomously -- is working the 'deal design' dimension of 3-D Negotiation (not just at-the-table tactics) with judgment on genuinely hard structures, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Lax & Sebenius, 3-D Negotiation: Powerful Tools to Change the Game in Your Most Important Deals (Harvard Business School Press, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the deal-structuring frameworks and negotiation approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the deal-structuring frameworks and negotiation approach others adopt is codifying the 3-D Negotiation setup-design-tactics method into the org's own adopted playbook for partnership deals. *Sources:* Lax & Sebenius, 3-D Negotiation: Powerful Tools to Change the Game in Your Most Important Deals (Harvard Business School Press, 2006).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets deal-structuring strategy and standards, anticipating risk and value-sharing dynamics.
  — *Why this level:* Setting deal-structuring strategy and standards while anticipating risk and value-sharing dynamics is applying Haspeslagh & Jemison's integration-design lens for step-change growth deals at the strategy-setting level, beyond any single negotiation. *Sources:* Haspeslagh & Jemison, Managing Acquisitions: Creating Value Through Corporate Renewal (Free Press, 1991).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines deal-making practice the field follows, externally credible on complex partnership structures.
  — *Why this level:* Defining deal-making practice the field follows, externally credible on complex partnership structures, is the alliance profession's own master-band recognition via ASAP's CSAP credential, which tests judgment across the full deal lifecycle. *Sources:* Association of Strategic Alliance Professionals, Certified Strategic Alliance Professional (CSAP) Certification (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="bd-04"></a>
##### BD-04 — Alliance & relationship management

*Type:* Behavioral — Manage ongoing alliances to sustain trust, joint value, and mutual accountability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains alliance records and check-ins under direction, with follow-ups reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining alliance records and check-ins under direction, with follow-ups reviewed, is explicit, checked relationship administration -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine alliance relationships independently, handling standard partner needs.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine alliance relationships independently and handling standard partner needs is executing the baseline alliance-function practices (tracking, coordination) Kale, Dyer & Singh found even non-specialized firms perform -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Kale, Dyer & Singh, Alliance Capability, Stock Market Response, and Long-Term Alliance Success: The Role of the Alliance Function, Strategic Management Journal 23(8), 747-767 (2002).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns strategic alliances, navigating ambiguous stakeholder dynamics and conflicts autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning strategic alliances -- navigating ambiguous stakeholder dynamics and conflicts autonomously -- is Alliance Advantage's central thesis in practice: it is ongoing management, not initial design, that determines success, applied with judgment to hard cases, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Doz & Hamel, Alliance Advantage: The Art of Creating Value through Partnering (Harvard Business School Press, 1998).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the alliance-management model and governance approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the alliance-management model and governance approach others adopt is synthesizing the alliance-lifecycle practices Kale & Singh's review identifies (partner selection, governance, evolution) into the org's own adopted internal model. *Sources:* Kale & Singh, Managing Strategic Alliances: What Do We Know Now, and Where Do We Go From Here?, Academy of Management Perspectives 23(3), 45-62 (2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets alliance strategy and relationship standards, anticipating shifts in partner priorities.
  — *Why this level:* Setting alliance strategy and relationship standards while anticipating shifts in partner priorities is running the dedicated alliance function at the organizational level Kale, Dyer & Singh's study ties to measurably higher stock-market and long-term success rates. *Sources:* Kale, Dyer & Singh, Alliance Capability, Stock Market Response, and Long-Term Alliance Success: The Role of the Alliance Function, Strategic Management Journal 23(8), 747-767 (2002).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes alliance-management practice the field references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping alliance-management practice the field references, externally recognized authority, is the Dreyfus master band the alliance profession recognizes through ASAP's Certified Strategic Alliance Professional credential covering the full lifecycle. *Sources:* Association of Strategic Alliance Professionals, Certified Strategic Alliance Professional (CSAP) Certification (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="bd-05"></a>
##### BD-05 — Joint go-to-market & co-selling

*Type:* Behavioral — Orchestrate joint offerings, co-selling, and shared pipeline with partners.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports joint GTM activities and co-sell tasks under direction, with plans reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting joint GTM activities and co-sell tasks under direction, with plans reviewed, is explicit, checked execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Executes routine joint campaigns and co-sell motions independently with partners.
  — *Why this level:* Executing routine joint campaigns and co-sell motions independently with partners is running The Channel Advantage's multi-channel go-to-market coordination on ordinary cases unsupervised -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns joint GTM for a partnership, resolving ambiguous alignment and attribution issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning joint GTM for a partnership -- resolving ambiguous alignment and attribution issues autonomously -- is Alliance Advantage's management-over-time thesis applied to the specific friction of joint execution (whose deal, whose credit), the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Doz & Hamel, Alliance Advantage: The Art of Creating Value through Partnering (Harvard Business School Press, 1998).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the joint-GTM and co-selling playbook other teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the joint-GTM and co-selling playbook other teams adopt is codifying Channel Advantage's channel-mix coordination method into the org's own adopted co-sell playbook. *Sources:* Friedman & Furey, The Channel Advantage: Going to Market with Multiple Sales Channels to Reach More Customers, Sell More Products, Make More Profit (Butterworth-Heinemann, 1999).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets co-sell strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in partner go-to-market dynamics.
  — *Why this level:* Setting co-sell strategy and standards while anticipating shifts in partner go-to-market dynamics is applying Platform Revolution's two-sided-market logic to how joint value is created and captured across an evolving partner ecosystem. *Sources:* Parker, Van Alstyne & Choudary, Platform Revolution: How Networked Markets Are Transforming the Economy and How to Make Them Work for You (W.W. Norton, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines joint-GTM practice the field follows, externally credible on co-selling at scale.
  — *Why this level:* Defining joint-GTM practice the field follows, externally credible on co-selling at scale, is orchestrating an ecosystem's keystone role the way Iansiti & Levien describe firms like Microsoft and Li & Fung doing -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Iansiti & Levien, The Keystone Advantage: What the New Dynamics of Business Ecosystems Mean for Strategy, Innovation, and Sustainability (Harvard Business School Press, 2004).

#### Partner Performance

<a id="bd-06"></a>
##### BD-06 — Partner performance & program management

*Type:* Technical — Track partner performance and run programs, tiers, and incentives that drive results.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks partner metrics and program tasks under direction, with reporting reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking partner metrics and program tasks under direction, with reporting reviewed, is explicit, checked measurement work -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages a standard partner program independently, handling routine performance and tiering.
  — *Why this level:* Managing a standard partner program independently and handling routine performance and tiering is executing baseline alliance-function tracking practices unsupervised on ordinary partners -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Kale, Dyer & Singh, Alliance Capability, Stock Market Response, and Long-Term Alliance Success: The Role of the Alliance Function, Strategic Management Journal 23(8), 747-767 (2002).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns program performance for a portfolio, diagnosing ambiguous underperformance and incentives autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Owning program performance for a portfolio and diagnosing ambiguous underperformance and incentives autonomously is applying Dyer, Kale & Singh's alliance-success diagnostics (drawn from 1,572 alliances) with judgment across a portfolio's hardest cases, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Dyer, Kale & Singh, How to Make Strategic Alliances Work, MIT Sloan Management Review 42(4), 37-43 (2001).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the partner-program design and performance frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the partner-program design and performance frameworks others adopt is synthesizing the alliance-management-lifecycle literature Kale & Singh review into the org's own adopted program-design framework. *Sources:* Kale & Singh, Managing Strategic Alliances: What Do We Know Now, and Where Do We Go From Here?, Academy of Management Perspectives 23(3), 45-62 (2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets partner-program strategy and standards, anticipating shifts in program economics.
  — *Why this level:* Setting partner-program strategy and standards while anticipating shifts in program economics is running the dedicated-alliance-function model at the strategy level Dyer, Kale & Singh's 200-corporation study found distinguishes durably successful partner programs. *Sources:* Dyer, Kale & Singh, How to Make Strategic Alliances Work, MIT Sloan Management Review 42(4), 37-43 (2001).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes partner-program practice the field references, externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping partner-program practice the field references, externally recognized authority, is the Dreyfus master band ASAP's Certified Strategic Alliance Professional credential formally recognizes across the alliance profession. *Sources:* Association of Strategic Alliance Professionals, Certified Strategic Alliance Professional (CSAP) Certification (accessed 2026-07).

### Customer Success & Account Management (CSM)

#### Onboarding & Adoption

<a id="csm-01"></a>
##### CSM-01 — Customer onboarding & adoption

*Type:* Technical — Guide new customers through implementation and drive early adoption to reach first value.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Completes assigned onboarding steps from a checklist for new customers, with each session reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Following a checklist to complete assigned onboarding steps under review is executing someone else's 30/60/90 transition plan rather than building one — Watkins' First 90 Days framework applied at the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Watkins, The First 90 Days (Harvard Business Review Press, 2003); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard onboarding plans independently, configuring setup and guiding customers to first value.
  — *Why this level:* Independently configuring setup and running a standard onboarding plan to first value is competently executing a known transition arc for routine cases — Dreyfus advanced beginner, correct on the standard sequence without adapting it. *Sources:* Watkins, The First 90 Days (Harvard Business Review Press, 2003); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Tailors onboarding to complex or ambiguous customer needs and is the team's go-to for tough launches.
  — *Why this level:* Tailoring onboarding to ambiguous or complex customer needs is doing the judgment work Mehta et al.'s 'time to first value' stage assumes a competent CSM supplies — the Dreyfus competent band, setting the local plan rather than following one. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the onboarding methodology others follow and rescues stalled or failing implementations.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the onboarding methodology other CSMs adopt, and rescuing failing implementations, is publishing the first-value playbook Mehta et al. describe as a defined organizational process — SFIA's ensure/advise reach beyond one's own accounts. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets onboarding strategy across segments and anticipates shifts in how customers reach value.
  — *Why this level:* Setting onboarding strategy across segments and anticipating how customers reach value next is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority over the onboarding model across the whole book of business, not one launch. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent onboarding means industry-wide and is sought externally for that expertise.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent onboarding means industry-wide, in the way the Customer Success canon itself became a shared vocabulary across the profession, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level extended to shaping the discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016).

<a id="csm-02"></a>
##### CSM-02 — Adoption monitoring & enablement

*Type:* Technical — Track usage signals and deliver targeted enablement to deepen adoption over time.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks basic usage metrics and flags low-adoption accounts for a reviewer to act on.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking basic usage metrics and flagging low-adoption accounts for someone else to act on is executing the measurement half of Mehta et al.'s adoption pillar without yet owning the intervention — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently monitors adoption signals and delivers standard enablement to lift feature usage.
  — *Why this level:* Independently monitoring adoption signals and running standard enablement plays to lift usage is routine, correct application of the CS adoption pillar to familiar account shapes — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses ambiguous adoption gaps and designs targeted enablement that reliably moves usage.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing ambiguous adoption gaps and designing enablement that reliably moves usage is the capability-building work TSIA's maturity model places at its 'Norming' phase, where ad hoc plays become a repeatable practice — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds the adoption-measurement and enablement frameworks the team adopts as standard.
  — *Why this level:* Building the adoption-measurement and enablement framework the whole team adopts as standard is carrying a CS org from TSIA's Norming into Performing phase — SFIA's ensure/advise reach across other CSMs' accounts. *Sources:* TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the adoption strategy and predicts which usage patterns precede expansion or churn.
  — *Why this level:* Setting adoption strategy and predicting which usage patterns precede expansion or churn is SFIA's initiate/influence band — anticipatory authority over the model, not just running it well. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline defines healthy adoption and is externally credible on enablement practice.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the discipline itself defines healthy adoption, at the level TSIA's own maturity research operates, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band extended to industry-wide practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).

#### Account Health & Retention

<a id="csm-03"></a>
##### CSM-03 — Account health & churn management

*Type:* Technical — Score account health from leading indicators and intervene proactively to prevent churn.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates health scores from defined inputs and escalates declining accounts to a reviewer.
  — *Why this level:* Updating a health score from defined inputs and escalating decline is applying Mehta et al.'s health-scoring concept as a fixed formula, not yet interpreting it — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently assesses account health and runs standard interventions on at-risk accounts.
  — *Why this level:* Independently assessing health and running standard save interventions on at-risk accounts is correct, routine execution of the health-score-to-playbook mapping — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Interprets conflicting health signals, diagnoses root causes, and is the go-to on hard cases.
  — *Why this level:* Interpreting conflicting signals and diagnosing root causes on hard cases is exactly the judgment Ascarza et al.'s retention-management review flags as the hard problem — distinguishing which at-risk customers are worth targeting, not just scoring risk — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Ascarza et al., In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions, Customer Needs and Solutions 5(1-2) (2018); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the health-scoring model and intervention playbooks others rely on.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the health-scoring model and intervention playbooks others rely on is operationalizing Ascarza et al.'s call for retention programs that target the right customers systematically — SFIA's ensure/advise reach across the team's book. *Sources:* Ascarza et al., In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions, Customer Needs and Solutions 5(1-2) (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets churn-management strategy and anticipates emerging drivers of attrition across the book.
  — *Why this level:* Setting churn strategy and anticipating emerging attrition drivers before they surface is SFIA's initiate/influence band — authority over where the model needs to evolve next. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice account health for the field and influences how others measure churn.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice account health for the field and influencing how peers measure churn is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band, extending the health-scoring discourse Mehta et al. and the retention-research literature both draw on. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016).

<a id="csm-04"></a>
##### CSM-04 — Renewal & expansion management

*Type:* Behavioral — Forecast, negotiate, and close renewals while growing upsell and cross-sell.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares renewal paperwork and flags upcoming dates, with quotes and terms reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing renewal paperwork and flagging dates for review is administering the mechanics of Mehta et al.'s renewal stage without yet owning the negotiation — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs straightforward renewals and surfaces routine expansion opportunities.
  — *Why this level:* Independently closing straightforward renewals and surfacing routine expansion is competent, standard execution of the renewal-to-expansion lifecycle stage — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Negotiates complex multi-stakeholder renewals and structures expansion deals autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Negotiating complex multi-stakeholder renewals and structuring expansion deals autonomously is doing the work SAMA's CSAM curriculum calls value co-discovery and account planning — the Dreyfus competent band, where the practitioner designs the deal, not just processes it. *Sources:* Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the renewal and expansion playbook and closes the deals others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the renewal/expansion playbook and closing deals others can't is applying SAMA's 'leading and influencing the strategic account' core at the level of teaching it to peers — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets renewal and expansion strategy and forecasts where account growth is heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting renewal and expansion strategy and forecasting where growth is heading is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching TSIA's monetization-pillar view of CS as a revenue-forecasting function, not just a retention one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what world-class renewal and expansion looks like and is sought for that authority.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what world-class renewal and expansion looks like, at the authority SAMA's own certification body claims for the discipline, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level extended industry-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="csm-05"></a>
##### CSM-05 — Risk identification & save planning

*Type:* Behavioral — Detect at-risk accounts and orchestrate cross-functional recovery and retention plays.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Identifies obvious risk signals and logs them for a reviewer to assess and act.
  — *Why this level:* Logging obvious risk signals for someone else to assess is flagging inputs into Mehta et al.'s save-play process without running it — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently spots common risks and executes standard save plans on routine cases.
  — *Why this level:* Independently spotting common risk and executing standard save plans on routine cases is correct application of a known save playbook — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Detects subtle, ambiguous risk early and builds save plans that recover hard accounts.
  — *Why this level:* Detecting subtle, ambiguous risk early and building recovery plans for hard accounts is the proactive, individually-judged retention Ascarza et al. contrast with reactive, rule-triggered saves — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Ascarza et al., In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions, Customer Needs and Solutions 5(1-2) (2018); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the risk-detection signals and save methodology the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the risk-detection signals and save methodology the team adopts is building the kind of continuous, systemic retention process Ascarza et al. argue should replace one-off discrete campaigns — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Ascarza et al., In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions, Customer Needs and Solutions 5(1-2) (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets save strategy and anticipates systemic risks before they surface across the portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Setting save strategy and anticipating systemic risk before it surfaces across the portfolio is SFIA's initiate/influence band — anticipatory authority Ascarza et al. identify as the frontier of retention management. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ascarza et al., In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions, Customer Needs and Solutions 5(1-2) (2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines the discipline's standard for risk and retention and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the discipline's standard for risk and retention, externally recognized, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band applied to the retention-research agenda itself. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ascarza et al., In Pursuit of Enhanced Customer Retention Management: Review, Key Issues, and Future Directions, Customer Needs and Solutions 5(1-2) (2018).

#### Value & Success Planning

<a id="csm-06"></a>
##### CSM-06 — Success planning & business reviews

*Type:* Behavioral — Build joint success plans and run reviews that align on goals, progress, and next steps.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assembles business-review materials from templates, with content reviewed before delivery.
  — *Why this level:* Assembling review materials from a template with content checked before delivery is populating Mehta et al.'s success-plan format without yet owning its strategy — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds success plans and runs standard business reviews with customers.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building success plans and running standard reviews is competent, routine delivery of the CS success-planning cadence — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Crafts executive-level success plans for complex accounts and leads ambiguous, high-stakes reviews.
  — *Why this level:* Crafting executive-level plans for complex accounts and leading ambiguous, high-stakes reviews is exercising CXPA's 'CX strategy' competency — formulating a cohesive plan aligned to business goals — rather than following a template, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Customer Experience Professionals Association, CXPA CX Framework and Certified Customer Experience Professional (CCXP) Competency Framework (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the success-planning and review framework others follow and coaches them on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the success-planning framework others follow and coaching them on it is teaching CXPA's strategy and culture-and-accountability competencies to peers — SFIA's ensure/advise reach across the team. *Sources:* Customer Experience Professionals Association, CXPA CX Framework and Certified Customer Experience Professional (CCXP) Competency Framework (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the strategy linking success plans to outcomes and anticipates shifts in customer priorities.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the strategy linking plans to outcomes and anticipating shifts in customer priorities is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching CXPA's metrics-and-ROI competency applied at organizational scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Customer Experience Professionals Association, CXPA CX Framework and Certified Customer Experience Professional (CCXP) Competency Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what great success planning means for the profession and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what great success planning means for the profession, externally credible, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level applied to shaping the CX-strategy competency CXPA itself certifies practitioners against. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Customer Experience Professionals Association, CXPA CX Framework and Certified Customer Experience Professional (CCXP) Competency Framework (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="csm-07"></a>
##### CSM-07 — Customer outcome & value realization

*Type:* Behavioral — Define target outcomes and quantify realized value to justify continued investment.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Collects outcome data and populates value summaries for a reviewer to validate.
  — *Why this level:* Collecting outcome data and populating value summaries for validation is feeding Mehta et al.'s value-realization stage without yet building its argument — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently maps customer goals to metrics and reports realized value on standard accounts.
  — *Why this level:* Independently mapping goals to metrics and reporting realized value on standard accounts is routine, correct execution of the outcome-mapping process — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Mehta, Steinman & Murphy, Customer Success: How Innovative Companies Are Reducing Churn and Growing Recurring Revenue (Wiley, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Quantifies value in ambiguous cases and is the go-to for proving complex business outcomes.
  — *Why this level:* Quantifying value in ambiguous cases and proving complex business outcomes is the capability TSIA's maturity model places past 'Norming' — value realization as a defensible, case-by-case argument rather than a template metric — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Builds the value-realization methodology and ROI models the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Building the value-realization methodology and ROI models the team adopts is operationalizing TSIA's value/monetization pillar as a repeatable organizational capability — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets value-measurement strategy and anticipates how customers will define success next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting value-measurement strategy and anticipating how customers will define success next is SFIA's initiate/influence band, the anticipatory posture TSIA's 'Performing' phase describes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines how the industry measures customer value and shapes outcome-realization practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how the industry measures customer value and shaping outcome-realization practice is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band extended to the research TSIA itself publishes for the field. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); TSIA (Technology & Services Industry Association), The Customer Success Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="csm-08"></a>
##### CSM-08 — Strategic account growth planning

*Type:* Behavioral — Map account whitespace and stakeholders to chart multi-year growth and expansion.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers account background and drafts growth notes for a reviewer to refine.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering account background and drafting notes for a reviewer to refine is assembling inputs to SAMA's SAM Playbook (CORE 0) without yet running the planning process — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds growth plans for individual accounts using standard approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building growth plans for individual accounts with a standard approach is competent application of SAMA's Value Co-Discovery and Strategic Account Planning core (CORE 1) to familiar accounts — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Develops multi-year growth strategies for complex accounts and navigates ambiguous stakeholder maps.
  — *Why this level:* Developing multi-year growth strategies for complex accounts and navigating ambiguous stakeholder maps is doing SAMA's Co-Creation and Quantification of Value work (CORE 2) unassisted on hard cases — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the strategic account-planning method others adopt and unlocks stalled growth.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the strategic-account-planning method others adopt and unlocking stalled growth is teaching SAMA's Leading and Influencing the Strategic Account core (CORE 3) to peers — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets portfolio-level growth strategy and anticipates where strategic accounts are heading.
  — *Why this level:* Setting portfolio-level growth strategy and anticipating where strategic accounts are heading is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching SAMA's Managing the Customer Relationship and Value Journey core (CORE 4) applied across a portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice strategic account growth for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice strategic account growth for the field, sought externally, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire level — the authority SAMA's own certification body claims to confer on the discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Strategic Account Management Association, Certified Strategic Account Manager (CSAM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).

#### Advocacy & Voice of Customer

<a id="csm-09"></a>
##### CSM-09 — Customer advocacy & voice-of-customer

*Type:* Behavioral — Cultivate references and advocates while channeling structured feedback into the business.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Captures customer feedback and references for a reviewer to route or act on.
  — *Why this level:* Capturing feedback and references for someone else to route is gathering raw input into Reichheld & Markey's closed-loop feedback process without yet closing the loop — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Reichheld & Markey, The Ultimate Question 2.0: How Net Promoter Companies Thrive in a Customer-Driven World (Harvard Business Review Press, 2011); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs standard advocacy programs and channels routine feedback to teams.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running standard advocacy programs and channeling routine feedback is competent execution of the Net Promoter System's feedback-routing mechanics — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Reichheld & Markey, The Ultimate Question 2.0: How Net Promoter Companies Thrive in a Customer-Driven World (Harvard Business Review Press, 2011); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Synthesizes ambiguous feedback into actionable insight and cultivates strong references autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Synthesizing ambiguous feedback into actionable insight and cultivating strong references autonomously is exercising CXPA's Customer Insights and Understanding competency, not just relaying data — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Customer Experience Professionals Association, CXPA CX Framework and Certified Customer Experience Professional (CCXP) Competency Framework (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the voice-of-customer program and advocacy framework the organization adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the voice-of-customer program and advocacy framework the organization adopts is building the closed-loop system Reichheld & Markey describe as full-fledged management infrastructure, not a survey — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Customer Experience Professionals Association, CXPA CX Framework and Certified Customer Experience Professional (CCXP) Competency Framework (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets advocacy strategy and anticipates which customer signals should shape direction.
  — *Why this level:* Setting advocacy strategy and anticipating which signals should shape direction is SFIA's initiate/influence band, the anticipatory use of NPS data Reichheld & Markey attribute to loyalty-leading companies. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Reichheld & Markey, The Ultimate Question 2.0: How Net Promoter Companies Thrive in a Customer-Driven World (Harvard Business Review Press, 2011).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines how the discipline practices voice-of-customer and is externally credible on advocacy.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how the discipline practices voice-of-customer, externally credible, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band — the reach the Net Promoter System itself achieved in reshaping how a generation of companies define advocacy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Reichheld & Markey, The Ultimate Question 2.0: How Net Promoter Companies Thrive in a Customer-Driven World (Harvard Business Review Press, 2011).

### Customer Support & Service Operations (SUP)

#### Case & Queue Management

<a id="sup-01"></a>
##### SUP-01 — Case management & triage

*Type:* Technical — Capture, categorize, and route service cases by urgency and impact for efficient resolution.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Logs and categorizes incoming cases per defined rules, with prioritization reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Logging and categorizing cases per defined rules with prioritization reviewed is the entry-level scope HDI's Support Center Analyst (HDI-SCA) certification tests — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently triages and manages standard cases through resolution with normal oversight.
  — *Why this level:* Independently triaging and managing standard cases through resolution under normal oversight is competent execution of the full HDI-SCA analyst scope on routine volume — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles ambiguous, high-volume triage decisions and is the go-to for tricky case prioritization.
  — *Why this level:* Handling ambiguous, high-volume triage decisions and being the go-to on tricky prioritization moves past individual analyst work into the judgment HDI's Support Center Team Lead (HDI-SCTL) standard expects of a supervising practitioner — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the triage model and case-handling standards the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the triage model and case-handling standards the team adopts is operating at the HDI-SCTL coaching-and-standards-setting level, publishing the model rather than just applying it — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets case-management strategy and anticipates how demand patterns will shift triage needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting case-management strategy and anticipating demand-pattern shifts is the operational-leadership scope of HDI's Support Center Manager (HDI-SCM) certification — SFIA's initiate/influence band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice case triage for the discipline and influences how others structure it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice case triage for the discipline and influencing how others structure it is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band, extending HDI's own certification standard-setting role to the practitioner's individual reputation. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="sup-02"></a>
##### SUP-02 — Service-level & queue management

*Type:* Technical — Monitor and balance work queues against service-level targets to control resolution times.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Monitors queues against targets and flags breaches for a reviewer to address.
  — *Why this level:* Monitoring queues against targets and flagging breaches for a reviewer is executing ITIL 4's service level management practice at its most mechanical — tracking targets someone else set — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages queues to meet service levels under routine load variation.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing queues to meet service levels under routine load variation is competent, standard operation of the service-level-management practice — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Balances competing queues under pressure and is the go-to for keeping SLAs intact in hard conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing competing queues under pressure and keeping SLAs intact in hard conditions is the real-time workforce-management judgment Cleveland's ICMI reference treats as the core skill separating a supervisor from an agent — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the queue-management and SLA strategy others follow.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the queue-management and SLA strategy others follow is publishing the forecasting-and-staffing model Cleveland's book documents as organizational practice — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets service-level strategy and anticipates demand shifts before they threaten targets.
  — *Why this level:* Setting service-level strategy and anticipating demand shifts before they threaten targets is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching ISO 18295's requirement that a contact centre proactively, not just reactively, meet customer needs. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 18295-1:2017 Customer contact centres — Part 1: Requirements for customer contact centres (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent service-level management means for the field and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent service-level management means for the field, externally credible, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band — the authority ISO 18295 itself represents as the first international quality standard for the discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 18295-1:2017 Customer contact centres — Part 1: Requirements for customer contact centres (2017).

<a id="sup-03"></a>
##### SUP-03 — Issue diagnosis & resolution

*Type:* Technical — Investigate reported problems systematically and apply or develop fixes to restore service.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Resolves well-defined issues using known steps, escalating anything unfamiliar.
