  — *Why this level:* Resolving well-defined issues using known steps and escalating the unfamiliar is applying ITIL 4's incident-management practice exactly as scripted — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently diagnoses and resolves standard issues with normal review of tricky ones.
  — *Why this level:* Independently diagnosing and resolving standard issues with normal review of tricky ones is competent, routine execution of the incident-restoration practice — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Solves ambiguous, multi-factor problems and is the go-to for the hardest tickets.
  — *Why this level:* Solving ambiguous, multi-factor problems as the go-to for the hardest tickets is running Kepner-Tregoe's structured problem-analysis process — comparing where a fault occurs against where it doesn't to isolate cause — rather than following a runbook, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines diagnostic approaches others adopt and resolves issues no one else can.
  — *Why this level:* Defining diagnostic approaches others adopt and resolving what no one else can is publishing the Kepner-Tregoe-style problem-analysis discipline as team practice — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets resolution strategy and anticipates emerging failure modes before they spread.
  — *Why this level:* Setting resolution strategy and anticipating emerging failure modes before they spread is SFIA's initiate/influence band — diagnostic authority applied ahead of the incident, not just during it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines the discipline's standard for diagnosis and is sought externally for hard problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the discipline's standard for diagnosis and being sought externally for hard problems is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band applied to the same structured-diagnosis tradition Kepner-Tregoe's methodology represents industry-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07).

#### Escalation & Incident Handling

<a id="sup-04"></a>
##### SUP-04 — Escalation & incident communication

*Type:* Behavioral — Manage tiered escalations and keep customers informed through service-impacting incidents.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Follows the escalation script and posts status updates that are reviewed before sending.
  — *Why this level:* Following the escalation script and having status updates reviewed before sending is applying ITIL 4's incident-management communication steps without yet owning their judgment calls — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard escalations and communicates clearly through routine incidents.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing standard escalations and communicating clearly through routine incidents is competent, correct execution of the incident-communication practice — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns communication on ambiguous, high-pressure incidents and is the go-to under crisis.
  — *Why this level:* Owning communication on ambiguous, high-pressure incidents as the go-to under crisis is exercising the major-incident judgment ITIL 4 reserves for cases the standard practice doesn't script — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the escalation and incident-communication protocols the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the escalation and incident-communication protocols the team adopts is publishing the major-incident procedure ITIL 4 expects an organization to define for itself — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets incident-communication strategy and anticipates stakeholder needs in major events.
  — *Why this level:* Setting incident-communication strategy and anticipating stakeholder needs in major events is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching the CX-operations foresight the COPC CX Standard requires of certified organizations. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); COPC Inc., COPC Customer Experience (CX) Standard (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice incident communication for the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice incident communication for the discipline, externally recognized, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band applied at the certification-setting scope the COPC CX Standard itself occupies. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); COPC Inc., COPC Customer Experience (CX) Standard (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="sup-05"></a>
##### SUP-05 — Problem & root-cause management

*Type:* Technical — Analyze recurring issues to identify root causes and drive permanent corrective actions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers incident details and documents findings for a reviewer to analyze.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering incident details and documenting findings for a reviewer to analyze is feeding ITIL 4's problem-management practice without yet running its analysis — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs root-cause analysis on standard recurring problems with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running root-cause analysis on standard recurring problems with normal review is competent, routine application of the problem-management practice — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Untangles ambiguous, systemic root causes and is the go-to for elusive recurring issues.
  — *Why this level:* Untangling ambiguous, systemic root causes as the go-to for elusive recurring issues is running Kepner-Tregoe's full problem-analysis method on cases where the standard practice's checklist runs out — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the problem-management methodology others adopt and cracks the hardest root causes.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the problem-management methodology others adopt and cracking the hardest root causes is publishing a Kepner-Tregoe-grade structured-diagnosis discipline as the team's own practice — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets problem-management strategy and anticipates systemic failures before they recur.
  — *Why this level:* Setting problem-management strategy and anticipating systemic failures before they recur is SFIA's initiate/influence band — using root-cause method proactively rather than after each recurrence. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines how the discipline practices root-cause management and shapes industry approaches.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how the discipline practices root-cause management and shaping industry approaches is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band, extending the reach Kepner-Tregoe's methodology has achieved as a widely adopted cross-industry standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kepner & Tregoe, Root Cause Analysis / Problem Analysis Methodology (Kepner-Tregoe Inc., accessed 2026-07).

#### Self-Service & Knowledge

<a id="sup-06"></a>
##### SUP-06 — Knowledge base & self-service design

*Type:* Technical — Design and curate knowledge content and self-service experiences that deflect and resolve issues.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts knowledge articles from templates, with accuracy and clarity reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting knowledge articles from templates with accuracy checked is applying KCS's 'capture in the workflow' practice as a fixed template, not yet judging what's worth capturing — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Consortium for Service Innovation, Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) v6 Practices Guide (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently authors and maintains standard self-service content to defined quality.
  — *Why this level:* Independently authoring and maintaining standard self-service content to defined quality is competent, routine execution of KCS's content-standard practice — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Consortium for Service Innovation, Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) v6 Practices Guide (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs self-service content for ambiguous needs and is the go-to for tough knowledge gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Designing self-service content for ambiguous needs as the go-to for tough knowledge gaps is applying Price & Jaffe's 'create engaging self-service' principle to cases with no existing article — the Dreyfus competent band, authoring the answer, not just capturing one. *Sources:* Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the knowledge architecture and authoring standards the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the knowledge architecture and authoring standards the team adopts is publishing KCS's structure-and-workflow processes as organizational practice, the way the Consortium for Service Innovation's own methodology is meant to be adapted — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Consortium for Service Innovation, Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) v6 Practices Guide (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets self-service strategy and anticipates what customers will need to solve themselves.
  — *Why this level:* Setting self-service strategy and anticipating what customers will need to solve themselves is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching Price & Jaffe's 'be proactive' principle applied at a program level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice knowledge and self-service design for the field and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice knowledge and self-service design for the field, externally credible, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band — the reach the KCS methodology itself achieved as a cross-industry certification standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Consortium for Service Innovation, Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) v6 Practices Guide (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="sup-07"></a>
##### SUP-07 — Support automation & deflection design

*Type:* Technical — Build automated assist and routing flows that resolve common requests without agent effort.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures simple automated responses from defined patterns, with logic reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring simple automated responses from defined patterns with logic reviewed is implementing one of Price & Jaffe's seven principles (eliminate dumb contacts) as a fixed rule set — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds standard deflection flows and tunes them to routine demand.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard deflection flows and tuning them to routine demand is competent, correct execution of the eliminate-dumb-contacts principle on familiar volume — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs automation for ambiguous, high-impact cases and is the go-to for complex deflection.
  — *Why this level:* Designing automation for ambiguous, high-impact cases as the go-to for complex deflection is applying Price & Jaffe's 'create engaging self-service' and 'be proactive' principles where no existing flow fits — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the automation and deflection framework others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the automation and deflection framework others adopt is codifying Price & Jaffe's seven principles into a team-wide design standard rather than applying them case by case — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets deflection strategy and anticipates which interactions automation should absorb next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting deflection strategy and anticipating which interactions automation should absorb next is SFIA's initiate/influence band — the anticipatory posture Price & Jaffe's 'own the actions across the company' principle demands at scale. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines how the discipline approaches support automation and shapes industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how the discipline approaches support automation and shaping industry practice is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band, extending the influence Price & Jaffe's framework has had in reshaping how the profession thinks about deflection. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Price & Jaffe, The Best Service is No Service: How to Liberate Your Customers from Customer Service, Keep Them Happy, and Control Costs (Jossey-Bass, 2008).

#### Quality & Performance

<a id="sup-08"></a>
##### SUP-08 — Quality assurance & CSAT management

*Type:* Technical — Audit interactions against quality standards and manage satisfaction metrics to improve service.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Scores cases against a defined rubric and flags issues for a reviewer.
  — *Why this level:* Scoring cases against a defined rubric and flagging issues for a reviewer is applying the COPC CX Standard's quality-monitoring process exactly as specified — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* COPC Inc., COPC Customer Experience (CX) Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently audits quality and manages routine CSAT follow-up with normal oversight.
  — *Why this level:* Independently auditing quality and managing routine CSAT follow-up under normal oversight is competent, standard execution of the COPC CX Standard's QA cycle — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* COPC Inc., COPC Customer Experience (CX) Standard (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Interprets ambiguous quality signals and is the go-to for improving stubborn CSAT problems.
  — *Why this level:* Interpreting ambiguous quality signals and improving stubborn CSAT problems is applying Dixon, Toman & DeLisi's finding that satisfaction doesn't predict loyalty — diagnosing effort and disloyalty drivers a simple CSAT score hides — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Dixon, Toman & DeLisi, The Effortless Experience: Conquering the New Battleground for Customer Loyalty (Portfolio/Penguin, 2013); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the quality rubric and CSAT-improvement program the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the quality rubric and CSAT-improvement program the team adopts is building an effort-based quality program around Dixon et al.'s Customer Effort Score research rather than a satisfaction score alone — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Dixon, Toman & DeLisi, The Effortless Experience: Conquering the New Battleground for Customer Loyalty (Portfolio/Penguin, 2013); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets quality and satisfaction strategy and anticipates emerging drivers of customer sentiment.
  — *Why this level:* Setting quality and satisfaction strategy and anticipating emerging sentiment drivers is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching the COPC CX Standard's organization-wide performance-management scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); COPC Inc., COPC Customer Experience (CX) Standard (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what support quality means for the discipline and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what support quality means for the discipline, externally credible, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band — the authority the COPC CX Standard itself has held as the field's quality benchmark for three decades. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); COPC Inc., COPC Customer Experience (CX) Standard (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="sup-09"></a>
##### SUP-09 — Support operations analytics & forecasting

*Type:* Technical — Analyze support data and forecast demand to inform staffing, trends, and performance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compiles support metrics into standard reports for a reviewer to interpret.
  — *Why this level:* Compiling support metrics into standard reports for a reviewer to interpret is producing raw inputs to the forecasting process Cleveland's ICMI reference describes, without yet running the forecast — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently analyzes operational data and produces routine forecasts with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently analyzing operational data and producing routine forecasts with normal review is competent, standard application of Cleveland's call-volume forecasting method to familiar patterns — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models ambiguous demand patterns and is the go-to for reliable forecasts in volatile conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling ambiguous demand patterns as the go-to for reliable forecasts in volatile conditions is doing the workforce-management judgment work Cleveland's book treats as the discipline's hardest problem — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the analytics and forecasting methodology others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the analytics and forecasting methodology others adopt is publishing a Cleveland-grade forecasting standard as team practice rather than applying an existing one — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets analytics strategy and anticipates how operational dynamics will shift forecasting needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting analytics strategy and anticipating how operational dynamics will shift forecasting needs is SFIA's initiate/influence band — anticipatory authority over the forecasting model itself, not just its outputs. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice support analytics for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice support analytics for the field, sought externally, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band, extending the reach Cleveland's reference has held as the industry's standard text on the subject. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012).

#### Workforce & Capacity

<a id="sup-10"></a>
##### SUP-10 — Workforce & shift planning for support

*Type:* Technical — Forecast contact volume and schedule staff to meet coverage and service-level requirements.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Slots agents into shifts using a defined schedule, with coverage reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Slotting agents into shifts using a defined schedule with coverage reviewed is executing a schedule Cleveland's ICMI reference describes as built by someone with forecasting authority — Dreyfus novice. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds standard schedules that meet routine coverage requirements.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard schedules that meet routine coverage requirements is competent, correct application of Erlang-based staffing calculations to familiar demand — Dreyfus advanced beginner. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Balances complex constraints and volatile demand and is the go-to for tough staffing puzzles.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing complex constraints and volatile demand as the go-to for tough staffing puzzles is the workforce-management judgment Cleveland's book treats as separating a scheduler from a workforce planner — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the workforce-planning model and scheduling standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the workforce-planning model and scheduling standards others adopt is publishing a Cleveland-grade staffing model as organizational practice — SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Cleveland, Call Center Management on Fast Forward: Succeeding in Today's Dynamic Customer Contact Environment, 3rd Edition (ICMI Press, 2012); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets workforce strategy and anticipates capacity needs ahead of demand shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting workforce strategy and anticipating capacity needs ahead of demand shifts is SFIA's initiate/influence band, matching ISO 18295's requirement that a contact centre provision resources to continuously meet customer needs, not just react to them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 18295-1:2017 Customer contact centres — Part 1: Requirements for customer contact centres (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice support workforce planning for the discipline and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice support workforce planning for the discipline, externally credible, is SFIA's set-strategy/inspire band — the authority ISO 18295 represents as the field's international requirements standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 18295-1:2017 Customer contact centres — Part 1: Requirements for customer contact centres (2017).

### Finance & Accounting (FIN)

#### Planning, Budgeting & Analysis

<a id="fin-01"></a>
##### FIN-01 — Financial planning & analysis (FP&A)

*Type:* Technical — Builds forecasts, budgets, and variance analysis to guide resource allocation and performance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Pulls data and updates planning templates, with analysis reviewed before use.
  — *Why this level:* Pulling data into planning templates with analysis reviewed before use is Dreyfus's novice band: applying a supplied structure without yet judging which drivers matter. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds standard analyses and variance reports with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard analyses and variance reports under normal review is the advanced-beginner band; IMA's competency framework places this recognized-pattern application at its foundation-to-applied proficiency tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Analyzes ambiguous business drivers and is the go-to for hard planning questions.
  — *Why this level:* Analyzing ambiguous business drivers unaided and being the team's go-to for hard planning questions is the Dreyfus competent band: exercising judgment on cases with no standard template, the level Brealey/Myers/Allen assume once past mechanical forecast construction. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brealey, Myers, Allen & Edmans, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the FP&A approach and analytical frameworks others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the FP&A approach and analytical frameworks other analysts adopt is SFIA9's ensure/advise band -- setting method, not applying one -- and IMA's competency framework marks this transition from applied to expert practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets FP&A strategy and anticipates how business dynamics will reshape planning.
  — *Why this level:* Setting FP&A strategy and anticipating how business dynamics will reshape planning is SFIA9's strategic-influence responsibility level: judgment that shapes direction for the whole finance function, not one forecast cycle. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent FP&A means for the profession and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent FP&A means for the profession and being externally credible on it is the pioneer band IMA's own framework reserves for practitioners whose methods become the field's reference points, and SFIA9's highest responsibility tier of setting strategy beyond one organization. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).

<a id="fin-02"></a>
##### FIN-02 — Budgeting & forecasting

*Type:* Technical — Develops operating and capital budgets and rolling forecasts aligned to financial targets.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Enters budget inputs and updates forecast templates, with figures reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Entering budget inputs and updating forecast templates with figures reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: executing a defined structure without owning the assumptions behind it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently prepares standard budgets and forecasts with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently preparing standard budgets and forecasts under normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying IMA's planning-domain competencies to recognized, low-uncertainty cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Builds forecasts under high uncertainty and is the go-to for reconciling conflicting assumptions.
  — *Why this level:* Building forecasts under high uncertainty and reconciling conflicting assumptions unaided is the Dreyfus competent band; Brealey/Myers/Allen's treatment of forecasting under uncertainty assumes exactly this unsupervised reconciliation of competing inputs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brealey, Myers, Allen & Edmans, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the budgeting and forecasting methodology others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the budgeting and forecasting methodology other planners adopt is authoring method rather than applying it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band and the expert tier of IMA's competency framework. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets forecasting strategy and anticipates shifts that will challenge planning assumptions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting forecasting strategy and anticipating shifts that will challenge planning assumptions is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, extending judgment beyond any single forecast cycle to the organization's planning posture. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice budgeting and forecasting for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice budgeting and forecasting for the field and being sought externally is the discipline-shaping pioneer band, the outer edge of IMA's competency ladder and SFIA9's highest responsibility tier. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).

<a id="fin-03"></a>
##### FIN-03 — Financial modeling & valuation

*Type:* Technical — Constructs quantitative models to value assets, businesses, and scenarios for decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Populates model inputs and runs defined scenarios, with outputs reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Populating model inputs and running defined scenarios with outputs reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: operating someone else's model structure without judging which valuation approach fits the asset. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds standard models and valuations with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building standard models and valuations under normal review is the advanced-beginner band: applying Damodaran's standard DCF and relative-valuation toolkit to recognized, well-behaved cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Damodaran, Investment Valuation: Tools and Techniques for Determining the Value of Any Asset, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2012).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models ambiguous, complex situations and is the go-to for defensible valuations.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling ambiguous, complex situations and being the go-to for defensible valuations is the Dreyfus competent band; Damodaran's own chapters on valuing distressed, illiquid, or unconventional assets assume a practitioner choosing and defending the right model unsupervised. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Damodaran, Investment Valuation: Tools and Techniques for Determining the Value of Any Asset, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2012).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines modeling standards and valuation approaches others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining modeling standards and valuation approaches others adopt is SFIA9's ensure/advise band -- setting the method Damodaran's text catalogs, not merely selecting from it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Damodaran, Investment Valuation: Tools and Techniques for Determining the Value of Any Asset, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2012).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets modeling strategy and anticipates which methods best fit emerging situations.
  — *Why this level:* Setting modeling strategy and anticipating which methods best fit emerging situations is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: judgment about valuation approach applied across the organization's whole deal and reporting pipeline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what rigorous financial modeling means for the profession and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what rigorous financial modeling means for the profession and being externally recognized is the pioneer band; it is the standing Damodaran himself holds as a reference point the field cites, not merely applies. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Damodaran, Investment Valuation: Tools and Techniques for Determining the Value of Any Asset, 3rd ed. (Wiley, 2012).

<a id="fin-04"></a>
##### FIN-04 — Capital planning & investment appraisal

*Type:* Technical — Evaluates capital projects using cash flow, payback, and return metrics to prioritize funding.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers project data and computes defined metrics, with appraisals reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering project data and computing defined metrics with appraisals reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: running someone else's appraisal formula without judging which metric governs the decision. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently appraises standard investments and prepares routine capital plans.
  — *Why this level:* Independently appraising standard investments and preparing routine capital plans under normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying Brealey/Myers/Allen's NPV and IRR toolkit to well-defined, low-ambiguity projects. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brealey, Myers, Allen & Edmans, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Evaluates ambiguous, high-stakes investments and is the go-to for tough capital decisions.
  — *Why this level:* Evaluating ambiguous, high-stakes investments and being the go-to for tough capital decisions is the Dreyfus competent band; the text's treatment of real options and risk-adjusted discount rates assumes exactly this unsupervised judgment on hard cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Brealey, Myers, Allen & Edmans, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the appraisal methodology and capital-planning framework others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the appraisal methodology and capital-planning framework others adopt is authoring the standard, not applying it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise responsibility band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Brealey, Myers, Allen & Edmans, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets capital-allocation strategy and anticipates how priorities will reshape investment.
  — *Why this level:* Setting capital-allocation strategy and anticipating how priorities will reshape investment is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, spanning the organization's whole capital portfolio rather than one project appraisal. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice capital planning for the discipline and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice capital planning for the discipline and being externally credible is the pioneer band -- shaping how the field itself, not just one organization, appraises capital. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Brealey, Myers, Allen & Edmans, Principles of Corporate Finance, 14th ed. (McGraw Hill, 2023).

#### Accounting & Reporting

<a id="fin-05"></a>
##### FIN-05 — Accounting & financial reporting

*Type:* Technical — Records transactions and prepares financial statements per applicable accounting standards.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares routine entries and report sections per standards, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing routine entries and report sections per standards with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: following codified GAAP rules without judging which standard applies to an ambiguous fact pattern. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently produces standard financial statements and disclosures with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently producing standard financial statements and disclosures under normal review is the advanced-beginner band: applying FASB's codified GAAP topics to recognized, routine transactions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Financial Accounting Standards Board, FASB Accounting Standards Codification (ASC), the single source of authoritative U.S. GAAP (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles ambiguous accounting treatments and is the go-to for complex reporting judgments.
  — *Why this level:* Handling ambiguous accounting treatments and being the go-to for complex reporting judgments is the Dreyfus competent band -- the judgment calls the Codification itself defers to preparer interpretation when a fact pattern doesn't map cleanly to one topic. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Financial Accounting Standards Board, FASB Accounting Standards Codification (ASC), the single source of authoritative U.S. GAAP (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines reporting standards and accounting policy the team adopts.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reporting standards and accounting policy the team adopts is SFIA9's ensure/advise band: writing the internal policy that operationalizes GAAP, not just applying the Codification case by case. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Financial Accounting Standards Board, FASB Accounting Standards Codification (ASC), the single source of authoritative U.S. GAAP (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets reporting strategy and anticipates how evolving standards will affect disclosure.
  — *Why this level:* Setting reporting strategy and anticipating how evolving standards will affect disclosure is SFIA9's strategic-influence level -- tracking and preparing the organization for standard-setting change before it lands. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice financial reporting for the profession and shapes how others apply it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice financial reporting for the profession and shaping how others apply it is the pioneer band: influencing how the wider profession interprets and applies the Codification, not just complying with it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Financial Accounting Standards Board, FASB Accounting Standards Codification (ASC), the single source of authoritative U.S. GAAP (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="fin-06"></a>
##### FIN-06 — Management & cost accounting

*Type:* Technical — Allocates and analyzes costs to support pricing, profitability, and management decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compiles cost data and updates standard cost reports, with allocations reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Compiling cost data and updating standard cost reports with allocations reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: executing a defined allocation rule without judging whether it fits the cost driver. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently prepares routine cost analyses and management reports with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently preparing routine cost analyses and management reports under normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying IMA's costing competencies to recognized, standard-cost cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs costing for ambiguous cases and is the go-to for complex allocation and margin questions.
  — *Why this level:* Designing costing for ambiguous cases and being the go-to for complex allocation and margin questions is the Dreyfus competent band; Kaplan & Atkinson's activity-based and transfer-pricing methods assume a practitioner choosing the right costing design unsupervised, not just running a fixed allocation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kaplan & Atkinson, Advanced Management Accounting, 3rd ed. (Prentice Hall, 1998).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the costing methodology and management-reporting framework others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the costing methodology and management-reporting framework others adopt is authoring the costing design Kaplan & Atkinson catalog, not applying a template -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kaplan & Atkinson, Advanced Management Accounting, 3rd ed. (Prentice Hall, 1998).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets cost-accounting strategy and anticipates how business changes will reshape costing.
  — *Why this level:* Setting cost-accounting strategy and anticipating how business changes will reshape costing is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, extending judgment across the organization's whole cost structure. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice management and cost accounting for the field and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice management and cost accounting for the field and being externally credible is the pioneer band, the expert-and-beyond tier IMA's own competency ladder points toward but does not itself define. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Institute of Management Accountants (IMA), IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework (2023).

<a id="fin-07"></a>
##### FIN-07 — Revenue recognition & billing operations

*Type:* Technical — Applies revenue standards and operates billing cycles to recognize and invoice earned revenue.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Processes routine billing and revenue entries per rules, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Processing routine billing and revenue entries per rules with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: following the codified recognition rule without judging which performance obligation it attaches to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently handles standard revenue recognition and billing with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently handling standard revenue recognition and billing under normal review is the advanced-beginner band: applying ASC 606's five-step model to recognized, single-obligation contracts. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); FASB, Accounting Standards Update No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) (2014).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous recognition cases and is the go-to for complex contract and billing scenarios.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous recognition cases and being the go-to for complex contract and billing scenarios is the Dreyfus competent band -- ASC 606's judgment-heavy steps, identifying distinct performance obligations and allocating variable consideration, assume exactly this unsupervised case-by-case reasoning. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); FASB, Accounting Standards Update No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) (2014).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines revenue-recognition policy and billing-operations standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining revenue-recognition policy and billing-operations standards others adopt is writing the internal policy that operationalizes ASC 606 across the business, not applying it contract by contract -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); FASB, Accounting Standards Update No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) (2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets revenue strategy and anticipates how new arrangements will affect recognition.
  — *Why this level:* Setting revenue strategy and anticipating how new arrangements will affect recognition is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: shaping deal and product design around recognition consequences before they arise. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice revenue recognition for the profession and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice revenue recognition for the profession and being sought externally is the pioneer band -- shaping how the wider profession interprets ASC 606's judgment areas, not just complying with them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); FASB, Accounting Standards Update No. 2014-09, Revenue from Contracts with Customers (Topic 606) (2014).

<a id="fin-08"></a>
##### FIN-08 — General ledger & financial close

*Type:* Technical — Manages ledger integrity and reconciliations for accurate, timely period-end closes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Posts routine entries and reconciliations per checklist, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Posting routine entries and reconciliations per checklist with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: following a defined close checklist without judging which items need investigation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs standard close tasks and reconciliations with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running standard close tasks and reconciliations under normal review is the advanced-beginner band: executing COSO's control-activities component on recognized, low-risk accounts without redesigning the process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous close issues and is the go-to for keeping a complex close on track.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous close issues and being the go-to for keeping a complex close on track is the Dreyfus competent band -- exercising the control-environment judgment COSO's framework assumes when a standard reconciliation breaks down. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the close process and ledger-control standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the close process and ledger-control standards others adopt is authoring the control design, not executing it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band, setting the GAAP-grounded close standard the team follows. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Financial Accounting Standards Board, FASB Accounting Standards Codification (ASC), the single source of authoritative U.S. GAAP (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets close strategy and anticipates how complexity will challenge the close.
  — *Why this level:* Setting close strategy and anticipating how complexity will challenge the close is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: redesigning the close operating model ahead of growth or system change, not fixing one period's exceptions. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice ledger and close management for the field and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice ledger and close management for the field and being externally credible is the pioneer band -- influencing how the profession itself designs close controls, the discipline-shaping tier beyond any one organization's COSO implementation. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).

#### Treasury & Capital

<a id="fin-09"></a>
##### FIN-09 — Treasury & cash management

*Type:* Technical — Manages liquidity, cash positioning, and short-term funding to optimize working capital.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records cash positions and processes routine transactions, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Recording cash positions and processing routine transactions with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: executing defined treasury transactions without judging liquidity trade-offs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard cash operations and short-term liquidity with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing standard cash operations and short-term liquidity under normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying AFP's CTP body-of-knowledge fundamentals, cash positioning and working-capital mechanics, to recognized, routine situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Association for Financial Professionals, Essentials of Treasury Management (Certified Treasury Professional body of knowledge), 7th ed..
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Manages ambiguous liquidity situations and is the go-to for tough cash-flow decisions.
  — *Why this level:* Managing ambiguous liquidity situations and being the go-to for tough cash-flow decisions is the Dreyfus competent band; the CTP body of knowledge's risk-and-exposure content assumes a practitioner exercising this judgment unsupervised. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Association for Financial Professionals, Essentials of Treasury Management (Certified Treasury Professional body of knowledge), 7th ed..
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the treasury and liquidity-management framework others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the treasury and liquidity-management framework others adopt is authoring the treasury operating model the CTP body of knowledge describes, not applying it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Association for Financial Professionals, Essentials of Treasury Management (Certified Treasury Professional body of knowledge), 7th ed..
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets treasury strategy and anticipates liquidity needs before they materialize.
  — *Why this level:* Setting treasury strategy and anticipating liquidity needs before they materialize is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: shaping the organization's funding and liquidity posture ahead of need, not managing today's cash position. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice treasury and cash management for the discipline and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice treasury and cash management for the discipline and being externally recognized is the pioneer band -- shaping the practice the CTP credential itself teaches, the tier beyond certified practitioner. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Association for Financial Professionals, Essentials of Treasury Management (Certified Treasury Professional body of knowledge), 7th ed..

<a id="fin-10"></a>
##### FIN-10 — Financial risk management & hedging

*Type:* Technical — Mitigates currency, rate, credit, and commodity exposures using hedging instruments.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers exposure data and applies defined hedging steps, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering exposure data and applying defined hedging steps with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: executing a prescribed hedge instruction without judging exposure or instrument fit. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently monitors standard risks and executes routine hedges with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently monitoring standard risks and executing routine hedges under normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying GARP's FRM Part I foundations, market and credit risk identification, to recognized exposures. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP), Financial Risk Manager (FRM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Assesses ambiguous, complex exposures and is the go-to for structuring difficult hedges.
  — *Why this level:* Assessing ambiguous, complex exposures and being the go-to for structuring difficult hedges is the Dreyfus competent band; Hull's treatment of exotic instruments and model choice assumes a practitioner structuring hedges unsupervised for non-standard exposures. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed. (Pearson, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the risk-management and hedging methodology others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the risk-management and hedging methodology others adopt is authoring the hedging approach Hull catalogs, not selecting from it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed. (Pearson, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets risk strategy and anticipates emerging exposures before they materialize.
  — *Why this level:* Setting risk strategy and anticipating emerging exposures before they materialize is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, matching GARP FRM Part II's shift from applying risk tools to managing enterprise risk appetite. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP), Financial Risk Manager (FRM) Program Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice financial risk management for the profession and shapes industry practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice financial risk management for the profession and shaping industry practice is the pioneer band -- the standing Hull's own text holds as the field's reference on derivatives and hedging practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hull, Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives, 11th ed. (Pearson, 2021).

<a id="fin-11"></a>
##### FIN-11 — Investor relations & capital markets

*Type:* Behavioral — Communicates performance and strategy to investors to support capital access and valuation.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assembles investor materials from templates, with content reviewed before release.
  — *Why this level:* Assembling investor materials from templates with content reviewed before release is the Dreyfus novice band: producing communications to a defined structure without judging market reaction. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently prepares standard investor communications and handles routine inquiries.
  — *Why this level:* Independently preparing standard investor communications and handling routine inquiries is the advanced-beginner band, applying NIRI's Body of Knowledge practice areas to recognized, low-stakes disclosure situations. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); National Investor Relations Institute (NIRI), Investor Relations Body of Knowledge, 2nd ed. (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Navigates ambiguous market questions and is the go-to for tough investor conversations.
  — *Why this level:* Navigating ambiguous market questions and being the go-to for tough investor conversations is the Dreyfus competent band; NIRI's Body of Knowledge domains on capital-markets judgment assume exactly this unsupervised handling of hard questions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); National Investor Relations Institute (NIRI), Investor Relations Body of Knowledge, 2nd ed. (2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the investor-relations and capital-markets approach others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the investor-relations and capital-markets approach others adopt is authoring the IR playbook NIRI's domains describe, not executing it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); National Investor Relations Institute (NIRI), Investor Relations Body of Knowledge, 2nd ed. (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets IR strategy and anticipates how market sentiment will shape positioning.
  — *Why this level:* Setting IR strategy and anticipating how market sentiment will shape positioning is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: shaping the organization's capital-markets narrative ahead of events, not reacting to inquiries. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice investor relations for the field and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice investor relations for the field and being externally credible is the pioneer band -- shaping the standards NIRI itself curates into its Body of Knowledge, not just applying them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); National Investor Relations Institute (NIRI), Investor Relations Body of Knowledge, 2nd ed. (2024).

#### Tax, Controls & Assurance

<a id="fin-12"></a>
##### FIN-12 — Tax planning & compliance

*Type:* Technical — Plans tax positions and prepares filings to optimize liability while meeting obligations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares routine tax filings and gathers documentation, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing routine tax filings and gathering documentation with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: following defined filing procedure without judging position or exposure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently handles standard compliance and filings with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently handling standard compliance and filings under normal review is the advanced-beginner band, applying AICPA's SSTS baseline standards to recognized, low-ambiguity positions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); AICPA, Statements on Standards for Tax Services (SSTS) Nos. 1-4, revised (effective 2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous tax positions and is the go-to for complex planning questions.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous tax positions and being the go-to for complex planning questions is the Dreyfus competent band; the SSTS's standards on realistic-possibility and reasonable-basis judgment assume a practitioner deciding position strength unsupervised. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); AICPA, Statements on Standards for Tax Services (SSTS) Nos. 1-4, revised (effective 2024).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines tax-planning approaches and compliance standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining tax-planning approaches and compliance standards others adopt is authoring the firm's internal application of SSTS judgment standards, not applying them case by case -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); AICPA, Statements on Standards for Tax Services (SSTS) Nos. 1-4, revised (effective 2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets tax strategy and anticipates how regulatory change will affect positions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting tax strategy and anticipating how regulatory change will affect positions is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: shaping the organization's tax posture ahead of legislative or regulatory shifts. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice tax planning for the profession and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice tax planning for the profession and being sought externally is the pioneer band -- shaping how the profession itself interprets standards like the SSTS, the tier beyond firm-level policy authorship. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); AICPA, Statements on Standards for Tax Services (SSTS) Nos. 1-4, revised (effective 2024).

<a id="fin-13"></a>
##### FIN-13 — Internal controls & financial governance

*Type:* Technical — Designs and operates control frameworks for reliable financial reporting and asset safety.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs assigned control checks and documents results, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Performing assigned control checks and documenting results with work reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: executing a defined control step without judging whether the control itself is adequate. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently operates and tests standard controls with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently operating and testing standard controls under normal review is the advanced-beginner band: applying COSO's control-activities component to recognized, already-designed controls. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses ambiguous control gaps and is the go-to for designing robust controls.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing ambiguous control gaps and being the go-to for designing robust controls is the Dreyfus competent band -- exercising the risk-assessment judgment COSO's framework requires to identify where a control design itself is insufficient. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the control framework and governance standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the control framework and governance standards others adopt is authoring the control environment that SOX Section 404(a) requires management to design and assess, not merely operating within it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); U.S. Congress, Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, Section 404 (Public Law 107-204, 116 Stat. 745).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets controls strategy and anticipates emerging risks that controls must address.
  — *Why this level:* Setting controls strategy and anticipating emerging risks that controls must address is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: redesigning the control framework ahead of new risk, the scope COSO's monitoring component assumes at an enterprise level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice financial governance for the discipline and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice financial governance for the discipline and being externally credible on it is the pioneer band -- shaping how the profession itself applies frameworks like COSO, not just implementing them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), Internal Control - Integrated Framework (2013).

<a id="fin-14"></a>
##### FIN-14 — External & financial audit coordination

*Type:* Technical — Plans and executes audit activities to verify accuracy and assess control effectiveness.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Collects requested evidence and tracks audit items, with submissions reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Collecting requested evidence and tracking audit items with submissions reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: fulfilling defined evidence requests without judging their sufficiency. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard audit requests and routine auditor liaison with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing standard audit requests and routine auditor liaison under normal review is the advanced-beginner band: supporting the evidence-gathering PCAOB AS 2201 requires for recognized, low-complexity accounts without owning the audit relationship. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles ambiguous audit matters and is the go-to for keeping a complex audit on track.
  — *Why this level:* Handling ambiguous audit matters and being the go-to for keeping a complex audit on track is the Dreyfus competent band; PCAOB AS 2201's integrated-audit evidence and material-weakness judgment calls assume a practitioner navigating this unsupervised. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the audit-coordination approach and readiness standards others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the audit-coordination approach and readiness standards others adopt is authoring the readiness model that operationalizes PCAOB AS 2201's integrated-audit evidence requirements across engagements, not just responding request by request -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets audit-coordination strategy and anticipates scrutiny before it arises.
  — *Why this level:* Setting audit-coordination strategy and anticipating scrutiny before it arises is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: shaping the organization's audit readiness posture ahead of the integrated ICFR audit PCAOB AS 2201 requires, not reacting during fieldwork. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice audit coordination for the field and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice audit coordination for the field and being externally recognized for it is the pioneer band -- shaping how the profession itself applies standards like PCAOB AS 2201, the tier beyond one organization's practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Public Company Accounting Oversight Board, AS 2201: An Audit of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting That Is Integrated with An Audit of Financial Statements.

### Procurement & Vendor Management (PROC)

#### Sourcing & Selection

<a id="proc-01"></a>
##### PROC-01 — Sourcing strategy & supplier selection

*Type:* Technical — Develops sourcing strategies and evaluates suppliers to select best-fit sources of supply.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers supplier information and scores bids against criteria others define, with selections reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering supplier information and scoring bids against criteria others define, with selections reviewed, is the Dreyfus novice band: applying someone else's evaluation criteria without judging which criteria fit the category. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard sourcing events end-to-end, shortlisting suppliers and recommending awards for routine categories.
