  — *Why this level:* Running standard sourcing events end-to-end and recommending awards for routine categories is the advanced-beginner band, matching CIPS's Global Standard competencies for practitioners executing recognized sourcing processes independently. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs sourcing approaches for ambiguous or complex needs and defends selection decisions to stakeholders.
  — *Why this level:* Designing sourcing approaches for ambiguous or complex needs and defending selection decisions to stakeholders is the Dreyfus competent band; Kraljic's portfolio matrix assumes a buyer classifying category risk and leverage and choosing posture unsupervised, not following a fixed process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines selection methodologies and weighting models that other sourcing professionals adopt across categories.
  — *Why this level:* Defining selection methodologies and weighting models other sourcing professionals adopt across categories is authoring the segmentation and evaluation method Kraljic's matrix exemplifies, not applying it to one category -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organizational sourcing strategy and anticipates shifts in supply markets that reshape selection.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organizational sourcing strategy and anticipating shifts in supply markets that reshape selection is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, the senior tier CIPS's Global Standard describes as shaping organization-wide procurement direction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry practice for evidence-based supplier selection and is cited externally as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry practice for evidence-based supplier selection and being cited externally as authoritative is the pioneer band -- shaping the discipline's method itself, the tier beyond any one organization's sourcing strategy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="proc-02"></a>
##### PROC-02 — Category management

*Type:* Technical — Segments spend into categories and applies tailored strategies to maximize value.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains category spend data and supplier lists under direction, flagging anomalies for review.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining category spend data and supplier lists under direction, flagging anomalies for review, is the Dreyfus novice band: tracking a defined dataset without owning category strategy. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages a defined category, tracking spend, suppliers, and renewals with routine guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Managing a defined category with routine guidance is the advanced-beginner band -- Van Weele's commercial-orientation stage, where a buyer runs competitive processes and tracks renewals within an established category structure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns complex categories, building multi-year category plans that balance cost, risk, and innovation.
  — *Why this level:* Owning complex categories and building multi-year plans that balance cost, risk, and innovation is the Dreyfus competent band; Kraljic's matrix assumes exactly this unsupervised judgment about treating strategic versus leverage categories differently. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kraljic, Purchasing Must Become Supply Management, Harvard Business Review 61(5), 109-117 (1983).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the category management operating model and coaches managers on advanced category strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the category management operating model and coaching managers on advanced strategy is Van Weele's internal-integration stage -- category management becomes a designed cross-functional discipline, not one buyer's practice -- and SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise category strategy and predicts category market trends years ahead.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise category strategy and predicting market trends years ahead is Van Weele's external-integration stage, extending category strategy into supplier and market foresight at SFIA9's strategic-influence level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers category management frameworks adopted as reference practice across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Pioneering category management frameworks adopted as reference practice across the profession is Van Weele's value-chain-orientation stage taken to its discipline-shaping limit -- the pioneer band beyond any one organization's category model. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).

<a id="proc-03"></a>
##### PROC-03 — Competitive bidding & tendering

*Type:* Technical — Designs and runs structured solicitation and evaluation to award competitive deals.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assembles tender documents and logs supplier responses against checklists, with steps reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Assembling tender documents and logging supplier responses against checklists, with steps reviewed, is the Dreyfus novice band: executing defined tender-administration steps without judging evaluation fairness or rigor. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard tenders independently, managing timelines, clarifications, and evaluation logistics.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard tenders independently, managing timelines, clarifications, and evaluation logistics, is the advanced-beginner band, matching CIPS's Global Standard competencies for practitioners executing recognized tender processes unaided. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Structures complex tenders with intricate requirements and resolves disputes and ambiguous responses.
  — *Why this level:* Structuring complex tenders with intricate requirements and resolving disputes and ambiguous responses is the Dreyfus competent band -- the fair, defensible-evaluation judgment CIPS's Global Standard expects once a tender departs from a standard template. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines tendering methods and evaluation frameworks others use for high-stakes competitions.
  — *Why this level:* Defining tendering methods and evaluation frameworks others use for high-stakes competitions is authoring the method CIPS's standard describes for advanced practitioners, not running one event -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's competitive bidding strategy and shapes how markets respond to its tenders.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's competitive bidding strategy and shaping how markets respond to its tenders is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: tender design decisions that alter supplier market behavior, not one competition's outcome. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes recognized standards for fair, defensible tendering across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing recognized standards for fair, defensible tendering across the discipline is the pioneer band -- contributing to the standard CIPS itself curates, the tier beyond applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).

#### Contracts & Negotiation

<a id="proc-04"></a>
##### PROC-04 — Supplier contract negotiation & administration

*Type:* Behavioral — Negotiates terms and administers contracts for favorable, enforceable agreements.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks contract terms and renewal dates and prepares standard clauses under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking contract terms and renewal dates and preparing standard clauses under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band: administering defined terms without yet negotiating them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Negotiates routine contract terms and administers agreements within established mandates.
  — *Why this level:* Negotiating routine contract terms and administering agreements within established mandates is the advanced-beginner band, applying Fisher, Ury & Patton's principled-negotiation basics, interests over positions, to recognized, bounded deals. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Leads complex negotiations, handling difficult counterparties and crafting bespoke commercial terms.
  — *Why this level:* Leading complex negotiations with difficult counterparties and crafting bespoke commercial terms is the Dreyfus competent band; Lax & Sebenius's 3-D negotiation tactics, deal design and setup, assume a negotiator operating unsupervised on non-standard, high-stakes deals. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Lax & Sebenius, 3-D Negotiation: Powerful Tools to Change the Game in Your Most Important Deals (Harvard Business School Press, 2006).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines negotiation playbooks and contract standards that other negotiators adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining negotiation playbooks and contract standards other negotiators adopt is authoring the method Fisher, Ury & Patton's framework exemplifies, not applying it deal by deal -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Fisher, Ury & Patton, Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In (Harvard Negotiation Project / Penguin, 1981, rev. 2011).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets contracting strategy and anticipates legal and commercial shifts affecting supplier agreements.
  — *Why this level:* Setting contracting strategy and anticipating legal and commercial shifts affecting supplier agreements is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, extending Lax & Sebenius's deal-design thinking across the organization's whole supplier-agreement portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Lax & Sebenius, 3-D Negotiation: Powerful Tools to Change the Game in Your Most Important Deals (Harvard Business School Press, 2006).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes contracting practice recognized industry-wide as the benchmark for sound supplier agreements.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping contracting practice recognized industry-wide as the benchmark for sound supplier agreements is the pioneer band -- discipline-shaping influence beyond any one organization's negotiation playbook. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Supplier Performance & Risk

<a id="proc-05"></a>
##### PROC-05 — Supplier relationship & performance management

*Type:* Behavioral — Builds supplier partnerships and monitors performance against service and value expectations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Collects supplier performance data and updates scorecards with results reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Collecting supplier performance data and updating scorecards with results reviewed is the Dreyfus novice band: recording defined metrics without owning the relationship. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine supplier relationships, running reviews and tracking SLAs independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine supplier relationships, running reviews and tracking SLAs independently, is the advanced-beginner band -- ISO 44001's early relationship-management stages, where structured monitoring exists but the relationship isn't yet actively developed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO, ISO 44001:2017 Collaborative Business Relationship Management Systems - Requirements and Framework.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns critical supplier relationships, resolving conflicts and driving performance improvement under ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Owning critical supplier relationships, resolving conflicts and driving performance improvement under ambiguity, is the Dreyfus competent band; ISO 44001's requirements for managing relationship risk and value creation assume this unsupervised judgment on a live, complex relationship. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO, ISO 44001:2017 Collaborative Business Relationship Management Systems - Requirements and Framework.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs SRM frameworks and performance models that others adopt across the supplier base.
  — *Why this level:* Designing SRM frameworks and performance models others adopt across the supplier base is authoring the collaborative-relationship management system ISO 44001 specifies, not operating within one relationship -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 44001:2017 Collaborative Business Relationship Management Systems - Requirements and Framework.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise supplier relationship strategy and foresees how key partnerships should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise supplier relationship strategy and foreseeing how key partnerships should evolve is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, the senior tier CIPS's Global Standard expects to shape the organization's whole supplier-relationship portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent supplier partnership means for the profession and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent supplier partnership means for the profession and being externally credible is the pioneer band -- discipline-shaping influence beyond any one organization's SRM program. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

<a id="proc-06"></a>
##### PROC-06 — Supplier risk & compliance

*Type:* Technical — Assesses and mitigates supplier financial, operational, and continuity risks.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Runs supplier risk checklists and compliance screens, escalating findings for review.
  — *Why this level:* Running supplier risk checklists and compliance screens, escalating findings for review, is the Dreyfus novice band: executing a defined risk-identification step without judging severity or response. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Assesses routine supplier risks and verifies compliance against standard requirements independently.
  — *Why this level:* Assessing routine supplier risks and verifying compliance against standard requirements independently is the advanced-beginner band, applying ISO 31000's risk-identification and evaluation process to recognized, well-understood exposures. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Evaluates complex, ambiguous supplier risks and designs mitigation for critical exposures.
  — *Why this level:* Evaluating complex, ambiguous supplier risks and designing mitigation for critical exposures is the Dreyfus competent band; ISO 31000's risk-treatment step assumes a practitioner selecting and defending mitigation for exposures with no standard playbook. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines supplier risk frameworks and compliance controls others apply across the supply base.
  — *Why this level:* Defining supplier risk frameworks and compliance controls others apply across the supply base is authoring the risk-management system COSO's ERM framework describes, not applying it to one supplier -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); COSO, Enterprise Risk Management - Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets supplier risk strategy and anticipates emerging regulatory and supply-chain threats.
  — *Why this level:* Setting supplier risk strategy and anticipating emerging regulatory and supply-chain threats is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, the enterprise-risk-appetite judgment COSO's ERM framework places at senior leadership. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); COSO, Enterprise Risk Management - Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers supplier risk and compliance practice regarded as authoritative across the industry.
  — *Why this level:* Pioneering supplier risk and compliance practice regarded as authoritative across the industry is the pioneer band -- shaping how the discipline itself applies frameworks like ISO 31000 and COSO ERM, not just implementing them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Spend & Operations

<a id="proc-07"></a>
##### PROC-07 — Spend analysis & cost optimization

*Type:* Technical — Analyzes spend to identify savings, consolidation, and total-cost-of-ownership opportunities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Cleans and categorizes spend data and produces standard reports under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Cleaning and categorizing spend data and producing standard reports under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: preparing data to a defined structure without judging where savings opportunities lie. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Analyzes spend independently to identify routine savings and reports cost opportunities.
  — *Why this level:* Analyzing spend independently to identify routine savings is the advanced-beginner band -- Van Weele's commercial-orientation stage, where spend consolidation and unit-price savings are pursued within a known category structure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Uncovers complex savings across fragmented spend and builds defensible optimization business cases.
  — *Why this level:* Uncovering complex savings across fragmented spend and building defensible optimization business cases is the Dreyfus competent band; Van Weele's purchasing-coordination stage assumes a practitioner finding savings that cross category boundaries, not one already-grouped category. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines spend analytics methods and cost-optimization approaches that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining spend analytics methods and cost-optimization approaches others adopt is authoring the analytical method at Van Weele's internal-integration stage, not running one analysis -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise cost strategy and predicts where structural savings will emerge.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise cost strategy and predicting where structural savings will emerge is SFIA9's strategic-influence level, matching Van Weele's external-integration stage where cost strategy extends into supplier and market foresight. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best practice for spend intelligence and cost optimization across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best practice for spend intelligence and cost optimization across the discipline is Van Weele's value-chain-orientation stage taken to its discipline-shaping limit -- the pioneer band beyond any one organization's spend program. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Van Weele, Purchasing and Supply Chain Management: Analysis, Strategy, Planning and Practice, 7th ed. (Cengage Learning EMEA, 2018).

<a id="proc-08"></a>
##### PROC-08 — Procure-to-pay process management

*Type:* Technical — Optimizes the end-to-end procure-to-pay cycle for accuracy, speed, control, and cash efficiency.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Processes requisitions, orders, and invoices following defined procedures, with exceptions escalated.
  — *Why this level:* Processing requisitions, orders, and invoices following defined procedures, with exceptions escalated, is the Dreyfus novice band: executing the P2P procedure without judging exception handling. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine procure-to-pay flows independently and resolves common exceptions.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine procure-to-pay flows independently and resolving common exceptions is the advanced-beginner band: operating within APQC's process-classification-framework baseline for cycle time and exception rates without redesigning the process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); APQC, Procure-to-Pay: Cross-Industry Report (Open Standards Benchmarking, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles complex P2P exceptions and redesigns local process steps to remove friction.
  — *Why this level:* Handling complex P2P exceptions and redesigning local process steps to remove friction is the Dreyfus competent band -- moving beyond APQC's benchmark process to unsupervised local process redesign when the standard flow breaks down. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); APQC, Procure-to-Pay: Cross-Industry Report (Open Standards Benchmarking, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines P2P process and control standards that operators across the function adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining P2P process and control standards that operators across the function adopt is authoring the process design CIPS's Global Standard expects of advanced practitioners, not operating within it -- SFIA9's ensure/advise band. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply (CIPS), The Global Standard for Procurement and Supply, 2nd ed. (2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets P2P strategy and anticipates how processes should evolve for control and efficiency.
  — *Why this level:* Setting P2P strategy and anticipating how processes should evolve for control and efficiency is SFIA9's strategic-influence level: redesigning the P2P operating model against APQC's cross-industry benchmarks ahead of need. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); APQC, Procure-to-Pay: Cross-Industry Report (Open Standards Benchmarking, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes procure-to-pay practice recognized as the benchmark across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing procure-to-pay practice recognized as the benchmark across the profession is the pioneer band -- becoming the reference other organizations and benchmarks like APQC's measure against, not just meeting the benchmark. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

### People & Talent (HR) (HR)

#### Talent Acquisition

<a id="hr-01"></a>
##### HR-01 — Talent acquisition & recruiting

*Type:* Behavioral — Owns end-to-end sourcing, assessment, and offer to fill roles with qualified candidates.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Screens applications and schedules interviews against defined criteria, with decisions reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Screening applications and scheduling interviews against defined criteria, with decisions reviewed, is explicit rule-following on a well-defined task -- Dreyfus's novice band, before independent judgment is trusted. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages requisitions end-to-end for standard roles, sourcing and closing candidates independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing requisitions end-to-end and closing standard roles without oversight is the operational HR competence SHRM's BASK certifies through the SHRM-CP -- independent execution of routine, well-understood work, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Fills hard-to-source and senior roles, handling ambiguous needs and complex stakeholder demands.
  — *Why this level:* Filling hard-to-source and senior roles under ambiguous stakeholder demands is Boudreau & Ramstad's talentship thesis in practice -- treating scarce, pivotal roles as a decision-science problem rather than a fill-the-req task -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines recruiting methods and assessment approaches that other recruiters adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining recruiting methods and assessment approaches other recruiters adopt is talentship's decision-science framework turned into a transferable methodology, moving from applying the science to authoring it for a function. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets talent acquisition strategy and anticipates shifts in talent markets and hiring needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting talent acquisition strategy and anticipating market shifts is exactly the strategic, direction-setting HR practice the SHRM-SCP certifies above the SHRM-CP's operational bar -- SFIA's set-strategy responsibility band applied to hiring. *Sources:* SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes recruiting practice recognized industry-wide as the standard for effective hiring.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping recruiting practice recognized industry-wide as the standard for effective hiring is talentship's decision science advanced from one organization's methodology into the field's shared body of practice -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007); SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="hr-02"></a>
##### HR-02 — Employer branding & candidate experience

*Type:* Behavioral — Shapes market reputation and candidate journey to attract and convert talent.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Publishes branded content and gathers candidate feedback following defined guidelines.
  — *Why this level:* Publishing branded content and gathering feedback against defined guidelines is explicit, template-following execution reviewed by others -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard employer-branding activities and improves candidate touchpoints independently.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard employer-branding activities and improving touchpoints independently is applying Minchington's employer-brand-development practice at the foundational maturity stage without needing design judgment -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Minchington, Employer Brand Leadership: A Global Perspective (Collective Learning Australia, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Crafts compelling employer narratives and resolves complex candidate-experience breakdowns.
  — *Why this level:* Crafting compelling narratives and resolving complex candidate-experience breakdowns is Employer Brand Leadership's higher-maturity practice -- brand strategy judgment applied to ambiguous, high-stakes situations -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Minchington, Employer Brand Leadership: A Global Perspective (Collective Learning Australia, 2010); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines branding and candidate-experience frameworks that other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining branding and candidate-experience frameworks other practitioners adopt is Minchington's own leadership-stage practice: an employer-brand program mature enough that its methodology becomes the template others copy. *Sources:* Minchington, Employer Brand Leadership: A Global Perspective (Collective Learning Australia, 2010).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets employer-brand strategy and anticipates how talent perceptions and channels will shift.
  — *Why this level:* Setting employer-brand strategy and anticipating channel and perception shifts is employer-brand leadership elevated to enterprise strategy -- SFIA's set-strategy/influence responsibility band. *Sources:* Minchington, Employer Brand Leadership: A Global Perspective (Collective Learning Australia, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what a leading employer brand and candidate experience look like for the field.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what a leading employer brand and candidate experience look like for the field mirrors Minchington's own global-perspective research role -- practice advanced from organizational program to field-defining reference, the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Minchington, Employer Brand Leadership: A Global Perspective (Collective Learning Australia, 2010).

<a id="hr-03"></a>
##### HR-03 — Workforce sourcing strategy & pipelining

*Type:* Behavioral — Builds proactive talent pools and sourcing channels to meet future hiring demand.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds candidate lists and maintains talent pools using defined search criteria.
  — *Why this level:* Building candidate lists and maintaining pools using defined search criteria is rule-bound execution under review -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs proactive sourcing campaigns and sustains pipelines for routine roles independently.
  — *Why this level:* Running proactive sourcing campaigns and sustaining pipelines for routine roles independently is talentship's workforce-supply discipline applied to ordinary, non-pivotal roles without needing to prioritize scarce impact -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs sourcing strategies for scarce skills and builds pipelines under high ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Designing sourcing strategies for scarce skills under high ambiguity is Boudreau & Ramstad's core talentship move -- identifying and resourcing pivotal roles where talent quality has outsized impact -- exercised with judgment, the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines sourcing and pipelining methodologies that other sourcers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining sourcing and pipelining methodologies other sourcers adopt is talentship's pivotal-role targeting turned into a transferable, org-adopted method rather than one person's practice. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise workforce-sourcing strategy and predicts future talent-supply gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise workforce-sourcing strategy and predicting future supply gaps is talentship's decision science applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting scope SFIA reserves for its highest responsibility levels. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers talent-pipelining practice recognized as authoritative across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized as authoritative across the profession for talent-pipelining practice is talentship's decision science advanced beyond one organization into the field's shared standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).

#### Total Rewards

<a id="hr-04"></a>
##### HR-04 — Total rewards & compensation design

*Type:* Technical — Designs pay structures, bands, and incentives that are equitable and market-competitive.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains pay data and benchmarks roles against defined bands, with results reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining pay data and benchmarking roles against defined bands, with results reviewed, is explicit, checklist-level execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Conducts standard compensation analysis and recommends routine pay decisions independently.
  — *Why this level:* Conducting standard compensation analysis and recommending routine pay decisions independently is applying Milkovich, Newman & Gerhart's total-compensation model to ordinary cases without needing to resolve competing design tensions -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Milkovich, Newman & Gerhart, Compensation, 12th Edition (McGraw-Hill Education, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs pay structures for complex roles and resolves contentious equity and market issues.
  — *Why this level:* Designing pay structures for complex roles and resolving contentious equity and market issues is Compensation's internal-equity-versus-market-competitiveness tension worked with judgment on ambiguous, high-stakes cases -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Milkovich, Newman & Gerhart, Compensation, 12th Edition (McGraw-Hill Education, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines compensation philosophy and design frameworks that other rewards professionals adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining compensation philosophy and design frameworks other rewards professionals adopt is building the kind of five-element Total Rewards architecture WorldatWork's model describes, at a scope others inherit rather than one team's practice. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets total rewards strategy and anticipates market and regulatory shifts in pay.
  — *Why this level:* Setting total rewards strategy and anticipating market and regulatory shifts in pay is the Total Rewards Model's organizational-context layer (business strategy, external influences) owned and steered -- SFIA's set-strategy responsibility band. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes compensation-design practice regarded industry-wide as the benchmark.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping compensation-design practice regarded industry-wide as the benchmark is total-rewards design theory and practice advanced from one organization's program into the field's reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically); Milkovich, Newman & Gerhart, Compensation, 12th Edition (McGraw-Hill Education, 2016).

<a id="hr-05"></a>
##### HR-05 — Benefits & wellbeing program management

*Type:* Technical — Administers health, retirement, leave, and wellbeing offerings across the workforce.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Administers enrollments and answers routine benefits questions following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Administering enrollments and answering routine benefits questions following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution under review -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard benefits and wellbeing programs and resolves common issues independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard benefits and wellbeing programs and resolving common issues independently is operating the benefits and well-being elements of WorldatWork's Total Rewards Model on routine cases without design judgment -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs benefits offerings for complex needs and resolves ambiguous coverage and vendor problems.
  — *Why this level:* Designing offerings for complex needs and resolving ambiguous coverage and vendor problems is the Total Rewards Model's benefits/well-being elements applied with judgment to non-routine, high-stakes cases -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines benefits and wellbeing program frameworks that other administrators adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining benefits and wellbeing program frameworks other administrators adopt is turning the Total Rewards Model's benefits element into a transferable program design others inherit rather than build themselves. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets benefits and wellbeing strategy and anticipates workforce-health and cost trends.
  — *Why this level:* Setting benefits and wellbeing strategy and anticipating workforce-health and cost trends is Total Rewards program design elevated to the strategy-setting, trend-anticipating responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for benefits and wellbeing across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading practice for benefits and wellbeing across the discipline is Total Rewards program design advanced from an organization's offering into the field's reference model -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* WorldatWork, Total Rewards Model: A Framework for Attracting, Motivating, and Retaining Employees (WorldatWork, updated periodically).

<a id="hr-06"></a>
##### HR-06 — Equity & long-term incentive administration

*Type:* Technical — Manages equity and long-term incentive programs and their governance and reporting.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records grants and processes vesting events following defined procedures, with checks reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Recording grants and processing vesting events following defined procedures, with checks reviewed, is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Administers standard equity and incentive plans independently, handling routine transactions.
  — *Why this level:* Administering standard equity and incentive plans independently, handling routine transactions, is the baseline knowledge CEPI's Equity Compensation Associate (Level 1) credential certifies -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Certified Equity Professional Institute (Santa Clara University), Certified Equity Professional (CEP) Program (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex equity events and edge cases across grants, taxation, and reporting.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex equity events and edge cases across grants, taxation, and reporting is exactly the cross-disciplinary mastery -- accounting, plan design, securities law, and taxation together -- the full Certified Equity Professional (CEP) credential tests, applied with judgment to ambiguous cases: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Certified Equity Professional Institute (Santa Clara University), Certified Equity Professional (CEP) Program (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines equity-administration controls and processes that other administrators adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining equity-administration controls and processes other administrators adopt is CEP-level cross-disciplinary mastery turned into a transferable control framework rather than individual case-handling skill. *Sources:* Certified Equity Professional Institute (Santa Clara University), Certified Equity Professional (CEP) Program (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets long-term incentive administration strategy and anticipates regulatory and plan-design shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting long-term incentive administration strategy and anticipating regulatory and plan-design shifts is equity-compensation expertise elevated to the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its highest levels. *Sources:* Certified Equity Professional Institute (Santa Clara University), Certified Equity Professional (CEP) Program (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes equity-administration practice recognized as the standard across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing equity-administration practice recognized as the standard across the profession is CEP-level mastery advanced from individual credentialed practice into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Certified Equity Professional Institute (Santa Clara University), Certified Equity Professional (CEP) Program (accessed 2026-07).

#### Learning & Org Development

<a id="hr-07"></a>
##### HR-07 — Learning & development program design

*Type:* Behavioral — Builds curricula, capability frameworks, and delivery models that grow workforce skills.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assembles learning materials and schedules sessions against defined objectives, with content reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Assembling learning materials and scheduling sessions against defined objectives, with content reviewed, is explicit, rule-following execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Designs and delivers standard learning programs independently for routine needs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing and delivering standard learning programs independently for routine needs is applying Kirkpatrick's reaction-and-learning evaluation levels to well-understood training needs without needing deeper behavior-and-results judgment -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs learning solutions for complex skill gaps and ambiguous capability needs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing solutions for complex skill gaps and ambiguous capability needs is extending Kirkpatrick's evaluation model into its harder behavior-and-results levels, exercised through ATD's capability-building domain of practice -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994); Association for Talent Development, Talent Development Capability Model (2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines instructional-design methods and learning frameworks that other designers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining instructional-design methods and learning frameworks other designers adopt is ATD's Talent Development Capability Model's own logic -- capability-building practice mature enough to be codified and taught to other practitioners. *Sources:* Association for Talent Development, Talent Development Capability Model (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise learning strategy and anticipates future capability and skill demands.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise learning strategy and anticipating future capability demands is ATD's organizational-capability-impact domain owned at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Association for Talent Development, Talent Development Capability Model (2019); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers learning-design practice recognized industry-wide as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized industry-wide as authoritative in learning-design practice is instructional-design theory advanced from organizational program into field-shaping contribution -- exactly the trajectory Kirkpatrick's own four-level model took from one practitioner's framework to the training industry's de facto standard. *Sources:* Association for Talent Development, Talent Development Capability Model (2019); Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994).

<a id="hr-08"></a>
##### HR-08 — Organizational development & culture programs

*Type:* Behavioral — Designs interventions that strengthen culture, values, and organizational effectiveness.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports culture initiatives and collects feedback following defined plans.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting culture initiatives and collecting feedback following defined plans is explicit, rule-bound execution under direction -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard OD and culture interventions independently for routine situations.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard OD and culture interventions independently for routine situations is administering Cameron & Quinn's Organizational Culture Assessment Instrument and its standard diagnostic playbook without needing to resolve deeper ambiguity -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Cameron & Quinn, Diagnosing and Changing Organizational Culture: Based on the Competing Values Framework, 3rd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2011).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Diagnoses complex organizational dysfunction and designs interventions under high ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing complex organizational dysfunction and designing interventions under high ambiguity is Schein's artifacts-values-underlying-assumptions model of culture worked below the surface, where diagnosis requires judgment rather than a standard instrument -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines OD methods and culture-change frameworks that other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining OD methods and culture-change frameworks other practitioners adopt is turning the Competing Values Framework and Schein's diagnostic model into a transferable, org-adopted intervention methodology rather than one practitioner's case work. *Sources:* Cameron & Quinn, Diagnosing and Changing Organizational Culture: Based on the Competing Values Framework, 3rd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2011); Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets organizational-development strategy and anticipates cultural shifts the organization must make.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organizational-development strategy and anticipating cultural shifts the organization must make is Schein's own thesis that leadership's central function is creating and managing culture, exercised at the strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes OD and culture practice regarded as the benchmark across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Being regarded as the benchmark across the discipline for OD and culture practice is organizational-culture theory advanced from applied diagnostic practice into the field's reference frameworks -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Cameron & Quinn, Diagnosing and Changing Organizational Culture: Based on the Competing Values Framework, 3rd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2011); Schein, Organizational Culture and Leadership, 4th ed. (Jossey-Bass, 2010).

<a id="hr-09"></a>
##### HR-09 — Talent management & succession programs

*Type:* Behavioral — Owns frameworks for identifying, developing, and retaining critical and high-potential talent.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains talent and succession data and prepares review materials under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining talent and succession data and preparing review materials under direction is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard talent-review and succession cycles independently for defined populations.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard talent-review and succession cycles independently for defined populations is administering Charan, Drotter & Noel's leadership-pipeline passages for well-understood, non-contested populations -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Charan, Drotter & Noel, The Leadership Pipeline: How to Build the Leadership-Powered Company, 2nd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2010).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs succession approaches for critical, ambiguous roles and resolves contested talent calls.
  — *Why this level:* Designing succession approaches for critical, ambiguous roles and resolving contested talent calls is navigating the Leadership Pipeline's passages under real organizational tension and disagreement, not just tracking them -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Charan, Drotter & Noel, The Leadership Pipeline: How to Build the Leadership-Powered Company, 2nd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2010); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines talent-management and succession frameworks that other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining talent-management and succession frameworks other practitioners adopt is turning the Leadership Pipeline's passage model into a transferable, org-adopted succession methodology rather than one team's cycle. *Sources:* Charan, Drotter & Noel, The Leadership Pipeline: How to Build the Leadership-Powered Company, 2nd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2010).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise succession strategy and anticipates future leadership and capability gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise succession strategy and anticipating future leadership and capability gaps is the Leadership Pipeline's passage model applied predictively at the strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Charan, Drotter & Noel, The Leadership Pipeline: How to Build the Leadership-Powered Company, 2nd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2010); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for talent management and succession across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading practice for talent management and succession across the profession is succession theory advanced from one organization's program into the field's shared reference model -- exactly the trajectory the Leadership Pipeline itself took to become the standard succession framework. *Sources:* Charan, Drotter & Noel, The Leadership Pipeline: How to Build the Leadership-Powered Company, 2nd Edition (Jossey-Bass, 2010).

<a id="hr-10"></a>
##### HR-10 — DEI program management

*Type:* Behavioral — Runs diversity, equity, and inclusion strategy, programs, and accountability measures.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports DEI activities and compiles representation data following defined plans.
  — *Why this level:* Supporting DEI activities and compiling representation data following defined plans is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard DEI programs independently and tracks routine progress measures.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard DEI programs independently and tracking routine progress measures is operating within the Title VII compliance baseline the EEOC enforces, applied to well-understood, non-contested situations -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs DEI interventions for complex, sensitive challenges under significant ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Designing interventions for complex, sensitive challenges under significant ambiguity is McKinsey's core Diversity Wins finding in practice -- that diversity alone doesn't produce inclusion, so closing the gap requires judgment beyond compliance and representation metrics -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Hunt, Prince, Dixon-Fyle & Yee, Diversity Wins: How Inclusion Matters (McKinsey & Company, 2020); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines DEI program frameworks and measurement approaches that other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining DEI program frameworks and measurement approaches other practitioners adopt is turning Diversity Wins's diversity-versus-inclusion distinction into a transferable measurement and intervention framework other organizations inherit. *Sources:* Hunt, Prince, Dixon-Fyle & Yee, Diversity Wins: How Inclusion Matters (McKinsey & Company, 2020).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise DEI strategy and anticipates shifts in equity expectations and regulation.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise DEI strategy and anticipating shifts in equity expectations and regulation is Diversity Wins's business-case research applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Hunt, Prince, Dixon-Fyle & Yee, Diversity Wins: How Inclusion Matters (McKinsey & Company, 2020); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers DEI practice recognized externally as authoritative across the field.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized externally as authoritative across the field in DEI practice is diversity-and-inclusion research and program design advanced from organizational practice into field-shaping, externally credible contribution -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Hunt, Prince, Dixon-Fyle & Yee, Diversity Wins: How Inclusion Matters (McKinsey & Company, 2020); U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07).

#### HR Partnering & Employee Relations

<a id="hr-11"></a>
##### HR-11 — HR business partnering

*Type:* Behavioral — Advises leaders on people strategy, organizational issues, and workforce decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Answers routine manager queries and gathers people data, with guidance reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Answering routine manager queries and gathering people data, with guidance reviewed, is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Advises managers on standard people matters independently within established policy.
  — *Why this level:* Advising managers on standard people matters independently within established policy is performing Ulrich's Administrative Expert and Employee Champion roles on well-understood cases without needing to negotiate strategic tension -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Ulrich, Human Resource Champions: The Next Agenda for Adding Value and Delivering Results (Harvard Business School Press, 1997).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Partners on complex, ambiguous people challenges and influences senior leaders' decisions.
  — *Why this level:* Partnering on complex, ambiguous people challenges and influencing senior leaders' decisions is stepping into Ulrich's Strategic Partner and Change Agent roles -- the two Human Resource Champions roles that require judgment under ambiguity, not procedure -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Ulrich, Human Resource Champions: The Next Agenda for Adding Value and Delivering Results (Harvard Business School Press, 1997); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines HR partnering approaches and coaching models that other partners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining HR partnering approaches and coaching models other partners adopt is HR from the Outside In's Credible Activist and Capability Builder competencies turned into a transferable coaching methodology other partners inherit. *Sources:* Ulrich, Younger, Brockbank & Ulrich, HR from the Outside In: Six Competencies for the Future of Human Resources (McGraw-Hill, 2012).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the HR partnering operating model and anticipates the business's future people needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the HR partnering operating model and anticipating the business's future people needs is Ulrich's Strategic Positioner competency exercised at the operating-model, anticipatory scope SFIA reserves for its top responsibility levels. *Sources:* Ulrich, Younger, Brockbank & Ulrich, HR from the Outside In: Six Competencies for the Future of Human Resources (McGraw-Hill, 2012); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what excellent HR partnering means for the discipline and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what excellent HR partnering means for the discipline and being externally credible is exactly the trajectory Ulrich's own research program took -- from one book's four-role model to a globally cited, repeatedly revalidated competency study that defines the field -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Ulrich, Younger, Brockbank & Ulrich, HR from the Outside In: Six Competencies for the Future of Human Resources (McGraw-Hill, 2012); Ulrich, Human Resource Champions: The Next Agenda for Adding Value and Delivering Results (Harvard Business School Press, 1997).

<a id="hr-12"></a>
##### HR-12 — Employee relations & investigations

*Type:* Behavioral — Handles grievances, conduct concerns, and workplace investigations fairly and consistently.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Documents cases and gathers evidence following defined procedures, with steps reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Documenting cases and gathering evidence following defined procedures, with steps reviewed, is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Handles routine ER cases and conducts standard investigations independently.
  — *Why this level:* Handling routine ER cases and conducting standard investigations independently is applying SHRM's seven-step workplace-investigation framework to well-understood, low-risk cases -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* SHRM, How to Conduct a Workplace Investigation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Manages complex, high-risk investigations and resolves sensitive disputes under ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Managing complex, high-risk investigations and resolving sensitive disputes under ambiguity is meeting the EEOC's promptness-and-adequacy standard -- impartial, thorough investigation reaching 'a reasonably fair estimate of truth' -- on contested, high-stakes cases: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* SHRM, How to Conduct a Workplace Investigation (accessed 2026-07); U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines investigation methods and ER frameworks that other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining investigation methods and ER frameworks other practitioners adopt is turning SHRM's investigation toolkit into a transferable, org-specific methodology other investigators inherit rather than one person's case practice. *Sources:* SHRM, How to Conduct a Workplace Investigation (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets employee-relations strategy and anticipates emerging workforce-conflict and legal risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting employee-relations strategy and anticipating emerging workforce-conflict and legal risks is EEOC compliance posture managed proactively at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes ER and investigations practice recognized as the standard across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing ER and investigations practice recognized as the standard across the profession is investigation methodology advanced from organizational practice into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* SHRM, How to Conduct a Workplace Investigation (accessed 2026-07); U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="hr-13"></a>
##### HR-13 — Employee engagement & listening programs

*Type:* Behavioral — Runs surveys and feedback systems to measure and act on workforce sentiment.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Administers surveys and compiles engagement results following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Administering surveys and compiling engagement results following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs standard listening cycles independently and reports routine engagement insights.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard listening cycles independently and reporting routine engagement insights is administering Gallup's Q12 framework and reporting its standard metrics without needing to diagnose deeper causes -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Gallup, State of the Global Workplace Report (2025).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs listening strategies for complex needs and turns ambiguous signals into action.
  — *Why this level:* Designing listening strategies for complex needs and turning ambiguous signals into action is exactly the harder move Gallup's own research highlights -- diagnosing why engagement is falling, such as the manager-engagement variance driving most of team-level engagement, and acting on it -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Gallup, State of the Global Workplace Report (2025); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines engagement and listening frameworks that other practitioners adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining engagement and listening frameworks other practitioners adopt is turning Q12-style measurement into a transferable listening-and-action methodology other practitioners inherit rather than one team's survey cycle. *Sources:* Gallup, State of the Global Workplace Report (2025).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise engagement strategy and anticipates shifts in workforce sentiment and expectations.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise engagement strategy and anticipating shifts in workforce sentiment and expectations is Gallup's global engagement research applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Gallup, State of the Global Workplace Report (2025); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers employee-listening practice regarded industry-wide as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Being regarded industry-wide as authoritative in employee-listening practice is engagement measurement advanced from organizational program into the field's shared standard -- exactly the trajectory Gallup's own Q12 instrument took to become the industry's default engagement framework. *Sources:* Gallup, State of the Global Workplace Report (2025).

#### People Operations & Compliance

<a id="hr-14"></a>
##### HR-14 — HR operations & lifecycle administration

*Type:* Technical — Administers accurate records and transactions across hire-to-retire lifecycle events.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Processes lifecycle transactions following defined procedures, escalating exceptions for review.
  — *Why this level:* Processing lifecycle transactions following defined procedures, escalating exceptions for review, is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine HR operations and lifecycle events independently, resolving common issues.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine HR operations and lifecycle events independently, resolving common issues, is the operational HR competence SHRM's BASK certifies through the SHRM-CP -- independent execution of well-understood transactional work, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles complex lifecycle exceptions and redesigns local processes to improve service.
  — *Why this level:* Handling complex lifecycle exceptions and redesigning local processes to improve service is applying Ulrich's shared-services logic -- separating standardized administration from judgment-requiring exceptions -- with design judgment on ambiguous cases: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Ulrich, Human Resource Champions: The Next Agenda for Adding Value and Delivering Results (Harvard Business School Press, 1997); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines HR operations standards and controls that other administrators adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining HR operations standards and controls other administrators adopt is turning SHRM-CP-level operational competence into a transferable control framework other administrators inherit rather than individual case-handling skill. *Sources:* SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets HR operations strategy and anticipates how lifecycle services should evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting HR operations strategy and anticipating how lifecycle services should evolve is HR operations competence elevated to the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band the SHRM-SCP and SFIA's top levels both reserve for senior practice. *Sources:* SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes HR operations practice recognized as the benchmark across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing HR operations practice recognized as the benchmark across the profession is transactional HR service design advanced from organizational program into the field's shared reference model -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* SHRM, Body of Applied Skills and Knowledge (BASK) and SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP Certification Framework (accessed 2026-07); Ulrich, Human Resource Champions: The Next Agenda for Adding Value and Delivering Results (Harvard Business School Press, 1997).

<a id="hr-15"></a>
##### HR-15 — HR compliance & employment law application

*Type:* Technical — Applies employment laws and regulations to policies, decisions, and practices.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies defined compliance checklists and flags potential issues for review.
  — *Why this level:* Applying defined compliance checklists and flagging potential issues for review is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Applies standard employment-law requirements to routine situations independently.
  — *Why this level:* Applying standard employment-law requirements to routine situations independently is applying Fair Labor Standards Act wage-and-hour rules to well-understood cases without needing to resolve ambiguity -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Interprets ambiguous legal requirements and advises on complex compliance risks.
  — *Why this level:* Interpreting ambiguous legal requirements and advising on complex compliance risks is moving beyond checklist application of Title VII and the FLSA into judgment about how the law applies to novel, contested situations -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07); U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines compliance frameworks and interpretive guidance that other practitioners adopt.
