  — *Why this level:* Defining compliance frameworks and interpretive guidance other practitioners adopt is turning statutory interpretation into a transferable interpretive framework other practitioners inherit rather than one person's case-by-case judgment. *Sources:* U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets HR compliance strategy and anticipates regulatory change affecting the workforce.
  — *Why this level:* Setting HR compliance strategy and anticipating regulatory change affecting the workforce is compliance practice elevated to the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes employment-compliance practice regarded as authoritative across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping employment-compliance practice regarded as authoritative across the discipline is statutory interpretation advanced from organizational practice into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* U.S. Congress, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as enforced by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (accessed 2026-07); U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division, Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="hr-16"></a>
##### HR-16 — People analytics & workforce planning

*Type:* Technical — Models workforce supply, demand, and trends to inform people decisions with data.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compiles workforce data and produces standard reports under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Compiling workforce data and producing standard reports under guidance is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Builds routine workforce analyses and forecasts independently for defined needs.
  — *Why this level:* Building routine workforce analyses and forecasts independently for defined needs is applying Fitz-enz's human-capital metrics -- his five key indexes of cost, time, quantity, quality, and human reactions -- to well-understood, defined analyses -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Fitz-enz, The ROI of Human Capital: Measuring the Economic Value of Employee Performance, 2nd Edition (AMACOM, 2009).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Models complex workforce scenarios and derives insight from ambiguous, messy data.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling complex workforce scenarios and deriving insight from ambiguous, messy data is combining Fitz-enz's human-capital measurement discipline with Boudreau & Ramstad's talentship decision science, exercised with judgment on real, unclean data -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Fitz-enz, The ROI of Human Capital: Measuring the Economic Value of Employee Performance, 2nd Edition (AMACOM, 2009); Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines analytics methods and workforce-planning models that other analysts adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining analytics methods and workforce-planning models other analysts adopt is turning talentship's decision-science approach and human-capital metrics into a transferable modeling methodology other analysts inherit. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007); Fitz-enz, The ROI of Human Capital: Measuring the Economic Value of Employee Performance, 2nd Edition (AMACOM, 2009).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets people-analytics strategy and anticipates the workforce shifts the organization must plan for.
  — *Why this level:* Setting people-analytics strategy and anticipating the workforce shifts the organization must plan for is talentship's decision science applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers people-analytics and workforce-planning practice recognized as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized as authoritative in people-analytics and workforce-planning practice is human-capital measurement and talentship theory advanced from organizational practice into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Fitz-enz, The ROI of Human Capital: Measuring the Economic Value of Employee Performance, 2nd Edition (AMACOM, 2009); Boudreau & Ramstad, Beyond HR: The New Science of Human Capital (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).

### Workplace, Facilities & Real Estate (WPL)

#### Facilities & Space

<a id="wpl-01"></a>
##### WPL-01 — Facilities & space management

*Type:* Technical — Plans, allocates, and maintains physical workspace to meet occupancy and operational needs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates space records and processes facilities requests following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Updating space records and processing facilities requests following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine space allocation and facilities services independently for standard needs.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine space allocation and facilities services independently for standard needs is the foundational competence IFMA's facility-management body of knowledge certifies at entry level -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* IFMA, Certified Facility Manager (CFM) 11-Competency Facility Management Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Solves complex space and utilization challenges and plans moves under significant ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Solving complex space and utilization challenges and planning moves under significant ambiguity is exercising the full breadth of IFMA's 11-competency CFM body of knowledge with judgment on ambiguous, high-stakes cases -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* IFMA, Certified Facility Manager (CFM) 11-Competency Facility Management Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines space-management standards and planning approaches that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining space-management standards and planning approaches others adopt is turning CFM-level competency mastery into the kind of systematic, documented facility-management system ISO 41001 codifies for others to follow. *Sources:* IFMA, Certified Facility Manager (CFM) 11-Competency Facility Management Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); ISO, ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise space strategy and anticipates how workplace demand will evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise space strategy and anticipating how workplace demand will evolve is ISO 41001's facility-management-system requirements owned at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for facilities and space management across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading practice for facilities and space management across the discipline is facility-management competency and systems practice advanced from organizational program into the field's shared standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IFMA, Certified Facility Manager (CFM) 11-Competency Facility Management Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); ISO, ISO 41001:2018 Facility Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018).

<a id="wpl-02"></a>
##### WPL-02 — Building operations & maintenance management

*Type:* Technical — Operates building systems and preventive maintenance to ensure reliable, safe facilities.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Logs maintenance requests and tracks routine tasks following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Logging maintenance requests and tracking routine tasks following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard building operations and planned maintenance independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard building operations and planned maintenance independently is the foundational operations competence within IFMA's facility-management body of knowledge -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* IFMA, Certified Facility Manager (CFM) 11-Competency Facility Management Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex building failures and optimizes maintenance under operational ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex building failures and optimizing maintenance under operational ambiguity is ISO 55001's core discipline -- balancing asset performance, risk, and expenditure across the asset lifecycle -- applied with judgment to ambiguous cases: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 55001:2014 Asset Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements (2014); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines maintenance and building-operations standards that other managers adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining maintenance and building-operations standards other managers adopt is turning ISO 55001's asset-lifecycle balancing act into a transferable operations standard other managers inherit rather than one building's practice. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 55001:2014 Asset Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements (2014).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets building-operations strategy and anticipates asset-lifecycle and reliability needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting building-operations strategy and anticipating asset-lifecycle and reliability needs is ISO 55001's Strategic Asset Management Plan discipline exercised at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 55001:2014 Asset Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements (2014); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes building-operations practice recognized as the benchmark across the profession.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing building-operations practice recognized as the benchmark across the profession is asset-management and facility-operations discipline advanced from organizational program into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* IFMA, Certified Facility Manager (CFM) 11-Competency Facility Management Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); ISO, ISO 55001:2014 Asset Management -- Management Systems -- Requirements (2014).

<a id="wpl-03"></a>
##### WPL-03 — Capital projects & fit-out delivery

*Type:* Technical — Delivers construction, renovation, and fit-out projects on scope, budget, and schedule.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks project tasks and documents progress following defined plans, with work reviewed.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking project tasks and documenting progress following defined plans, with work reviewed, is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard fit-out projects independently, controlling scope, schedule, and budget.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard fit-out projects independently, controlling scope, schedule, and budget, is applying PMBOK's core performance domains to well-understood, predictable projects -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Delivers complex projects and resolves difficult scope, cost, and contractor problems.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering complex projects and resolving difficult scope, cost, and contractor problems is PMBOK's tailoring guidance -- selecting and adapting the development approach to the situation rather than following one fixed process -- exercised with judgment: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines project-delivery methods and fit-out standards that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining project-delivery methods and fit-out standards others adopt is turning PMBOK's performance domains into a transferable delivery methodology other project managers inherit rather than one project's playbook. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets capital-projects strategy and anticipates how the portfolio's space must change.
  — *Why this level:* Setting capital-projects strategy and anticipating how the portfolio's space must change is project-delivery discipline applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers capital-project delivery practice recognized industry-wide as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Pioneering capital-project delivery practice recognized industry-wide as authoritative is project-management discipline advanced from organizational practice into the field's shared standard -- exactly the trajectory PMBOK itself took from one institute's guide to the profession's default reference. *Sources:* Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).

#### Real Estate & Portfolio

<a id="wpl-04"></a>
##### WPL-04 — Real estate & lease management

*Type:* Technical — Manages the property portfolio, leases, and occupancy costs across locations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains lease records and tracks critical dates following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining lease records and tracking critical dates following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Administers leases and routine real-estate transactions independently within mandates.
  — *Why this level:* Administering leases and routine real-estate transactions independently within mandates is applying IFRS 16's single lessee-accounting model to well-understood, standard leases without needing to resolve structuring ambiguity -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* IFRS Foundation, IFRS 16 Leases (2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Negotiates complex leases and resolves ambiguous occupancy and landlord disputes.
  — *Why this level:* Negotiating complex leases and resolving ambiguous occupancy and landlord disputes is CoreNet's Master of Corporate Real Estate competency in practice -- financial analysis, business-case development, and risk mitigation applied under real negotiating ambiguity -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); IFRS Foundation, IFRS 16 Leases (2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines lease-management and transaction standards that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining lease-management and transaction standards others adopt is turning MCR-level financial and risk competency into a transferable transaction standard other practitioners inherit rather than one deal's negotiation. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets real-estate strategy and anticipates market and occupancy shifts affecting the portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Setting real-estate strategy and anticipating market and occupancy shifts affecting the portfolio is MCR's enterprise-alignment competency exercised at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes real-estate and lease-management practice regarded as the benchmark.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping real-estate and lease-management practice regarded as the benchmark is corporate real-estate competency advanced from organizational program into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="wpl-05"></a>
##### WPL-05 — Workplace portfolio strategy & site selection

*Type:* Behavioral — Sets location strategy and evaluates sites against business, cost, and talent needs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compiles site and portfolio data and prepares comparison materials under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Compiling site and portfolio data and preparing comparison materials under direction is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Evaluates standard site options and supports routine portfolio decisions independently.
  — *Why this level:* Evaluating standard site options and supporting routine portfolio decisions independently is applying Gensler's workplace-survey data to well-understood, non-contested comparisons -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Gensler Research Institute, U.S./Global Workplace Survey (annual, ongoing since 2005).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs site-selection approaches for complex needs and resolves competing location trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Designing site-selection approaches for complex needs and resolving competing location trade-offs is CoreNet's Master of Corporate Real Estate enterprise-alignment and workplace-strategy competency applied with judgment to genuinely ambiguous trade-offs -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines portfolio-strategy and site-selection frameworks that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining portfolio-strategy and site-selection frameworks others adopt is turning MCR-level strategic competency into a transferable site-selection framework other practitioners inherit rather than one decision's analysis. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise portfolio strategy and anticipates how location needs will evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise portfolio strategy and anticipating how location needs will evolve is MCR's enterprise-alignment competency exercised at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for workplace portfolio strategy across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading practice for workplace portfolio strategy across the discipline is corporate real-estate strategy advanced from organizational program into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* CoreNet Global, Master of Corporate Real Estate (MCR) Designation Curriculum (accessed 2026-07); Gensler Research Institute, U.S./Global Workplace Survey (annual, ongoing since 2005).

#### Workplace Experience

<a id="wpl-06"></a>
##### WPL-06 — Workplace experience & services

*Type:* Behavioral — Designs on-site services and amenities that support productivity and employee experience.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Delivers routine workplace services and gathers user feedback following defined plans.
  — *Why this level:* Delivering routine workplace services and gathering user feedback following defined plans is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard workplace-experience services independently and resolves common issues.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard workplace-experience services independently and resolving common issues is operating within Leesman's baseline workplace-effectiveness measurement, the Lmi score, on well-understood, routine service issues -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Leesman, The Leesman Index: Global Workplace Effectiveness Database (ongoing).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs experience improvements for complex needs and resolves ambiguous service breakdowns.
  — *Why this level:* Designing experience improvements for complex needs and resolving ambiguous service breakdowns is diagnosing the gap Leesman's own research repeatedly finds -- office experience trailing home experience -- and closing it with judgment, informed by Gensler's workplace-activity data: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Leesman, The Leesman Index: Global Workplace Effectiveness Database (ongoing); Gensler Research Institute, U.S./Global Workplace Survey (annual, ongoing since 2005).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines workplace-experience standards and service models that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining workplace-experience standards and service models others adopt is turning Leesman's workplace-impact and work-activities measurement into a transferable service model other practitioners inherit. *Sources:* Leesman, The Leesman Index: Global Workplace Effectiveness Database (ongoing).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets workplace-experience strategy and anticipates shifts in employee expectations.
  — *Why this level:* Setting workplace-experience strategy and anticipating shifts in employee expectations is Gensler's longitudinal workplace-survey research applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* Gensler Research Institute, U.S./Global Workplace Survey (annual, ongoing since 2005); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers workplace-experience practice recognized industry-wide as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Being recognized industry-wide as authoritative in workplace-experience practice is workplace-effectiveness measurement advanced from organizational program into the field's shared benchmarking standard -- exactly what Leesman's 425,000-respondent global database represents. *Sources:* Leesman, The Leesman Index: Global Workplace Effectiveness Database (ongoing); Gensler Research Institute, U.S./Global Workplace Survey (annual, ongoing since 2005).

<a id="wpl-07"></a>
##### WPL-07 — Sustainability & energy management

*Type:* Technical — Manages energy use, emissions, and sustainability of the built environment and operations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records energy and sustainability data and runs standard reports under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Recording energy and sustainability data and running standard reports under guidance is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine energy and sustainability initiatives independently for defined targets.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine energy and sustainability initiatives independently for defined targets is pursuing standard LEED credit requirements on well-understood, defined projects without needing to resolve competing constraints -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* U.S. Green Building Council, LEED Rating System (ongoing).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs sustainability and energy solutions for complex sites under significant ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Designing sustainability and energy solutions for complex sites under significant ambiguity is ISO 50001's systematic energy-management-system integration into operational, strategic, and financial decisions, exercised with judgment on ambiguous sites -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 50001:2018 Energy Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines sustainability and energy-management frameworks that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining sustainability and energy-management frameworks others adopt is turning ISO 50001's systematic EnMS approach and LEED's credit framework into a transferable program other practitioners inherit. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 50001:2018 Energy Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); U.S. Green Building Council, LEED Rating System (ongoing).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets sustainability strategy and anticipates regulatory and resource shifts affecting the portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Setting sustainability strategy and anticipating regulatory and resource shifts affecting the portfolio is ISO 50001's continual-improvement discipline applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 50001:2018 Energy Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for workplace sustainability and energy across the discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading practice for workplace sustainability and energy across the discipline is green-building and energy-management practice advanced from organizational program into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* U.S. Green Building Council, LEED Rating System (ongoing); ISO, ISO 50001:2018 Energy Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018).

#### Health, Safety & Security

<a id="wpl-08"></a>
##### WPL-08 — Environmental health & safety

*Type:* Technical — Ensures safe working conditions and compliance with occupational health and safety standards.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Conducts routine safety checks and logs incidents following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Conducting routine safety checks and logging incidents following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard EHS programs and investigations independently within policy.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard EHS programs and investigations independently within policy is applying OSHA's 29 CFR 1910 general-industry standards to well-understood, defined hazards -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* U.S. OSHA, 29 CFR Part 1910 Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex safety hazards and ambiguous compliance situations under risk.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex safety hazards and ambiguous compliance situations under risk is ISO 45001's full hazard-identification-and-risk-assessment management system exercised with judgment beyond OSHA's baseline rules, on ambiguous, high-stakes cases -- the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 45001:2018 Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); U.S. OSHA, 29 CFR Part 1910 Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines EHS standards and risk-assessment methods that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining EHS standards and risk-assessment methods others adopt is turning ISO 45001's OH&S management-system discipline into a transferable risk-assessment standard other practitioners inherit rather than one site's program. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 45001:2018 Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets EHS strategy and anticipates emerging hazards and regulatory change.
  — *Why this level:* Setting EHS strategy and anticipating emerging hazards and regulatory change is ISO 45001's leadership-and-worker-participation discipline applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 45001:2018 Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Establishes environmental-health-and-safety practice recognized as authoritative across the field.
  — *Why this level:* Establishing environmental-health-and-safety practice recognized as authoritative across the field is occupational health and safety management advanced from organizational program into the field's shared reference standard -- the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* ISO, ISO 45001:2018 Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems -- Requirements with Guidance for Use (2018); U.S. OSHA, 29 CFR Part 1910 Occupational Safety and Health Standards (General Industry).

<a id="wpl-09"></a>
##### WPL-09 — Physical security & access management

*Type:* Technical — Protects people and premises through access control, monitoring, and security operations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Monitors access systems and logs incidents following defined procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Monitoring access systems and logging incidents following defined procedures is explicit, rule-bound execution -- the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine physical-security operations and access controls independently.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine physical-security operations and access controls independently is operating within the Physical Security domain of ASIS's CPP body of knowledge on well-understood, defined situations -- the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* ASIS International, Certified Protection Professional (CPP) Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex security incidents and designs controls for ambiguous threats.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex security incidents and designing controls for ambiguous threats is drawing on the CPP's full seven-domain breadth -- physical, personnel, and information security, investigations, and crisis management together -- with judgment on ambiguous, high-stakes threats: the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* ASIS International, Certified Protection Professional (CPP) Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines physical-security standards and access frameworks that others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining physical-security standards and access frameworks others adopt is turning CPP-level cross-domain mastery into a transferable security-control framework other practitioners inherit rather than one site's operations. *Sources:* ASIS International, Certified Protection Professional (CPP) Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets physical-security strategy and anticipates emerging threats to people and assets.
  — *Why this level:* Setting physical-security strategy and anticipating emerging threats to people and assets is CPP's crisis-management and business-principles domains applied at the anticipatory, strategy-setting responsibility band SFIA reserves for its top levels. *Sources:* ASIS International, Certified Protection Professional (CPP) Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Pioneers physical-security and access-management practice recognized industry-wide as authoritative.
  — *Why this level:* Pioneering physical-security and access-management practice recognized industry-wide as authoritative is security-management discipline advanced from organizational practice into the field's shared credentialing standard -- exactly what ASIS's CPP body of knowledge itself represents for the security profession. *Sources:* ASIS International, Certified Protection Professional (CPP) Body of Knowledge (accessed 2026-07).

### Legal, Privacy & Compliance (LEG)

#### Commercial & Transactional Law

<a id="leg-01"></a>
##### LEG-01 — Contract drafting & negotiation

*Type:* Technical — Draft, review, and negotiate contractual terms that allocate risk and obligations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Drafts standard clauses from approved templates; flags deviations and negotiation points for supervising counsel review.
  — *Why this level:* Drafting standard clauses from approved templates and flagging deviations for review is Dreyfus's novice band — rule-following without discretionary judgment — and ABA Model Rule 5.1/5.3 places the duty to catch drafting errors on supervising counsel at this stage, not the drafter. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Drafts and redlines routine commercial agreements independently, negotiating standard terms with normal counsel oversight.
  — *Why this level:* Redlining routine commercial agreements independently under normal oversight is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band, recognizing situational patterns without full context-independence, and meets Model Rule 1.1's 'reasonable preparation' floor for competent representation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles bespoke, high-ambiguity contracts and contentious negotiations autonomously; the go-to drafter for novel deal terms.
  — *Why this level:* Handling bespoke, high-ambiguity contracts and contentious negotiations with no one reviewing each move is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band: the drafter sets the local standard others bring novel deal terms to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs clause libraries and negotiation playbooks others adopt; resolves drafting impasses that stall complex deals.
  — *Why this level:* Designing clause libraries and negotiation playbooks that other drafters adopt across a practice group is SFIA's level 5 'Ensure, advise' responsibility — authoritative guidance and accountability for outcomes beyond a single deal. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's contracting standards and risk posture; anticipates emerging clauses and shifts negotiation strategy.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's contracting standards and shifting negotiation strategy ahead of emerging clauses is SFIA's level 6 'Initiate, influence': organization-wide policy shaping, not deal-by-deal execution. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines contracting best practice recognized across the profession; authors model terms others treat as market standard.
  — *Why this level:* ABA's Rule 1.1 commentary names this ceiling directly — a 'lawyer of established competence in the field' whom other lawyers are directed to consult — the Dreyfus mastery band applied to the profession's own referral standard, here exercised by authoring model terms the market treats as baseline. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="leg-02"></a>
##### LEG-02 — Commercial & transactional law

*Type:* Technical — Advise on the legal structuring of commercial deals, financing, and transactions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Researches commercial-law questions and prepares routine transactional documents under close supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Researching commercial-law questions and preparing routine documents under close supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; ABA Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps final review responsibility with supervising counsel. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Advises on standard commercial matters and structures routine transactions independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Advising on standard commercial matters and structuring routine transactions independently with normal review is the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's competence floor through 'reasonable preparation' rather than deep specialization. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous commercial-law issues and structures non-standard deals autonomously; the local subject expert.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous commercial-law issues and structuring non-standard deals autonomously as the local subject expert is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band — no case requires escalation for a ruling on approach. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines transaction structures and risk frameworks others follow; cracks problems that stall sophisticated deals.
  — *Why this level:* Defining transaction structures and risk frameworks that other counsel follow is SFIA level 5 'Ensure, advise': accountable guidance across matters, not a single transaction. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the firm's commercial-law approach and anticipates regulatory and market shifts affecting transactions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the firm's commercial-law approach and anticipating regulatory and market shifts is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' — decisions that shape policy ahead of any one deal. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes commercial-law practice industry-wide; externally cited authority on transactional structuring.
  — *Why this level:* Being externally cited as the transactional-structuring authority is the profession's own ceiling case under Rule 1.1's commentary — the 'lawyer of established competence in the field' — Dreyfus mastery exercised industry-wide. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="leg-03"></a>
##### LEG-03 — M&A & corporate transactions (legal)

*Type:* Technical — Provide legal support for due diligence, structuring, and execution of corporate transactions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assembles diligence checklists and supporting documents for deals under senior supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Assembling diligence checklists under senior supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps the supervising deal lawyer accountable for what a checklist alone can't catch. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Runs defined diligence workstreams and drafts routine deal documents independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Running defined diligence workstreams and drafting routine deal documents independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's reasonable-preparation floor for a lawyer handling recurring deal patterns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Manages full deal legal workstreams and negotiates complex provisions autonomously through ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Managing full deal legal workstreams and negotiating complex provisions through ambiguity without a supervisor resolving each point is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Architects deal structures and diligence approaches others adopt; resolves issues that threaten closing.
  — *Why this level:* Architecting deal structures and diligence approaches other teams adopt is Haspeslagh & Jemison's integration-design work for step-change organizational growth, operating at SFIA level 5 accountability across the deal portfolio rather than one transaction. *Sources:* Haspeslagh & Jemison, Managing Acquisitions: Creating Value Through Corporate Renewal (Free Press, 1991); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's M&A legal strategy; anticipates structuring and regulatory risks across the deal lifecycle.
  — *Why this level:* Setting M&A legal strategy and anticipating structuring and regulatory risk across the deal lifecycle is the strategic-integration-design view Haspeslagh & Jemison describe at the acquiring organization's level, matching SFIA level 6 organizational influence. *Sources:* Haspeslagh & Jemison, Managing Acquisitions: Creating Value Through Corporate Renewal (Free Press, 1991); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines deal-execution practice recognized industry-wide; sought externally on landmark transactions.
  — *Why this level:* Being sought externally on landmark transactions is the Rule 1.1 commentary's 'lawyer of established competence in the field' ceiling, Dreyfus mastery recognized beyond the hiring organization. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).

#### Corporate & Regulatory Counsel

<a id="leg-04"></a>
##### LEG-04 — Corporate & entity governance

*Type:* Technical — Maintain legal entity structures, board governance, and statutory corporate obligations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains entity records and prepares routine corporate filings and minutes under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining entity records and preparing routine filings under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps review responsibility with supervising counsel for anything beyond the template. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages governance for standard entities and prepares board materials independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing governance for standard entities and preparing board materials independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's reasonable-preparation floor for recurring corporate-secretarial work. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles complex multi-entity governance and novel corporate-secretarial questions autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Handling complex multi-entity governance and novel corporate-secretarial questions autonomously is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band — no escalation needed to resolve a first-of-its-kind structure question. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs governance structures and entity frameworks others adopt; resolves intractable governance conflicts.
  — *Why this level:* Designing governance structures and entity frameworks other teams adopt operationalizes the G20/OECD Principles' board-and-ownership-function chapters as a template, at SFIA level 5 accountability across entities rather than one filing. *Sources:* OECD, G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise governance strategy and anticipates regulatory shifts affecting entity structures.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise governance strategy and anticipating regulatory shifts is applying the OECD Principles at the policy-setting level the Principles themselves address to boards and regulators, matching SFIA level 6 organizational influence. *Sources:* OECD, G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines governance best practice recognized across the field; externally credible authority.
  — *Why this level:* Being an externally credible governance authority mirrors the standing of practitioners whose input shapes revisions to instruments like the G20/OECD Principles themselves — Dreyfus mastery exercised at the standard-setting level, not just applying it. *Sources:* OECD, G20/OECD Principles of Corporate Governance (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).

<a id="leg-05"></a>
##### LEG-05 — Regulatory & licensing compliance

*Type:* Technical — Interpret and apply sector regulations, permits, and licensing requirements to operations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks licensing requirements and prepares routine regulatory filings under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking licensing requirements and preparing routine filings under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps a supervising lawyer accountable for filings beyond the routine. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard licensing and compliance obligations independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard licensing and compliance obligations independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, satisfying Rule 1.1's reasonable-preparation floor for recurring regulatory tasks. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous regulatory-interpretation questions and handles complex licensing autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous regulatory-interpretation questions and complex licensing autonomously is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band — the practitioner others bring first-of-a-kind interpretation questions to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs compliance approaches to novel regulation others adopt; resolves contested regulatory positions.
  — *Why this level:* Designing compliance approaches to novel regulation that others adopt, and resolving contested regulatory positions, is SFIA level 5 'Ensure, advise' — authoritative guidance accountable across the licensing portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets regulatory strategy and engages regulators; anticipates emerging requirements ahead of enforcement.
  — *Why this level:* Setting regulatory strategy and engaging regulators directly, ahead of enforcement, is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' — organizational-level policy engagement, not case-by-case filing. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes regulatory practice and interpretation industry-wide; externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping regulatory interpretation industry-wide is the Rule 1.1 commentary's 'lawyer of established competence in the field' ceiling — Dreyfus mastery recognized by regulators and peers beyond any one employer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="leg-06"></a>
##### LEG-06 — Intellectual property management

*Type:* Technical — Protect, register, and enforce trademarks, patents, copyrights, and trade secrets.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains IP records and prepares routine filings and renewals under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining IP records and preparing routine filings and renewals under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps a supervising IP lawyer accountable for prosecution decisions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard IP portfolios and prosecution tasks independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard IP portfolios and prosecution tasks independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's competence floor for recurring filing and renewal work. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Handles complex IP strategy, contested rights, and licensing questions autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Handling complex IP strategy, contested rights, and licensing questions autonomously moves beyond the WIPO Handbook's administrative-prosecution chapters into its enforcement and licensing chapters — Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO Intellectual Property Handbook: Policy, Law and Use, Second Edition.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs IP protection and enforcement strategies others adopt; resolves the hardest portfolio disputes.
  — *Why this level:* Designing IP protection and enforcement strategies other counsel adopt applies the WIPO Handbook's cross-jurisdictional enforcement guidance as an internal playbook, at SFIA level 5 accountability across the portfolio. *Sources:* World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO Intellectual Property Handbook: Policy, Law and Use, Second Edition; SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise IP strategy aligned to business value; anticipates shifts in IP law and risk.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise IP strategy aligned to business value and anticipating shifts in IP law is SFIA level 6 organizational influence applied to the treaty and policy landscape the WIPO Handbook maps. *Sources:* World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO Intellectual Property Handbook: Policy, Law and Use, Second Edition; SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines IP-management practice recognized across the field; externally cited authority.
  — *Why this level:* Being an externally cited IP authority is Dreyfus mastery exercised at the level the WIPO Handbook itself documents as shaping international IP policy and treaty development, not merely applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); World Intellectual Property Organization, WIPO Intellectual Property Handbook: Policy, Law and Use, Second Edition.

<a id="leg-07"></a>
##### LEG-07 — Employment & labor law advisory

*Type:* Technical — Advise on workforce legal matters including hiring, conduct, terminations, and labor relations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Researches employment questions and drafts routine policy and correspondence under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Researching employment questions and drafting routine correspondence under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps supervising counsel accountable for advice given. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Advises on standard employment matters and handles routine cases independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Advising on standard employment matters and handling routine cases independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's reasonable-preparation floor. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous, high-stakes employment disputes and complex workforce questions autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous, high-stakes employment disputes and complex workforce questions autonomously is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band — no case needs escalation for a first read. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines employment-risk frameworks and advisory approaches others adopt; solves the hardest cases.
  — *Why this level:* Defining employment-risk frameworks and advisory approaches other counsel adopt, and solving the hardest cases, is SFIA level 5 'Ensure, advise' — accountability across the workforce-risk portfolio. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise employment-law strategy; anticipates regulatory and workforce-law shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise employment-law strategy and anticipating regulatory and workforce-law shifts is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' — policy shaping ahead of case volume. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes employment-law practice industry-wide; externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping employment-law practice industry-wide is the Rule 1.1 commentary's 'lawyer of established competence in the field' ceiling, Dreyfus mastery recognized beyond any one employer. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).

#### Dispute & Litigation Management

<a id="leg-08"></a>
##### LEG-08 — Litigation & dispute management

*Type:* Technical — Manage litigation strategy, proceedings, and resolution of legal disputes and claims.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Supports litigation by preparing documents and tracking deadlines under close supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing documents and tracking deadlines under close supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps the supervising litigator accountable for strategy and filings. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine disputes and defined litigation tasks independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine disputes and defined litigation tasks independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's competence floor for recurring matter types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Drives complex, high-exposure litigation strategy and settlement decisions autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Driving complex, high-exposure litigation strategy and settlement decisions autonomously is Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band — the litigator others defer strategy calls to. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines dispute-strategy frameworks others adopt; resolves the most intractable, bet-the-company matters.
  — *Why this level:* Defining dispute-strategy frameworks other litigators adopt, and resolving the most intractable matters, is SFIA level 5 'Ensure, advise' — authoritative guidance across the docket. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise litigation strategy and risk appetite; anticipates emerging dispute exposures.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise litigation strategy and risk appetite, and anticipating emerging dispute exposures, is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' — org-wide policy, not one case. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines litigation-management practice recognized across the profession; externally credible authority.
  — *Why this level:* Being an externally credible litigation authority across the profession is Rule 1.1 commentary's 'lawyer of established competence in the field' ceiling — Dreyfus mastery recognized by peers and courts beyond one firm. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="leg-09"></a>
##### LEG-09 — Legal hold & evidence management

*Type:* Technical — Preserve, collect, and govern records and evidence in anticipation of proceedings.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Issues standard legal-hold notices and tracks acknowledgments under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Issuing standard hold notices and tracking acknowledgments under supervision covers only EDRM's identification and preservation stages under guidance — Dreyfus's novice band, rule-following without judgment on scope. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); EDRM, Electronic Discovery Reference Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages routine holds and evidence-preservation processes independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine holds and preservation processes independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, executing EDRM's preservation and collection stages for known-pattern matters without redesigning the process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); EDRM, Electronic Discovery Reference Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs and defends holds for complex, contested matters autonomously through ambiguity.
  — *Why this level:* Designing and defending holds for complex, contested matters autonomously through ambiguity means owning EDRM's information-governance-through-collection stages end to end — Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band. *Sources:* EDRM, Electronic Discovery Reference Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines preservation and collection methodologies others adopt; resolves spoliation-risk challenges.
  — *Why this level:* Defining preservation and collection methodologies other teams adopt, and resolving spoliation-risk challenges, is SFIA level 5 accountability applied across EDRM's full model rather than one matter's holds. *Sources:* EDRM, Electronic Discovery Reference Model (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise preservation strategy; anticipates evidentiary and regulatory shifts in discovery.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise preservation strategy and anticipating evidentiary and discovery shifts is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' — organization-wide policy ahead of any single hold. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines evidence-preservation best practice recognized across the field; externally cited authority.
  — *Why this level:* Defining evidence-preservation best practice recognized across the field is Dreyfus mastery exercised at the level EDRM's own framework was created at — shaping the reference model other practitioners apply, not applying it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); EDRM, Electronic Discovery Reference Model (accessed 2026-07).

#### Data Protection & Privacy

<a id="leg-10"></a>
##### LEG-10 — Data protection & privacy law

*Type:* Technical — Apply data protection and privacy legal requirements to the handling of personal information.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Researches privacy-law questions and completes routine assessments under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Researching privacy-law questions and completing routine assessments under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; GDPR Art. 38 keeps ultimate accountability with the designated DPO/supervising counsel at this stage. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Union, General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) (2016).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Advises on standard privacy matters and conducts routine assessments independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Advising on standard privacy matters and conducting routine assessments independently with normal review matches the practitioner tier IAPP's CIPP certification is built for — the advanced-beginner band applying settled law to recurring fact patterns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IAPP, Privacy Certification Programs: CIPP/CIPM/CIPT (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves ambiguous cross-jurisdictional privacy questions and complex processing autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving ambiguous cross-jurisdictional privacy questions and complex processing autonomously requires the accountability judgment GDPR Art. 5(2) assigns to the controller's own risk owner — Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band, beyond certified-practitioner routine work. *Sources:* European Union, General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) (2016); IAPP, Privacy Certification Programs: CIPP/CIPM/CIPT (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines privacy-law interpretation and risk frameworks others adopt; solves the hardest questions.
  — *Why this level:* Defining privacy-law interpretation and risk frameworks others adopt is the program-design competence IAPP's CIPM certification targets, at SFIA level 5 accountability across the organization's processing activities. *Sources:* IAPP, Privacy Certification Programs: CIPP/CIPM/CIPT (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise privacy-law strategy; anticipates regulatory and enforcement shifts ahead of peers.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise privacy-law strategy and anticipating enforcement shifts ahead of peers is SFIA level 6 organizational influence exercised over the accountability obligations GDPR Art. 5(2) places on the organization as a whole. *Sources:* European Union, General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) (2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes privacy-law practice and interpretation industry-wide; externally recognized authority.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping privacy-law practice and interpretation industry-wide is Dreyfus mastery exercised at the level regulators and courts cite when interpreting GDPR's principles — beyond applying the regulation to authoritatively defining how it is read. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); European Union, General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) (2016).

<a id="leg-11"></a>
##### LEG-11 — Privacy program management

*Type:* Technical — Operate the privacy governance program including rights handling, notices, and accountability.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains privacy-program records and supports defined controls under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining privacy-program records and supporting defined controls under supervision is the 'Partial' tier of the NIST Privacy Framework — ad hoc, individually executed activities — matching Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Operates standard privacy-program processes and assessments independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Operating standard privacy-program processes and assessments independently with normal review is the NIST Privacy Framework's 'Risk Informed' tier — approved but not yet organization-wide — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Runs a full privacy program through ambiguity and complex incidents autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Running a full privacy program through ambiguity and complex incidents autonomously is the NIST Privacy Framework's 'Repeatable' tier — formalized, organization-wide practice — Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band. *Sources:* NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs privacy-program architectures and operating models others adopt; resolves the hardest gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Designing privacy-program architectures and operating models other teams adopt is the NIST Privacy Framework's 'Adaptive' tier applied at SFIA level 5 accountability — practice that improves based on lessons learned and shares them elsewhere. *Sources:* NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise privacy-program strategy; anticipates regulatory and operational shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise privacy-program strategy and anticipating regulatory and operational shifts is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' operating at the Adaptive tier's outward-facing edge — proactive, not reactive to new obligations. *Sources:* NIST, NIST Privacy Framework: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management, Version 1.0 (2020); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines privacy-program best practice recognized across the field; externally credible authority.
  — *Why this level:* Defining privacy-program best practice recognized across the field is Dreyfus mastery at the level IAPP's certification bodies themselves draw on when updating the CIPM body of knowledge — externally credible beyond any one program. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); IAPP, Privacy Certification Programs: CIPP/CIPM/CIPT (accessed 2026-07).

#### Legal Operations & Advisory

<a id="leg-12"></a>
##### LEG-12 — Legal operations & matter management

*Type:* Technical — Run the legal function's intake, workflow, knowledge, and outside-counsel management.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks matters and maintains legal-ops records and reports under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking matters and maintaining legal-ops records under supervision sits in CLOC's 'Reactive' maturity stage — ad hoc execution — Dreyfus's novice band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Corporate Legal Operations Consortium (CLOC), Core 12 Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages standard matter-intake, vendor, and reporting processes independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard matter-intake, vendor, and reporting processes independently with normal review is CLOC's 'Emerging' maturity stage, the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band applying defined processes without redesigning them. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Corporate Legal Operations Consortium (CLOC), Core 12 Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Optimizes complex matter portfolios and resolves ambiguous operational issues autonomously.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing complex matter portfolios and resolving ambiguous operational issues autonomously is CLOC's 'Developing' maturity stage — Dreyfus's competent-to-proficient band, no escalation needed to adapt the process. *Sources:* Corporate Legal Operations Consortium (CLOC), Core 12 Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs legal-ops processes and metrics frameworks others adopt; solves the hardest operating problems.
  — *Why this level:* Designing legal-ops processes and metrics frameworks other teams adopt is CLOC's 'Leading' maturity stage across its Core 12 competencies, at SFIA level 5 accountability beyond one department's operations. *Sources:* Corporate Legal Operations Consortium (CLOC), Core 12 Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise legal-operations strategy; anticipates shifts in delivery models and tooling.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise legal-operations strategy and anticipating shifts in delivery models and tooling is SFIA level 6 'Initiate, influence' — organization-wide policy, not process execution. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines legal-operations best practice recognized across the profession; externally cited authority.
  — *Why this level:* Defining legal-operations best practice recognized across the profession is Dreyfus mastery exercised at the level CLOC's own Core 12 framework was built from — contributing to the field's reference model rather than climbing its maturity stages. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Corporate Legal Operations Consortium (CLOC), Core 12 Maturity Model (accessed 2026-07).

<a id="leg-13"></a>
##### LEG-13 — Legal advisory & business partnering

*Type:* Behavioral — Provide practical, risk-balanced legal guidance to business stakeholders on decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Answers routine business questions and escalates appropriately under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Answering routine business questions and escalating appropriately under supervision is Dreyfus's novice band; Rule 5.1/5.3 keeps the supervising lawyer accountable for advice on anything non-routine. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Advises business stakeholders on standard matters independently with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Advising business stakeholders on standard matters independently with normal review is the advanced-beginner band, meeting Rule 1.1's reasonable-preparation floor for recurring business questions. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); American Bar Association, Model Rules of Professional Conduct (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Provides decisive counsel on ambiguous, high-stakes business questions autonomously; the trusted go-to advisor.
