*Type:* Behavioral — Design, run, and continuously improve core business processes for efficiency and quality.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maps and documents existing process steps under guidance, flagging obvious bottlenecks for review.
  — *Why this level:* Mapping and documenting existing process steps under guidance, flagging obvious bottlenecks for review, is the novice band: following a defined mapping method without discretion over what to redesign. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs standard process improvements, gathering data and implementing routine fixes with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running standard process improvements -- identifying waste per Womack & Jones's value-stream mapping and implementing routine fixes with normal review -- is the advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Womack & Jones, Lean Thinking: Banish Waste and Create Wealth in Your Corporation (Simon & Schuster, 1996).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously redesigns ambiguous, cross-team processes end-to-end and sets the local standard for how work flows.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously redesigning ambiguous, cross-team processes end-to-end is the competent band -- Hammer & Champy's reengineering explicitly requires starting from a blank page rather than optimizing an existing flow, which is judgment with no fixed method to follow. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hammer & Champy, Reengineering the Corporation: A Manifesto for Business Revolution (HarperBusiness, 1993).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the improvement methodology others adopt and untangles processes others find intractable.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the improvement methodology other teams adopt and untangling processes others find intractable is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's redesign approach becomes the org's standard reengineering method. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hammer & Champy, Reengineering the Corporation: A Manifesto for Business Revolution (HarperBusiness, 1993).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets operational-excellence strategy across the business and anticipates where process capability must head next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting operational-excellence strategy across the business and anticipating where process capability must head next is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- enterprise-wide scope beyond any one process. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good operational practice means industry-wide and is sought externally for process expertise.
  — *Why this level:* Operational practice recognized industry-wide and sought externally -- the standing lean thinking achieved as a cross-industry management discipline beyond its Toyota origin -- is SFIA's top set-strategy level. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Womack & Jones, Lean Thinking: Banish Waste and Create Wealth in Your Corporation (Simon & Schuster, 1996).

<a id="biz-02"></a>
##### BIZ-02 — Operating model & organization design

*Type:* Behavioral — Structure functions, roles, and workflows to align operations with strategy.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Documents current roles, handoffs, and reporting lines under direction for a single team.
  — *Why this level:* Documenting current roles, handoffs, and reporting lines under direction for a single team is the novice band: recording a given structure without discretion over design choices. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently designs structure for one function, clarifying routine roles and decision rights with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently designing structure for one function, clarifying routine roles and decision rights with review, is the advanced-beginner band -- applying Galbraith's Star Model dimensions to a bounded, single-function redesign. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kates & Galbraith, Designing Your Organization: Using the STAR Model to Solve 5 Critical Design Challenges (Jossey-Bass, 2007).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously designs operating models for ambiguous multi-function areas, resolving overlap and accountability gaps.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously designing operating models for ambiguous multi-function areas, resolving overlap and accountability gaps, is the competent band -- Nadler & Tushman's architecture-design judgment across units has no template, unlike single-function structuring. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nadler, Tushman & Nadler, Competing by Design: The Power of Organizational Architecture (Oxford University Press, 1997).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines org-design approaches others follow and solves structural problems that have stumped leadership.
  — *Why this level:* Defining org-design approaches other designers follow and solving structural problems that have stumped leadership is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's application of the Star Model becomes the org's design method. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kates & Galbraith, Designing Your Organization: Using the STAR Model to Solve 5 Critical Design Challenges (Jossey-Bass, 2007).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise operating-model strategy and anticipates structural shifts the organization will need.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise operating-model strategy and anticipating structural shifts the organization will need is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- enterprise-wide design authority, not one function. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline conceives operating models and is externally recognized for the craft.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the discipline conceives operating models, externally recognized for the craft, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing organizational-architecture scholarship achieves as a field reference. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nadler, Tushman & Nadler, Competing by Design: The Power of Organizational Architecture (Oxford University Press, 1997).

<a id="biz-03"></a>
##### BIZ-03 — Cross-functional initiative leadership

*Type:* Behavioral — Drive complex initiatives spanning multiple functions toward shared operational outcomes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Coordinates tasks and tracks actions for a small initiative under a lead's guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Coordinating tasks and tracking actions for a small initiative under a lead's guidance is the novice band: executing defined coordination tasks with no discretion over how the initiative is run. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs a defined cross-team initiative, managing routine dependencies and stakeholders with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running a defined cross-team initiative, managing routine dependencies and stakeholders with review, is the advanced-beginner band -- applying PMBOK's standard performance domains to a bounded initiative. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously leads ambiguous, contentious initiatives spanning many functions to landed outcomes.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously leading ambiguous, contentious initiatives spanning many functions to landed outcomes is the competent band -- Bossidy & Charan's execution discipline is precisely the judgment-under-resistance that a defined project plan doesn't supply. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bossidy, Charan & Burck, Execution: The Discipline of Getting Things Done (Crown Business, 2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines how complex initiatives are run here and rescues efforts others cannot move.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how complex initiatives are run and rescuing efforts others cannot move is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's execution approach becomes the org's method, beyond running any one initiative well. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bossidy, Charan & Burck, Execution: The Discipline of Getting Things Done (Crown Business, 2002).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the strategy and operating cadence for the organization's most critical cross-functional bets.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the strategy and operating cadence for the organization's most critical cross-functional bets is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- portfolio-wide authority over which initiatives matter and how they run. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry-leading practice for cross-functional execution and is sought externally to teach it.
  — *Why this level:* Industry-leading practice for cross-functional execution, sought externally to teach it, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing a body of knowledge like PMBOK achieves as the field's shared standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).

#### Revenue & GTM Operations

<a id="biz-04"></a>
##### BIZ-04 — Revenue operations & go-to-market systems

*Type:* Technical — Design and orchestrate end-to-end revenue processes across marketing, sales, and service.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures simple GTM workflow and field changes under supervision, following established conventions.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring simple GTM workflow and field changes under supervision, following established conventions, is the novice band: executing defined configuration tasks without discretion over system design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds and maintains standard revenue workflows and integrations with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building and maintaining standard revenue workflows and integrations with normal review is the advanced-beginner band -- correctly implementing known building blocks of the revenue stack per Diorio & Hummel's systems model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Diorio & Hummel, Revenue Operations: A New Way to Align Sales & Marketing, Monetize Data, and Ignite Growth (Wiley, 2022).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously designs end-to-end GTM system architecture across marketing, sales, and success, handling messy edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously designing end-to-end GTM system architecture across marketing, sales, and success, handling messy edge cases, is the competent band -- Diorio & Hummel's nine-building-block system requires connecting the whole stack, not implementing one workflow, which has no fixed template for a given org's edge cases. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Diorio & Hummel, Revenue Operations: A New Way to Align Sales & Marketing, Monetize Data, and Ignite Growth (Wiley, 2022).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the revenue-systems blueprint others adopt and solves integration problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the revenue-systems blueprint others adopt and solving integration problems others can't is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's architecture becomes the org's RevOps standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Diorio & Hummel, Revenue Operations: A New Way to Align Sales & Marketing, Monetize Data, and Ignite Growth (Wiley, 2022).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets RevOps systems strategy and anticipates how the GTM tech stack must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting RevOps systems strategy and anticipating how the GTM tech stack must evolve is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- enterprise-wide authority over the whole revenue system, not one integration. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good revenue operations looks like for the field and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good revenue operations looks like for the field and being externally credible on it is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing RevOps has achieved as a named discipline with its own literature and practitioner community. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Diorio & Hummel, Revenue Operations: A New Way to Align Sales & Marketing, Monetize Data, and Ignite Growth (Wiley, 2022).

<a id="biz-05"></a>
##### BIZ-05 — Revenue operations analytics

*Type:* Technical — Measure pipeline, conversion, and retention to optimize revenue performance and efficiency.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Pulls standard pipeline and funnel reports under guidance, checking figures before sharing.
  — *Why this level:* Pulling standard pipeline and funnel reports under guidance, checking figures before sharing, is the novice band: executing a defined reporting task without discretion over which metrics matter. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds routine revenue analyses and dashboards, explaining trends with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently building routine revenue analyses and dashboards, explaining trends with normal review, is the advanced-beginner band -- correctly computing and reporting Skok's standard SaaS metrics (CAC, LTV, churn) rather than defining new ones. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Skok, SaaS Metrics 2.0 -- A Guide to Measuring and Improving What Matters (forEntrepreneurs.com, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously models ambiguous revenue questions end-to-end and becomes the trusted source for GTM numbers.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously modeling ambiguous revenue questions end-to-end and becoming the trusted source for GTM numbers is the competent band -- deciding which of Skok's metric framework applies to a novel revenue question, and defending the model, has no fixed procedure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Skok, SaaS Metrics 2.0 -- A Guide to Measuring and Improving What Matters (forEntrepreneurs.com, 2013).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the analytical frameworks and metric definitions others adopt across revenue teams.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the analytical frameworks and metric definitions other revenue teams adopt is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's metric definitions become the org's standard, the same role Skok's own framework plays industry-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skok, SaaS Metrics 2.0 -- A Guide to Measuring and Improving What Matters (forEntrepreneurs.com, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets revenue-analytics strategy and anticipates which signals will drive future growth decisions.
  — *Why this level:* Setting revenue-analytics strategy and anticipating which signals will drive future growth decisions is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- authority over the whole measurement system, not one dashboard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline measures revenue performance and is recognized externally for the methods.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the discipline measures revenue performance, recognized externally for the methods, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing Skok's SaaS Metrics framework achieved as the field's reference vocabulary for revenue measurement. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Skok, SaaS Metrics 2.0 -- A Guide to Measuring and Improving What Matters (forEntrepreneurs.com, 2013).

<a id="biz-06"></a>
##### BIZ-06 — Pricing, deal & monetization operations

*Type:* Technical — Operationalize pricing, quoting, and deal processes to maximize realized revenue.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Processes standard deal desk requests and applies approved discount rules under review.
  — *Why this level:* Processing standard deal desk requests and applying approved discount rules under review is the novice band: executing given rules without discretion over pricing judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages routine pricing approvals and deal structuring within set guardrails.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing routine pricing approvals and deal structuring within set guardrails is the advanced-beginner band -- applying Nagle, Hogan & Zale's value-based pricing policy correctly to a standard deal, not setting the policy. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nagle, Hogan & Zale, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 6th Edition (Routledge, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously structures complex, non-standard deals and sets local norms for monetization mechanics.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously structuring complex, non-standard deals and setting local norms for monetization mechanics is the competent band -- Nagle, Hogan & Zale's pricing-policy layer exists precisely because non-standard deals require judgment a price list can't encode. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nagle, Hogan & Zale, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 6th Edition (Routledge, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines deal-desk and monetization approaches others follow and cracks pricing problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining deal-desk and monetization approaches others follow and cracking pricing problems others can't is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's pricing policy becomes the org's method, beyond applying value-based pricing well. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nagle, Hogan & Zale, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 6th Edition (Routledge, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets monetization and pricing-operations strategy and anticipates shifts in how value is captured.
  — *Why this level:* Setting monetization and pricing-operations strategy and anticipating shifts in how value is captured is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- enterprise-wide pricing authority, not one deal. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for pricing operations across the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Leading practice for pricing operations across the field, sought externally for it, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing Nagle's value-based pricing framework achieved across decades of editions as the discipline's core text. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nagle, Hogan & Zale, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing: A Guide to Growing More Profitably, 6th Edition (Routledge, 2016).

#### Planning & Performance

<a id="biz-07"></a>
##### BIZ-07 — Forecasting & planning operations

*Type:* Technical — Run cyclical forecasting and planning processes to align targets, capacity, and resources.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates forecast inputs and assembles planning templates under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Updating forecast inputs and assembling planning templates under guidance is the novice band: populating a given template without discretion over forecasting method. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently produces standard forecasts and plans, reconciling routine variances with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently producing standard forecasts and plans, reconciling routine variances with review, is the advanced-beginner band -- running a defined forecast cycle correctly, not yet questioning whether the cycle itself fits the business. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hope & Fraser, Beyond Budgeting: How Managers Can Break Free from the Annual Performance Trap (Harvard Business School Press, 2003).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously builds forecasting models for ambiguous situations and owns the planning cadence end-to-end.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously building forecasting models for ambiguous situations and owning the planning cadence end-to-end is the competent band -- Hope & Fraser's central claim is that rigid annual budgeting fails precisely where judgment must replace the fixed cycle, which is the P2-to-P3 boundary. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hope & Fraser, Beyond Budgeting: How Managers Can Break Free from the Annual Performance Trap (Harvard Business School Press, 2003).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the forecasting methodology others adopt and resolves planning problems others cannot.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the forecasting methodology others adopt and resolving planning problems others cannot is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's adaptive planning approach becomes the org's method, echoing Hope & Fraser's beyond-budgeting model being adopted org-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hope & Fraser, Beyond Budgeting: How Managers Can Break Free from the Annual Performance Trap (Harvard Business School Press, 2003).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise planning strategy and anticipates the dynamics future forecasts must capture.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise planning strategy and anticipating the dynamics future forecasts must capture is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- authority over the whole planning system, not one cycle. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-in-class forecasting practice for the discipline and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Best-in-class forecasting practice recognized externally is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing the Beyond Budgeting Round Table achieved as a cross-industry reference model for planning practice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hope & Fraser, Beyond Budgeting: How Managers Can Break Free from the Annual Performance Trap (Harvard Business School Press, 2003).

<a id="biz-08"></a>
##### BIZ-08 — Operational analytics & business intelligence

*Type:* Technical — Turn operational data into reporting and insight that drives business decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds basic reports and dashboards from defined requirements under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Building basic reports and dashboards from defined requirements under supervision is the novice band: executing a given spec without discretion over what to measure. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently delivers standard BI analyses and self-serve dashboards with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently delivering standard BI analyses and self-serve dashboards with normal review is the advanced-beginner band -- correctly building on Kimball's dimensional-modeling conventions rather than defining new semantic structures. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously frames ambiguous business questions and builds the analytics the organization relies on.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously framing ambiguous business questions and building the analytics the organization relies on is the competent band -- Davenport & Harris's stage model shows this is where an org moves past reporting into analytics that actually answers undefined questions, requiring judgment no dashboard spec supplies. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Davenport & Harris, Competing on Analytics: The New Science of Winning (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines BI standards, semantic models, and methods others adopt across the business.
  — *Why this level:* Defining BI standards, semantic models, and methods others adopt across the business is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's schema and metric definitions become the org's standard, the role Kimball's dimensional-modeling method plays industry-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Kimball & Ross, The Data Warehouse Toolkit: The Definitive Guide to Dimensional Modeling, 3rd Edition (Wiley, 2013).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the operational-analytics strategy and anticipates the decisions data must soon support.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the operational-analytics strategy and anticipating the decisions data must soon support is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- Davenport & Harris's higher maturity stages describe exactly this org-wide anticipatory analytics posture. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Davenport & Harris, Competing on Analytics: The New Science of Winning (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline practices business intelligence and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the discipline practices business intelligence, externally credible on it, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing Davenport & Harris's analytical-competitor model achieved as the field's reference framework. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Davenport & Harris, Competing on Analytics: The New Science of Winning (Harvard Business School Press, 2007).

#### Data & Systems Operations

<a id="biz-09"></a>
##### BIZ-09 — Operational data governance & quality

*Type:* Technical — Steward the integrity, definitions, and quality of operational data across systems.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs defined data cleanup and quality checks under guidance, escalating anomalies.
  — *Why this level:* Performing defined data cleanup and quality checks under guidance, escalating anomalies, is the novice band: executing given quality rules without discretion over what quality requires here. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently maintains data standards and resolves routine quality issues with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently maintaining data standards and resolving routine quality issues with review is the advanced-beginner band -- applying Redman's quality dimensions (accuracy, completeness, timeliness) to known issue types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Redman, Data Quality for the Information Age (Artech House, 1996).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously designs governance and quality controls for ambiguous, messy data domains.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously designing governance and quality controls for ambiguous, messy data domains is the competent band -- DAMA-DMBOK's stewardship function requires designing controls for domains with no established rulebook, unlike applying Redman's known dimensions to a defined issue. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the governance framework others adopt and remediates data problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the governance framework others adopt and remediating data problems others can't is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's stewardship model becomes the org's DAMA-DMBOK-aligned standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise data-governance strategy and anticipates emerging quality and stewardship needs.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise data-governance strategy and anticipating emerging quality and stewardship needs is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- authority over the whole governance program, not one domain. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good operational data governance means for the field and is externally recognized.
  — *Why this level:* What good operational data governance means for the field, externally recognized, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing DAMA-DMBOK itself achieved as the discipline's body-of-knowledge reference. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge, 2nd Edition (Technics Publications, 2017).

<a id="biz-10"></a>
##### BIZ-10 — Business systems & workflow administration

*Type:* Technical — Configure and maintain business systems and automated workflows that run operations.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs routine system configuration and user support tasks under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Performing routine system configuration and user support tasks under supervision is the novice band: executing defined configuration steps without discretion over system design. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently administers business systems and builds standard workflows with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently administering business systems and building standard workflows with normal review is the advanced-beginner band -- correctly following ITIL 4's service-request and change-enablement practices for known request types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (TSO/AXELOS, 2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously designs complex automations and system configurations, handling tricky edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Autonomously designing complex automations and system configurations, handling tricky edge cases, is the competent band -- ITIL 4's value-stream design requires judgment for cases the standard practices don't script, unlike routine service requests. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (TSO/AXELOS, 2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines administration standards and architecture others adopt and fixes what others cannot.
  — *Why this level:* Defining administration standards and architecture others adopt and fixing what others cannot is SFIA's ensure/advise level -- the practitioner's system design becomes the org's operating standard, beyond running ITIL practices well. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (TSO/AXELOS, 2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets business-systems strategy and anticipates how the workflow platform landscape must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting business-systems strategy and anticipating how the workflow platform landscape must evolve is SFIA's initiate/influence level -- enterprise-wide platform authority, not one system. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading practice for business-systems administration and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Leading practice for business-systems administration, sought externally for it, is SFIA's top set-strategy level -- the standing ITSM frameworks like ITIL achieve as the field's shared standard, adopted and taught worldwide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (TSO/AXELOS, 2019).

### Program & Portfolio Management (PPM)

#### Portfolio Governance

<a id="ppm-01"></a>
##### PPM-01 — Portfolio prioritization & governance

*Type:* Behavioral — Select, sequence, and govern the enterprise portfolio to align investment with strategy.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains the portfolio inventory and prepares governance materials under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining the inventory and prepping governance materials under direction is Dreyfus's novice band -- explicit rules, no independent judgment on governance calls yet. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs routine intake and prioritization scoring within an established framework.
  — *Why this level:* Running intake and scoring independently inside a fixed framework is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band and SFIA Level 3 Apply -- situational judgment stays inside guardrails set by others. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously facilitates contentious prioritization and sets local governance standards across the portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Facilitating contentious prioritization and setting local governance rules autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band; PMI's Standard for Portfolio Management treats governance-model choice as a portfolio-manager judgment call, not a scripted intake step. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the prioritization and governance model others adopt and resolves the toughest trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the prioritization/governance model other portfolio owners adopt is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the framework PMI's standard describes rather than applying someone else's. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise portfolio-governance strategy and anticipates shifts in investment priorities.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise portfolio-governance strategy and anticipating investment shifts matches SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- governance choices now shape strategy across the whole investment portfolio, the top scope band PMI's standard describes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice portfolio governance for the discipline and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice portfolio governance for the discipline and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- the practitioner now operates at the level that writes standards like PMI's rather than following them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).

<a id="ppm-02"></a>
##### PPM-02 — Benefits realization & value tracking

*Type:* Technical — Define, track, and verify the benefits and value delivered by portfolio investments.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records benefit measures and tracks realization against plan under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Recording benefit measures and tracking against plan under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band: applying a prescribed tracking template, no interpretation of ambiguous value claims yet. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently monitors benefits and reports realization, flagging routine shortfalls with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently monitoring benefits and flagging routine shortfalls under review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band / SFIA Level 3 Apply -- recognizing common shortfall patterns without owning the value case. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously defines value cases for ambiguous initiatives and owns realization tracking end-to-end.
  — *Why this level:* Defining value cases for ambiguous initiatives and owning realization end-to-end is the Dreyfus competent band; PMI's Benefits Realization Management guide places case-authorship and life-cycle ownership at the practitioner-autonomy tier, not the reporting-only tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, Benefits Realization Management: A Practice Guide (2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the benefits-realization methodology others adopt and salvages value others miss.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the benefits-realization methodology other teams adopt, and salvaging value others miss, is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the life-cycle model PMI's guide describes rather than executing someone else's. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, Benefits Realization Management: A Practice Guide (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise value-tracking strategy and anticipates how benefits should be measured next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise value-tracking strategy and anticipating how benefits should be measured next is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- scope moves from a single value case to how the whole enterprise measures value. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, Benefits Realization Management: A Practice Guide (2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading benefits-realization practice for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading benefits-realization practice for the field and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the authorship tier that produces guidance like PMI's, not the tier that consumes it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, Benefits Realization Management: A Practice Guide (2019).

<a id="ppm-03"></a>
##### PPM-03 — Portfolio reporting & performance analytics

*Type:* Technical — Aggregate portfolio health, progress, and risk into insight for executive decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Compiles status data into standard portfolio reports under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Compiling status data into standard reports under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- following a fixed reporting template with no interpretive judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently produces routine portfolio dashboards and performance summaries with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently producing routine dashboards and summaries with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band / SFIA Level 3 Apply -- the format is given, the analyst fills it in. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously builds analytics that surface portfolio risks and becomes the trusted reporting source.
  — *Why this level:* Building analytics that surface portfolio risk and becoming the trusted reporting source autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band; PMI's Standard for Portfolio Management treats performance-signal design as portfolio-manager judgment, beyond filling a template. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines portfolio-reporting standards and metrics others adopt across programs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining portfolio-reporting standards and metrics others adopt across programs is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now sets the measurement system, echoing how EIA-748 fixes the 32 EVMS criteria programs must report against rather than reporting to someone else's criteria. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NDIA/SAE International, EIA-748 Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) Standard, Revision D (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets portfolio-analytics strategy and anticipates the signals leadership will need to steer.
  — *Why this level:* Setting portfolio-analytics strategy and anticipating what signals leadership will need next is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- analytics choices now shape enterprise decision-making, the top scope PMI's standard addresses. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Shapes how the discipline reports portfolio performance and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Shaping how the discipline reports portfolio performance and being externally credible on it is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- the practitioner now operates at the standard-writing tier, not the standard-following tier. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).

#### Program Delivery

<a id="ppm-04"></a>
##### PPM-04 — Program & dependency management (enterprise)

*Type:* Behavioral — Coordinate interrelated programs and cross-program dependencies toward strategic outcomes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Tracks program tasks and logs cross-team dependencies under a manager's direction.
  — *Why this level:* Tracking program tasks and logging cross-team dependencies under a manager's direction is the Dreyfus novice band -- recording, not resolving, dependency conflicts. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs a defined program, managing routine dependencies and milestones with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently running a defined program and managing routine dependencies with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band / SFIA Level 3 Apply -- one program, standard milestone patterns. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously orchestrates large enterprise programs, resolving tangled cross-program dependencies.
  — *Why this level:* Orchestrating large enterprise programs and resolving tangled cross-program dependencies autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band; PMI's Standard for Program Management scopes this exact multi-project coordination as program-manager-level work, distinct from single-project delivery. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines how enterprise programs are run here and untangles dependency knots others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining how enterprise programs are run and untangling dependency knots others can't is SFIA Level 5/6 territory -- the practitioner now authors the coordination model PMI's program standard formalizes, rather than following it inside one program. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise program-management strategy and anticipates systemic delivery constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise program-management strategy and anticipating systemic delivery constraints is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- scope expands from one program's dependencies to the delivery system's structural constraints. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-in-class enterprise program management and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-in-class enterprise program management and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the standard-body-adjacent tier that shapes practice PMI's standard itself codifies. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017).

<a id="ppm-05"></a>
##### PPM-05 — Project delivery methods & standards

*Type:* Technical — Establish and steward delivery methodologies, standards, and practices across the enterprise.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Applies prescribed delivery methods and templates to tasks under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Applying prescribed delivery methods and templates under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- following PMBOK-style process groups by the book, no method-selection judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently delivers standard projects using established methods with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently delivering standard projects using established methods with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; PMBOK 7 principles are applied as given, not adapted. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously tailors delivery methods to ambiguous projects and sets the local standard.
  — *Why this level:* Tailoring delivery methods to ambiguous projects and setting the local standard autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- PMBOK 7's performance-domain model explicitly expects practitioners to tailor its principles to context rather than follow one prescribed process. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the delivery methodology and standards others across teams adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the delivery methodology and standards other teams adopt is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the tailoring PMBOK 7 only frames as a principle, turning it into a concrete adopted standard. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's delivery-method strategy and anticipates where practice must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting the organization's delivery-method strategy and anticipating where practice must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- method choice now shapes the whole delivery organization, not one team's tailoring. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good delivery practice means for the discipline and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good delivery practice means for the discipline and being externally credible is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- the practitioner operates at the tier that writes standards like PMBOK, not the tier that applies them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), 7th ed. (PMI, 2021).

<a id="ppm-06"></a>
##### PPM-06 — Program risk, issue & quality assurance

*Type:* Technical — Assure program quality and manage risks and issues across the delivery portfolio.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Logs risks and issues and updates the register under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Logging risks and issues and updating the register under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- mechanical register maintenance, no risk-treatment judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages routine risks, issues, and QA reviews with normal oversight.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine risks, issues, and QA reviews independently with normal oversight is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band; ISO 31000's identify-analyze-evaluate-treat process is executed as a standard cycle, not adapted. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously runs risk and assurance for complex programs, surfacing what others overlook.
  — *Why this level:* Running risk and assurance for complex programs and surfacing what others overlook autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- ISO 31000 frames risk identification and evaluation as requiring embedded judgment at this level, beyond registering known risks. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the risk and quality-assurance approach others adopt and resolves systemic exposures.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the risk and quality-assurance approach others adopt and resolving systemic exposures is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now designs the risk framework ISO 31000 leaves organization-specific, for others to follow. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise program-assurance strategy and anticipates emerging delivery risks.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise program-assurance strategy and anticipating emerging delivery risks is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- ISO 31000's principle of embedding risk management into governance and strategy now operates at enterprise scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading program-assurance practice for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading program-assurance practice for the field and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- the practitioner now shapes risk practice at the tier ISO's standard-setting committees occupy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO, ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management - Guidelines.

#### Resource & Financial Control

<a id="ppm-07"></a>
##### PPM-07 — Resource & capacity management (portfolio)

*Type:* Technical — Balance demand against people and capacity across the portfolio to optimize throughput.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates resource allocations and availability data under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Updating resource allocations and availability data under direction is the Dreyfus novice band -- data entry against a plan someone else built. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages routine resourcing and capacity plans across a few programs with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently managing routine resourcing and capacity plans across a few programs with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band / SFIA Level 3 Apply -- standard allocation rules, limited scope. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously balances contended capacity across the portfolio, resolving conflicts and bottlenecks.
  — *Why this level:* Balancing contended capacity across the portfolio and resolving conflicts autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band; PMI's Standard for Portfolio Management names capacity management as a core governance domain requiring judgment across competing programs, not single-program allocation. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the capacity-planning approach others adopt and solves the hardest allocation trade-offs.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the capacity-planning approach others adopt and solving the hardest allocation trade-offs is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- this is the buffer-management and resource-leveling authorship Goldratt's Critical Chain describes as the project/portfolio manager's design decision, not a rule others hand you. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Goldratt, Critical Chain (North River Press, 1997).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets portfolio resource strategy and anticipates future capacity and skills constraints.
  — *Why this level:* Setting portfolio resource strategy and anticipating future capacity and skills constraints is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- capacity decisions now shape the enterprise portfolio's investment strategy, PMI's standard's top scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Portfolio Management, 4th Edition (2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice portfolio capacity management and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice portfolio capacity management and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- the practitioner now originates capacity-management theory at the tier Goldratt's own contribution occupies, not applying it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Goldratt, Critical Chain (North River Press, 1997).

<a id="ppm-08"></a>
##### PPM-08 — Program financial management & cost control

*Type:* Technical — Plan, track, and control program budgets, costs, and financial performance to baseline.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records program costs and updates budget trackers under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Recording program costs and updating budget trackers under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- data capture against a baseline set by others. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages a program budget, tracking spend and routine variances with review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing a program budget independently and tracking spend/routine variances with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- EIA-748's cost/schedule variance reporting is executed as designed, not customized. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NDIA/SAE International, EIA-748 Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) Standard, Revision D (2019).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously controls complex program finances, forecasting and resolving ambiguous cost issues.
  — *Why this level:* Controlling complex program finances and resolving ambiguous cost issues autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- EIA-748 expects the program's EVMS implementation to be scaled and interpreted by the practitioner to the program's needs at this tier. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); NDIA/SAE International, EIA-748 Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) Standard, Revision D (2019).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines program financial-control practices others adopt and recovers troubled budgets others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining program financial-control practices others adopt and recovering troubled budgets others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now designs the EVMS implementation EIA-748 leaves organization-specific. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NDIA/SAE International, EIA-748 Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) Standard, Revision D (2019).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise program-finance strategy and anticipates cost and funding pressures ahead.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise program-finance strategy and anticipating cost and funding pressures ahead is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- financial-control judgment now spans the program portfolio PMI's program standard scopes. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Project Management Institute, The Standard for Program Management, 4th ed. (PMI, 2017).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading program financial-management practice and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading program financial-management practice and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the standards-committee tier that revises EIA-748 itself, not the tier that implements it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NDIA/SAE International, EIA-748 Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) Standard, Revision D (2019).

### Operations & Supply Chain (SCM)

#### Planning & Demand

<a id="scm-01"></a>
##### SCM-01 — Demand planning & forecasting

*Type:* Technical — Predict demand using historical, market, and statistical signals to drive supply decisions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Maintains demand data and runs standard forecast updates under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining demand data and running standard forecast updates under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- executing a fixed forecast model, no interpretation of demand signals. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently produces routine demand forecasts and adjusts for known seasonality with review.
  — *Why this level:* Independently producing routine forecasts and adjusting for known seasonality with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- the SCOR Plan process's standard demand-planning sub-steps are followed as designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously forecasts volatile, ambiguous demand and owns the forecasting process end-to-end.
  — *Why this level:* Forecasting volatile, ambiguous demand and owning the process end-to-end autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- SCOR's Plan process assumes practitioner judgment to reconcile conflicting demand signals at this tier, not just running a model. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the demand-planning methodology others adopt and forecasts what others can't model.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the demand-planning methodology others adopt and forecasting what others can't model is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- Chopra & Meindl treat forecasting-method selection and error-driven safety-stock design as the senior planner's authored decision, not a fixed procedure. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets demand-planning strategy and anticipates shifts in market and demand signals.
  — *Why this level:* Setting demand-planning strategy and anticipating shifts in market signals is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- scope moves from one forecast cycle to how the whole supply chain's Plan process should be built. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-in-class demand planning for the discipline and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-in-class demand planning for the discipline and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the ASCM-standards-committee tier that writes the SCOR Plan process, not the tier that runs it. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.

<a id="scm-02"></a>
##### SCM-02 — Supply & capacity planning

*Type:* Technical — Balance supply, capacity, and constraints against demand to create executable plans.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates supply and capacity plans from given inputs under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Updating supply and capacity plans from given inputs under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- transcribing numbers into a plan someone else designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds routine supply plans, balancing standard constraints with review.
  — *Why this level:* Building routine supply plans and balancing standard constraints independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Orlicky's MRP time-phasing logic is executed as specified, not adapted. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Orlicky, Material Requirements Planning: The New Way of Life in Production and Inventory Management (McGraw-Hill, 1975).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously plans supply under ambiguous constraints, resolving shortages and bottlenecks.
  — *Why this level:* Planning supply under ambiguous constraints and resolving shortages/bottlenecks autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Orlicky's MRP framework requires the planner to interpret and override system-generated plans exactly when constraints get ambiguous, the behavior this level names. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Orlicky, Material Requirements Planning: The New Way of Life in Production and Inventory Management (McGraw-Hill, 1975).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the supply-planning approach others adopt and solves constraint problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the supply-planning approach others adopt and solving constraint problems others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the Plan/Source/Make coordination SCOR describes as a process-design choice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets supply and capacity strategy and anticipates structural capacity needs ahead.
  — *Why this level:* Setting supply and capacity strategy and anticipating structural capacity needs ahead is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- planning judgment now spans the SCOR model's full network, not one plan cycle. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading supply-planning practice for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading supply-planning practice for the field and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the tier that originated MRP as a discipline, the position Orlicky's own book occupies. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Orlicky, Material Requirements Planning: The New Way of Life in Production and Inventory Management (McGraw-Hill, 1975).

<a id="scm-03"></a>
##### SCM-03 — Sales & operations planning

*Type:* Behavioral — Align commercial, financial, and operational plans through cross-functional consensus.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares S&OP inputs and meeting materials under direction.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing S&OP inputs and meeting materials under direction is the Dreyfus novice band -- assembling data for a process someone else runs. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs routine S&OP cycles, reconciling standard supply-demand gaps with review.
  — *Why this level:* Running routine S&OP cycles and reconciling standard supply-demand gaps independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Wallace & Stahl's standard monthly cycle is executed as designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wallace & Stahl, Sales and Operations Planning: The How-To Handbook, 3rd Edition (T.F. Wallace & Co., 2004).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously facilitates contentious S&OP, balancing trade-offs across functions to consensus.
  — *Why this level:* Facilitating contentious S&OP and balancing cross-functional trade-offs to consensus autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Wallace & Stahl place executive-consensus facilitation, not cycle mechanics, as the differentiator of a mature S&OP practitioner. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Wallace & Stahl, Sales and Operations Planning: The How-To Handbook, 3rd Edition (T.F. Wallace & Co., 2004).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the S&OP process others adopt and reconciles imbalances others cannot.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the S&OP process others adopt and reconciling imbalances others cannot is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now designs the cycle Wallace & Stahl's handbook describes as an implementation choice, not runs an existing one. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wallace & Stahl, Sales and Operations Planning: The How-To Handbook, 3rd Edition (T.F. Wallace & Co., 2004).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise S&OP strategy and anticipates the integrated-planning capabilities needed next.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise S&OP strategy and anticipating the integrated-planning capabilities needed next is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- S&OP design decisions now shape the whole enterprise's planning-maturity path. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wallace & Stahl, Sales and Operations Planning: The How-To Handbook, 3rd Edition (T.F. Wallace & Co., 2004).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice sales and operations planning and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice sales and operations planning and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the practice-authoring tier the S&OP handbook's own authors occupy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Wallace & Stahl, Sales and Operations Planning: The How-To Handbook, 3rd Edition (T.F. Wallace & Co., 2004).

<a id="scm-04"></a>
##### SCM-04 — Supply chain network design

*Type:* Technical — Model and optimize facility and route structure to balance cost, service, and risk.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Gathers network data and runs predefined scenario models under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Gathering network data and running predefined scenario models under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- operating someone else's model, not designing scenarios. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently models standard network changes and evaluates routine trade-offs with review.
  — *Why this level:* Modeling standard network changes and evaluating routine trade-offs independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Chopra & Meindl's facility-location trade-off framework is applied to known scenario types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously designs network configurations for ambiguous, multi-constraint problems end-to-end.
  — *Why this level:* Designing network configurations for ambiguous, multi-constraint problems end-to-end autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Chopra & Meindl frame network design as balancing responsiveness against efficiency under genuine uncertainty, the judgment this level names. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines network-design methods others adopt and solves optimization problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining network-design methods others adopt and solving optimization problems others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the driver framework (facilities, inventory, transportation) Chopra & Meindl present as a design toolkit for others to apply. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets supply-chain network strategy and anticipates how the footprint must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting supply-chain network strategy and anticipating how the footprint must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- network judgment now shapes long-horizon enterprise footprint strategy, not one redesign project. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading network-design practice for the discipline and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading network-design practice for the discipline and being externally credible is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the academic/practice-authoring tier the textbook's own framework represents. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).

#### Inventory & Materials

<a id="scm-05"></a>
##### SCM-05 — Inventory & materials management

*Type:* Technical — Plan, position, and control stock and material flows to meet service targets at optimal cost.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records stock movements and performs counts under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Recording stock movements and performing counts under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- mechanical data capture, no reorder-policy judgment. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages routine inventory levels and replenishment with normal review.
