  — *Why this level:* Managing routine inventory levels and replenishment independently with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- a fixed EOQ-style reorder rule is applied as calculated, not re-derived. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Harris, How Many Parts to Make at Once, Factory: The Magazine of Management 10, 135-136 (1913).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously optimizes inventory policy under ambiguous demand and supply variability.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing inventory policy under ambiguous demand and supply variability autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Harris's EOQ model only holds under stable assumptions, so applying it under real variability requires the judgment this level names, beyond mechanical formula use. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Harris, How Many Parts to Make at Once, Factory: The Magazine of Management 10, 135-136 (1913).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines inventory-management methods others adopt and resolves chronic stock problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining inventory-management methods others adopt and resolving chronic stock problems others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the inventory-positioning policy SCOR's Source/Make processes leave organization-specific. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets inventory strategy and anticipates how stocking and materials needs will shift.
  — *Why this level:* Setting inventory strategy and anticipating how stocking needs will shift is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- inventory judgment now spans the whole supply chain's stocking strategy, not one SKU's reorder point. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice inventory management for the field and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice inventory management for the field and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the origin-theory tier Harris's own 1913 formulation occupies, still the textbook baseline a century later. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Harris, How Many Parts to Make at Once, Factory: The Magazine of Management 10, 135-136 (1913).

<a id="scm-06"></a>
##### SCM-06 — Warehousing & storage operations

*Type:* Technical — Manage receiving, storage, picking, and handling for accuracy, safety, and throughput.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs defined put-away, picking, and storage tasks under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Performing defined put-away, picking, and storage tasks under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- following a fixed slotting plan, not designing one. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs routine warehouse operations and standard slotting with review.
  — *Why this level:* Running routine warehouse operations and standard slotting independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Frazelle's standard slotting and pick-path methods are applied as documented. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Frazelle, World-Class Warehousing and Material Handling (McGraw-Hill, 2002).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously optimizes warehouse flow and layout under ambiguous, high-variability conditions.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing warehouse flow and layout under ambiguous, high-variability conditions autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Frazelle's warehouse master-planning method assumes the practitioner adapts layout and flow to conditions the standard playbook doesn't cover. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Frazelle, World-Class Warehousing and Material Handling (McGraw-Hill, 2002).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines warehousing methods and layouts others adopt and fixes operations others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining warehousing methods and layouts others adopt and fixing operations others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the master plan Frazelle's methodology treats as a site-specific design exercise. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Frazelle, World-Class Warehousing and Material Handling (McGraw-Hill, 2002).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets warehousing strategy and anticipates future storage and throughput requirements.
  — *Why this level:* Setting warehousing strategy and anticipating future storage and throughput requirements is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- layout judgment now spans the network's warehousing strategy, not one facility's slotting. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Frazelle, World-Class Warehousing and Material Handling (McGraw-Hill, 2002).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading warehousing practice for the discipline and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading warehousing practice for the discipline and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the tier that writes reference texts like Frazelle's rather than applies them. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Frazelle, World-Class Warehousing and Material Handling (McGraw-Hill, 2002).

#### Manufacturing & Production

<a id="scm-07"></a>
##### SCM-07 — Manufacturing & production operations

*Type:* Technical — Convert inputs into finished goods through planned, controlled, efficient production.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs defined production tasks and records output under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Performing defined production tasks and recording output under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- following a standard work instruction exactly. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs standard production lines, handling routine variation with review.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard production lines and handling routine variation independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Ohno's standardized work is executed as specified, with recognized variation handled by rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ohno, Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production (Productivity Press, 1988).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously manages complex production with ambiguous disruptions, holding output and quality.
  — *Why this level:* Managing complex production through ambiguous disruptions while holding output and quality autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Ohno's Toyota Production System expects line leaders to stop-and-fix (jidoka) and improvise recovery from disruptions standard work doesn't anticipate, exactly this level's behavior. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Ohno, Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production (Productivity Press, 1988).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines production-operations methods others adopt and resolves problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining production-operations methods others adopt and resolving problems others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the standardized-work and kaizen system TPS describes as a design responsibility, not follows one line's instructions. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ohno, Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production (Productivity Press, 1988).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets manufacturing-operations strategy and anticipates how production capability must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting manufacturing-operations strategy and anticipating how production capability must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- production judgment now spans plant-wide capability strategy, not one line's recovery. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ohno, Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production (Productivity Press, 1988).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-in-class manufacturing operations and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-in-class manufacturing operations and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the tier Ohno himself occupied in originating TPS as an industry-shaping system. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Ohno, Toyota Production System: Beyond Large-Scale Production (Productivity Press, 1988).

<a id="scm-08"></a>
##### SCM-08 — Production scheduling & shop-floor control

*Type:* Technical — Sequence, schedule, and monitor production to optimize throughput and on-time output.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Updates schedules and logs shop-floor status from given inputs under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Updating schedules and logging shop-floor status from given inputs under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- data entry against a schedule someone else built. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently builds routine production schedules and manages standard sequencing with review.
  — *Why this level:* Building routine production schedules and managing standard sequencing independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- a fixed sequencing rule is applied without diagnosing where the true bottleneck sits. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Goldratt & Cox, The Goal: A Process of Ongoing Improvement (North River Press, 1984).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously schedules under volatile constraints, rebalancing the floor to hold commitments.
  — *Why this level:* Scheduling under volatile constraints and rebalancing the floor to hold commitments autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Goldratt's Theory of Constraints requires identifying and subordinating the floor to the shifting bottleneck in real time, the judgment this level names. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Goldratt & Cox, The Goal: A Process of Ongoing Improvement (North River Press, 1984).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines scheduling and control methods others adopt and resolves the hardest sequencing problems.
  — *Why this level:* Defining scheduling and control methods others adopt and resolving the hardest sequencing problems is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the constraint-exploitation strategy Goldratt frames as a design decision for the plant, not applies a fixed dispatch rule. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Goldratt & Cox, The Goal: A Process of Ongoing Improvement (North River Press, 1984).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets shop-floor scheduling strategy and anticipates how control systems must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting shop-floor scheduling strategy and anticipating how control systems must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- scheduling judgment now spans how the plant's whole control system should be architected. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Goldratt & Cox, The Goal: A Process of Ongoing Improvement (North River Press, 1984).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading production-scheduling practice for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading production-scheduling practice for the field and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the origin-theory tier The Goal itself occupies in the scheduling discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Goldratt & Cox, The Goal: A Process of Ongoing Improvement (North River Press, 1984).

<a id="scm-09"></a>
##### SCM-09 — Asset & maintenance management

*Type:* Technical — Sustain reliability of physical assets through preventive and corrective maintenance.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records asset data and completes scheduled maintenance tasks under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Recording asset data and completing scheduled maintenance tasks under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- executing a fixed PM checklist, no diagnosis. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs routine preventive maintenance and work orders with review.
  — *Why this level:* Running routine preventive maintenance and work orders independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Nakajima's scheduled-PM cycle is executed as designed, before autonomous-maintenance judgment is expected. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nakajima, Introduction to TPM: Total Productive Maintenance (Productivity Press, 1988).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously diagnoses ambiguous failures and optimizes maintenance strategy for critical assets.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing ambiguous failures and optimizing maintenance strategy for critical assets autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Nakajima's TPM explicitly assigns root-cause diagnosis and strategy selection (breakdown vs. preventive vs. predictive) to this autonomy tier, beyond following the PM calendar. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Nakajima, Introduction to TPM: Total Productive Maintenance (Productivity Press, 1988).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines maintenance and reliability methods others adopt and solves failures others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining maintenance and reliability methods others adopt and solving failures others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the asset-management policy ISO 55000 leaves organization-specific, rather than executes one asset's maintenance plan. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 55000:2014 Asset Management -- Overview, Principles and Terminology.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets asset-management strategy and anticipates lifecycle and reliability needs ahead.
  — *Why this level:* Setting asset-management strategy and anticipating lifecycle and reliability needs ahead is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- ISO 55000's principle of aligning asset management with organizational objectives now operates at enterprise scope. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 55000:2014 Asset Management -- Overview, Principles and Terminology.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice asset and reliability management and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice asset and reliability management and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the tier Nakajima occupied in codifying TPM as a discipline other plants then adopted. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Nakajima, Introduction to TPM: Total Productive Maintenance (Productivity Press, 1988).

<a id="scm-10"></a>
##### SCM-10 — Quality management & control

*Type:* Technical — Define, inspect, and assure that products and processes meet quality standards.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs defined inspections and records quality results under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Performing defined inspections and recording quality results under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- checking against a spec someone else set. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs routine quality controls and investigates standard defects with review.
  — *Why this level:* Running routine quality controls and investigating standard defects independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- ISO 9001's process-approach controls are executed as documented, without redesigning the QMS. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems -- Requirements.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously diagnoses ambiguous quality issues and sets local control standards end-to-end.
  — *Why this level:* Diagnosing ambiguous quality issues and setting local control standards end-to-end autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- ISO 9001's Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle expects this tier to close the loop on root cause and control-standard design, not just detect defects. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems -- Requirements.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the quality-management system others adopt and resolves root causes others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the quality-management system others adopt and resolving root causes others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the QMS ISO 9001 specifies as a set of requirements to design into, rather than operates within one someone else designed. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems -- Requirements.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets enterprise quality strategy and anticipates emerging quality and compliance demands.
  — *Why this level:* Setting enterprise quality strategy and anticipating emerging quality and compliance demands is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- quality judgment now spans enterprise QMS strategy, not one process's control plan. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems -- Requirements.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good quality management means for the discipline and is externally credible.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good quality management means for the discipline and being externally credible is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the standards-committee tier that writes revisions to ISO 9001 itself. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); International Organization for Standardization, ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management Systems -- Requirements.

#### Logistics & Fulfillment

<a id="scm-11"></a>
##### SCM-11 — Logistics & distribution management

*Type:* Technical — Plan and execute movement and delivery of goods across transport modes and channels.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Schedules routine shipments and tracks deliveries under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Scheduling routine shipments and tracking deliveries under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- executing a fixed shipping plan. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages standard freight and distribution lanes with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing standard freight and distribution lanes independently with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Chopra & Meindl's mode/lane trade-off rules are applied to known lane types. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously optimizes complex distribution under ambiguous disruptions and cost pressures.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing complex distribution under ambiguous disruptions and cost pressures autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- SCOR's Deliver (Fulfill) process assumes the practitioner resolves disruption trade-offs in real time at this tier, beyond running a fixed lane plan. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines logistics methods and carrier strategy others adopt and resolves problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining logistics methods and carrier strategy others adopt and resolving problems others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the transportation-network design Chopra & Meindl frame as a strategic driver choice for others to execute. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets distribution strategy and anticipates how logistics networks must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting distribution strategy and anticipating how logistics networks must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- logistics judgment now spans the whole Deliver process's network design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading logistics practice for the discipline and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading logistics practice for the discipline and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the framework-authoring tier the textbook's own driver model occupies. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Chopra & Meindl, Supply Chain Management: Strategy, Planning, and Operation, 6th Edition (Pearson, 2016).

<a id="scm-12"></a>
##### SCM-12 — Order management & fulfillment

*Type:* Technical — Process, allocate, and fulfill orders accurately from capture through delivery and returns.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Processes standard orders and resolves routine exceptions under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Processing standard orders and resolving routine exceptions under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- following the exception playbook, not writing it. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages order flow and standard fulfillment issues with review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing order flow and standard fulfillment issues independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- SCOR's Fulfill process's standard order-to-delivery steps are executed as designed. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously orchestrates complex multi-source fulfillment and resolves ambiguous exceptions.
  — *Why this level:* Orchestrating complex multi-source fulfillment and resolving ambiguous exceptions autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- SCOR's Fulfill process assumes cross-source allocation judgment at this tier when standard rules don't resolve an exception. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines order-management practices others adopt and fixes fulfillment breakdowns others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining order-management practices others adopt and fixing fulfillment breakdowns others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the allocation/orchestration policy SCOR's Fulfill process leaves organization-specific. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets fulfillment strategy and anticipates how order orchestration must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting fulfillment strategy and anticipating how order orchestration must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- fulfillment judgment now spans the enterprise's whole order-to-deliver design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice order management and fulfillment and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice order management and fulfillment and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the ASCM-standards tier that defines the Fulfill process itself. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.

<a id="scm-13"></a>
##### SCM-13 — Reverse logistics & returns management

*Type:* Technical — Manage returns, repairs, recycling, and disposal flows to recover value and reduce waste.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Processes standard returns and records dispositions under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Processing standard returns and recording dispositions under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- applying a fixed disposition rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently manages routine returns flows and standard disposition rules with review.
  — *Why this level:* Managing routine returns flows and standard disposition rules independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Rogers & Tibben-Lembke's standard gatekeeping rules are applied as documented. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rogers & Tibben-Lembke, Going Backwards: Reverse Logistics Trends and Practices (Reverse Logistics Executive Council, 1998).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously designs returns and recovery processes for ambiguous, high-volume situations.
  — *Why this level:* Designing returns and recovery processes for ambiguous, high-volume situations autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Rogers & Tibben-Lembke identify gatekeeping and disposition-process design, not rule execution, as the differentiator once return volume and ambiguity rise. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Rogers & Tibben-Lembke, Going Backwards: Reverse Logistics Trends and Practices (Reverse Logistics Executive Council, 1998).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines reverse-logistics methods others adopt and recovers value others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining reverse-logistics methods others adopt and recovering value others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the recovery-channel strategy Rogers & Tibben-Lembke frame as an organizational design choice. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Rogers & Tibben-Lembke, Going Backwards: Reverse Logistics Trends and Practices (Reverse Logistics Executive Council, 1998).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets returns and circularity strategy and anticipates evolving recovery demands.
  — *Why this level:* Setting returns and circularity strategy and anticipating evolving recovery demands is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- returns judgment now spans the enterprise's whole SCOR Return process design. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ASCM (APICS), Supply Chain Operations Reference (SCOR) Digital Standard.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading reverse-logistics practice for the field and is externally recognized for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading reverse-logistics practice for the field and being externally recognized is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the field-founding tier Rogers & Tibben-Lembke's own study occupies in naming reverse logistics as a discipline. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Rogers & Tibben-Lembke, Going Backwards: Reverse Logistics Trends and Practices (Reverse Logistics Executive Council, 1998).

#### Service Operations

<a id="scm-14"></a>
##### SCM-14 — Service delivery operations

*Type:* Technical — Plan, deliver, and control execution of services to meet scope, quality, and timeliness.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Executes defined service tasks and logs outcomes under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Executing defined service tasks and logging outcomes under supervision is the Dreyfus novice band -- delivering to a fixed script. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently runs standard service delivery, meeting routine SLAs with review.
  — *Why this level:* Running standard service delivery and meeting routine SLAs independently with review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- Fitzsimmons's standard service-encounter design is executed as specified. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bordoloi, Fitzsimmons & Fitzsimmons, Service Management: Operations, Strategy, Information Technology, 10th Edition (McGraw-Hill, 2023).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously manages complex service operations, holding performance under ambiguous demand.
  — *Why this level:* Managing complex service operations and holding performance under ambiguous demand autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Fitzsimmons frame capacity-demand matching under variable service demand as requiring active managerial judgment at this tier, not a fixed staffing script. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Bordoloi, Fitzsimmons & Fitzsimmons, Service Management: Operations, Strategy, Information Technology, 10th Edition (McGraw-Hill, 2023).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines service-delivery methods others adopt and resolves operational failures others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining service-delivery methods others adopt and resolving operational failures others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the service-strategy design Fitzsimmons treat as a deliberate managerial choice, for other teams to execute. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bordoloi, Fitzsimmons & Fitzsimmons, Service Management: Operations, Strategy, Information Technology, 10th Edition (McGraw-Hill, 2023).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets service-operations strategy and anticipates how service capability must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting service-operations strategy and anticipating how service capability must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- service judgment now spans enterprise service-capability strategy, not one team's SLA. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bordoloi, Fitzsimmons & Fitzsimmons, Service Management: Operations, Strategy, Information Technology, 10th Edition (McGraw-Hill, 2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-in-class service delivery for the discipline and is externally credible on it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-in-class service delivery for the discipline and being externally credible is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the textbook-authoring tier that defines service-management practice for the field. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bordoloi, Fitzsimmons & Fitzsimmons, Service Management: Operations, Strategy, Information Technology, 10th Edition (McGraw-Hill, 2023).

<a id="scm-15"></a>
##### SCM-15 — Field operations & dispatch coordination

*Type:* Behavioral — Coordinate dispatch, routing, and on-site service to meet commitments and customer needs.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Assigns routine jobs and updates dispatch status under guidance.
  — *Why this level:* Assigning routine jobs and updating dispatch status under guidance is the Dreyfus novice band -- following a fixed assignment rule. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Independently coordinates standard field schedules and routing with normal review.
  — *Why this level:* Coordinating standard field schedules and routing independently with normal review is Dreyfus's advanced-beginner band -- a static routing plan is applied to known job patterns without re-optimizing under disruption. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Dantzig & Ramser, The Truck Dispatching Problem, Management Science 6(1), 80-91 (1959).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Autonomously optimizes dispatch under volatile demand, resolving conflicts and emergencies.
  — *Why this level:* Optimizing dispatch under volatile demand and resolving conflicts and emergencies autonomously is the Dreyfus competent band -- Dantzig & Ramser's routing-optimization problem becomes a live, judgment-driven re-optimization task exactly when demand turns volatile, the behavior this level names. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Dantzig & Ramser, The Truck Dispatching Problem, Management Science 6(1), 80-91 (1959).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines field-coordination methods others adopt and solves dispatch problems others can't.
  — *Why this level:* Defining field-coordination methods others adopt and solving dispatch problems others can't is SFIA Level 5 Ensure-and-advise -- the practitioner now authors the routing/dispatch model Dantzig & Ramser's problem formalizes, for others to run day to day. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dantzig & Ramser, The Truck Dispatching Problem, Management Science 6(1), 80-91 (1959).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets field-operations strategy and anticipates how dispatch and routing must evolve.
  — *Why this level:* Setting field-operations strategy and anticipating how dispatch and routing must evolve is SFIA Level 6 Initiate-and-influence -- field judgment now spans the enterprise's whole field-service capability strategy, the top scope service-management theory addresses. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Bordoloi, Fitzsimmons & Fitzsimmons, Service Management: Operations, Strategy, Information Technology, 10th Edition (McGraw-Hill, 2023).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading field-operations practice for the field and is sought externally for it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading field-operations practice for the field and being sought externally is SFIA Level 7 Set-strategy-and-inspire -- this is the origin-theory tier the Dantzig-Ramser routing formulation occupies, the seed of modern dispatch optimization. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Dantzig & Ramser, The Truck Dispatching Problem, Management Science 6(1), 80-91 (1959).

### Corporate IT & Workplace Technology (CIT)

#### Service Management & Support

<a id="cit-01"></a>
##### CIT-01 — IT service management & service desk

*Type:* Technical — Operate request, incident, and problem management to restore and sustain employee IT services.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Logs and triages incoming tickets using set scripts, escalating anything beyond well-defined fixes.
  — *Why this level:* Logging and triaging tickets by set scripts, escalating anything beyond well-defined fixes, is ITIL 4's incident/request-management practice run with no situational judgment — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Resolves standard incidents and service requests independently within SLA, escalating only genuine edge cases.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving standard incidents and requests independently within SLA is the same ITIL 4 practices run competently on routine variation without escalation — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns ambiguous and high-impact incidents end-to-end, sets local triage and escalation conventions.
  — *Why this level:* Owning ambiguous, high-impact incidents end-to-end and setting local triage conventions is HDI's Team Lead tier — coordinating escalation and setting process for a team, not just following it — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the ticket taxonomy, SLA tiers, and queue-routing model that other support staff adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the ticket taxonomy, SLA tiers, and routing model other support staff adopt is HDI's Support Center Manager tier applied to process design, matching SFIA's ensure/advise responsibility level. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the service-management strategy and metrics framework across the organization's support function.
  — *Why this level:* Setting service-management strategy and metrics across the whole support function is SFIA's initiate/influence responsibility band, turning ITIL 4's continual-improvement practice into enforced organizational policy rather than one team's convention. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines what good service management looks like for the discipline and shapes external practice.
  — *Why this level:* Defining what good service management looks like for the discipline and shaping external practice is the ITIL Master tier's own bar — proposing and defending original service-management approaches to a review panel — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).

<a id="cit-02"></a>
##### CIT-02 — Change & release management

*Type:* Technical — Govern controlled introduction of changes to enterprise systems to minimize disruption.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Prepares change records and gathers approvals for low-risk, pre-templated changes under review.
  — *Why this level:* Preparing change records and gathering approvals for pre-templated, low-risk changes under review is ITIL 4's change-enablement practice run as scripted paperwork, not judgment — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Plans and executes standard changes independently, writing usable rollback steps and impact notes.
  — *Why this level:* Planning and executing standard changes independently, with usable rollback steps and impact notes, is the same change-enablement practice run competently on routine work — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Owns risky, multi-team changes, judges risk and ambiguity, and is the go-to change coordinator.
  — *Why this level:* Owning risky, multi-team changes and judging risk under ambiguity is exactly the change-authorization judgment ITIL 4 reserves for cases the standard workflow doesn't script — the Dreyfus competent band, the go-to coordinator. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the change-control and release process, risk-tiering, and CAB model others follow.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the change-control, risk-tiering, and CAB model others follow is applying the DevOps Handbook's Second Way — reducing approval friction while containing risk — as team-wide process design, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Kim, Humble, Debois & Willis, The DevOps Handbook (IT Revolution Press, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets release-governance strategy balancing change velocity and stability across the organization.
  — *Why this level:* Setting release-governance strategy that balances velocity and stability is applying Accelerate's empirically validated finding that change failure rate and deployment frequency move together, not in tension, for elite performers — as enforced organizational policy. *Sources:* Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines industry-credible release-management practice and influences how the discipline operates.
  — *Why this level:* Defining industry-credible release-management practice and shaping how the discipline operates is producing the kind of empirically grounded, externally adopted practice Accelerate's own research program represents — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Forsgren, Humble & Kim, Accelerate: The Science of Lean Software and DevOps (IT Revolution Press, 2018); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).

<a id="cit-03"></a>
##### CIT-03 — End-user support & enablement

*Type:* Behavioral — Resolve user issues and build employee proficiency with workplace technology.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Handles common how-to questions and walk-throughs at the desk, escalating unfamiliar issues.
  — *Why this level:* Handling common how-to questions at the desk and escalating unfamiliar issues is explicit, rule-following practice — the Dreyfus novice band; HDI's entry Support Center Analyst tier covers exactly this scope. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Resolves most end-user problems independently and produces clear self-help guidance for users.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving most end-user problems independently and producing clear self-help guidance is HDI's Analyst tier performed competently and without escalation on routine issues — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Tackles the hardest user-enablement cases and sets local standards for guidance and onboarding.
  — *Why this level:* Tackling the hardest user-enablement cases and setting local standards for guidance and onboarding is HDI's Team Lead tier — setting team practice, not just executing it — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* HDI, Support Center Analyst / Team Lead / Manager Certification Standards (accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the enablement program, training curriculum, and support model others deliver against.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the enablement program, training curriculum, and support model others deliver against is building training to Kirkpatrick's reaction/learning/behavior/results structure at program-design scope, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's strategy for user adoption, digital literacy, and support experience.
  — *Why this level:* Setting organization-wide strategy for adoption, digital literacy, and support experience is applying Kirkpatrick's evaluation levels — especially level 4, organizational results — as the frame for a strategy spanning every team's enablement, not one program's curriculum. *Sources:* Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice end-user enablement for the field and shapes how others teach it.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice end-user enablement for the field and shaping how others teach it is externally credible contribution to training-evaluation practice itself, beyond applying Kirkpatrick's model — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Kirkpatrick, Evaluating Training Programs: The Four Levels (Berrett-Koehler, 1994).

#### Endpoint & Workplace

<a id="cit-04"></a>
##### CIT-04 — Endpoint & device management

*Type:* Technical — Provision, configure, secure, and maintain employee devices across their lifecycle.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Enrolls, images, and configures devices following documented build steps under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Enrolling, imaging, and configuring devices from documented build steps under supervision is NIST SP 800-124's mobile-device enrollment baseline followed by checklist, not judgment — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* NIST, SP 800-124 Rev. 2: Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages device fleets, policies, and patching independently for standard configurations.
  — *Why this level:* Managing device fleets, policies, and patching independently for standard configurations is running SP 800-124's device-management baseline competently across routine variation without escalation — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* NIST, SP 800-124 Rev. 2: Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise (2023); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex endpoint, compliance, and policy issues; sets local device-management standards.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex endpoint, compliance, and policy issues and setting local device-management standards is applying CIS Controls v8's Safeguards (inventory, secure configuration) to cases the baseline checklist doesn't resolve — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Center for Internet Security, CIS Critical Security Controls, Version 8 (2021); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the endpoint architecture, policy baseline, and lifecycle model others implement.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the endpoint architecture, policy baseline, and lifecycle model others implement is authoring an organization's own Control 1/Control 4 implementation others follow, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Center for Internet Security, CIS Critical Security Controls, Version 8 (2021); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets endpoint strategy across platforms, anticipating shifts in management and security posture.
  — *Why this level:* Setting endpoint strategy across platforms, anticipating shifts in management and security posture, is SFIA's initiate/influence band applied to migrating endpoint trust from perimeter assumptions toward the device-posture checks NIST SP 800-207's zero-trust architecture requires. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative endpoint-management practice and influences the discipline externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative endpoint-management practice and influencing the discipline externally is the expert-consensus contribution that builds CIS Controls itself — a global practitioner community authoring the standard, not just applying it — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Center for Internet Security, CIS Critical Security Controls, Version 8 (2021); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).

<a id="cit-05"></a>
##### CIT-05 — Collaboration & productivity platform management

*Type:* Technical — Administer messaging, document, and collaboration environments for employees.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Configures user accounts, groups, and shared spaces in the platform following set procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Configuring user accounts, groups, and shared spaces by set procedure is the entry associate-level scope Microsoft's Administrator Expert path presupposes before independent work — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Microsoft, Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (Exam MS-102, accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Administers collaboration services independently, handling routine config, permissions, and issues.
  — *Why this level:* Administering collaboration services independently — routine config, permissions, issues — is exactly the associate-certification (Endpoint/Teams/Identity Administrator) scope performed competently without escalation — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Microsoft, Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (Exam MS-102, accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex platform, governance, and integration problems; sets local configuration standards.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex platform, governance, and integration problems and setting local configuration standards is the tenant-wide judgment the MS-102 Administrator Expert exam tests — identity, security, and compliance governance across the estate — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Microsoft, Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (Exam MS-102, accessed 2026-07); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the platform architecture, governance, and adoption model that administrators follow.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the platform architecture, governance, and adoption model administrators follow moves from passing the Expert exam's scenarios to authoring the tenant governance model those scenarios assume, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Microsoft, Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (Exam MS-102, accessed 2026-07); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's collaboration-platform strategy and roadmap across the workplace estate.
  — *Why this level:* Setting collaboration-platform strategy and roadmap across the whole workplace estate is SFIA's initiate/influence responsibility band, applied beyond one tenant's governance model to organizational technology strategy. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Microsoft, Microsoft 365 Certified: Administrator Expert (Exam MS-102, accessed 2026-07).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines leading collaboration-platform practice and shapes how the discipline is run elsewhere.
  — *Why this level:* Defining leading collaboration-platform practice and shaping how the discipline is run elsewhere is externally credible, discipline-shaping contribution beyond any one organization's tenant — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).

#### Enterprise Applications

<a id="cit-06"></a>
##### CIT-06 — Enterprise application administration

*Type:* Technical — Configure, maintain, and support shared business applications across corporate functions.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs routine application config and user-provisioning tasks under guidance and review.
  — *Why this level:* Performing routine application config and user-provisioning tasks under guidance is ITIL 4's service-request-management practice run by checklist — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Administers an enterprise application independently, handling standard config and support tasks.
  — *Why this level:* Administering an application independently — standard config and support tasks — is the same practice run competently on routine work without escalation — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex configuration, upgrade, and data issues; is the go-to admin for the application.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex configuration, upgrade, and data issues as the go-to admin is exercising the judgment ITIL 4 reserves for cases the standard runbook doesn't cover — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* AXELOS, ITIL Foundation: ITIL 4 Edition (2019); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the application's configuration baseline, upgrade approach, and governance others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the configuration baseline, upgrade approach, and governance others adopt is instantiating one of COBIT 2019's management objectives — e.g., managed configuration and change — as a concrete, team-adopted practice, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* ISACA, COBIT 2019 Framework: Governance and Management Objectives (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the administration strategy and standards across the enterprise application portfolio.
  — *Why this level:* Setting administration strategy and standards across the whole application portfolio is COBIT 2019's governance layer — aligning IT-enabled services with enterprise goals — applied at SFIA's initiate/influence band rather than one system's configuration. *Sources:* ISACA, COBIT 2019 Framework: Governance and Management Objectives (2018); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative enterprise-application administration practice recognized beyond the organization.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative enterprise-application administration practice recognized beyond the organization is externally credible contribution to the governance discipline COBIT itself codifies — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* ISACA, COBIT 2019 Framework: Governance and Management Objectives (2018); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).

<a id="cit-07"></a>
##### CIT-07 — Business systems integration & automation

*Type:* Technical — Connect enterprise systems and automate workflows to streamline business processes.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Builds simple, pre-specified integrations or automations from templates under review.
  — *Why this level:* Building simple, pre-specified integrations from templates under review is applying a single pattern from Hohpe & Woolf's catalog without yet choosing which pattern fits — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Develops standard integrations and automated workflows independently with normal testing and review.
  — *Why this level:* Developing standard integrations and automated workflows independently is selecting and applying Enterprise Integration Patterns competently on routine, well-understood system pairs — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Designs complex, multi-system integrations and resolves the hardest data and reliability problems.
  — *Why this level:* Designing complex, multi-system integrations and resolving the hardest data and reliability problems is composing Hohpe & Woolf's patterns to solve cases the catalog doesn't hand you pre-assembled — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Defines the integration patterns, automation framework, and standards other builders adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Defining the integration patterns, automation framework, and standards other builders adopt is publishing a house dialect of Enterprise Integration Patterns as team practice, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets the organization's integration and automation strategy across business systems.
  — *Why this level:* Setting integration and automation strategy across all business systems is SFIA's initiate/influence band, applied to which pattern language and platform the whole organization standardizes on rather than one integration. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice systems integration and automation and influences the broader discipline.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice systems integration and influencing the broader discipline is externally credible pattern-catalog-shaping work in Hohpe & Woolf's own tradition — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); Hohpe & Woolf, Enterprise Integration Patterns: Designing, Building, and Deploying Messaging Solutions (Addison-Wesley, 2003).

#### Identity & Asset Governance

<a id="cit-08"></a>
##### CIT-08 — Identity & access administration (internal)

*Type:* Technical — Manage employee identities, accounts, and access rights across enterprise systems per policy.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Provisions accounts and applies access requests following defined approval workflows under review.
  — *Why this level:* Provisioning accounts and applying access requests through a defined approval workflow under review is NIST SP 800-53's AC-2 account-management control executed by checklist — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* NIST, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, SP 800-53 Revision 5 (2020, updated 2021); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Manages identities, groups, and access independently, handling standard joiner-mover-leaver flows.
  — *Why this level:* Managing identities, groups, and access independently for standard joiner-mover-leaver flows is the same AC-2 practice run competently without escalation on routine changes — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* NIST, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, SP 800-53 Revision 5 (2020, updated 2021); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex access, entitlement, and recertification issues; sets local identity standards.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex access, entitlement, and recertification issues is exercising AC-6 least-privilege judgment on ambiguous cases the standard workflow doesn't resolve — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* NIST, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, SP 800-53 Revision 5 (2020, updated 2021); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the access model, role structure, and provisioning approach others implement.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the access model, role structure, and provisioning approach others implement is authoring the identity-and-policy-engine components NIST SP 800-207's zero-trust architecture requires an organization to define for itself, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets identity-and-access strategy, including governance and least-privilege posture, organization-wide.
  — *Why this level:* Setting identity-and-access strategy, including governance and least-privilege posture, organization-wide is SFIA's initiate/influence band applied to adopting zero-trust architecture as enforced policy rather than one system's access model. *Sources:* NIST, Zero Trust Architecture, SP 800-207 (2020); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative internal identity-administration practice and shapes the discipline externally.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative internal identity-administration practice and shaping the discipline externally is what Google's engineers did in originating BeyondCorp — publishing a perimeter-less identity practice that later became the NIST SP 800-207 standard — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Ward & Beyer, BeyondCorp: A New Approach to Enterprise Security, ;login: 39(6), 6-11 (USENIX, 2014); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).

<a id="cit-09"></a>
##### CIT-09 — IT asset & license management

*Type:* Technical — Track and optimize IT hardware, software, and license inventories across lifecycle and cost.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Records assets and license entitlements in the register following documented procedures.
  — *Why this level:* Recording assets and license entitlements in the register by documented procedure is ISO/IEC 19770-1's baseline process tier followed without judgment — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* ISO/IEC, Information Technology - IT Asset Management - Part 1: IT Asset Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 19770-1:2017; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Maintains asset and license data independently, tracking lifecycle and reconciling routine discrepancies.
  — *Why this level:* Maintaining asset and license data independently, tracking lifecycle and reconciling routine discrepancies, is running ISO/IEC 19770-1's core process areas competently on standard cases — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* ISO/IEC, Information Technology - IT Asset Management - Part 1: IT Asset Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 19770-1:2017; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex license-compliance and asset-optimization issues; sets local asset standards.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex license-compliance and asset-optimization issues is exercising judgment on the ISO/IEC 19770-1 process areas the standard tier doesn't script — the Dreyfus competent band, the local go-to. *Sources:* ISO/IEC, Information Technology - IT Asset Management - Part 1: IT Asset Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 19770-1:2017; Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the asset-lifecycle and license-management model and controls others adopt.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the asset-lifecycle and license-management model and controls others adopt is moving an organization up ISO/IEC 19770-1's tier structure by authoring the controls that tier requires, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* ISO/IEC, Information Technology - IT Asset Management - Part 1: IT Asset Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 19770-1:2017; SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets asset-and-license strategy, optimizing cost and compliance across the organization.
  — *Why this level:* Setting asset-and-license strategy, optimizing cost and compliance across the organization, is SFIA's initiate/influence band applied to running ISO/IEC 19770-1 at its most mature, optimized tier organization-wide. *Sources:* SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024); ISO/IEC, Information Technology - IT Asset Management - Part 1: IT Asset Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 19770-1:2017.
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines best-practice asset and license management and influences how the discipline operates.
  — *Why this level:* Defining best-practice asset and license management and influencing how the discipline operates is externally credible contribution to the ITAM practice ISO/IEC 19770-1 itself codifies — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980); ISO/IEC, Information Technology - IT Asset Management - Part 1: IT Asset Management Systems - Requirements, ISO/IEC 19770-1:2017.

#### Infrastructure & Operations

<a id="cit-10"></a>
##### CIT-10 — Enterprise infrastructure operations

*Type:* Technical — Operate and maintain corporate compute, storage, and network for reliable internal services.

- **[P1 — Assisted](proficiency_scale.md#p1):** Performs routine infrastructure monitoring and maintenance tasks following runbooks under supervision.
  — *Why this level:* Performing routine monitoring and maintenance from runbooks under supervision is Limoncelli's standard-operating-procedure practice followed step by step, not yet adapted — the Dreyfus novice band. *Sources:* Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P2 — Independent](proficiency_scale.md#p2):** Operates and maintains infrastructure services independently, handling standard incidents and changes.
  — *Why this level:* Operating and maintaining infrastructure independently, handling standard incidents and changes, is The Practice of System and Network Administration's operational discipline run competently without escalation — the Dreyfus advanced-beginner band. *Sources:* Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P3 — Proficient](proficiency_scale.md#p3):** Resolves complex outages and capacity issues; sets local operational standards and is the go-to operator.
  — *Why this level:* Resolving complex outages and capacity issues as the go-to operator is exercising the diagnostic and capacity-planning judgment Limoncelli's book treats as separating a senior admin from a junior one — the Dreyfus competent band. *Sources:* Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
- **[P4 — Expert](proficiency_scale.md#p4):** Designs the operational architecture, resilience approach, and runbook standards others follow.
  — *Why this level:* Designing the operational architecture, resilience approach, and runbook standards others follow is authoring the org-wide operations practice Limoncelli's later chapters describe as senior/lead scope, SFIA's ensure/advise reach. *Sources:* Limoncelli, Chalup & Hogan, The Practice of System and Network Administration: DevOps and Other Best Practices for Enterprise IT, Volume 1, 3rd Edition (Addison-Wesley Professional, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P5 — Authority](proficiency_scale.md#p5):** Sets infrastructure-operations strategy, anticipating capacity, resilience, and platform shifts.
  — *Why this level:* Setting infrastructure-operations strategy and anticipating capacity, resilience, and platform shifts is the SRE book's org-level reliability-strategy chapters — capacity planning, launch and product reviews — applied at SFIA's initiate/influence band. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); SFIA Foundation, Skills Framework for the Information Age, version 9 (2024).
- **[P6 — Pioneer](proficiency_scale.md#p6):** Defines authoritative infrastructure-operations practice and shapes the discipline beyond the organization.
  — *Why this level:* Defining authoritative infrastructure-operations practice beyond the organization is the externally published, industry-shaping contribution the SRE book itself represents — the Dreyfus master band. *Sources:* Beyer, Jones, Petoff & Murphy (eds.), Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems (O'Reilly/Google, 2016); Dreyfus & Dreyfus, A Five-Stage Model of the Mental Activities Involved in Directed Skill Acquisition (1980).
